comments.author: voicebox-gate-recover
comments.text:
AUTHOR HANDOFF — IN_REVIEW pending coord-routed cross-family reviewer. Branch origin/fleet/jeye-boot-order@13ee325 (clean, matches remote; based on origin/main a81c667). Test-timing fix only: 2 files, +29/-1 (tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs and the docs sentence that describes it). No production file changes.

THE FAILURE, AND WHY IT IS A RACE RATHER THAN A BAD TEST FILE:
· Sealed full manifest for the landed tree 3d19617: this file IS present — tier browser, selection full-roster, dispatch ran, status passed, 5 tests / 5 pass, 8.656s, timeout 300000. So the gate ran it GREEN inside the shard queue while it failed STANDALONE on the merger's box.
· Mechanism (both conditions explained by one fact): the arm waited only for `#mic-device-state`, then read `#out-device-state`. The output row's FIRST branch reads `canChooseOutput`, a fact ONLY the live client knows, and that client is published by `public/live-voice.js` — a DIFFERENT module script from the one that boots the surface (`public/fused.js`) whose body awaits. Completion order between the two is therefore NOT fixed, and differs between a loaded shard queue and an idle standalone box. Where live-voice.js lost the race, `audioDeviceController.refresh()` at fused.js boot ran with no client, so `canChooseOutput` was false and the row painted "This browser uses system output. Change the output in your device's sound settings." — a correct module, a stale row, and the assertion `rows.out.includes("Studio monitors")` failed at line 210. The gate's own concurrency is what made it pass there.
· Reproduced DETERMINISTICALLY on a81c667 (the race does not trigger on this box standalone, so the losing order was forced): with no client at refresh time, the old arm's read path yields "This browser uses system output. Change the output in your device's sound settings." and the assertion FAILS; the fixed path yields "Studio monitors is not connected. No reply playing."

THE FIX (the ezu7 lesson applied — the wait covers EVERY observable the arm asserts, not just the first one it happens to see):
1. wait for `window.__voiceboxDevices` (as before);
2. wait for the live client to be published — the fact the output row actually depends on;
3. DRIVE a refresh (`await window.__voiceboxDevices.refresh()`) — the same call the real user path makes when the settings dialog opens, so the arm no longer reads whatever the boot refresh happened to paint;
4. wait for the OUTPUT row to name its saved device, and only then
5. wait for the MIC row (the row it used to rely on).
The assertion itself is untouched (`rows.out.includes("Studio monitors")`), so it keeps its teeth: it still fails if the module stops naming the chosen-but-absent output.

SENSITIVITY, proved rather than asserted (so the new wait cannot pass vacuously): the control removes the live client, refreshes, and requires the SAME row to paint "This browser uses system output…" — i.e. the row really reads the client fact — then restores the client, refreshes, and requires the saved device to be named again. That also documents the race in the test for the next reader instead of hiding it behind a wait.

VERIFICATION (coord asked for >=20 repeated standalone runs plus the gate's shard condition):
· 24/24 repeated STANDALONE runs of the fixed file PASSED (5/5 tests each, 54s for the 24) — `fleet-gate jeye-verify`, log /tmp/gate-recover-jeye-verify.log, per-run logs /tmp/jeye-run-*.log.
· 12 further runs at FOUR CONCURRENT PROCESSES x 3 rounds (the shard-queue condition rather than the idle one) ALL PASSED 5/5 — /tmp/jeye-load-*.log.
· The gate's own shard condition, same worker count: `node scripts/gate-tier.mjs --tier unit` -> 94 recorded, 94 passed, 0 failed, 0 not terminal (every file in the lane has a terminal record). exit 0.
· Canonical unit-only fast gate on the exact tree: PASS, rc 0, 36s, cmd `npm run test:unit`, tree c1c05dce2c04de4f60c5be35be272f5b628805a4, coverage UNKNOWN (unit-only, NOT behaviour proof on its own; the browser arms above are).
· Honest limit, stated rather than papered over: the race does NOT trigger on this box standalone, so the 24 green runs are not on their own proof that the old arm would have failed here — the proof of mechanism is the deterministic forced-losing-order reproduction on a81c667 quoted above, plus the gate-vs-standalone split coord supplied from the sealed manifest. What the runs do establish is that the fixed arm is stable under both conditions rather than merely lucky in one.
OBSERVATION, NOT FIXED HERE (P3 candidate, deliberately not bundled into a P1 gate fix): because the surface's boot refresh can run before the live client exists, the device rows as painted at boot can carry the "This browser uses system output…" line on a machine that does offer output selection, and nothing repaints them until a `devicechange` or a refresh driven from outside (the settings-open path drives one, which is why the user-visible path self-heals and the owner test stays green). The row's own fact is therefore only guaranteed after a refresh that knows the client. Two ways to close it if coord wants it: have `public/live-voice.js` drive a device refresh when it publishes the client, or have the row's `canChooseOutput` read live at paint time. Both are production behaviour changes on the device surface and want their own bead and review.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs's row-readout arm no longer waits only for the mic row and then reads the output row: it waits for the live client, drives the device refresh the settings-open path drives, and waits for BOTH rows it asserts, with a control that removes the client and requires the system-output line to appear (and the saved device to return once it is restored). The docs sentence describing that arm records why.
WHY: the output row's first branch reads a `canChooseOutput` fact published by live-voice.js, a different module script from the booting fused.js, so the arm's outcome depended on which module won a race that differs between the gate's shard queue (where it passed at 8.656s) and a standalone run (where it failed with "the output row must name its own saved device"). A correct module was being reported as a broken gate, blocking every landing on main.
EFFECT: none for users — no production file changed. The device rows keep telling the truth exactly as before, and the gate is no longer order-dependent: the arm now measures the module rather than the scheduler.

title: deleteMiniApp causes cross-deletion data loss between colliding workspace pages and shelf apps (lib/mini-app-store.mjs:712)
description:
Reviewed voicebox-beads-rtsr delta 2abb42a..d5112f0 (d5112f0 = sha).
Repro: In node with rootPath containing collision.html (Unrelated Page, unproven page) and hostDir/mini-apps containing collision.html + collision.meta.json (Collision App, host shelf app), call deleteMiniApp("Unrelated Page", { rootPath, hostDir }).
Observed: shelfDir/collision.html and collision.meta.json are deleted from disk! In reverse, deleteMiniApp("Collision App", { rootPath, hostDir }) deletes rootPath/collision.html.
Expected: Deleting an unproven workspace page must never touch shelfDir, and deleting a host-only shelf app must never delete unproven workspace files.
Evidence: lib/mini-app-store.mjs:712-748 rmSync candidates unconditionally wipe both shelf and root paths without checking app.kind or provenance.
Fix owner: voicebox-shard-rtsr
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: voicebox-shard-rtsr
comments.text:
P1 HOTFIX IN_REVIEW (separate main-based branch, per coord sequencing). Branch `fleet/collision-hotfix`, tip `d861fe3` (= pushed origin tip). Base 6c306f6.

MAIN EXPOSURE, REPRODUCED (disposable tmp fixture /tmp/rtsr-fix-fixture.mjs against 2abb42a code; the store file is identical at 6c306f6 — `git diff 2abb42a 6c306f6 -- lib/mini-app-store.mjs` is empty):
- REVERSE: `deleteMiniApp("Collision App", {rootPath, hostDir})` deletes the unrelated `rootPath/collision.html` as well as the shelf copy+meta -> "PAGE DELETED" on base.
- SAVE OVERWRITE: `saveMiniApp({fileName:"collision.html", ...})` overwrites the same-slug shelf app's html and record with the page's content; the app's bytes are gone with no way back -> "OVERWRITTEN with the page | PREVIOUS COPY NOT PRESERVED".
- The FORWARD direction (deleting the page by its own title, which removes the shelf app) is NOT reachable on main (one entry per name) and is fixed on `fleet/shard-rtsr` with the classification.

FIX (lib/mini-app-store.mjs; no classification, no UI change):
- Ownership is asked per artifact, answered by the shelf record: the record (matched by the appId inside it) owns the shelf copy it names and its own `.meta.json`; it owns a WORKSPACE file only when it proves it -- `workspacePath` (now written by every save that has a workspace copy) or byte-for-byte equality with the shelf copy for pre-existing records. Unproven workspace files are left on disk. The guessed-at candidates (`<slug>.html`, a second basename) are gone: a name is not evidence.
- A save still replaces the copy at its slug, because on this base an app update and a different file sharing the name are byte-identical states (record + file already written), so refusing would also refuse legitimate updates of pre-existing apps. Instead the replaced copy AND its record are preserved one generation deep in `<hostDir>/mini-app-backups/previous-<slug>.{html,meta.json}` (replaced by the next save, invisible to discovery, removed with the app). No bytes are destroyed; the previous version stays recoverable.
- `workspacePath` makes later ownership decidable by reading the record instead of comparing bytes, which a concurrent write can race.

EVIDENCE: the same test file is RED on the base (8/11; the 3 new cases fail) and GREEN here (11/11): the unrelated workspace file survives deleting the app; a valid saved app still deletes both copies + record + preserved copy (positive control); a save preserves the previous copy and its record; a host-only record names no workspace file and its deletion leaves a same-named unowned workspace file alone.
Focused real-API + browser gate and the exact-tip fast verdict follow in the next comment; independent reviewer next. Not to be closed until landed.

comments.author: voicebox-shard-rtsr
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the comment above (per coord 2026-10-13T04:04Z, which supersedes my first cut): the design is now strict and the tip is `b023709`, not d861fe3.
1. DELETION: a workspace file is deleted ONLY when the shelf record NAMES it (`workspacePath`). The byte-equality fallback is REMOVED — an unrelated file that happens to be identical is indistinguishable from a copy, so a legacy record (no workspacePath) proves nothing about the workspace and the file is left in place (fail closed). The app's own shelf copy and record still go.
2. SAVE: a save that would write a workspace copy is REFUSED `mini-app-name-taken` when the record at that slug does not name the file being saved, checked BEFORE any write of any kind (not even a directory) — no preservation/backup design remains. A host-only save (no workspace root) still updates the app's own shelf copy in place; `workspacePath` is still written by every save that has a workspace copy.
Known transitional cost, stated plainly: an app saved by a build that predates `workspacePath` cannot be updated THROUGH its workspace file until its record names one — the file is saved, the shelf write is refused with the owning app named, and the recovery is to delete that app and re-save (or save with no workspace root). Documented in docs/17 §5 and README.
Branch `fleet/collision-hotfix` = b023709 (6c306f6..b023709). Tests RED on base 8/13 -> GREEN 13/13 (5 new cases). Focused real-API + browser gate and the exact-tip fast verdict in flight; reviewer next. P1 stays OPEN until landed and verified.

comments.author: voicebox-shard-rtsr
comments.text:
HAND-OFF for landing (P1 hotfix). Branch `fleet/collision-hotfix`, tip `cd7f572` = origin (created non-force through the normal pre-push hook, unit lane 633 tests / 0 fail). Reviewed range will be `merge-base(origin/main)..origin/fleet/collision-hotfix` = 6c306f6..cd7f572. Gemini reviewer lane `rev-rtsr-hotfix` (different model family) briefed and running; clearance + merge-queue follow its PASS.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: lib/mini-app-store.mjs stops deciding ownership by name. deleteMiniApp removes a workspace file only when the shelf record NAMES it (workspacePath, written by every save that has a workspace copy); the byte-equality and appId signals are gone, so a legacy record proves nothing and the file is left in place. saveMiniApp refuses mini-app-name-taken when a workspace copy would be written and the record at that slug does not name the file being saved, checked before any write of any kind. saveMiniApp writes workspacePath into the record, so later ownership is read rather than compared. README and docs/17 §5 state the rule, including the transitional cost.
WHY: a workspace page and a shelf app can share a slug and a file name. deleteMiniApp deleted candidates by name, so deleting the app destroyed an unrelated rootPath/collision.html (P1 data loss, reproduced on 2abb42a/6c306f6), and saveMiniApp overwrote the same-slug app's copy and record with the page's content, unrecoverably.
EFFECT: deleting a Mini-App leaves any same-named workspace file it cannot prove is its own, so a colliding page survives; saving a file as a Mini-App whose name is held by another app is refused with the owning app named instead of overwriting it. A Mini-App saved before workspacePath existed cannot be updated through its workspace file until it is deleted and re-saved once (documented in docs/17 §5). No other user-visible behaviour changes; the fast gate is unchanged (unit lane 633 tests, ~23-31s measured, same as before).

EVIDENCE on cd7f572: store tests `tests/mini-app-store.test.mjs` RED on base 8/13 -> GREEN 13/13 (5 new cases: unowned workspace file survives deleting the app; identical bytes are not provenance; a saved app is updated in place then deletes both copies + record; a save over a name it cannot prove it owns is refused with no entry written anywhere; host-only update still works and its deletion does not reach a same-named unowned file). Real-route pin `tests/sandbox-subdirectories.test.mjs` RED on base (POST /api/mini-apps answered 200) -> GREEN (400 mini-app-name-taken with the app's copy untouched; DELETE /api/mini-apps leaves the page standing). Fast verdict for cd7f572: PASS exit 0, job f2c9950c07aa54a3fed98b62f110ddd3f87f3b1a, 633 tests / 0 fail (record's coverage line says UNKNOWN by heuristic; the log names the executed suites). Focused browser + real-API gate on cd7f572: exit 0, 10/10, log /tmp/shard-rtsr-rtsr-hotfix-focus3.log (preempted once by the merger, requeued, so it ran the full set). No full author suite was run; no real workspace file was touched by any check.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (lane voicebox-inv-dev-auth, read-only; worktree detached @ 48b71f8, tree clean, == report revision main@48b71f8)

VERDICT: no defect in the Vite proxy or in Origin handling. The 401s are the documented gate-on behaviour (`loopback-unauthenticated`) triggered by a cookie HOST mismatch between the printed bootstrap URL (127.0.0.1:8787) and the dev front (localhost:5173). One URL away from fixed; nothing is broken in the code path.

EVIDENCE
1. package.json: `"dev": "vite"`, `"serve": "node --watch server.mjs"`. `npm run dev` starts ONLY the Vite front; server.mjs must already be running. `npm run serve`/`npm start` serves public/ by itself (docs/08 "how it runs") — Vite is a dev-only extra.
2. 401 is gate-only: server.mjs:353 `const LOOPBACK_AUTH = process.env.VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH === "1";` (DEFAULT OFF); :4218 `if (LOOPBACK_AUTH && !sessionCookieOk(req))`; :4236 `json(res, 401, { ok:false, refused:"loopback-unauthenticated", why })`. Exempt list :4225-4230 = GET /api/health, POST /api/bootstrap, the `?bootstrap=` page, host-token requests. That is exactly Paul's shape — /api/health ok, every other /api 401 — so the 8787 backend was started with VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH=1. `rg -n VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH` finds no .env and nothing that sets it (`ls -a | grep -i env` empty), so it was set explicitly on the command line. With the gate off (default) no 401 exists at all — so a "dev front is broken" theory is ruled out.
3. The actual trap — cookie host scoping. Banner prints the API origin only:
   server.mjs:5783 `console.log(\`bootstrap  http://127.0.0.1:${bound}/?bootstrap=${ticket}\`)`.
   Redeemed cookie carries NO Domain attribute:
   server.mjs:4132-4136 `res.writeHead(303, { location: plain, "set-cookie": \`${SESSION_COOKIE}=${LOOPBACK_SESSION}; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/\` })`.
   The check itself is host-agnostic (server.mjs:380-388 reads the Cookie header), so the browser must send it — and a cookie minted at 127.0.0.1 is host-scoped to 127.0.0.1, never sent to localhost:5173. Origin is not the problem: server.mjs:326-327 already lists `http://localhost:5173` and `http://127.0.0.1:5173` in localOrigins.
4. The dev-front door exists but nothing points at it: vite.config.js:127-152 `loopback-bootstrap-proxy` intercepts any `?bootstrap=` on the :5173 front, forwards it to the API, and returns status/Set-Cookie to the browser on the :5173 origin (redirect Location deliberately relative, so the browser stays on :5173 and the cookie rides every proxied /api and WS upgrade). Documented only in docs/18 §2 and the vite comment; `rg -n 5173 server.mjs` returns just the Origin list and a comment — the banner (:5782-5785) and the 401 `why` (:4229-4234) never mention the dev front.
5. Out-of-sync banner (Paul's "UI local server not responding"): public/fused.js:4658-4690 `stampBuild()` raises sync-toast on either (a) page stamp != server commit -> "UI and server are on different revisions. Reload the page or restart the server." or (b) /api/health did not answer -> server null -> "Local server is not responding — UI and server are out of sync." Its ONLY input is GET /api/health (fused.js:2030, 2041, 2061), which is 401-exempt — so a bare missing-cookie state does NOT raise that banner. It fired because health did not answer (backend not yet up / proxy 502) or because the two stamps differed. Which branch fired for Paul is NOT ESTABLISHED from here (no access to his browser; nothing listens on 5173/8787 on this VM — `ss -ltnp | grep -E "8787|5173"` empty — so live reproduction was impossible; this is a code+docs verdict).

SUPPORTED USE (the question "which command/URL is supported"):
- One command suffices: `npm run serve` (or `npm start`), then browse `http://127.0.0.1:8787`, opening the printed `?bootstrap=` URL once when the gate is on. `serve` alone is the supported path.
- With the Vite front, run BOTH, and redeem the ticket ON the front you browse: `http://localhost:5173/?bootstrap=<ticket>`. The printed 8787 link is right for the 8787 origin only.
- Zero-friction dev: do not set VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH (default off) -> no cookie, no 401, server prints the gate-off exposure warning.

RECOVERY, no restart needed (not executed here — no such instance on this VM; host-token path per docs/18 §5):
  curl -s -X POST -H "x-voicebox-host-token: $(cat ~/.config/voicebox/.host-token)" http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/bootstrap
then open the returned `?bootstrap=<ticket>` on `http://localhost:5173/` (NOT on 127.0.0.1). Note the printed ticket is single-use: opening it at 8787 first consumes it, which is why retrying the 5173 front keeps answering 401. No secret was accessed, stored or reproduced here; the ticket value is not in this comment.

NEXT ACTIONS: (1) Paul recovery URL above. (2) Filed voicebox-beads-t43w (P3) — banner + 401 body should name the dev-front redemption origin. (3) If Paul is not intentionally running the gate, the simpler remedy is to drop VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH for local dev.

comments.author: voicebox-inv-dev-auth
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP (narrow, read-only, main@8148318 via `git show origin/main:public/fused.js`; worktree detached @ 48b71f8, no edits, no token access)

ANSWER: the out-of-sync toast IS explained, deterministically, from the 401s alone — and it is a MISREPORT, not a stuck/recoverability failure. My earlier note ("a cookie-less state cannot raise that banner") was WRONG and this corrects it: I read `stampBuild()` in isolation and missed that `health()`'s try-block also awaits non-exempt routes.

MECHANISM (line numbers on origin/main, public/fused.js)
- `async function health()` (:2028) does, in ONE try block: `const answer = await request("/api/health")` (:2030, 401-EXEMPT, answers 200) → … → `stampBuild(answer.build ?? null)` (:2041) → `await loadRoot()` (:2042) → `await renderEnvironments()` → `await renderExtensions()`.
- `loadRoot()` (:1637) is `const answer = await request("/api/root")`; `renderEnvironments()` (:1855) is `await request("/api/environments")`. Under the gate with no cookie those answer 401 `{ok:false, refused:"loopback-unauthenticated", why}`.
- `request()` (:1077) THROWS on `!response.ok` and copies the named refusal onto the error: `:1091-1095  if (!response.ok) { const err = new Error(...); if (body?.refused) err.refused = body.refused; if (body?.why) err.why = body.why; throw err; }`.
- So the throw lands in `health()`'s catch (:2049) even though /api/health answered 200, and the catch does exactly the offline sequence: `els.dot.dataset.ok = "false"` (:2052), the visible line "the environment list could not be read — fix the file" (`err.refused` is set, :2055 — it blames a FILE, and its title claims `source: GET /api/environments` although /api/root threw first), and `stampBuild(null)` (:2061).
- `stampBuild(null)` (:4658) → `serverUnreachable = server === null && (pageSha !== null || initialServerCommit !== null)` (:4669) is TRUE on both fronts (Vite stamps the meta at vite.config.js:190-209; server.mjs replaces it at :4139) → `updateSyncToast({outOfSync:true, reason:"Local server is not responding — UI and server are out of sync.", key:"offline"})` (:4676-4681). That is verbatim Paul's banner.

REFRESH / CLEAR after a transient failure — traced, no stuck-toast bug:
- `setInterval(() => { if (typeof busy !== "undefined" && busy) return; health(); }, ROOT_POLL_MS = 20000)` (:5410-5413) re-runs health() every 20s.
- On a fully successful run, `stampBuild(commit)` reaches the `else if (server?.commit)` branch (:4683) → `updateSyncToast({outOfSync:false})` (:4627-4633) → `currentSyncKey=""`, `dismissedSyncKey=null`, `toast.hidden = true`. So a transient initial health failure DOES clear within one poll.
- `busy` is not declared or assigned anywhere in public/fused.js (`rg -n '\bbusy\b'` returns only aria-busy attributes plus this guard), so the guard is inert unless another script defines the global; the poll runs.
- What does NOT clear is the 401 case: every 20s poll re-throws at /api/root and re-asserts the offline toast and `data-ok="false"` — a LIVE server rendered as dead, and the real remedy (redeem the ticket on the origin you browse, or drop VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH) is never shown. `initialServerCommit` is only ever written, never reset (:4664-4665) — harmless here, but it is what keeps `serverUnreachable` true for a page whose health never succeeds again.
- Build stamp: server.mjs memoizes `buildIdentity()` at startup (the :4138 comment naming voicebox-beads-4oj6) — it does not change until restart, so the `mismatch` branch (`rev:…` key, "UI and server are on different revisions. Reload the page or restart the server.") is a separate, correct trigger and is NOT what fired here unless the server predated a landed commit.

DETERMINISTIC FOCUSED REPRO (no mutation of the repo, no fetch interception needed — the :5173 front serves the page shell itself; only /api, /live, /channel and source prefixes are proxied, vite.config.js:255-340):
  1. `VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH=1 PORT=8877 node server.mjs`
  2. `PORT=8877 npx vite`   (API_TARGET derives from PORT: vite.config.js:33)
  3. Open http://localhost:5173/ with no cookie and observe: page renders, `GET /api/health` 200, `GET /api/root` 401 loopback-unauthenticated, `#sync-toast` visible with "Local server is not responding — UI and server are out of sync.", `#dot[data-ok]="false"`, `#where` text blaming a file.
  Proposed mutant for tests/page-acceptance.mjs Phase B (private instance, per its own convention at :545-560): assert the toast is hidden and `data-ok="true"` whenever /api/health is 200 — i.e. pin "a 401 on /api/root must not be reported as machine-unreachable". NOT RUN HERE: investigator is read-only with no deps/tests, so this is a code-path proof by reading, not an observed run; nothing listens on 5173/8787 on this VM so there was no live instance to drive.

NEXT ACTION (one): coord routes voicebox-beads-t2qf (P2, filed by this lane) — separate `health()`'s health verdict from its downstream GETs so a 401/refusal on /api/root or /api/environments renders an auth remedy and leaves the dot and the sync toast alone; the repro above is its acceptance check. If instead the P1 is deemed closed by the two findings, Paul needs no further evidence from me — but if the banner fired with /api/health NOT answering, then the exact Network tab status for /api/health is the one datum I could not obtain from here.

ROOT CAUSE: /usr/bin/npm did not exist on this VM (the distro copy was removed in the Oct 9 node change). npm is installed ONLY under nvm (/home/exedev/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin/npm -> lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js), which is outside the tool-pin generator's confined lookup dirs (system bin dirs only). So tools.pins.yaml carried '# npm: not found in the pinned lookup dirs — no pin', while node/npx stayed pinned (/usr/bin/node exists; /usr/bin/npx had been relinked earlier by the nightly preflight). npm is a trusted tool the secret-scan pre-pass executes, so lib/tool_pins refused the station with the exact log error — correct fail-closed behaviour, not a bug in the factory.

WHY IT IS HOST-SIDE (not voicebox product code): the pins file is HOST-LOCAL config (~/.config/factory/tools.pins.yaml, FACTORY_TOOL_PINS); the generator is ~/agents/tools/generate-tool-pins.sh; the failing runner is ~/fleet/remote/factory-nightly.sh. fleet-nightly's own comment records the same class on the hub 2026-10-10 (distro npm diverging from the pin). No voicebox repo change can fix it; the hash is host-specific by design, so it cannot live in a shared repo (generator header says so).

FIX (local, mirrors the existing npx arrangement exactly):
1. sudo ln -sfn /home/exedev/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js /usr/bin/npm  (readlink -f /usr/bin/npm = npm-cli.js, same shape as /usr/bin/npx -> npx-cli.js)
2. Regenerated pins with the generator's DEFAULT system-dir lookup so the diff is minimal: exactly ONE line changed — '# npm: not found…' -> npm: {path: /usr/bin/npm, sha256: 8e5f6f34…cbe7}. Every other entry (bwrap/gh/git/node/npx/pi/claude) byte-identical; deliberately did NOT regenerate with provisioning's extra --lookup-path because that would also re-point the pi pin from /usr/local/bin/pi to ~/.local/bin/pi (out of scope, reviewable separately).
3. Installed it.

VERIFICATION: factory's own resolver now returns npm -> .../npm-cli.js and authenticates it; sandbox _resolutions over the nightly PATH (fleet/bin excluded) finds 3 npm launch paths and ALL THREE authenticate. NEGATIVE CONTROL: with the npm entry stripped, the resolver raises the exact log error verbatim. Never set FACTORY_ALLOW_UNPINNED_TOOLS.

RERUN: fleet-gate c9dl-audit-rerun (bound 5400s) running ~/fleet/remote/factory-nightly.sh detached; last full line took ~17 min. Will report the scorecard + delta when it lands.

RESIDUAL OWNERSHIP ITEM (hub/fleet repo, reported to fleet-manager): provisioning's generator call passes --lookup-path "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.local/pi" — no nvm dir — so on any VM where the system npm is absent while node/npx are present, npm silently ends up unpinned and the whole nightly halts at station 1. Durable fix belongs in ~/fleet/remote/provision.sh (add the nvm bin dir to the lookup path, or assert /usr/bin/{node,npm,npx} exist during provisioning).

comments.author: voicebox-urllog
comments.text:
Resolution for voicebox-beads-y63q:

1. Root Cause Analysis:
- In lib/pi-acp.mjs, openPiAcpProbe previously hardcoded 'exec /usr/bin/node' in its bwrap launcher script and only bound /usr into the container. When Node is installed in user paths (such as ~/.nvm/... on this VM), /usr/bin/node does not exist or points into /home, which is masked by bwrap's '--tmpfs /home', causing execvp /usr/bin/node to fail with ENOENT / exit 127.
- openPiAcpProbe was discarding child stderr completely on error exit and mapping any exit code != 78 to an opaque 'TaskInterrupted: harness-ended-outcome-unknown'.
- tests/pi-acp-probe-runtime.test.mjs checked 'fs.existsSync("/usr/bin/bwrap")' rather than verifying whether unprivileged user namespaces are actually permitted by kernel posture.

2. Code Changes:
- lib/pi-acp.mjs: resolves active Node binary via fs.realpathSync(process.execPath), binds '--ro-bind nodeBinary /packages/node' in bwrap, and invokes 'exec /packages/node' in launch.sh, decoupling the probe from host /usr/bin/node existence or user-directory symlinks.
- lib/pi-acp.mjs: captures child stderr up to 512 bytes on unexpected child exit (without stdout displacement) and attaches exit code + stderr to TaskInterrupted detail.
- tests/pi-acp-probe-runtime.test.mjs: upgraded hasBwrap to an injectable functional execution canary (canBwrap) verifying unprivileged user namespaces and mirroring the host's /lib64 target.
- tests/pi-acp-probe-runtime.test.mjs: added unit tests verifying stderr capture on error exit without stdout displacement (Finding P1) and canary negative controls with mock runners (Finding P2).
- docs/11-acp-adapter.md: documented probe Node runtime binding and stderr diagnostic.

3. Verification Evidence:
- Branch: fleet/urllog-y63q @ commit 994105f
- Pre-push gate: 587 unit tests passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped (76.8s)
- Focused tests: node --test tests/pi-acp-probe-runtime.test.mjs: 5/5 passed
- Static checks: single-owner, docs-touched, docs-check all OK

title: Nightly factory line ANDONs at station 1: factory-nightly.sh never exports FACTORY_TOOL_PINS, so fail-closed pinning refuses git (0/11 stations)
description:
**Goal & priority (P1, fleet-owned):** The nightly `fleet-factory.timer` project-audit line has produced ZERO audit coverage since fail-closed tool pinning landed: it ANDONs at station 1 (`secret-scan`) and SKIPS the other 10 stations. This blocks the nightly-coverage inspection that voicebox-beads-xacp / jyj1 depend on. It will repeat every night until the launcher environment exports the pin file.

**Distinguish failure type:** This is a HOST TOOL-PIN CONFIGURATION FAILURE, not a verified finding. The run produced 0 new / 0 regressed / 0 fixed findings (delta report marks the line INCOMPLETE). Nothing about the voicebox tree at 4c1a63c was scanned.

**Evidence (2026-10-09T03:19Z run, origin/main@4c1a63c):**
- `/home/exedev/.fleet/factory/20261009.log:21` — ANDON: `trusted tool 'git' is not pinned (no git.sha256 in tools.yaml nor the FACTORY_TOOL_PINS host file)`.
- Run artifact `/home/exedev/agents/runs/secret-scan-voicebox-factory-20261009-031935/` contains only a 0-byte `.active` marker — the station never executed.
- Delta report `~/agents/findings/voicebox-factory-delta.md` — 0/0/0, INCOMPLETE, 11 stations with no verdict.
- Contrast `~/ .fleet/factory/20261008.log` — COMPLETE, 11/11 PASS. Regression introduced 2026-10-08 by pin enforcement: `agents-7bj` 3152a21 + 7f50d9c, `agents-3g6` dfd998c.

**Root cause:** `/home/exedev/fleet/remote/factory-nightly.sh` sources `~/.fleet/env` and `~/fleet/fleet.conf` but NEVER exports `FACTORY_TOOL_PINS`; `~/.fleet/env` does not set it either, and `/etc/systemd/system/fleet-factory.service` has no `Environment=`/`EnvironmentFile=`. So the fail-closed default in `~/agents/lib/tool_pins.py` is in force and the host pin file is ignored.

**The pins file already exists and is correct:** `~/.config/factory/tools.pins.yaml` pins git → `/usr/bin/git` (sha256 `2a8c18fb…`), plus gh/bd/node/npm/npx.

**Direct resolver proof (read-only, no factory run):** with `FACTORY_TOOL_PINS` unset, `resolve_tool('git')` is REFUSED (same message as the log); with `FACTORY_TOOL_PINS=~/.config/factory/tools.pins.yaml` it resolves `OK -> /usr/bin/git`. Same result for `node`, `npm`, `gh`, `bd`. This also disproves the earlier "a duplicated node on PATH makes fail-closed pinning unsatisfiable" concern carried in the voicebox-beads-zljj report — node resolves cleanly under the host pins file.

**Scope & owned seams:** host/fleet launcher configuration — NOT the voicebox repo. Do not edit the foreign repo from voicebox; send a scoped hub handoff to `~/fleet`.

**Precise next step (one line of config):** add
`export FACTORY_TOOL_PINS="$HOME/.config/factory/tools.pins.yaml"`
to `~/fleet/remote/factory-nightly.sh` (next to the `source "$HOME/.fleet/env"` line) or to `~/.fleet/env`. `FACTORY_ALLOW_UNPINNED_TOOLS=1` is a dev/test opt-out only and must not be the nightly answer.

**Scoped verification:** after the export, verify with the NEXT scheduled timer run (or a single bounded station run, e.g. `FACTORY_TOOL_PINS=$HOME/.config/factory/tools.pins.yaml factory run secret-scan --target <wt> --engine pi --sink file`); expect station 1 to return a verdict and the scorecard to show 11 verdicts rather than ERROR/SKIPPED. Do not rerun the full 11-station line from triage.

**Acceptance:** `git` resolves under pinning in the nightly launcher's environment and the next nightly scorecard reports a verdict for every station.

It is inherited, not introduced by V4/V5: miniapps' branch was already reviewed and its gate already green, so coord has ruled that no retroactive hold is possible and this is a new owned bug.
THE VERIFIED CHAIN (mine, from the source at the landed revision bccb5d6):
- public/fused.js:4100-4113 (the envPickFolderBtn handler) writes #env-root-status ONLY inside `if (picked)`. There is no else, so the failure path writes nothing to the dialog.

2. With showDirectoryPicker throwing a denial, the same is true and the message carries the picker's reason.
3. NEGATIVE CONTROL: a cancel (AbortError) must NOT be reported as a failure in the dialog, and must not create or switch anything — cancelling is not an error.
4. The read-only remedy must not point at a control that is behind the modal.
5. Independent review from a different model family. 6. One exact-tree full gate on the frozen integrated tree.
NOT IN SCOPE (found by the same review, deliberately NOT folded in silently, and left as separate decisions rather than smuggled into this commit): the OPFS branch losing its cause at the dialog seam (review minor 1), and the stale stored-active-folder name that skips renderRoomFoldersBar (review minor 3).

THE CHAIN, LANDED REVISION:
- public/fused.js:4100-4113 — the envPickFolderBtn handler writes #env-root-status ONLY inside `if (picked)`; there is no else, so failures write nothing to the dialog.
- openRoomFolder() reports every failure only through setReport(...): fused.js:569 when `showDirectoryPicker` is not a function, fused.js:588 for a picker error. setReport writes els.report, and `report: "turn-report"` (fused.js:23) is public/index.html:472.
- #envs spans public/index.html:351-410, so #turn-report:472 is OUTSIDE the dialog: behind the top layer, inert and covered while it is open. In Firefox/Safari (no showDirectoryPicker) every click looks like a dead button.
- Related, same path: the read-only SUCCESS message at fused.js:4108 says to click "Restore access" "above", but that chip is in the room folder bar, also behind the dialog.
FOUR SPECIFICS THAT ARE EASY TO MISS, each of which the review caught somewhere in this work:
1. A CANCEL IS NOT A FAILURE. openRoomFolder() returns early on AbortError (fused.js:576) and that path must show NOTHING in the dialog. A negative control for it belongs in the test, otherwise the fix turns "I changed my mind" into an error message.
2. If you retry readwrite as read (fused.js:578-581) and the SECOND call throws, that error reaches the outer catch, so the in-dialog message must carry the picker's own reason rather than a generic line.
3. Do not let the failure text be matched by a wait that would also match a success line: in this dialog the OPFS string "browser storage" appears in both "Switched to browser storage (OPFS)" and "Could not switch to browser storage (OPFS)", so a wait on that substring alone is satisfiable by either. Assert dataset.ok too.
4. Do not assert the static HTML default ("no folder chosen yet") as evidence that wiring works — it passes with the handler dead. Assert a value the act produced.
WHAT I WAS GOING TO PROVE, offered as the acceptance shape (take it or improve on it): drive it in a real browser on three branches — showDirectoryPicker absent; showDirectoryPicker throwing a denial; and the ABORT/CANCEL control asserting no error appears and nothing switches — each asserting the refusal is readable INSIDE the dialog via checkVisibility while the dialog stays open, plus the room's report line still carrying it. NOT MINE AND NOT CLAIMED by the closed 8lds: minor 3 from the same review (a stale stored-active-folder name makes active null and skips renderRoomFoldersBar on that path, so other restored folders are not shown; pre-change code fell back to the first folder) and the four nits. comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
PREPLAN (scout complete, read-only, in an independent --no-local clone at main tree ccea3be6afaa). NOT CLAIMED, NOT STARTED, nothing edited - this waits for nqrl to land. Coordinates verified by me directly against the code, not taken on trust.
VERIFIED FACTS THAT SHAPE THE FIX
1. The discovery test asserts ONLY res.ok === true and res.watcherErrors === 0 (tests/factory-review-adapter.test.mjs:759-761). It never asserts that a candidate was discovered, and the ambient origin has ZERO branches matching fleet/miniapps-test. So the test has been a vacuous pass: it proves nothing about discovery while still running the prune. The fix must add the assertion the test's own name promises.
2. runReviewWatcher returns { ok, exitCode, scannedCount, watcherErrors, cursor } (scripts/factory-review-watcher.mjs:259), so scannedCount is the field to assert (the existing fixture pattern asserts trigger invocations instead - either works, use both).
3. Discovery reads REMOTE-TRACKING refs only: git rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/<branch> (:127), then git merge-base origin/main <tip> (:139) and requires base !== tip (:144). So the fixture's bare origin needs refs/heads/main AND refs/heads/fleet/<candidate> with the candidate at least one commit ahead.
4. The watcher itself performs NO identity check (grep: no getCheckoutRepoIdentity in scripts/factory-review-watcher.mjs) - identity is checked by the trigger (scripts/factory-review-trigger.mjs:210-214). So a local bare-path origin is entirely safe for the discovery fixture, and no network is needed.
5. The TRIGGER HAS NO FETCH CALL (grep -n fetch scripts/factory-review-trigger.mjs returns nothing), so the sibling test may safely pin its fixture origin to https://github.com/PaulKinlan/voicebox.git - exactly the identity-pin coord asked for - without ever hitting the network.
6. The old discovery test also WRITES INSIDE THE MEASURED TREE: tmpPrivate is ROOT/tests/fixtures/watcher-test-private (:754) and is removed at the end of the body, so a mid-test failure leaves the tree dirty (the gate excludes only .beads/). The fixture must own its private dir under its own tmpdir and clean up in t.after, as nqrl and 7nto do.
FIX PLAN, ONE FILE ONLY (tests/factory-review-adapter.test.mjs)
A. Discovery test: own fixture = bare origin (origin.git) + work clone under mkdtemp, work clone's origin a LOCAL PATH to the bare dir (offline, and the watcher does not check identity); push refs/heads/main and refs/heads/fleet/miniapps-test, the latter one commit ahead; pass rootDir: workDir; owned --private-dir inside the fixture; assert res.ok, res.watcherErrors === 0, scannedCount === 1, exactly one trigger invocation naming bead-1, and that the foreign bead-2 and the fleet/rescued-1234 artifact bead-3 are NOT scanned; t.after ownership for every dir; hygiene = absolute /usr/bin/git with accessSync(X_OK), fixture env with no PATH, owned HOME/XDG, GIT_CONFIG_{NOSYSTEM,GLOBAL,SYSTEM} pinned, GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1, core.hooksPath and init.templateDir pointed at an owned empty dir, and a rev-parse --show-toplevel assertion against the fixture root BEFORE any write.
B. Sentinel, which both proves isolation and stops the test becoming vacuous: inject refs/remotes/origin/stale-sentinel in the WORK clone (the bare origin does not have it), assert it exists before the run and is GONE after - gone if and only if git fetch origin --prune ran in workDir. If the fetch is removed from the watcher the sentinel survives and the test fails, so the change cannot be satisfied by deleting the fetch path.
C. Sibling test (--base HEAD~1): owned fixture repo with a real parent commit and a known ops-category diff, fixture origin pinned to https://github.com/PaulKinlan/voicebox.git (safe: no fetch in the trigger), owned --private-dir, then assert ok, exitCode 0, dryRun === true, station === 'log-check' and a computed cacheKey. Asserting the exact station is what makes it fail for the right reason.
MUTANTS THAT MUST FAIL: discovery predicate broken (scannedCount 0); candidate branch never pushed to the bare origin (0 candidates); rootDir accidentally left as ROOT (sentinel survives); fixture diff removed for the sibling test (station null); the watcher's fetch/prune deleted (sentinel survives).
RED-OLD/GREEN-NEW, to drive at claim time in a clone at HEAD == origin/main: old discovery body passes while discovering ZERO candidates and pruning the REAL origin; old sibling body fails on an empty HEAD commit ('selected a station', actual null) - both already independently reproduced by the reviewer. Then the fixed bodies pass at main AND on the feature branch, with the sentinel pruned inside the fixture only.
OUT OF SCOPE, FLAGGED NOT FOLDED IN: a third test in the same file (~:472) calls getCheckoutRepoIdentity(ROOT) and asserts 'paulkinlan/voicebox', so it fails wherever the checkout's origin is not the approved URL. That is read-only brittleness, not a mutation hazard; I will not touch it without coord's word.

1. An explicit --base IS supported (parsed at line 173, documented at line 190: "Base git ref or commit SHA (default: merge-base with origin/main)"). Note dryRun:true is only returned on the station-selected path (line 280).
2. getCheckoutRepoIdentity (line 143) reads remote.origin.url and only returns a slug for an approved host; the refusal at lines 211-214 triggers only when that identity is NON-EMPTY and differs from the target repo. So a fixture repo with NO origin remote, or an origin that is a local path, yields an empty identity and is NOT refused. `repo` itself defaults to VOICEBOX_FACTORY_REPO || "PaulKinlan/voicebox" (line 165).
PROVEN DESIGN, driven end to end just now, not reasoned about: a self-contained fixture repo under mkdtemp with two commits (a base commit, then a commit adding ops-change.log) plus an OWNED foreign repo used as the poison - never ~/agents/.git - invoked as runReviewTrigger(["--dry-run","--base",base,"--tip",tip], { env: poisonedEnv, rootDir: fixtureRepo }) with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE pointing at the owned foreign repo. That is the whole point: it passes because of the FIXTURE's deterministic diff, so it cannot depend on where the checkout sits relative to main. The fixture had no origin remote and was not refused, confirming fact 2. comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — fleet/miniapps-xacp, REVIEWER voicebox-roboticon (deepseek family; author is Gemini family). READ-ONLY: no repo file was touched; every drive ran from a detached worktree at /tmp/xacp-review; nothing in the author's worktree was read-modified or executed.

SCOPE: base 78b4443 (exact merge-base, verified as an ancestor of origin/main) .. tip 53548ef, tree ba1f9c020bdb38afbaff8357c4334f1851834b69. 9 files, +351/-20.

CACHED GATE VERDICT, quoted as-is, not re-run: {"state":"PASS","tree":"ba1f9c020bdb38afbaff8357c4334f1851834b69","sha":"53548ef","lane":"miniapps","rc":0,"secs":452,"done":"2026-10-08T02:27:28Z"}

=== P1 — THE TRUST FILTER DROPS EXTERNAL ISSUES. tools/factory-issue-router.mjs:14 TRUSTED_AUTHORS = {OWNER, COLLABORATOR, MEMBER}; the check is at :149 and the skip reason at :185. Driven through the module's own exported routeIssue() with ONE field changed and everything else identical:
    NONE                  -> ok:false  "author_association 'NONE' is not in trusted set (OWNER, COLLABORATOR, MEMBER)"
    CONTRIBUTOR           -> ok:false  (an external person whose commits are already merged)
    FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR-> ok:false
    OWNER/COLLABORATOR/MEMBER -> ok:true
  Consequence: every inbound issue from anyone who is not already an owner, member or collaborator is discarded, which is the entire public surface this poller exists to read. LIVE PROOF, not inference: ~/.voicebox/factory-reports/factory-issue-cursor.json records "#18: author_association 'NONE' is not in trusted set (OWNER, COLLABORATOR, MEMBER)", skipped=true, and #18's own body is "This is a SELF-TEST issue for the voicebox factory inbound promotion path (voicebox-beads-h1u0). It simulates a HUMAN-filed issue: no factory fingerprints in the body." So the factory's own simulated-human inbound report was silently dropped by the filter, and #17 (also NONE, "[factory/high] perf-review: ...") was dropped for fingerprint reasons too. Both are non-PR issues; #18 is the only non-PR, non-fingerprinted inbound report that has ever existed here, and it did not survive. This is exactly the outcome coord named as unacceptable. Fix shape: do not discard on association - quarantine instead. Record the issue, mark it untrusted, and let a human or a read-only path decide, so a legitimate report is never lost; if the filter stays, it must at minimum surface skipped NONE issues somewhere an operator sees, and it currently does not (see below).
  Note: the drop is not the only silent one. A skipped issue leaves the run's exit code at 0 (runner: scripts/factory-issue-poller-runner.sh:42-45), so a poll that dropped reports is indistinguishable from a clean one by exit status or by systemd Result (observed: Result=success).

=== P1 — THE REVIEW GATE IS NOT DURABLY INVOKED. scripts/factory-review-gate.sh has NO caller in the repository except its own test (tests/factory-review-adapter.test.mjs:524,546 asserts the help text) and the docs. Grepped the whole tree, plus ~/voicebox scripts/hooks and ~/fleet/bin and ~/fleet/*.conf: no hook, no pre-push stage, no station, no timer. The documented integration path (docs/28-factory-review-adapter.md:174-177) is a PROPOSED EDIT to ~/fleet/roles/implementer.md and ~/fleet/roles/merger.md "via hub delegation" - i.e. it requires exactly the merger-role change coord ruled out, and until that lands, nothing runs this gate on a new review diff except a human remembering to. A gate nobody is obliged to run is a convention, not a gate. Recommend: either wire it into the existing pre-push/handoff path in this repo (so the diff itself enforces it) or state plainly in the docs and on the bead that it is advisory-only until the fleet roles change.

=== P2 — THE TIMER CAN EXECUTE CODE FROM A LANE WORKTREE. The installed service's ExecStart is: RUNNER=%h/voicebox/scripts/factory-issue-poller-runner.sh; [ -x "$RUNNER" ] || RUNNER=%h/worktrees/voicebox-miniapps/scripts/factory-issue-poller-runner.sh; exec "$RUNNER". LIVE EVIDENCE that the fallback is the live path today: ~/.voicebox/factory-reports/poller.log shows "Starting issue poller in /home/exedev/worktrees/voicebox-miniapps". Pre-landing that fallback is a reasonable bootstrap (the canonical checkout does not have the file yet). Post-landing it is a landmine: if the canonical file is ever missing, an unattended hourly timer silently executes whatever is in a MUTABLE lane worktree, and the reviewer of that worktree is not the reviewer of the timer. Recommend dropping the fallback once this lands - resolve to the canonical checkout, and fail loudly and visibly if it is absent, rather than quietly running someone's branch. Related: scripts/factory-review-gate.sh:12 sets ROOT_DIR from the script's own location, so the same "which checkout does automation run" question applies to it.

=== P2 — "DEFERRED FOR NIGHTLY" IS NOT HONOURED, AND THE DOCS SAY IT IS. The gate runs at most ONE primary station and records the rest as "Deferred secondary stations for nightly line" (docs/28 §2.2, and the trigger prints it). The nightly does something else entirely: /etc/systemd/system/fleet-factory.service runs ~/fleet/remote/factory-nightly.sh, which at line 13 runs `factory line ${FLEET_FACTORY_LINE:-project-audit}` - the project-audit LINE (fleet.conf:64), on a fresh worktree of origin/<default>, with the file sink, under a 3h bound. Nothing maps a review diff's deferred stations onto that run, and the nightly executes against main, not against the reviewed tip. So a station deferred at review time is executed only if project-audit happens to include it, against different code. docs/28:45 "No review run falsely claims complete coverage over unexecuted domains" is honest about the review run, but the deferral sentence implies coverage that no mechanism provides. Recommend rewording to "deferred to the nightly project-audit line, which does not run per-diff" or adding a real per-diff nightly queue.

=== P2 — THIS DIFF WOULD BE REVIEWED AS DOCUMENTATION. Driven through selectReviewStation() with this diff's own file list: {"station":"docs-drift","category":"docs","deferred":[{"category":"ops","station":"log-check"}],"matchedCategories":["docs","ops"]}. A change that adds a trust filter, an unattended hourly timer and a publisher is classified as a docs-drift review with log-check deferred - because DOMAIN_PATTERNS maps docs/ and *.md to docs, and the ops fallback ("log-check", "issue-triage") is the only bucket scripts/*.sh and tools/*.mjs reach, while security (secret-scan, deps-supply-chain) and perf (perf-review, bundle-size) match only paths like auth/creds/public js/package.json. So the automated review of an automation change is a documentation check. This is a classification gap, not a bug in the ordering: recommend mapping scripts/**/*.mjs and *.sh, and anything touching ~/.config/systemd or a publisher, to security or ops with a code-aware station.

=== P2 — A MISSING DELTA REPORT IS READ AS A CLEAN PASS. scripts/factory-review-trigger.mjs:313 logs "No delta report produced by station 'X' (clean pass)" and :316-318 requires zero skipped and zero failed findings for PASS. That is stronger than I expected and worth crediting. But the fleet has a documented upstream bug in the same shape - TO-SHELLEY.md fleet-810: "Factory project-audit delta report is overwritten on EVERY station dispatch, so any audit can print 'Clean Delta' from one station's empty slice" - so a clobbered or absent report is indistinguishable from a genuinely clean one, and this gate would print PASS. I could not settle it without executing a station, which I deliberately did not do. Recommend asserting evidence of execution (a run dir, a station log, a finding count) rather than treating absence as clean.

=== BELOW-P2 OBSERVATIONS (recorded because coord asked for gaps, not to inflate them)
  - poller.log grows with >> and has no rotation (7458 bytes / 124 lines now): fine for years at this rate, unbounded by design.
  - The log line "Highest recorded: #0" prints highestIssueNumber, which the cursor always keeps at 0 while the real dedupe lives in processedIssues (18 entries). Misleading to a reader diagnosing coverage.
  - No OnFailure= unit and no alerting: a failed poll is visible in the journal and poller.log, but nothing pushes it anywhere. The runner's lock-contention path exits 0 with a log line, so a skipped run looks exactly like a successful one to systemd.
  - The service's After=network.target is inert for a user unit (user managers do not provide that target); harmless, but it reads as ordering that does not exist.
  - docs/28:31 states the cache key is SHA256(DiffHash : Station : FactoryRef); the code (tools/factory-issue-router.mjs:133) also mixes in repo, which is strictly stronger. Docs drift, in the safe direction.

=== VERIFIED GOOD, with the drive that showed it

comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW, ROUND 2 — tip moved to 2c97755 during review. Base 78b4443 (verified ancestor of origin/main) .. tip 2c97755, tree a4bb1e626fe4dc517e256b4c460dea8a034e913a. READ-ONLY: no repo file touched, everything driven from detached worktrees (/tmp/xacp-review at the old tip, /tmp/xacp-r2 at the current one); the author's worktree was never executed or modified. Round 1 (53548ef) is superseded; findings below are re-derived or re-driven on the CURRENT tip, and where a claim comes from reading code rather than a drive I say so.

CACHED GATE, quoted as-is, not re-run: tree ba1f9c0 = {"state":"PASS","rc":0,"secs":452,...} (that is the OLD tip). I have asked miniapps for the gate state of a4bb1e6 since the tip moved.

STATE CHANGE OBSERVED DURING THE REVIEW: at 02:17 the user timer voicebox-factory-issue-poller.timer was enabled+active with NextElapse 03:00:19; by 03:0x it is is-enabled=disabled, is-active=inactive, units still installed (mtime 02:17). Someone disabled it during the review. Whoever re-enables it gets the behaviour below, so the findings stand regardless.

=== P1 — THE REVIEW GATE'S VERDICT IS HOLLOW, AND A WRONG PASS IS STICKY (this is the most serious finding, and it upgrades my round-1 P2 which understated it)
scripts/factory-review-trigger.mjs:68-73 locateRunDeltaReport looks for `${basename(rootDir)}-${station}-delta.md` inside its own run dir. The factory does not write that name there. ~/agents/lib/findings.py:510-511 writes `{target}-{agent}-delta.md` when station_only is set and `{target}-delta.md` otherwise, and station_only is set ONLY by the line path (~/.local/bin/factory:577); the `run` subparser never sets it, which is why this diff removes --station-only from both call sites - a genuine fix, since `factory run` does not accept it and the old form died in argparse.
DRIVEN, both directions, on the current tip: locateRunDeltaReport("/tmp/xdelta", "/tmp/vb-factory-x", "secret-scan") returns the path when the name carries the station suffix, and returns "" for the name the factory actually writes (`vb-factory-x-delta.md`). So the lookup is correct and the contract is wrong.
CONSEQUENCE, driven: trigger:312-314 logs "No delta report produced by station '<x>' (clean pass)", leaves publishExit=0, so publishOk/ok are true, the verdict is PASS (trigger:322-324) and that PASS is written to the cache (trigger:339-348). A review diff whose station finds something CRITICAL and a diff where nothing ran are the same cached PASS, and because only exit-0 entries are cached and a hit returns exit-0 immediately, the wrong PASS is sticky until --force.
LIVE PROOF it never worked: the private dir it writes has NO review-cache.json and NO run-* attempt directory, so the trigger has never completed a single run on this VM; the poller's per-issue dirs (issue-14/15/16) are all EMPTY (0 files) while the real station output sits at ~/agents/findings/voicebox-miniapps-delta.md (660 bytes, 02:09). Round 1 I called this "cannot be distinguished from a clobbered report"; the truth is that the report is never found at all.

=== P1 — THE TRUST FILTER DROPS EXTERNAL ISSUES (carried, re-driven on the current tip)
tools/factory-issue-router.mjs:14 TRUSTED_AUTHORS = {OWNER, COLLABORATOR, MEMBER}, check at :180-190. Driven through routeIssue() with one field changed: NONE, CONTRIBUTOR and FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR all return ok:false with "is not in trusted set"; only OWNER/COLLABORATOR/MEMBER pass. There is no bypass: the constant is not env- or flag-configurable and the only env read in the file is ISSUE_PAYLOAD for CLI stdin. LIVE: the cursor records "#18: author_association 'NONE' is not in trusted set", and #18's own body is "a SELF-TEST issue for the voicebox factory inbound promotion path ... simulates a HUMAN-filed issue". The factory's own simulated human report was silently dropped.
SILENCE AND DURABILITY, read from code: the skip writes only one stdout line (poller:152-160) plus a cursor record; the run still returns exitCode 0 (runner:45), so a poll that lost a report is indistinguishable from a clean one by exit code or systemd Result; and because the skip stores updatedAt, the next poll hits the dedupe `continue` at poller:144-145 which has NO log line at all, so the skip is announced exactly once and is invisible forever after. The watermark line "Highest recorded: #N" (poller:135) reads cursor.highestIssueNumber, which only advances on a fully successful comment, so it prints #0 forever next to "Fetched 18 issue(s)" - a false all-clear.
SECOND TRUST POLICY, read not driven: the fallback fetch path (poller:125-127) derives trust from the author's LOGIN (`iss.author?.login === repo.split("/")[0] ? "OWNER" : "NONE"`), a narrower and undocumented rule that admits anything authored by the PaulKinlan account, and it also does not map pull_request, so the PR rule stops working on a gh outage.
Fix shape: quarantine rather than discard, and make a skip visible (non-zero signal, an alert, or at minimum a reason that persists in the log).

=== P1 — NOTHING INVOKES THE REVIEW GATE (carried; the docs are honest about this)
Verified by me on the current tip: the only references to scripts/factory-review-gate.sh anywhere are its own file, tests/factory-review-adapter.test.mjs:524,546 (help-text assertions) and docs/28:149,154,157,174,177. Nothing in .githooks, pre-push, docs-touched, the nightly, or any systemd unit calls it, and nothing calls factory-review-trigger.mjs except the gate itself. docs/28 §5.4 marks the fleet hookup as "Proposed Fleet Nightly Hook (Hub Handoff for ~/fleet)" - honest, and it means the activation is deliberately out of this repo's reach: grep of ~/fleet/remote/factory-nightly.sh for "nightly-publisher" is EMPTY, so the nightly publisher is also unactivated. Net state: this branch adds two automation paths that nothing yet runs; only the issue poller was ever activated, and it has since been disabled.

=== P2 — THE NIGHTLY PUBLISHER CANNOT FAIL, AND REPORTS A BOGUS EXIT CODE
scripts/factory-nightly-publisher.sh:71-74: every refusal is logged as a Warning and the loop continues, so the script exits 0 even when all reports were refused. DRIVEN: with three reports in a temp dir - one incomplete, one whose station name does not resolve, one foreign-targ - the triage refused them (correctly) while the publisher printed "Warning: failed to process ... (exit 0)" for each and finished with exit 0. The "(exit 0)" is a shell bug: line 72 interpolates $(basename ...) before $?, so the command substitution clobbers the status (measured: the triage exited 1 and the message said 0). published_count (line 74) also increments for failed reports, so the closing line overstates. An all-refused night is indistinguishable from a successful one.

=== P2 — --allow-foreign-target IS PASSED UNCONDITIONALLY, DISABLING THE FAIL-CLOSED FOREIGN-TARGET REFUSAL
factory-triage.mjs:1106-1120 refuses a report whose target is not --repo, with the reasoning "Publishing repo B's finding into repo A's tracker is silent and public, so the mismatch is a REFUSAL". DRIVEN A/B on a report NAMED for voicebox whose header targets isocan: without the flag it refuses, exit 1, with that exact message; with the flag there is no refusal and the pipeline proceeds to route the finding. That is the flag the nightly passes for every report.
EXPOSURE IS BOUNDED TODAY, and I will not overstate it: (1) the publisher globs voicebox-factory-*-delta.md, and a foreign-named report (isocan-factory-secret-scan-delta.md) is simply not picked up - driven: the publisher processed exactly the two voicebox-named fixtures and ignored the foreign one; (2) ~/agents/findings currently holds ZERO non-voicebox *.md and ZERO foreign *-delta.md, though it does hold voicebox-merger, voicebox-miniapps and voicebox-pathauth reports, which the glob correctly does not match; (3) an incidental identity check fired in my drive ("identity mismatch: the recomputed fingerprint does not match the report's prefix"), so a mutated report's finding was skipped rather than published. So the mechanism is real, the live exposure is latent, and my honest verdict is P2-with-P1-mechanism: the header check that exists for exactly this case is switched off for the whole nightly, and the only thing standing between the shared directory and a cross-project publication is a filename convention. I have asked miniapps whether the unconditional flag is deliberate; if it is, it should be documented as a design choice with the filename convention as the compensating control, and if it is not, the flag should go and the glob should be the only scope.

=== P2 — DEFERRED STATIONS ARE SENT TO A NIGHTLY LINE THAT NEVER RUNS THEM
VERIFIED MYSELF: ~/agents/lines/project-audit.yaml lists exactly 11 stations (secret-scan, threat-model, vuln-discovery, vuln-verify, vuln-triage, deps-supply-chain, modern-web, ui-ux-audit, perf-review, docs-drift, qa-station), while ~/agents/targets/voicebox.yaml offers 20. The trigger's deferral list is drawn from CATEGORY_STATIONS, so a CSS/HTML diff defers accessibility and modern-web, and a general diff defers log-check and issue-triage - of which accessibility, bundle-size, log-check and issue-triage are never run by the nightly at all. A deferral message that says "for nightly line" therefore promises coverage that does not exist for 4 of the 9 non-nightly stations.

=== P2 — DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION WOULD REVIEW AUTOMATION AS DOCUMENTATION
DRIVEN with this diff's own file list: selectReviewStation(files) returns {"station":"docs-drift","category":"docs","deferred":[{"category":"ops","station":"log-check"}],"matchedCategories":["docs","ops"]}. A change that adds a trust filter, an unattended hourly timer and a public publisher is classified as a documentation-drift review with log-check deferred, because scripts/*.sh and tools/*.mjs only reach the ops bucket while security and perf match paths like auth/creds/public js/package.json.

=== P2 — UNBOUNDED PIECES IN THE NEW PATHS
The gate wrapper itself is a bare node call with no timeout and not through fleet-heavy (factory-review-gate.sh:71); the trigger's publisher call is likewise unbounded and unqueued (trigger:294-299); the poller's per-station spawnSync and every gh call have no timeout (poller:186-190, 97/115/211/242). LIVE CONSEQUENCE: the poller's 600s outer bound killed a run at 02:09:44 with exit code 124, after four stations for issue #16 and five for #14, leaving issue #14 unprocessed - the per-station protection that would have made that graceful does not exist. The station run and the poller runner are correctly bounded (fleet-heavy timeout 900 / timeout -k 30 600, plus flock).

=== VERIFIED GOOD (driven, credited because it is real work)
- Incomplete or timed-out reports ARE withheld: a report declaring 3 actionable findings while containing 1 is refused in BOTH modes, unchanged by the foreign-target flag, with "the report is INCOMPLETE (a killed or timed-out run looks like this), so nothing from it is published", and the nightly publisher withholds it too. This is the rule I most wanted to see survive, and it does.
- File sink everywhere in the new paths (poller:186, trigger:224/230/231) with the nightly's file sink matching the fleet's deliberate project-VM policy; --include-low defaults true and the triage mirror keeps low and info, so all severities survive to the publisher; skipped findings can never be cached as PASS (trigger:319-324).
- Cadence and overlap: units installed and byte-identical to the branch copies, systemd-analyze calendar hourly -> "*-*-* *:00:00", OnCalendar=hourly + RandomizedDelaySec=120 + Persistent=true, Type=oneshot plus the runner's flock -n, and an observed run of about one second, so no timer starves landing.
- Secret safety: no credential-shaped string added anywhere in the delta; poller log lines pass through sanitizeLogOutput and comment bodies through sanitizeFindingText; gh calls use argv arrays, not a shell; the private dir is 0700. One honest caveat: trigger:239-240 writes a station's raw stdout+stderr unsanitized to <privateDir>/run-<ts>/<station>.log - acceptable because that directory is 0700 and never published, but it is the one unsanitized sink and --private-dir is user-controlled.
- No .github or workflow change of any kind: zero CI cost, consistent with Paul's rule.
- The loop guard is real and load-bearing (router:163-177): it matches the exact markers the publisher writes, is independent of author association, and the live cursor shows issue #17 skipped by it for that reason.

=== TESTS AND DOCS
The +59 lines add existence checks for the four new files, substring assertions on the unit files, and --help smoke tests for the gate, trigger and poller - plus one assertion pinning the new PR rule. There is no behavioural test of the trust drop, the report lookup (this is why the P1 above is invisible to CI), the publisher outcomes, the deferral-to-nightly claim, the poller's bounds, or the fact that anything invokes the gate. docs/28: :150-151 claims the gate is invoked "during IN_REVIEW handoff" (nothing invokes it - :174-177 is the honest version), :160 claims findings are published via the triage (unreachable in practice, per the P1), :171 heads a column "Uncovered Stations in Target Definition" but lists log-check and release-notes which are not in that target file, and :60 (pre-existing) cites VOICEBOX_FACTORY_PRIVATE_DIR, which nothing in the factory reads.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
- I did not execute a station or the poller end to end, so the publisher leg was reviewed from code, its cached tests and targeted plan-mode drives; in particular whether a genuine, self-consistent foreign report's findings would be PUBLISHED once the flag disables the refusal, or skipped by the fingerprint identity check, is not settled - my mutated fixture took the identity-mismatch path.

    valid-manifest-report        rc=0  gh=0  bd=0   processed (dry-run: no publication)

=== P1 (NEW) - A MISSING DELTA REPORT IS A SUCCESS, AND THE BATCH IS MARKED PUBLISHED. This is the fail-closed case coord prioritized, and it does not hold.
DRIVEN: a manifest (complete=true, target voicebox-factory, line project-audit, fresh generated) whose station entry advertises `status: PASS, findings_count: 5, criticals: 1`, with NO delta report file anywhere. Output:

DELTA REVIEW (027d3e5..e7dcab2 from base 78b4443) was completed in round 16 and I restate it because coord asked for this delta specifically: scripts/factory-review-watcher.mjs +6/-6 (the injected test seam) and tests/factory-review-adapter.test.mjs +90/-37. The trigger is UNCHANGED by this delta, so the hash logic I clarify below is the same code that was in play when I first hit it.

THE ANSWER: the comparison is WITHIN one invocation, but its BASELINE is the file as left by the PREVIOUS run. Concretely, in scripts/factory-review-trigger.mjs:
  line 294, before the station is invoked: `const hashBefore = existsSync(defaultReportPath) ? createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(defaultReportPath)).digest("hex") : null;`
  line 359, after the station returns: that same hashBefore is passed into validateStationReportProvenance(...)
  lines 100-102, inside the validator: `const hashAfter = createHash("sha256").update(content).digest("hex"); if (hashBefore && hashAfter === hashBefore) return { ok: false, error: "report_unchanged_from_prior_attempt" };`
So there is NO stored/cached hash across runs: the comparison itself is pre-run versus post-run inside a single invocation, exactly as the author's "pre/post hash delta verification" describes. The subtlety is what "pre-run" means on a RETRY: the default report is a persistent file, so on the second attempt the pre-run content IS the first attempt's output. Consequence, stated precisely: a station whose retry writes BYTE-IDENTICAL output is refused as report_unchanged_from_prior_attempt - not because the guard is wrong, but because the file it compares against is the previous attempt's own artefact.
WHY THIS IS NOT A PRACTICAL BLOCKER, on the evidence rather than on optimism: a genuine factory report carries a `Generated:` timestamp in its header (the h1u0 golden fixture does: "Generated: 2026-10-07T19:32:36.485838+00:00"), and the validator's own documented checks require that timestamp to be present, valid and not older than the run start. So a regenerated genuine report differs from its predecessor by at least the timestamp, and the guard does not fire. RESIDUAL RISK, honestly bounded: if any station ever emits a genuinely deterministic, timestamp-free report byte-for-byte across two runs, its retry after a failed publication would be refused, and the recovery would be to force a fresh run or change the report content. I would rather the author confirm that path exists than assume it. That is the whole of the question; I consider it clarified rather than open.
BONUS FACT from the same read, which corroborates my earlier drive: the header check is `content.match(/^# Software Factory Delta Report:\s*([^\n]+)/m)`, which is exactly why my stub's `# voicebox... delta report` was refused as missing_factory_delta_header - only a genuine factory report matches that literal prefix.

h1u0 OPEN->IN_REVIEW. Branch fleet/roboticon-h1u0 @ 929c559 (base/merge-base 56b3fde), 11 files +1722. WHAT IT DOES: reads a factory delta report written with --sink file from the private root (default $VOICEBOX_FACTORY_PRIVATE_DIR else ~/.voicebox/factory-reports), refuses any report path inside the repo (symlink escape included), recomputes each finding fingerprint exactly as lib/findings.py does, and emits sanitised bead specs; --apply files them with the factory's own external-ref factory:<sha256> + Fingerprint: convention so both filing paths dedupe against each other; an unreadable board files nothing.

POLICY (mirrored from lib/embargo.py / lib/redaction.py, not invented): identity-critical stations (secret-scan, vuln-discovery, vuln-verify, vuln-triage, threat-model) route critical whatever the badge says; unknown/missing severity fails closed to critical; critical (any class) and identity-critical findings are DEFERRED to a private escalations.jsonl (0600) with no public bead; high from a non-sensitive station files sanitised P1; medium P2; low/info below band unless --include-low (P3); a remediation that changes behaviour files BLOCKED + human-review label + the one decision needed; credential-class snippets withdrawn wholesale; every other string masked with the factory's shapes; home paths and the private root elided. EVIDENCE: 36/36 focused tests pass; 9 mutations each turn the suite red (identity elevation, fail-closed severity, masking, in-repo refusal, station resolution, dedupe, critical deferral, identity reason, low-band skip). Three mutants were green on the first pass and exposed real weaknesses: a vacuous severity test that asserted a value it computed itself, a test leaning on the factory's routed badge, and DEAD CODE in routing (an identity-critical station already routes critical, so the separate identity branch could never fire) - collapsed to one decision with the identity kept in the human-readable reason. Fingerprints cross-checked against the factory's Python compute_fingerprint to the character. npm run docs:check OK; scripts/single-owner.mjs OK; the test classifies into the unit lane. NOT verified: no live station run (that is cbxo) - the run cost belongs to whoever arms the schedule.

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
DELTA REVIEW RETURNED on c0c3cec (reviewer = gemini-3.8-flash, independent family): CHANGES REQUESTED. It confirmed all three previous findings fixed (title elision, credential-rule withholding, lexical+realpath symlink refusal), confirmed no bead path from a scan, and confirmed the review/closed/double-promotion gates. It then found 5 new issues, 2 of them P1, and it FALSIFIED a claim I made — recording both accurately:

P1-1 (mine, real): describePlan prints finding.ruleId and finding.path RAW, and serialisablePlanEntry emits raw rule_id/path in --json. A scanner rule id can carry a token and a path can carry a home dir, so both leak into a CI log and into a machine-readable artefact. Fix: sanitise both on every output surface.

P1-2 (mine, real): the withheld-evidence notice interpolates the RAW path before elide exists, and snippet never passes through elide — so a NON-identity-critical station reporting a credential finding publishes '[withheld: matched value not published (/home/exedev/src/auth.ts:42)]' into a public issue body. Fix: build the notice from the elided path, elide the snippet, and treat credential findings as refused for evidence purposes (not just identity-critical ones).

P2-3: promote posts 'Promoted to bead <id> by null' when --reviewed-by is omitted — it uses opts.reviewedBy instead of the reviewedBy resolved from the issue comment. Fix + a test that asserts the comment text.

P2-4 (CORRECTS A CLAIM I MADE ON THIS BEAD): the --self-test flag is parsed and NEVER USED (dead flag, so it cannot inject the marker), and promote checks self-test markers in the issue BODY ONLY. My earlier receipt said '#17 carries factory-self-test AND factory-promoted, so it is refused twice over' — that is WRONG: the marker I added to #17 was posted as a COMMENT, which promote does not inspect, so only the already-promoted guard protects it. The live self-test refusal I demonstrated did work, but only because my stub put the marker in the body. Fix: check self-test markers in comments too, wire --self-test through to the published issue, and correct the record.

P2-5 (my mutation claim, stated precisely): my 11 chosen mutants did all go red — that part was accurate — but the reviewer tested OTHER mutations and found 6 that stay GREEN, i.e. real blind spots: (i) the falsePositive skip in routeFinding, (ii) the state==='unchanged' skip, (iii) maskText inside displayTitle, (iv) privateRoot elision inside displayTitle, (v) the bd create failure check, (vi) the gh issue create failure check. Fix: tests for all six, then re-run those mutants to prove they now go red.

REVIEWER'S ANSWER TO MY QUESTION 4: publishing model-authored vuln prose is ACCEPTABLE WITH BOUNDS, with the recommendation that vulnerability findings be flagged for human verification before bead promotion (they are already forced to critical). I am implementing that as humanReview:true for the identity-critical stations plus a doc sentence, rather than leaving it implicit.

PROCESS NOTE: the obsolete gate for e437dca0 was holding the heavy slot and STARVING the ca6fab15 gate while measuring a worktree it no longer described (mixed content) — I killed its whole descendant tree by process group (wrapper, inner timeout, npm, the node --test lanes) so the legitimate gate could run. It left no cached verdict. I am NOT editing the worktree while ca6fab15 runs: the fixes are being developed and verified in a /tmp copy and will be applied once that gate returns.

POLICY (reviewer question 4): an identity-critical station's prose is model-authored and published unreviewed, so those findings are flagged for human verification (humanReview true, [human-review] title, and a promoted bead is filed BLOCKED). Documented in docs/27.

CALLER-CONTRACT TRAP FOUND AND DRIVEN (miniapps said their adapter redacts before invoking the publisher). My CLI recomputes each finding's fingerprint from the report content and compares it with the prefix the report declares; a disagreement skips that finding with "identity mismatch: the recomputed fingerprint does not match the report's prefix - publishing under an unverified identity would defeat dedupe". Drove it by rewriting one fingerprint prefix in a fixture: 0 issues created and exit 2. So an adapter that rewrites the artifact (redacting fields that feed the fingerprint: rule, location, snippet) can make EVERY finding skip, and it ends at exit 2 - which that adapter treats as "nothing actionable = success". Nothing is published and nothing looks wrong. Told miniapps: redaction is the publisher's side (sanitises at publication time, mirroring lib/redaction.py, and withholds an identity-critical raw candidate); pass the artifact unmodified and redact a copy only for display.

RECEIPT SEMANTICS, for a caller that parses them:
- something published: "published: <fp16> -> <issue URL>" per finding, then "issues: N published, M duplicate[, K FAILED]"; exit 0, or exit 1 when a publication FAILED.
- nothing published: "Plan: N to publish as issues · M not published (each with a reason below)", one "[NOT PUBLISHED] <prio> <severity> <station> <rule> <location> (<report>)" line per finding, and an indented reason under each; exit 2.
- incomplete report: exit 1, nothing published, "the report is INCOMPLETE ... re-run the station".
So exit 2 alone cannot distinguish "everything was already filed" (fine) from "findings were skipped" (not fine). Told miniapps to assert a "published:" line or the absence of skip reasons rather than trusting the exit code alone.

STAGED, optional and small: a ", K skipped" count on the "issues: ..." line so the mixed case (some published, some skipped) is explicit in the line a caller parses. title: cross-realm audit loss: every page realm writes the same 'phone' instance file (no identify sent)
description: From the 2g7p review (proven, not this diff's regression): browser/worker.ts:63 defaults instance = M0_INSTANCE ('phone', core/audit.ts:84) and NO UI code ever sends identify (only tests/two-agents.test.mjs does). So two same-origin tabs on one project write the SAME audit file <root>/.audit/phone-<hash>.jsonl from two realms — the in-memory append chain (2g7p) is per-realm and cannot help. Measured by the reviewer: 6 existing lines + 20 reads per realm in two realms -> 27 physical lines, 19 lost, torn lines in merged reads; control with a distinct identify -> 46/46, zero loss. Fix directions: Web Locks (navigator.locks) around the append (cross-realm safe, Baseline), or a per-realm instance name (crypto.randomUUID per boot) so each realm gets its own writer file (the design's one-file-per-(root,writer) already merges them). ALSO fold in the two wording fixes the review required: (1) browser/storage.ts:140-142's 'cross-realm writers are excluded' claim is false until this lands — qualify it; (2) docs/09-agent-loop.md:60's 'never interleave' needs the same qualification.
