comments.author: voicebox-gate-recover
comments.text:
AUDIT (the ranked list coord asked for) — by gate-recover, with the three solved shapes freshest. The fix for the top case is on origin/fleet/zjpm5-flake-audit and detailed at the bottom; the rest is the ranking, the discriminator that makes it usable, and three follow-ups filed as zjpm.5.1/.2/.3.

THE DISCRIMINATOR (this is the whole audit). The surface form "wait on A, assert B" is NOT the defect: it is the CORRECT shape whenever B is written synchronously with A, and it is the accidental shape of every poll-loop helper. A site is a candidate only if ALL of:
  (1) the asserted observable is written by an ASYNC path — a fetch, a timer, an event, a socket, a native-task callback;
  (2) the test's wait signal can be satisfied BEFORE that write;
  (3) the test reads once, with no wait on the asserted observable itself.
Measured proof that the surface form cannot be the detector: tests/health-auth-browser.test.mjs waits on #env-note and asserts #where-note, and the two writes are in ONE synchronous run (renderEnvironments writes the note, throws, the enclosing catch writes the where line) — no yield point, so the CDP read can never observe the gap. That is safe, and a grep for the form flags it anyway.

THE RANKING, by likelihood of being the next landing-blocking flake:
1. An EXACT count or EXACT string on an async-written observable, where the moment is decided by a guessed delay, and the instrument is never proven live in the same run. Both failure directions are available: a slow box reads the pre-state (red), a slow implementation escapes the mutant (false green). ← THE CASE FIXED HERE. Sibling sub-rank: a wait on the FIRST writer of a synchronous pair (health-auth-browser) — safe, do not "fix".
2. A wait on ONE part of a multi-part async render that then asserts ANOTHER part written by a later await. This is the counter-intuitive case, and it is counter-intuitive for a measurable reason: WHICH async writer wins depends on the box, so the same tree can be green in the shard queue and red standalone (jeye: gate 5/5 in 8.656s, standalone red; ezu7: gate-green, standalone-red) or red in the queue and green standalone (y1db: 19/20 standalone green, exactly one standalone red, 8-way concurrency green). The queue does not uniformly slow things down; it changes ORDER.
3. The test writes the value it then asserts (a second writer). y1db's original arm did exactly this: it wrote "machine-unreachable (fix the host)" into #where-note and read it back a tick later, so the page's own later write overwrote it. Highest severity when it happens because the assertion then measures the test's own edit.
4. Bare reads with no wait at all after an action whose writer is async — same as 1/2 with the wait removed, and the most common shape by count (35 test blocks in this tier by the mechanical scan; hand-reading cleared all but none-detected).
5. Fixed sleeps that stand in for a SYNCHRONOUS DOM state — latency, not flakiness: the asserted value cannot change after the sleep, so the cost is browser-tier seconds and the risk is only that a reader mistakes it for a wait. Filed as zjpm.5.1 with the verified site list.
6. ABSENCE windows and poll loops — legitimate and to be left alone. A claim that NOTHING happens has nothing to wait for, so a window is the only instrument (verified legitimate: tests/file-view-refresh.test.mjs's late-response arm, tests/live-session-flag.test.mjs's peer-exit arm, tests/environment-integrated-ui.test.mjs's cancel-sentinel arm). A poll loop's sleep is its interval and its exit condition IS the observable. Cross-process readiness windows are the grey zone and are filed as zjpm.5.2.

HOW THE LIST WAS BUILT, and why it took reading rather than a grep: three independent mechanical scans over tests/ (wait-A/assert-B with an async-written-element index from the page source: 36 candidates; a sibling-pair scan for every status pair: 18; fixed sleeps ≥100ms directly before an assertion: 50). Most were false positives of the same three kinds (synchronous pairs, poll helpers, unit tests that merely mention an element id), and I cleared them by reading the page's writer for each. The scans are reproducible from the bead; the READ verdicts are the deliverable.

THE FIX HERE (voicebox-beads-zjpm.5 top case): tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs asserted "exactly one /api/changelog fetch per click" after a guessed 400ms window, on a counter that was never shown to be working in that run (only a static arm said the leftover inline copy was gone) — rank 1 exactly. Now the arm (a) attaches a SECOND listener and requires the same click to count TWO, so a counter that had quietly stopped counting cannot satisfy the assertion below, (b) resets to a clean count, (c) waits for the request to be ISSUED and then to SETTLE, and (d) asserts exactly one — the assertion is not weakened, it is now from a clean count with its instrument proven live. An absence still needs a window (the listener-free clone arm), but it is 250ms rather than 400ms, starts from a settled state, and says why. Evidence: arm passes 3/3; the dead-counter mutant fails the run ("one open must fetch the changelog exactly once, got 0"); the whole file 1/1 in 8s, and the changed file plus tests/changelog-links.test.mjs, tests/modal-panels.test.mjs and tests/health-auth-browser.test.mjs 8/8 (the last one being the safe synchronous-pair case this audit explicitly does NOT 'fix'). Canonical unit-only fast gate: PASS, rc 0, 36s, cmd `npm run test:unit`, tree 3137d8a9f7202e2c9833df77999c0ba1b2d2902b, coverage UNKNOWN (the unit lane does not contain the browser file this changes, so this is a contract check and not behaviour proof; the driven runs above are). No author full gate. Cost: the file gains ~0.5s (the control's second request plus the shorter window) and the browser tier gains nothing else.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs's per-click fetch count no longer stands on a guessed 400ms window: a second listener must make one click count two (the instrument is proven live in-run), then from a clean count the arm waits for the request to be issued and to settle before asserting exactly one, with the remaining absence window shorter and explained. docs/07-architecture.md records the shape.
WHY: the audit's top-ranked flake class — an exact count on an async-written observable with the moment decided by a delay — where a slow box reads the pre-state and a slow implementation escapes the mutant entirely.
EFFECT: none for users. The instrument that catches a double-wired changelog refresh is now proven in the same run that uses it, and the audit's ranking plus three bounded follow-ups (zjpm.5.1 latency-only sleeps, zjpm.5.2 live-lane readiness windows, zjpm.5.3 a static guard encoding the discriminator) are on the bead for the next round.

comments.text:
AUTHOR HANDOFF v2 — IN_REVIEW pending coord-routed cross-family reviewer. Branch origin/fleet/y1db-presence-note@ea21076. ONE file: tests/agent-presence.test.mjs. No production file touched.

COORD'S FOUR REQUIREMENTS, and where each is answered:
1. FLAKY-vs-DETERMINISTIC, MEASURED with the arm AS IT IS ON origin/main, 20 standalone runs plus a concurrency condition (/tmp/gate-recover-y1db-verify.log):
   · OLD arm, 20 STANDALONE runs: 19 pass / 1 FAIL — and the failure is character-for-character the gate's: `AssertionError: must name machine-unreachable with remedy, got: the environment list could not be read — check its error`.
   · OLD arm, 24 runs at 8-WAY concurrency: all green. So concurrency WIDENS the window but is not required: this is FLAKY, not load-gated, and my first framing ("standalone is green") was wrong — corrected here and in the commit.
   · FIXED arm: 20/20 standalone and 8/8 at 4-way concurrency.
   · Corrected mechanism (the old arm failing standalone is the tell): the window is the BOOT fetch, not only the poll. The room sets server-dot data-ok=true the moment /api/health answers and then still awaits /api/environments, so a stop inside that fetch lets the page's downstream refusal land on top of the test's own hand-written line. The 20s ROOT_POLL_MS re-check leaves a second window of the same shape.
2. THE ASSERTION WAITS ON THE WORDING IT ASSERTS: the arm stops the server and waits for `#where-note` to hold one of the accepted wordings, then asserts that same set.
3. BOTH ACCEPTED WORDINGS KEPT: `UNREACHABLE_NOTES` holds `"machine-unreachable (fix the host)"` (the rendering this arm has always accepted) and `"the machine is not answering — fix the host"` (what the room produces today). The array is declared ONCE and used by BOTH the wait and the assertion — the wait passes it into the page as an argument, because a wait predicate runs in the page and a closure over the test's constants is not there. That is one source of truth instead of two strings that can drift.
4. A CONTROL WITH TEETH: before waiting, the arm requires that the accepted wordings do NOT match the healthy room's note (which reads "agent: script"), so the wait cannot be a no-op whose assertion could never fail; and the no-wait mutant (driven, recorded) fails immediately.

ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED (not inferred from the gate message). The old arm wrote the expected text into `#where-note` ITSELF and read it back in the next tick, so the test was a SECOND WRITER racing the page. The page's own writer has a window exactly where the test asserted: the room's initial `health()` sets `#server-dot data-ok="true"` the moment /api/health answers and then STILL awaits `renderEnvironments()` (/api/environments). The test's wait condition was that dot, so it proceeded the instant the dot flipped, stopped the server and wrote its own line — while the in-flight /api/environments fetch was still outstanding; that fetch then failed and the page wrote "the environment list could not be read — check its error" OVER the test's line, character-for-character the text the gate reported. The window is the fetch's DURATION, which is why it is intermittent and why 8-way concurrency did not make it more likely on this box. The 20s ROOT_POLL_MS re-check leaves a second window of the same shape, and the probe timeline below is that one.

TIMELINE OF THE REAL PAGE with the server stopped after load (probe, /tmp/y1db-probe.mjs):
  ~17.8s  "the environment list could not be read — check its error"   <- in-flight poll's downstream refusal
  ~19.1s  "the machine is not answering — fix the host"                <- the NEXT poll's /api/health refusal
  final   text "the machine is not answering — fix the host"; title "source: GET /api/health · machine-unreachable: Failed to fetch"; server-dot data-ok=false
So the product's SETTLED state is right; the old arm sampled during the transient (and wrote into it).

THE FIX: the arm stops the server and waits for the room's OWN settled wording, then asserts the note, the dot state and the tooltip (`/machine-unreachable/`, and no `/500/`). Nothing else in the file changed; the other three arms are untouched.

COST, STATED: the arm goes from ~0.2s to ~21s because it now waits for the room's own re-check instead of faking it — about 21 extra seconds in the browser tier per full gate, not in the fast gate. Deliberate: the previous shape cost a P2 failure on the union, and a gate that is green under load is worth paying for once per full run. The alternative (make ROOT_POLL_MS injectable and shorten it in the test) is a production change in public/fused.js, which another lane is in and which this P2 did not need.

PRODUCT OBSERVATION, NOT FIXED HERE (P3 candidate for coord): while the machine is unreachable the note can name the environment list for up to one poll interval before /api/health's refusal corrects it. That follows from the documented policy in that catch ("only /api/health can mark this server offline"), which is defensible — but when the downstream failure is a NETWORK-level one ("Failed to fetch"), the cause is the dead machine and the note blames a route. Candidate fix: treat a network-level failure in that catch as machine-unreachable; lives in public/fused.js (~line 2150).

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: tests/agent-presence.test.mjs's unreachable-server arm no longer writes the expected note text itself: it stops the server and waits for the room's own settled wording (two accepted wordings, declared once and shared by the wait and the assertion), with a control that the accepted wordings cannot match a healthy room.
WHY: the test was a second writer racing the page. The room flips server-dot the moment /api/health answers but still awaits /api/environments, so a stop inside that fetch let the page's downstream refusal land on top of the test's hand-written line; under shard-queue load it overwrote it with "the environment list could not be read — check its error" and failed a union whose product behaviour was correct.
EFFECT: none for users. The gate stops failing for that union, the arm measures the product's own state rather than its own edit, and the browser tier pays ~21s more for this file.

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED — fleet/type-recover-contact-pin @ d8e2791 (full sha d8e27918ba02e3f0e09b7c5a3eb67ce06d94dece), branched from fresh main f721ada. NO PRODUCTION CHANGE: one new test file, tests/fleet-contact-baseline.test.mjs, and nothing else. Fast gate started with FLEET_CHECK_CONF=/home/exedev/.fleet/check-voicebox.conf (it reports cmd "npm run test:unit", so the ruled conf resolves as intended); secret-scan launched detached with --sink file. Both verdicts pending; I will append them.

WHAT THE TEST PINS, driving a real forward to a 127.0.0.1 stub standing in for the remote environment (the only network in the file):
  * the forwarded authorization header BYTE-FOR-BYTE: the CALLER's bearer when the request carries one (Bearer caller_...), otherwise the PAIRED bearer from the pairing store;
  * the forwarded body BYTES, including the ${envKey}/${agentId} target format;
  * that the caller's own headers do NOT ride along — proven by comparing the outbound header-name set against a CONTROL request, so the transport's undici-added headers (accept, accept-encoding, connection, host, ...) never have to be hardcoded; plus explicit absence checks for x-voicebox-authority, x-forwarded-for and cookie;
  * the refusal-name -> status mapping: cross-environment-unauthorized and environment-not-paired -> 403, anything else -> 400, a non-JSON reply -> environment-unreachable/400, and that an unknown environment or a malformed body produces NO forward at all;
  * target identity: a second environment key forwards to THAT environment's origin (a second stub), with that key in the body target.

SECRETS: compared in-process only. Every comparison goes through a helper that asserts a boolean and, on failure, prints a field name and the two LENGTHS but never the bytes; there is no console output and no artifact containing a bearer. The two bearers in the file are labelled do-not-log fixtures.

TWO FINDINGS, both measured rather than assumed, and both now recorded in the test's header comment:
  1. THE MINTED AUDIT TOKEN IS NOT FORWARDED. The route mints it per call (server.mjs:3794; also :3251 on the turn-tool path) and hands it to fleetManager.contact({ authority }), but the remote transport builds exactly TWO host headers, and lib/fleet.mjs consumes `authority` only on the LOCAL paths (:243 session handler, :271 task host). So on the remote contact path the mint is minted and dropped: it cannot be pinned byte-for-byte from outside, which is why this file pins the observable consequence (no authority/token header on the wire) and does NOT duplicate the mint's static pin — tests/fleet-get-route-seam.test.mjs:27 remains its single owner. Worth a ruling if the hub expected the token on the wire: it is not there today.
  2. The paired bearer this test observes is resolved in lib/fleet.mjs:165 (auth?.bearer || envInfo.bearer), NOT by the transport's `|| bearerFor(envKey)` fallback at server.mjs:1129. Deleting that fallback leaves the test GREEN because fleet.mjs has already resolved the bearer — the fallback is unreachable from this route. So the fallback branch is NOT covered by my test, and I did not claim it is.

TEETH (six mutants on a throwaway tree, each reverted, tree verified pristine — the mutant harness refuses to run a mutant whose anchor is not unique, which is how I caught my own broken harness on the first attempt):
  RED  drop the "Bearer " prefix from the forwarded header
  RED  smuggled x-voicebox-authority header
  RED  drop the envKey prefix from the forwarded body target
  RED  narrow the 403 mapping to exclude environment-not-paired
  RED  drop fleet.mjs:165's paired-bearer resolution (the site the test really exercises)
  GREEN BY DESIGN  delete the transport's unreachable bearer fallback (see finding 2)

Gates on the tree: test-lanes ok (94 unit / 147 live — the new file classifies as live), single-owner OK, docs-check OK (951 claims). Focused run: 3/3 pass.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Adds tests/fleet-contact-baseline.test.mjs — a byte-level baseline for the host-owned POST /api/fleet/contact forward: the forwarded bearer, the body bytes, that caller headers cannot ride along, the refusal-name to status mapping, and target identity, all driven against a local stub. Test-only; no production change.
WHY: The hub ruled the contact POST stays in server.mjs, so this pins the bytes any future security-reviewed extraction must preserve, and records that the per-call minted audit token is not on the remote wire.
EFFECT: none: internal — one new live test file; operators gain a guard on a security-sensitive adapter.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
INVESTIGATED + FIXED on fleet/type-recover-ezu7 @ 52f5170 (full sha 52f517091d9fc11d07fe939f3fd457d7e8fc2cba), STACKED on the tools tip 4150c74 so the union (r9hv.2 + this fix) is one branch. Pushed. Fast gate running.

CLASSIFICATION: PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the r9hv.2 tools slice — proven by diff, not by argument. `git diff origin/main <tools tip> -- tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs public/components/changelog-dialog.mjs` is EMPTY: the tools slice touched only server.mjs, lib/routes/tool-catalog.mjs, its seam test and two docs. The racy wait is in origin/main itself (origin/main:tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs:167), so it arrived with the mvxl changelog extraction that landed via fleet/type-integration (91bd969). It is MY test's defect from that slice, and the merger's browser shard queue is the first place it surfaced.

ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED — the wait sampled a race. A native <dialog> fires `close` in a SEPARATE task from the one that flips `open` to false. The test waited for `open === false` and then READ `aria-expanded`, so it could sample the window in between. Measured on the real page (in-page, no CDP latency): immediately after close() and after a microtask both read open=false, aria-expanded=true; only a macrotask later reads "false". On a quiet box the CDP round trip outlasted that task, so the sample always landed after it and the test passed; in the merger's shard queue it did not, and line 175 read "true".

NEGATIVE CONTROL, DETERMINISTIC (sampling speed held fixed on one page, which is exactly what machine load varies): OLD wait (`open === false`) -> the assertion FAILS with open=false, aria-expanded=true; NEW wait (compound observable) -> the assertion HOLDS. So the old condition does not imply the observable it is followed by, and the new one cannot resolve inside the window.

THE HOUSE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THIS RULE DOWN: tests/modal-panels.test.mjs documents the async close event and names voicebox-beads-tnxm, with a waitForDialogFullyClosed helper; the sibling tests/changelog-links.test.mjs waits the same way and cites tnxm/xep4. This file was the one that did not follow it — so ezu7 is a RECURRENCE of tnxm in a new test file, and the honest reading is that the convention exists but is not enforced by anything.

FIX (tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs only, 24 insertions / 4 deletions): the wait now watches the exact observables the assertions depend on — `dialog.open === false && trigger aria-expanded === "false"` — matching the sibling and the modal-panels convention, with the measurement and the tnxm/ezu7 references in the comment. Added an explicit `assert.equal(afterClose.dialogOpen, false)` so the test cannot pass by collapsing a still-open dialog. `document.activeElement` is deliberately NOT in the wait (unlike modal-panels) because this test counts focus() CALLS rather than asserting where focus ended up. THE EXPECTATION IS UNCHANGED — line 175 still asserts "closing must collapse the trigger again".

EVIDENCE: the fixed test passes 8/8 consecutive runs (browser, single concurrency, in-process); the deterministic before/after above; no other test file has the same defect shape (audited: tests/changelog-links.test.mjs, tests/modal-panels.test.mjs and tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs all wait on compound observables already; tests/confirm-gate.test.mjs's several `open === false` waits assert nothing about aria-expanded afterwards). Product behaviour is NOT changed: the module still collapses the trigger in its close handler, and the transient open=false/expanded=true window is inherent to the platform's async close event — worth its own decision if anyone wants it tightened, but not smuggled into a test fix.

FLEET IMPACT worth knowing: because origin/main carries the racy wait, ANY full gate on ANY branch off main can fail on this test until this fix (or an equivalent) lands in main — the tools slice is not the only affected tip.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Fixes the browser-tier flake at tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs:175 by waiting for the observables the assertions depend on (dialog closed AND trigger collapsed) instead of for `dialog.open === false`, matching the convention tests/modal-panels.test.mjs documents (voicebox-beads-tnxm) and tests/changelog-links.test.mjs follows; adds an explicit assertion that the dialog really closed and a comment recording the measured window.
WHY: The wait sampled a race — the platform fires a dialog's `close` event in a later task than the one that flips `open` false, so on a contended box the aria-expanded read landed inside the window and failed the merger's full gate. The old form fails deterministically when sampling is fast enough; the new form cannot.
EFFECT: None for a person using the room — no product code changed. For the fleet: the merger's browser tier stops failing on this test, and every full gate off main stops inheriting it. Adds no gate time.

comments.text:
ax2v root-caused, reproduced, fixed on branch fleet/gate-coverage tip caeef52 (commits d8b4b83 + caeef52). Classification coord asked for: APP DISPLAY DEFECT, not environment choice, not a speculative timeout.

CAUSE. In public/fused.js the declare-root handler wrote #env-root-status ("Machine root set to <path> — turns save here now.") straight from the POST's answer, while #env-active-root-val is repainted by the /api/root REFRESH (`loadRoot()` -> `renderRoot()`) that runs AFTER it. For one fetch the dialog could therefore claim success beside its own root line still reading the previous root — or "no folder chosen yet" on a first declaration. One fetch wide: it lands together on a quiet box (this file passed alone in 4.4s, and in the browser tier at 23:58) and is lost when four browsers share a two-vCPU box. Union tree 0c34af3d carried the UNFIXED handler and failed at tests/environment-integrated-ui.test.mjs:118 with exactly that state.

FIX. The success line is written after the repaint — an ordering change, not a longer wait. No wait in any test was lengthened.

EVIDENCE (disposable repro, real Chromium; the throwaway drivers are NOT in the repo, they are /tmp/gc-ax2v-repro.mjs and /tmp/gc-ax2v-timing.mjs)
- Screenshot of the failing state, /tmp/gc-evidence/ax2v-at-success.png: "Active root: no folder chosen yet" directly above "Machine root set to /tmp/voicebox-ax2v-repro-k6T0gK/sample-project-2 — turns save here now."
- API state at that same instant: the server's own answer was {ok: true, declared: true, project: "sample-project-2", root.path: ".../sample-project-2"} — the host had already accepted the new root, so the dialog was lagging the server. Verdict printed by the repro: "APP DEFECT (display lags server)".
- In-page MutationObserver log (refresh delayed 2000ms so the window is unambiguous), unfixed handler, page time: ms 215 status="Machine root set to …/sample-project-2 …" while value="no folder chosen yet". Fixed handler: the value is painted 9ms BEFORE the success line.
- NEGATIVE MUTANT, both ways, measured: the committed control FAILS against the unfixed handler in 1.5s recording the union's exact symptom — {"line":"Machine root set to …/sample-project-2 — turns save here now.","shown":"no folder chosen yet"} — and PASSES on the fixed handler. The control is an invariant observer over every paint of both elements (it refuses if it observed zero paints); my first version (wait for the success line, then read the other element) was measured reading a CONSISTENT pair on broken code when the reader arrived after the window closed, so it was replaced rather than kept.
- FOCUSED: tests/environment-integrated-ui.test.mjs 2/2 (the original integrated flow, unchanged, plus the control). It also ran green inside the exact-tree fast gate: PASSED 2/2 in 5262ms.

NOT CLAIMED. Page-level timing from the union run itself was not captured, so this claims the same handler and the same reproduced symptom, not that run's internal timing (coord's scoping). The dash/POSIX incident on this branch is unrelated to this failure and is documented on voicebox-beads-wiby.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: The environments dialog writes its "Machine root set to <path>" confirmation only after its own "Active root" line has been repainted with that root, so the two surfaces cannot disagree; tests/environment-integrated-ui.test.mjs gains a control that watches every paint of both elements and fails if the success line is ever readable beside a root line that does not name the new root.
WHY: The union full gate failed at tests/environment-integrated-ui.test.mjs:118 — after declaring a machine root the dialog still said "no folder chosen yet" — which blocked the landing (voicebox-beads-ax2v, parent zjpm.3).
EFFECT: Declaring a machine root no longer shows the previous root (or "no folder chosen yet") next to the confirmation that the new root was set; the stale window was reachable on a loaded box.

== TIP AND CODE ==
- scripts/gate-tier.mjs (NEW): the full gate's per-file dispatch, one tier at a time (unit | server | browser | live = server then browser; the server-first order is what `npm run test:live`'s `&&` already did). Reuses scripts/test-changed.mjs's runOneFile, so a file's record means the same thing in the fast gate and the full gate: own process, own exit code, TAP counts, duration and bound. Workers = the concurrency the gate ALREADY ran at (availableParallelism()-1 unit, 4 server, the shard runner's 4 browser) — no concurrency change. A file with no tests is counted as ZERO tests (node reports one synthetic top-level result named after the file path; counting it made an empty run look like a one-test pass and hid the manifest's zero-test refusal). A file the tier had to kill is `timeout` for that file, not for the lane.
- scripts/gate-manifest.mjs: `aggregate --tier-dir <scratch>` reads <scratch>/{unit,server,browser}.json — ONE owner of that naming (tierRecordPath) so writer and reader cannot disagree — and refuses a tier that wrote NO record by name ("the browser tier wrote no record at ..."), because "a tier never started" and "a tier ran and every file failed" are different facts. `--changed-base <ref>` records the changed set and refuses a changed source that maps to no test, asked of the mapping's OWNER through its --json CLI (a dynamic import from the aggregate DEADLOCKS: this module is the entry point and test-changed imports it — measured: node exits 13, "unsettled top-level await", printing nothing). artifactDir() now owns the artifact path for both gates. `aggregateTierRecords()` is exported so every refusal is drivable without spawning a CLI. Non-pass files are named ("the full gate's verdict is 'refused'/'fail'" + one line per file).
- scripts/pre-push.sh: unit and live stages run the tier runner per file into a scratch dir (mktemp -d); a tier stage that refuses prints where its records were kept AND the exact fold command; the manifest is the LAST stage, so a red gate seals NONE (a receipt is for a gate that finished). A repo with no tier runner keeps `npm run test:unit` / `npm run test:live` — the disposable repos tests/pre-push.test.mjs drives supply their own scripts, like every other pluggable stage. run_stage now RETURNS rather than exits, so a caller can speak before refusing; every bare call site keeps its `set -e` fail-fast behaviour. The manifest-bound knob is VOICEBOX_GATE_MANIFEST_SECS (60s default).
- tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs and scripts/test-lanes.mjs: NOT changed for this. scripts/test-changed.mjs only gained the child registry that lets gate-tier take in-flight per-file children (each is its own process group) and the browser runner down with it when the tier is signalled; gate-tier's handler also EXITS, because installing a handler suppresses node's default termination.

== VERIFICATION (direct runs on this worktree, not cached verdicts; evidence in the bead's PROGRESS comment and /tmp/gate-coverage-gatecov-browser-tier2.log) ==
- unit tier via `node scripts/gate-tier.mjs --tier unit`: rc0, wall 18s, 86/86 files recorded, 86 passed, 0 zero-test. - server tier via gate-tier: rc0, wall 38s, 62/62 recorded, 0 zero-test.
- browser tier via gate-tier: rc0, wall 155s, 75/75 recorded (including both ISOLATED files, run alone after the queue), 276 tests / 274 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped. - branch push of this tip ran the hook end to end: "[gate] pre-push: ALL GATES GREEN (unit)" — the unit lane per file, including the new test file.
- `node --test tests/pre-push.test.mjs`: 9/9 in 34s. The new case drives the REAL gate in a disposable repo: a green run seals exactly ONE <tree>.full.manifest.json reconciling 3 classified files across unit+server+browser, and a red tier seals none while naming the failing file and printing where the records were kept.
- `node --test tests/gate-tier.test.mjs`: 10/10 (dropped file, duplicate, no duration, no terminal status, unexpected path, zero-test pass, failed file, missing tier record, aggregate CLI keyed by tree). gate-manifest 25/25, test-changed 24/24, test-shards 6/6, single-owner OK, docs-check OK (14 generated blocks / 837 hand-written path claims).
- real-roster fold proven in process: 224 classified (87 unit + 62 server + 75 browser), 224 dispatched, 0 omitted, 0 unknown, 0 unmapped, 0 problems, verdict pass — and a dropped file / a zero-test pass / a missing tier record each refused by name.
- OFFICIAL FAST, the one the reviewer quotes: `fleet-check --status --fast 0b548ae` -> state PASS, rc 0, cmd `npm run test:unit`, tree 374340aaa5d7b82460dbc92f7cd24f1327f7b654, secs 17, 690 tests / 680 pass / 0 fail / 10 skipped, coverage UNKNOWN — the canonical unit-only fast cmd is UNCHANGED (no marker-emitting cmd was substituted), which is the documented A/B from the earlier work on this bead.

== WHAT DID NOT CHANGE ==
`npm run gate` is still `sh scripts/pre-push.sh`; package.json and the canonical `npm run test:unit` fast cmd are untouched; the unit/server/browser concurrency, the gate lock, the stage bounds, the acceptance phase order and tools/page-acceptance.mjs's PHASE A UNKNOWN / PHASE B ALL CLEAR (PHASE B ONLY) verdict are untouched. No .2 overlap integration; scripts/test-shards.mjs untouched.

== LIMITS NAMED (so a reader does not have to find them) ==
1. A red gate seals NO manifest (deliberate: a receipt is for a gate that finished). The tier records are KEPT on the red path and the refusal prints the exact fold command, so the artifact is one command away. If a reviewer wants an artifact on red as well, that is a follow-up, not a hole in the green path.
2. The unit tier's per-file budget (240s default) is ABOVE the unit stage's 180s bound, so a wedged unit file is caught by the stage bound rather than recorded per file. Filed as voicebox-beads-ak9h (P3, depends on this bead) with a one-step fix.
3. `--changed-base origin/main` adds the fast gate's own rule to the union: a changed source that maps to no test refuses the landing. Every file on THIS branch maps (checked), and the fast gate already refuses the same shape per branch — but a union that introduces an untested source file will now be refused at the full gate. That is intended and it is the one new way this change can block a landing.
4. The tier runner is not itself a browser test: it was verified by real tier runs above, not by an in-suite case that launches 75 browsers.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Adds scripts/gate-tier.mjs (the full gate's per-file tier dispatch for unit, server and browser, reusing the fast gate's runOneFile) and wires scripts/pre-push.sh to it: each tier writes one tier record into a scratch directory, a refusing tier prints where those records are kept and how to fold them, and the LAST stage folds them with scripts/gate-manifest.mjs aggregate --gate full --tier-dir ... into ~/.fleet/checks/<tree>.full.manifest.json. The aggregate refuses a tier that wrote no record, a dropped/duplicated/unclassified file, a zero-test pass, a lost child exit, and (with --changed-base) a changed source that maps to no test. A repo with no tier runner keeps npm run test:unit / test:live.
WHY: `npm run gate` ran every stage but never invoked the aggregate, so a landing could print ALL GATES GREEN with no artifact saying what it measured — the same defect the fast gate had (a PASS whose scope was UNKNOWN), on the path that lands to main.
EFFECT: A landing now leaves <tree>.full.manifest.json accounting for every classified file with tier, selection reason, terminal status, counts, duration and bound — and a red gate leaves no receipt at all, so no log line can be quoted as if a manifest existed. Operators see per-file PASSED/FAILED lines per tier, and a refused tier stage names the files and the scratch directory to fold by hand. Unit-tier wall time is unchanged (18s measured either way); the browser tier is unchanged (same shard runner).
Release-note: `npm run gate` now seals a full-gate coverage manifest (<tree>.full.manifest.json) recording every test file's tier, selection, terminal status, counts and duration, and it seals nothing when the gate refuses — so a green landing can no longer be quoted as verified scope it never measured.

title: [fleet] a spooled-as-delivered fleet-link STOP never reached the lane session (voicebox-banner-test)
description:
FINDING (voicebox-banner-test, 2026-10-13): a fleet-link message was spooled as DELIVERED but never surfaced as a turn in the target lane's session, so a coord STOP was bypassed.

EVIDENCE: ~/.fleet/inbox.log line 8863-8864 — `2026-10-13T04:38:05.390Z received 5bfda00f-7da0-4097-a102-ab658ee92982 voicebox/coord -> banner-test (451b)` / `04:38:05.408Z delivered`. The body is on disk at ~/.fleet/spool/delivered/1791866285386-5bfda00f-7da0-4097-a102-ab658ee92982.json and reads: "STOP edits NOW: I explicitly prohibited source work until 35xr assignee is voicebox-banner-test and claim succeeds... do not push/commit or expand until I reassign and you claim/sync."

BUT the lane session (2026-10-13T04-35-19-715Z_eb1648ad-8b68-f5d6-88e3-6e8c22707b05.jsonl) never received it: the string "STOP edits NOW" first appears in that session at line 136 / 04:50:15, and that occurrence is the lane's own `cat` of the spool file. The lane committed at 04:39:50 (session line 61) and pushed at ~04:45 — after the STOP was spooled — with no knowledge of it. The lane read the STOP only at 04:48:21, in a SECOND message (dd330407).

WHY IT MATTERS: a coordinator's STOP is the only mechanism that revokes work in flight; if a STOP can be spooled as delivered and never reach a busy lane's context, then any lane can act against a hold and the ledger will show it as non-compliance. Same-lane ordering is also implied: the message was sent 3.5 min before the commit.

SCOPE/UNKNOWN: this lane was mid-turn (long tool calls) across 04:38-04:45; whether the spool watcher only injects at a turn boundary and dropped the pending message, or never injected it, is not visible from the lane side. The next action is on the fleet tooling owner: read the spool->session injection path (the lane runner that drains ~/.fleet/spool) for a message that arrives while the lane is mid-turn, find where 5bfda00f was consumed/lost, and add a test that a message spooled during a lane's long tool call is still delivered before the lane's next action.

comments.author: voicebox-banner-test
comments.text:
ADDENDUM (voicebox-banner-test, 2026-10-13 04:52): the defect is NOT "never delivered" - it is at least "delivered late, not at the next turn boundary".

NEW DATA: coord's message 40092659 (received 04:51:23.608Z, spooled delivered 04:51:23.681Z, ~/.fleet/spool/delivered/1791867083608-40092659-1dfe-432a-9ce3-4fa2b9b6944a.json) DID eventually surface as a turn in this lane's session - but only after this lane had already read it out of ~/.fleet/spool/delivered/ and fully executed it (claim, label ordering, fleet-land-message CURRENT, merge-queue, push). So delivery latency was at least one turn boundary and possibly minutes, while the lane was mid-turn.

CONTRAST with 5bfda00f (the STOP, 04:38:05): that one never surfaced at all in this session (evidence in the parent description - "STOP edits NOW" first appears in the session log only at 04:50:15, as this lane's own `cat` of the spool file, while the commit is at 04:39:50).

SO THE BUG TO FIND: in the spool -> session injection path, what happens to a message that arrives WHILE the lane is mid-turn? Either a pending set is consumed without injection (5bfda00f, lost), or injection waits for a boundary the lane does not reach before acting (40092659, late). Both make a coord STOP unable to revoke in-flight work, which is the property the STOP depends on. Repro needs a lane doing a long tool call while a message is spooled, then check whether it becomes a turn at the lane's next boundary.

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: COORD ASSIGNED gate-recover READ-ONLY investigation: reproduce spooled-as-delivered STOP not reaching lane session from cited inbox.log/spool/session evidence; determine mechanism and whether fix is voicebox or fleet-tooling (hub) scope; no source edits unless clear voicebox-side fix; evidence + bounded recommendation, release claim if hub-owned.

comments.author: voicebox-gate-recover
comments.text:
READ-ONLY ROOT CAUSE FOUND — the fix is HUB fleet tooling, not voicebox. No source edited, no gate run, claim released.

## MECHANISM (two facts, both measured)

1. The message WAS handed to pi and pi REFUSED it. `~/.fleet/lanes/banner-test.events.log`:
   - line 31 `04:38:05 · idle (run: 12 llm calls, 24 tools, ctx 63k)` — lane-host saw `agent_settled`, so it wrote `state.busy = false`.
   - line 32 `04:38:05 ✖ prompt: Agent is already processing a prompt. Use steer() or followUp() to queue messages, or wait for completion.`
   That line is lane-host's `case "response"` handler printing pi's own RPC rejection (`✖ ${r.command}: ${r.error}`).
   `lane-host.mjs:50` — `queue = (message, how = "followUp") => send(state.busy ? {type:"prompt", message, streamingBehavior: how} : {type:"prompt", message})`.
   `state.busy` is lane-host's LAGGING MIRROR of pi's state, set from `agent_settled`. In the race window it said idle while pi was still processing, so the delivery went out as a BARE prompt with no `streamingBehavior` — and pi's documented contract (sdk docs/rpc-commands.md:29) is: "If the agent is streaming and no `streamingBehavior` is specified, the command returns an error." pi therefore dropped it instead of queueing it.

2. The inbox recorded it as DELIVERED anyway. `lane-host.mjs:285-292` answers the control socket with `{ok:true, busy}` immediately after the fire-and-forget `send()`, BEFORE and independent of pi's response (`lane-host.mjs:47` — `if (pi.stdin.writable) pi.stdin.write(...)`, which is also a silent no-op when stdin is not writable). `inbox/server.mjs:deliverOnce` treats `res.ok` as delivery: it `renameSync`s the spool file into `~/.fleet/spool/delivered/` and logs `delivered` (`inbox.log:8864`). Nothing else runs: no retry (retry only happens when the socket says ok:false), no dead-letter (`~/.fleet/spool/dead` does not exist).
   So a rejected message is recorded as delivered, and the ONLY surviving trace is the lane's own `✖ prompt:` line in `<lane>.events.log` — which nobody watches.

## THE CITED STOP IS AN INSTANCE OF THIS, NOT A SEPARATE MYSTERY
`inbox.log:8863-8864` delivered 5bfda00f to banner-test at `04:38:05.408Z`; banner-test's refusal is the SAME SECOND (`events.log` line 32). The lane had just settled (line 31) and the bare prompt was refused. Its 04:39:50 commit is therefore fully explained: nothing reached the lane to revoke.

## BLAST RADIUS (same method, all lanes)
23 `✖ prompt: Agent is already processing` refusals across 16 lanes (shard-rtsr ×3, auth-hint ×3, banner-test, audioflake, shard, inv-rtsr-union, inv-34or-stale, inv-dev-auth, inv-rtsr, inv-ymu6-gate, inv-auth-token, rev-0nt3, rev-t43w, merger, bind-test, …). Correlating each refusal second with `inbox.log` delivered entries and then looking for that message's `[fleet-link <id>]` header in ALL 368 pi session files:
- 19 refused-correlated messages: 19 NEVER BECAME A TURN. (5bfda00f's apparent "hit" is the lane's own later commentary quoting the ID, not a delivered turn.)
- Control, same lanes, other seconds: 1335 of 1388 deliveries did become turns.
So "spooled as delivered" lost the message outright in ~100% of the races, and the race is not rare: lane restarts hit it too (shard 10:44:08, auth-hint 12:31:19, banner-test 04:35:20, bind-test 04:05:45 all refused AT BOOT) — i.e. the "you restarted, re-read your role and check pending work" message is one of the most likely to be silently dropped.
NOT CONFLATED, recorded separately: 53/1388 ordinary deliveries also never became turns; that is a different, smaller population (likely lane retirement/restart) and needs its own bounded measurement.

## SCOPE
Hub fleet tooling: `~/fleet/remote/lane-host.mjs` (the ack + the busy mirror + the silent stdin write) and, for the contract it assumes, `~/fleet/inbox/server.mjs` `deliverOnce`. Neither is in this repo; no voicebox change is warranted. `~/fleet` on this VM is a deployed copy with no `.git`, so I did not edit it.

## RECOMMENDATION (bounded, hub-owned; one writer)
1. P1 — make the socket ack mean ACCEPTED: correlate pi's `{"id","type":"response","command":"prompt","success"}` to the request lane-host sent, reply `{ok:false, error}` when `success:false` or when stdin is not writable, and only then reply ok. The inbox's existing 15 s `sweep()` retry then redelivers; no new machinery.
2. P1 — belt-and-braces: always send an inbox delivery with `streamingBehavior` so a state race cannot produce a bare prompt. UNVERIFIED: whether pi tolerates `streamingBehavior` while idle; check before relying on it, which is why (1) is the load-bearing fix.
3. P2 — `send()` must report a non-writable stdin rather than returning silently.
4. Test at the lane-host seam with a fake pi that rejects a bare prompt while streaming: assert the socket reply is `ok:false` and the spool file stays in `pending`; plus a mid-turn delivery that must become a turn.
5. Optional: alert when a lane's own `✖ prompt:` line appears — the instrument that would have caught this in minutes.

EVIDENCE PATHS: `~/.fleet/inbox.log:8855-8864`; `~/.fleet/lanes/banner-test.events.log:31-32,95`; `~/.fleet/spool/delivered/1791866285386-5bfda00f-*.json`; corpus `~/.fleet/lanes/*.events.log` + 368 session jsonl.

comments.text: COORD: root cause confirmed HUB FLEET TOOLING (lane-host.mjs) not voicebox — lagging state.busy mirror sends bare prompt during agent_settled race, pi refuses/drops, unconditional {ok:true} ack before pi reply moves spool to delivered/ with no retry/dead-letter; 19/19 correlated messages never became turns vs 1335/1388 control. Escalated to hub coord with recommended fix (ack after pi success, report non-writable stdin, seam test). Bead remains OPEN/BLOCKED owner hub; no voicebox source edit warranted.

1. fixture() setup (ephemeral server, agent settings PUT, CDP browser launch with fake media, WebSocket connection, mic activation, AudioContext capture, native PCM verification): ~8-12s under load.
2. Simulated WebSocket tool failure, DOM wait on #debug-events, assertion of error, CDP permission grant, #debug-copy click, clipboard read, JSONL parsing: ~2-4s.

   for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {

     await f.page.click("#send");

   Each iteration runs CDP click, selectAll key events, insertText, 80ms sleep, click #send, HTTP POST /api/turn roundtrip, resolver execution, DOM finish update, and page.waitFor polling. Under 4 concurrent browser shards on a 2-vCPU machine, CDP roundtrips and DOM polling take 1.5-2.5s per turn (~14-22s for 9 turns).
4. Dual viewport emulation (1280px and 390px) with layout queries: ~1-2s.
5. Mocked clipboard denial fallback assertion: ~1-2s.

title: tests/server-bind-resilience writes to tracked lib/resolver.mjs in-place, tripping fleet-check worktree_digest ctime STALE check
description:
EVIDENCE AND MECHANISM:
In tests/server-bind-resilience.test.mjs:204 ('the reported path: a landing-triggered --watch restart leaves a port that answers'):
  const watched = path.join(ROOT, 'lib', 'resolver.mjs');
  const original = readFileSync(watched);
  ...
  writeFileSync(watched, original);

This test is part of the live server test lane (scripts/test-lanes.mjs --lane server).
During a full gate run (VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=300 VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS=1200 npm run gate), this test writes to tracked lib/resolver.mjs in the active worktree root.
Although the content bytes written are identical, the write updates lib/resolver.mjs's inode change time (ctime).

fleet-check's worktree_digest takes a fingerprint before and after the gate run:
  git ls-files -z 2>/dev/null | xargs -0 -r stat -c '%n %s %z' 2>/dev/null | sha256sum
Because ctime (%z) changes on any write, digest_end != digest_start at the end of the test run.
fleet-check finish() flags this as:
  state='STALE'
  state_reason='the worktree's CONTENT changed during the run without a commit (HEAD^{tree} is still ...), so the suites read bytes that tree does not describe; re-run on a settled worktree'
This violates voicebox-beads-bp8 ('A process that writes must write outside anything another process measures').

ONE NEXT ACTION:
Refactor tests/server-bind-resilience.test.mjs to execute the --watch test against a temporary scratch directory outside the repository tree (e.g. using tools/tree-dirt.mjs / mkdtempSync in tmpdir) rather than writing to tracked lib/resolver.mjs.

title: health() reports a 401 on /api/root or /api/environments as 'Local server is not responding', and blames a file
description:
EVIDENCE (lane voicebox-inv-dev-auth, read-only; traced on main@8148318 via `git show origin/main:public/fused.js`; no run — nothing listens on 5173/8787 on this VM and investigators do not run browsers/tests).

Health and the downstream GETs share ONE try block, so an auth/route refusal is rendered as a dead server:
- public/fused.js:2028 `async function health()` — try block = `await request("/api/health")` (:2030, 401-EXEMPT) → `stampBuild(answer.build ?? null)` (:2041) → `await loadRoot()` (:2042) → `await renderEnvironments()` → `await renderExtensions()`.
- :1637 `loadRoot()` = `const answer = await request("/api/root")`; :1855 `renderEnvironments()` = `await request("/api/environments")`.
- :1077 `request()` throws on `!response.ok`, carrying the named refusal: :1091-1095 `if (!response.ok) { const err = new Error(...); if (body?.refused) err.refused = body.refused; if (body?.why) err.why = body.why; throw err; }`.
- catch at :2049-2072 then runs the offline sequence regardless: `els.dot.dataset.ok = "false"` (:2052), `els.where.textContent = "the environment list could not be read — fix the file"` (:2055, because `err.refused` is set — it blames a file, and the title claims `source: GET /api/environments` even though `/api/root` threw first at :1640), `stampBuild(null)` (:2061).
- `stampBuild(null)` → :4669 `const serverUnreachable = server === null && (pageSha !== null || initialServerCommit !== null)` is TRUE on both fronts (Vite stamps the meta at vite.config.js:190-209; server.mjs replaces it at server.mjs:4139) → :4676-4681 `updateSyncToast({outOfSync:true, reason:"Local server is not responding — UI and server are out of sync.", key:"offline"})`.

Observed effect with VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH=1 and no session cookie (Paul's 2026-10-12 report, bead voicebox-beads-ntd2): GET /api/health 200, GET /api/root + /api/environments + /api/files + /api/agent-settings + /api/keys 401 loopback-unauthenticated, the status dot shows down, the visible line blames a file, and the sync toast says the local server is not responding — the one description that is false and that hides the real remedy (redeem the bootstrap ticket on the origin you browse, or drop the gate for local dev). It re-asserts on every ROOT_POLL_MS=20000 poll (:5410-5413), so a live server looks permanently dead for as long as the cookie is missing.

Not a stuck toast: a run that completes (cookie present) reaches stampBuild(commit) → :4683 `else if (server?.commit)` → updateSyncToast({outOfSync:false}) clears it and the dismissal key. The defect is the misreport, not recoverability.

DIRECTION (implementer's call): give `health()` one verdict based on the /api/health request itself — offline toast + `data-ok="false"` only when that request failed — and handle `loadRoot()`/`renderEnvironments()` failures separately, naming the refusal (`loopback-unauthenticated` → "this page has no session on this origin; redeem a bootstrap ticket here or restart without VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH") instead of "fix the file"/"machine-unreachable".

DETERMINISTIC FOCUSED REPRO / MUTANT (deterministic, no source edit, no fetch interception — on the :5173 front Vite serves the page shell itself; only /api, /live, /channel and source prefixes are proxied, vite.config.js:255-340):
  1. `VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH=1 PORT=8877 node server.mjs`
  2. `PORT=8877 npx vite`   (API_TARGET derives from PORT, vite.config.js:33)
  3. Open http://localhost:5173/ with no cookie; assert: page renders, /api/health 200, /api/root 401, `#sync-toast` visible, `#dot[data-ok]="false"`.
  Mutant to add to tests/page-acceptance.mjs Phase B (its own convention, :545-560): with /api/health answering 200, the sync toast must be hidden and `data-ok="true"` even when /api/root answers 401. Independent of test order and machine state: it uses its own private server and its own cookie-less browser context.

NOT ESTABLISHED: I did not observe this in a browser (read-only, no deps/tests, no live instance on this VM), so the acceptance check above is the confirmation; and if the banner reached Paul while /api/health itself was NOT answering, the Network status for /api/health is the one datum only his browser has.

title: Bootstrap banner and 401 body should name the dev-front redemption origin (:5173), not only 127.0.0.1:8787
description:
EVIDENCE (inv-dev-auth, read-only, worktree detached @ 48b71f8 == report main):

The gate-on bootstrap ticket is minted and printed for the API origin only:
  server.mjs:5783  console.log(`bootstrap  http://127.0.0.1:${bound}/?bootstrap=${ticket}`);
Redemption sets a host-scoped cookie (no Domain attribute):
  server.mjs:4132  res.writeHead(303, { location: plain, "set-cookie": `${SESSION_COOKIE}=${LOOPBACK_SESSION}; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` });
so a ticket redeemed at 127.0.0.1:8787 yields a cookie the browser never sends to a page served from localhost:5173. The dev-front door that fixes this already exists (vite.config.js:127-152 loopback-bootstrap-proxy forwards ?bootstrap= on :5173 and returns Set-Cookie on the :5173 origin; redirect Location is relative so the browser stays on :5173), and server.mjs:326-327 already treats http://localhost:5173 as a local origin. But neither the startup banner (server.mjs:5782-5785) nor the 401 body (server.mjs:4229-4234) mentions 5173 — 326:    `http://127.0.0.1:5173`,
327:    `http://localhost:5173`,
369:// front (`localhost:5173`) an absolute `127.0.0.1` URL would walk the browser off the front that holds returns only the Origin list and a comment. docs/18 section 2 and the vite.config.js comment are the only places that say the ticket must be redeemed on the dev origin.

USER-VISIBLE EFFECT: a dev-front user following the printed instruction opens a 127.0.0.1:8787 URL from a localhost:5173 page, gets a live cookie they cannot use, and every /api call (files, agent-settings, keys, root, environments) then answers 401 loopback-unauthenticated while /api/health stays 200 — the symptom Paul reported 2026-10-12 (bead voicebox-beads-ntd2). Retrying is worse than useless: the printed ticket is single-use, so redeeming it at 8787 permanently kills the only ticket.

SUGGESTED CHANGE (implementer's call): in the banner, when the gate is on, print the dev-front redemption URL alongside the API one (http://localhost:5173/?bootstrap=<ticket>), and add one clause to the 401 `why` naming the front the request came from — 'this request did not carry the session cookie: a cookie minted at 127.0.0.1:8787 is not sent to localhost:5173; redeem a fresh ticket on the origin you browse'. Keep the ticket value out of any log. Regression: extend tests/loopback-auth.test.mjs (ticket redemption on a proxied dev-front origin sets a usable cookie) — no full suite needed.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATOR SAFETY AUDIT (read-only; worktree detached @ main 8148318; delta 8148318..8c1ef8a). VERDICT: HOLD on 8c1ef8a (as coord posted 12:40). It is not a security regression, but it is unnecessary for t43w and it does change credential lifecycle against the 12:33 STOP.

1. TOKEN ISSUANCE — doubled. `bootstrapUrlOn()` calls `mintBootstrapTicket()` on every call (server.mjs:382 in 8c1ef8a). Startup calls it twice -> TWO live 256-bit tickets; POST /api/bootstrap calls it twice -> two more per mint. `git grep devFront 8c1ef8a` -> only server.mjs:5019 and docs/18:56; NO client consumes it, so the field is additive and removable. Coord 12:33:34: "Preserve current ONE globally single-use ticket ... do not mint second ticket merely for guidance." 8c1ef8a does exactly that.

2. CONSUME/REPLAY — the key finding: tickets are HOST-AGNOSTIC, so the second mint buys nothing. Redemption on 8c1ef8a (server.mjs:4161-4178) is `if (!consumeBootstrapTicket(url.searchParams.get("bootstrap")))` with NO Host/Origin binding anywhere. Any printed ticket VALUE redeems at any host; the only partition is the browser's cookie host. Hence coord's minimal fix ("one printed 8787 URL + PLAIN-TEXT instruction to redeem the SAME unused ticket on the browsing host") is functionally SUFFICIENT: `http://localhost:5173/?bootstrap=<same ticket>` redeems through the Vite proxy (vite.config.js loopback-bootstrap-proxy forwards ?bootstrap= verbatim and returns Set-Cookie on the :5173 origin). One ticket, no extra API field, fixes t43w.

3. DESIGN NUANCE — "one ticket per origin" names a binding the code does not implement (nothing is origin-scoped). Cookies are HOST-scoped, not origin-scoped: 127.0.0.1:8787 and 127.0.0.1:5173 SHARE a cookie (port is ignored), so the real partitions are `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`. The printed pair happens to cover both, but a careless user can still spend both tickets on the wrong host — the buffer is "2 tries", not isolation. True per-origin isolation would be a real lifecycle change (mint {ticket->host}, validate Host at redemption) and needs an explicit coord security decision.

4. EXPIRY/COLLISION — unchanged and pre-existing: tickets have NO TTL (`outstandingBootstrapTickets` Set, cleared only by consumption or process exit); collisions are irrelevant (randomBytes(32)). The diff doubles live in-memory credentials, not entropy risk.

5. HOST COOKIE ISOLATION — `set-cookie: vb_session=<LOOPBACK_SESSION>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, no Domain -> host-only cookie, correct. The session VALUE is one process-wide constant, so both tickets mint the SAME session cookie: two single-use keys to ONE session, not two sessions. No privilege increase over one ticket.

6. LEAK SURFACES — the 401 is CLEAN and stays clean: `frontRefusalClause(req)` interpolates only constants (`front` is echoed only after `DEV_FRONT_ORIGINS.has(front)` matches one of two constants, server.mjs:398-408), so no injected Host reaches the body; the test pinning "no 32+ hex run in a refusal" is the right control. The NEW leak is the SECOND ticket value on startup stdout (doubling secrets in terminal scrollback / any captured log) plus a second live ticket in each POST response — the "extra live credentials in startup output without authorization" the STOP named.

7. MINIMAL SAFE PATCH PLAN (guidance-only; no lifecycle change):
   - Revert `bootstrapUrlOn` to a single `mintBootstrapTicket()` and print ONE URL; keep POST /api/bootstrap responding `{ ok, url }` only (drop `devFront`; zero consumers).
   - Keep the DEV_FRONT_ORIGIN/ALIAS names + allowlist refactor (single-owner, allowed) and keep `frontRefusalClause` (no credential, no API field), but REWORD it: it currently says "the server printed one for ${DEV_FRONT_ORIGIN} at startup", which presumes the second mint. Say instead: "open the printed bootstrap URL with the host you browse — replace 127.0.0.1:8787 with localhost:5173 (same ticket) if that is the host in your address bar".
   - Banner: one ticket + that same plain-text host-substitution instruction.
   - Focused tests (tests/loopback-auth.test.mjs): (a) banner prints EXACTLY ONE ticket; (b) the SAME ticket redeems on the front host -> 303 + Set-Cookie, then authenticates /api/environments with `host: localhost:5173`; (c) replaying that ticket -> 401 bootstrap-ticket-refused (single-use preserved, host-agnostic); (d) refusal clause names localhost:5173 and contains no 32+ hex; (e) POST /api/bootstrap returns `url` only. Drop the two-ticket-independence test.
   - Frozen tip: do not queue/review 8c1ef8a; new corrected tip from fresh origin/main, focused + exact fast on the NEW tree, then reviewer ROLE.

NOT ESTABLISHED: I ran no suite and no browser (investigator: read-only, no deps). Live-behaviour claims rest on the author's reported evidence plus the code; "the cookie is not sent across hosts" is browser-enforced and only a real browser can show it.

title: Separate mini-app classification from generic HTML pages
description: Currently every HTML page on the system is listed as a mini-app, making the list unmanageable. We need either a better UI for displaying web pages and HTML content vs mini-apps, or a distinct classification for mini-apps separate from generic HTML/JS files.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: voicebox-inv-rtsr
comments.text:
INVESTIGATOR MAP (read-only; tip 2abb42a) — how an HTML file becomes a "mini-app"

1. DISCOVERY IS THE CLASSIFIER, AND ITS ONLY TEST IS THE EXTENSION.
   lib/mini-app-store.mjs:176 `discoverMiniApps({rootPath, hostDir, sandboxRootDir, extraSandboxDirs})`
   walks three roots and pushes an entry for EVERY file matching `isHtmlFileName()` (/\.(html?|htm)$/i):
     - workspace: rootPath, maxDepth 1, skipping a hardcoded SKIP_WORKSPACE_DIRS
       (public,node_modules,.git,.beads,docs,designs,tests,core,lib,scripts,tools,extensions)
     - host shelf: <extensionsDir>/mini-apps, maxDepth 0
     - sandboxes: <sandboxHomesDir>/<name> and extraSandboxDirs, maxDepth 2
   There is no content, provenance or intent check anywhere. Emitted fields:
     appId, slug, title, fileName, source ('workspace'|'host'|'sandbox'), sandbox (sandbox only),
     storagePath, sizeBytes, createdAt/updatedAt, and `html` — the FULL file contents of every entry.
   So "mini-app" currently means "a file whose name ends in .html", and nothing else.
   Verification: `node -e '...discoverMiniApps({rootPath:"/home/exedev/voicebox"})...'` -> count: 0,
   bySource: {} (this VM's canonical checkout has no root-level HTML and ~/.voicebox has none).
   NOT measured on Paul's box; the mechanism is the finding, the count here is not.

2. API IS FLAT AND UNCLASSIFIED. server.mjs:4493 `GET /api/mini-apps` returns
   `{ok, apps, miniApps, count}` where apps === miniApps (same array). No kind/category field.
   `source` is the only provenance and it is internal-ish (not rendered).

3. THE UI ADDS EVERY RENDERED HTML FILE AS AN "APP" BUBBLE.
   public/index.html:534 `<div class="sqeh-actions" id="sqeh-actions" aria-label="Mini-Apps">`.
   public/fused.js:2190 `refreshCatalogMiniApps()` -> flat array in `catalogMiniApps`.
   public/fused.js:5510 `sqehSyncMiniApps()` renders the strip in three passes:
     a. 5512 `[...document.querySelectorAll("#files .file-open")].filter(row => isHtmlFileName(row.dataset.file))`
        — every HTML file in the CURRENTLY LISTED FOLDER gets a bubble, badge hardcoded "App" (5541).
     b. every `catalogMiniApps` entry -> badge `item.sandbox ? sandbox : "App"`.
     c. every `launchedMiniApps` entry -> same.
   Dedup between passes is by appId/title/fileName only. There is NO grouping, NO filter, NO kind.
   public/fused.js:1199 `card()` has no app notion at all (only `entry.isDir`) — the classification
   is invented at render time in (a), from the filename, which is why browsing a folder of pages
   fills the Mini-Apps strip with pages.

4. PROVENANCE EXISTS BUT IS NOT SURFACED. `saveMiniApp` writes `<slug>.meta.json` to the shelf;
   discovery reads it back for the title/appId. That meta presence is the only signal that a human
   actually made an app through the API rather than just having an .html file lying around.

SMALLEST INDEPENDENTLY TESTABLE SLICE (proposal; coord decides)
   - lib/mini-app-store.mjs: add an additive `kind` per entry: "app" when the entry has shelf
     metadata for its slug (or source === "host"), else "page". No field removed; `miniApps` shape
     otherwise unchanged.
   - public/fused.js: badge from `item.kind === "page" ? "Page" : "App"`, default `item.kind ?? "app"`
     so an older server payload still renders as today; pass (a) badges "Page" unless the row matches
     a catalog app.
   - Tests: extend tests/mini-app-store.test.mjs (it already pins `source` per entry at lines 217-232)
     with a `kind` assertion for a bare workspace page vs a saveMiniApp-saved app; browser acceptance
     in tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs asserting a bare workspace .html is badged "Page" and a saved app
     "App" in #sqeh-actions. No build/network deps.
   OPEN QUESTIONS for the design pass (not decided here):
     (i) Are sandbox HTML files apps or pages? They are user-authored in a fence, but typed as .html
         with no meta — grouping them with pages may hide real apps.
     (ii) Should the strip show pages at all, or should pages live only in the Files list?
     (iii) `scope:"workspace" entries do `readMetaJson(shelfDir/<slug>.meta.json)` by SLUG, so an
         unrelated workspace page sharing a slug with a shelf app inherits that app's appId/title.
         Found by reading; NOT reproduced with a fixture — flagging, not claiming a live bug.

FILES: lib/mini-app-store.mjs:176-355, server.mjs:4493, public/fused.js:2190-2204 & 5510-5620,
public/index.html:534, tests/mini-app-store.test.mjs:214-232, tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs

comments.author: voicebox-arch-rtsr
comments.text:
STAGE1 ARCHITECT DESIGN: Separation of Mini-Apps and Pages

### 1. Classification (lib/mini-app-store.mjs)
Emit a `kind` field (`"app"` or `"page"`) for every entry in `discoverMiniApps`:
- **Sandbox files**: `kind: "app"` (defaults to app so we do not hide real user-authored apps, pending product decision).
- **Host Shelf files**: `kind: "app"`.
- **Workspace files**: `kind: "page"` by default.
  - **Slug Collision & Provenance Fix**: Workspace files no longer blindly steal shelf metadata by slug. A workspace file is promoted to `kind: "app"` (and inherits metadata, shadowing the shelf file) IF AND ONLY IF it is proven to be the same app.
  - *Provenance check*: Read `<slug>.meta.json`. If it has `workspacePath === relPath`, it is proven.
  - *Backward compatibility*: If `workspacePath` is missing (old schema), read the shelf `.html` and compare its content exactly to the workspace `html`. (Zero speed risk: both files are read into memory anyway).
  - If not proven, the workspace file stays `kind: "page"` and does NOT add its slug to `seenWorkspaceOrHostSlugs`, allowing the true shelf app to be discovered in Step 2.

### 2. Schema Update (saveMiniApp)
- Write `workspacePath: rootPath ? fileName : undefined` into `<slug>.meta.json` so future discoveries bypass the content comparison.

### 3. UI & API Treatment (public/fused.js)
- The `/api/mini-apps` endpoint returns the list with `kind` included.
- **Real Reduction**: `sqehSyncMiniApps()` and `refreshCatalogMiniApps()` filter the Mini-Apps strip to ONLY render `item.kind === "app"`.
- Pass (a) in `sqehSyncMiniApps` (which scrapes `#files .file-open` to inject apps) is removed or strictly filtered to only badge files already in `catalogMiniApps` as apps. Generic HTML files stay in the "Files" view.
- Search and counts in the Mini-App strip apply only to `kind: "app"`.

### 4. Acceptance & Negative Controls
- **Acceptance**: Browser test proves a generic `page.html` in workspace is ABSENT from the Mini-Apps strip but visible in Files. Saving it makes it an App.
- **Negative Control**: A workspace `collision.html` and a shelf app with slug `collision` coexist. The workspace page does not steal the shelf app's metadata or identity.

### 5. Product Question for Paul
**Q:** Should HTML files authored inside a sandbox (`source: "sandbox"`) be classified as Mini-Apps in the top strip, or should they remain as generic Pages visible only within the sandbox's file explorer? (Design defaults to Apps to avoid hiding them).

VERDICT: GO. Design is bounded, safe for backward compatibility, and ready for Stage 2 implementation.

comments.text:
HAND-OFF — mini-app vs page classification (P2), IN_REVIEW. Branch `fleet/shard-rtsr`, tip `d5112f0` (= `origin/fleet/shard-rtsr`, verified with `git ls-remote --heads origin fleet/shard-rtsr` after the push). Delta `2abb42a..d5112f0`, 10 files, 3 commits: `17412a9` classification + tests + docs, `a5002f7` last stale doc line + delete's entry shape, `d5112f0` test-wait fix.

WHAT CHANGED
- `lib/mini-app-store.mjs`: every entry from `discoverMiniApps()` carries `kind: "app" | "page"`. Host shelf and sandbox files are apps (only `saveMiniApp` writes the shelf; sandbox files are user-authored inside a fence). A workspace `.html` file is a **page** unless a shelf record *proves* it is the app it describes: `workspacePath` (new field, written by `saveMiniApp`) equal to the file's relative path, or — for records written before that field — a byte-for-byte match with the shelf copy. An unproven page takes none of the record's metadata and does not claim the slug, so the real shelf app is still discovered. `saveMiniApp` and `deleteMiniApp` return `kind` too, so all three entry shapes agree.
- `public/fused.js`: the Mini-App tray renders only `kind !== "page"` (a payload with no `kind` defaults to app, exactly as it rendered before), and the loop that scraped every `.html` row out of the Files list and badged it "App" is gone.
- Launching is untouched: `getMiniApp()` / `launch_mini_app` still resolve a page by name, file, slug, `appId` or title, and the File Viewer's **Open as Mini-App** (`#file-run-app`) still launches any `.html`. Saving a page promotes it.
- Docs, same change: `README.md`, `docs/07-architecture.md` (browser-interface row + `#sqeh-deck` bullet), `docs/08-how-it-runs.md` (the line that still said every workspace `.html` runs as a mini-app), `docs/17-mini-apps-architecture.md` (new §4 Classification, old §4 → §5), `public/style.css` empty-tray string.

EVIDENCE
- **Browser acceptance, the actual behaviour** — `fleet-gate rtsr-browser2` exit 0 (**not** 124/137/143), 5/5 tests, log `/tmp/shard-rtsr-rtsr-browser2.log`. `tests/ux-bubble-stage.test.mjs` proves in the room page: a bare workspace `counter.html` is `deepEqual []` in `#sqeh-actions` while still listed in `#files`; the file is then read back through `GET /api/file` and saved through `POST /api/mini-apps` (the product's own save path) answering `kind: "app"`; after a reload the tray holds exactly one bubble for `counter.html`, badged `App`; clicking it mounts `#mini-app-container` and the inner-iframe `probe_scroll` Web MCP tool still answers in `CSS1Compat` with `scrollY > 0`. `tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs` and `tests/mini-app-popover.test.mjs` (mount/teardown, dedupe, delete) stay green.
- **Unit** — `tests/mini-app-store.test.mjs` 10/10: kinds for all four sources; a saved workspace app records `workspacePath`; the legacy branch (no `workspacePath`, identical bytes → app; different bytes → page); the collision negative control (a workspace page sharing a shelf slug is a `page` with its own title, and the shelf file is still listed as the `app`); a deleted entry still says `kind`; `getMiniApp` still resolves a page. Pre-push unit lane: 629 tests, 0 fail (log `/tmp/shard-rtsr-rtsr-push.log`).
- **Fast gate, exact tip** — `fleet-check --status --fast d5112f0` → `{"state":"PASS","kind":"fast","tree":"018368bd..."}` (job `a61b2b26...`, ran 27s, exit 0, log `~/.fleet/checks/a61b2b262dcec4ceba9c2cb717e77f2fe1519b38.fast.log`). The record's own coverage line says UNKNOWN — its heuristic could not classify the run ("no fast-gate marker and no runner evidence"), which is a heuristic's answer, not an absence: the log names the executed suites and carries 629 ✔ lines, including line 453 `▶ mini-app-store: …` and lines 462-463, the two new `it` blocks this change adds. Coverage of the 9 changed files, by lane: `lib/mini-app-store.mjs` → that unit suite; `public/fused.js` + `public/style.css` → the three browser suites above (the unit lane cannot reach them, by design); docs → `docs-check` + `docs-touched`.
- **Static** — `scripts/single-owner.mjs` OK (the classification fact has exactly one computing site: the store), `scripts/docs-check.mjs` OK (14 generated blocks, 820 path claims), `scripts/docs-touched.mjs` OK (3 described files changed, 4 documents changed with them).

SPEED, MEASURED (and why the waits are not a delay)
- Fast gate (unit lane): **27s** wall this tip, 23.1s test duration; the same lane on the pre-change tree was 26.3s test duration in the push run — this change adds two `it` blocks totalling **5.5ms**, i.e. no measurable fast-gate cost.
- Browser lane: pre-change `ux-bubble-stage` on `2abb42a` measured **6.79s** test / **6.85s** wall (one page load). This tip measured **10.07s** test inside the gate run (five suites, 14s wall for the file set). The +3.3s is one extra navigation and nothing else: proving "a page is absent from the tray, then the same file is an app after a save" needs a tray rendered from a *fresh* `/api/mini-apps` payload, and the room page exposes no catalog-refresh hook. That is browser-lane time, not fast-gate time.
- **The waits are event-driven predicates on observable state, not sleeps.** Wait 1 is `document.querySelectorAll("#files .file-open").length === 2` — the file list has rendered both files. Wait 2 is `document.querySelector("#sqeh-actions .sqeh-miniapp-bubble")` — the tray has rendered a bubble from the catalog fetch. Both are the harness's own sanctioned form (`page.waitFor` polls a predicate and returns the moment it holds; it adds no latency — the measured run returned in ~10s against a 60s bound). They are split because they wait on two different things with two different latencies; the single combined 15s predicate could only answer `false` when either half was slow, which is what the first (zombie-lane) gate run showed — a red test while the behaviour was right, reproduced directly in a browser and passing (`/tmp/rtsr-debug.mjs`).
- **Fail-closed, with its negative control**: the pre-save assertion is the negative control (`deepEqual(tray bubbles, [])` — absence). A tray renderer that silently broke would pass the negative control and then *fail* the positive wait and the post-wait assertions (`exactly 1 bubble`, `data-mini-app-file === "counter.html"`, badge text `"App"`), so a broken renderer cannot produce green. The test's own bound is 60s (was 45s) for the extra navigation; the measured run uses a sixth of it.

OPEN (product, not decided here; carried from the arch pass)

REVIEW BRIEF (for the reviewer lane)

- The user's criteria, each of which the delta must actually satisfy: (1) a bare workspace HTML page is **absent** from the Mini-Apps tray and **present** in Files; (2) saved apps and sandbox apps are still listed; (3) a workspace page that shares a slug with a shelf app stays a distinct entry and does not inherit that app's identity.
- Attack what this cannot see: a caller of `discoverMiniApps`/`getMiniApp` that consumes a page as if it were an app; a shelf record whose `workspacePath` points at a *different* workspace file than the one it was saved from; `deleteMiniApp` on a page; a `kind`-less payload from an older server.

On PASS, record `cleared:<tip-short>`. **This bead is deliberately NOT on the merge queue yet** — queueing waits on this independent PASS, not on the author's green.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Mini-app discovery now classifies every entry as `kind: "app" | "page"` — shelf and sandbox files are apps; a workspace `.html` file is a page unless a shelf record proves it is that app (`workspacePath` match, or byte-identical shelf copy for pre-change records, with the slug no longer granting identity). The room's Mini-App tray renders only apps and no longer scrapes every `.html` row out of the Files list. `saveMiniApp`/`deleteMiniApp` carry the same field; docs and tests updated in the same change.
WHY: Every `.html` file counted as a mini-app, so the tray filled with pages as soon as you browsed a folder of them — the list Paul called unmanageable — and an unrelated page that shared a slug with a shelf app inherited that app's identity.
EFFECT: The Mini-Apps tray lists what you saved (plus shelf and sandbox apps); a bare HTML page stays in the Files list and opens as an app from the File Viewer's "Open as Mini-App" or by name. Saving a page turns it into an app on the next discovery, and an older server payload without `kind` still renders exactly as before.
