title: tests/permission-policy.test.mjs:75 is wall-clock-racy (80ms deadline vs setImmediate) and can fail the FULL gate on any tree
description:
P2 review-finding from read-only investigator `voicebox-inv-perm-race` (dispatched by coord 2026-10-12 09:35).

FACT: the FULL gate failure on merger union a8fa807 / tree 1ab88417 is a WALL-CLOCK RACE inside `tests/permission-policy.test.mjs`, not a ymu6 defect and not a product bug. It can (and did) fail the full gate on a tree whose permission-policy/acp-client/test blobs are byte-identical to main's base.

EVIDENCE (commands + output)

1. Cached gate verdict, /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/1ab88417985d8b45203d7393a08e42edaedac82c.json:
   state=FAIL kind=full tree=1ab88417 sha=a8fa807 rc=1 secs=52
   tail: `AssertionError 0 !== 1 at tests/permission-policy.test.mjs:75:10`
   plus: "generated asynchronous activity after the test ended ... ACP 'session/prompt' timed out after 15000ms"
   626 tests, 615 pass, 1 fail, duration_ms 44305.

2. SAME TREE, fast gate PASS 616/0/10 in ~33s (ymu6 comment 2026-10-12T08:57:36Z, tree 1ab88417).
   The failing file was NOT a changed file, so the fast lane never ran it. Conclusion: the full unit run is where this surfaces; the flake is latent on main.

3. Base/tip blobs identical (git rev-parse on this checkout):
   tests/permission-policy.test.mjs base cc37470 = tip 62dc22a = 1714c68dacb499a75e12bd26ea27f9e3fc87e4af
   lib/permission-policy.mjs      = a2fb17b6e17fa363303cbb8f3b6b0844dcc471f5 (identical)
   lib/acp-client.mjs             = f83787925245cb5662b3b85ddcad15182bfd76b2 (identical)
   merge-base(cc37470,62dc22a)=cc37470; union a8fa807 tree == author tip tree.

4. Mechanism, from the code as it is:
   - tests/permission-policy.test.mjs:47 creates `createPermissionPolicy({ timeoutMs: 80 })`.
   - :74 `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))`; :75 `assert.equal(policy.pending().length, 1)`.
   - lib/permission-policy.mjs decide(): registers the record, then `setTimeout(..., Math.max(1, expiresAt - now()))` = ~80ms; on fire it sets reason `unattended-expired` and `pendingRequests.delete(requestId)`.
   - lib/acp-client.mjs:164-184 decidePermission(): validates, then `verdict = await decide(asked)` — decide() runs synchronously inside the mock's `queueMicrotask` reply, so the record IS registered before any timer; the ONLY way `pending()` can be 0 at :75 is the 80ms deadline having already fired.
   - In one libuv iteration the timers phase runs BEFORE the check phase (setImmediate). If the process's loop is starved for >=80ms after registration (full unit run = 626 tests across parallel child processes on a 2-vCPU host), the 80ms timer fires first and removes the record; setImmediate then observes 0 -> the exact `0 !== 1`.

5. BOUNDED RED-BEFORE CONTROL (single focused run, /tmp, no repo edit; query only permission-policy.mjs which is pure node builtins):
   $ node /tmp/perm-race-control.mjs
     pending().length after setImmediate = 0 | elapsed_ms = 130
     after expiry: history reason = unattended-expired | pending = 0
   The script registers via `policy.decide(asked)`, stalls the loop 120ms (>80ms), then awaits setImmediate — reproduces the gate's `0 !== 1` signature with `unattended-expired` provenance.

NON-VACUOUS, EVENT-DRIVEN INVARIANT TO ASSERT (the fix shape; NOT implemented here)

- The security invariant is time-independent and must be asserted from the terminal record: the delegate's answer is ALWAYS `{outcome:{outcome:"cancelled"}}`, never `selected`/allow, and `policy.history().at(-1).reason === "unattended-expired"`. That holds no matter how the loop is scheduled.
- The transient "it is pending" state must be observed from the policy's own synchronous `onPending` callback (createPermissionPolicy already accepts `onPending`/`onSettled`), i.e. `await new Promise(r => { policy = createPermissionPolicy({timeoutMs:80, onPending:r, onSettled:...}) })` or capture the record in onPending (called synchronously inside decide(), strictly before the timer can fire). Then await settlement via `onSettled` / the decide() promise instead of `setTimeout(120)`.
- Never read `pending()` (or any wall-clock-polled state) after an `await` when a real deadline of the same magnitude is armed. Keep `timeoutMs: 80` only if the observation is event-ordered; otherwise drive expiry by event, not sleep.
- RED-before for the fix: the existing `0 !== 1` under a >timeout stall (control above) must go green, and the four focused permission tests must stay green.

UNCERTAINTY (what is NOT established)

a) I did not run the real test file from this worktree (no node_modules / TS loader for `core/tasks.ts`), so the actual stall duration inside the merger's 52s run is inferred from the mechanism + the 44.3s/626-test load, not witnessed. The mechanism itself is confirmed in isolation.
b) Whether this file has failed any earlier full gate on main was not searched (only two commits touch it: e0b4a99 feat, c94d728 adapter contract).
c) No claim that the full gate now passes, and no requeue of the cached failing tree: this bead is the repair, gated before ymu6 can land.

NEXT ACTION (one): an implementer lane (not the ymu6 author) makes tests/permission-policy.test.mjs event-ordered per the invariant above — no sleep increase, no deadline bump alone — then runs the focused file plus one full `fleet-check` on the new tree; ymu6's landing waits on that tip.

Owner: voicebox-coord to route (proposed implementer: a lane that is not voicebox-audioflake). No code was modified, no branch created and no cached verdict re-run by this investigator.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
v25a STAGE 1: COLD-START IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF. Read-only; no source edits, no branch. Fresh main 13b4c76. Every claim below was re-checked against the file; where a mapping number did not reconcile I say so rather than repeat it.

## 1. WHAT THE CLUSTER IS (verified, not taken on trust)
`public/fused.js` is 6937 lines and is loaded as an ES MODULE (index.html:32). It already imports from ./debug-transcript.js, ./window-manager.mjs and ./theme.mjs, so the extraction is a module-to-module move, not a classic-script seam. The correct precedent is public/theme.mjs (named exports + initTheme(ui = {}) taking its DOM dependencies), NOT environment-root.js / environment-dialogs.js, which are page-local classic scripts for the standalone Environment page.

Boundaries verified by reading each line: plainCaps 1775-1786, extRow 1788-1814, extSection 1816-1826, extensionApproval 1837-1954, openManageExt 1958-1994, renderExtensions 2066-2195, event wiring 3904-3976 and 3979+, plus one installLightDismissFallback(els.exts) call and the extension element refs in the WANTED block.

## 2. LINE REDUCTION - AND A NUMBER I COULD NOT RECONCILE
The eight named ranges I verified sum to 477 lines. Adding the element refs (~25) and the light-dismiss call (1) gives roughly 500 lines out of 6937, i.e. about 7%, not the 8.7% / 602 lines proposed during mapping. The proposed figure does not reconcile with its own ranges, so I am reporting the number I measured (477 in the eight spans) and treating the reduction as ~500 lines / ~7% until Stage 2 counts it exactly on the real cut. Anyone quoting 602 should re-count.
The ranges are not contiguous - e.g. the block that begins at 3979 (extManageClose) runs past 4047, where the file has moved on to unrelated code about a heading tooltip. A cut at a guessed boundary would take unrelated code with it, so the first Stage 2 step is to fix exact end lines per block rather than trust the ranges above.

## 3. DOM (disjoint from every other surface)
Dialog #exts plus trigger/closer #exts-open / #exts-close / #exts-count / #ext-note; seven list containers #ext-shelf, #ext-running, #ext-failed, #ext-waiting, #ext-present, #ext-refused, #ext-catalogue; create form #ext-create-form and its five fields; manage dialog #ext-manage-dialog and its ~14 fields including hidden #ext-manage-id, #ext-manage-mode, #ext-manage-token. Classes .env-item/.env-head/.env-dot/.env-label/.env-empty/.ext-*, plus details.ext-plan[data-plan-state]. No id is shared with another surface. The one cross-surface reader is fused.js:220, the ?open=extensions URL router calling els.extsOpen - that ref must stay in fused.js or be exported.

## 4. STATE - THE ONE REAL COUPLING
openPlanIds (line 1831), planCache (1835) and lastRunningExtensions (1956) are strictly owned by this cluster; only extensionApproval(), renderExtensions() and the manage-delete handler touch them, and they exist to survive the 20s health poll without flicker (voicebox-beads-ujay). Move them wholesale.
lastToolStatus is NOT owned by this cluster and is the extraction's single genuine coupling. Verified sites: defined 1998, READ in renderExtensions 2141, WRITTEN by window.__voiceboxOnToolCalls 5646-5647, guarded at 5685, and a second, unrelated lastToolStatus: new Map() property at 6223 (a different object - do not merge them). So the module must NOT reach for this global. Pass a getToolStatus(name) accessor into the init call, or export a recordToolCallStatus() for fused.js to call on each frame. This is the boundary that decides whether the cut is clean, and it is the one thing a cold-start editor could plausibly get wrong.

## 5. NETWORK, MODAL AND CRUD (all first-party, all CSP-clean today)
GET /api/extensions, /api/extensions/catalogue, /api/extensions/proposals/:id/plan; POST /api/extensions/approve, /refuse, /sideload, /local, /reconfigure; DELETE /api/extensions/:id. The manage form is the only place that reads <meta name="voicebox-session-token"> and attaches x-voicebox-session-token (+ optional x-voicebox-host-token) - an auth path that must move with the handler or the extraction breaks reconfiguration and removal. Zero innerHTML (textContent only), zero timers, zero localStorage. Refresh is driven externally: health() at 2386, the propose_extension verb at 3392-3397, the URL router at 220, form submits, and the WebSocket tool-call hook at 5685.

## 6. PROPOSED MODULE INTERFACE (theme.mjs shape, single owner)
export plainCaps, extRow, extSection, renderExtensions({ getToolStatus, request, els }), openManageExt(els, ext, mode), and one entry point initExtensionsUI({ els, request, on, installLightDismissFallback, getToolStatus }) which is the ONLY place listeners are attached. fused.js keeps the imports and the five call sites it already owns (health, the propose verb, the URL router, the WebSocket hook) and passes its existing request/on/installLightDismissFallback helpers in rather than re-implementing them - that is also what keeps the ymu6 extraction from duplicating them.
CSP/theme/import-timing: no inline handlers are added, all listeners stay addEventListener via the passed `on`, form submits keep preventDefault + fetch, and the module is imported by fused.js so it inherits module ordering. NO pre-paint or FOUC sensitivity: this UI lives entirely inside modal dialogs, so unlike theme-boot.js it needs no classic boot script. Confirmed against the MWG guides that bear on it (declarative-dialog-popover-control, light-dismiss-a-dialog, accessibility, html): the extraction must preserve the native <dialog> semantics and focus return, which the existing code already does via showModal/close and a focus restore on close - the interface should keep those in the module, not split them.

## 7. TEST PLAN (focused, non-vacuous)
Existing browser-tier coverage is real and already targets this surface: tests/extensions-ui.test.mjs (396 lines), tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs (335), tests/wasm-room-ui.test.mjs (65), tests/modal-panels.test.mjs (254). They run in the browser tier, which the fast unit gate does not execute - so Stage 2 must run them focused, and the merger's union gate is what covers them at landing. Backend tests (extensions-route-seam, extensions, extensions-create, extension-approval) are unit tier and stay untouched.
Negative control, evidenced now rather than asserted: driving the real UI in Chromium at 13b4c76, clicking #exts-open opens #exts (count text "Extensions - 0 running - 0 waiting"; the seven sections render, six as empty placeholders and the catalogue with 4 real entries; 10 li rows total). Then, with NO source edit, I detached the trigger's listeners at runtime and re-drove the same assertion: the dialog did not open (open=false), so the open-path assertion FAILS without the wiring. That is the non-vacuous negative mutant for Stage 2 - break the init wiring, the browser test must go red. Note honestly: rows stayed at 10 after the mutation, so the ROW assertions alone would not catch a broken open path; the assertion that bites is the dialog-open one.

## 8. SHARED SURFACE WITH ymu6 - AND THE SINGLE-WRITER RULE
Overlap is real but narrow. Shared helpers both extractions need: request (1074), installLightDismissFallback (4255), on (148) - pass them in, do not duplicate. Shared container classes .envs/.settings-modal but no shared form elements: #ext-manage-dialog reconfigures extension host bounds and revocation, #settings handles providers, vision, FPS, thinking, PTT, debug. Zero shared state. The collision is structural: both cut into fused.js, both touch WANTED (35-133), both touch dialog wiring in the 3900-4800 region and the light-dismiss calls at 4265-4269.
So: exactly ONE fused.js writer at a time. ymu6 must not start until v25a has landed, and the safest sequencing is that whichever extraction lands second rebases onto the first rather than the two sharing a branch. If Stage 2 finds that the WANTED block or the light-dismiss calls cannot be split cleanly, that is a signal to extract the shared helpers into a small util module FIRST and land that alone - one writer, three small landings, instead of two branches fighting over the same lines.

## 9. NEXT ACTION (one)
Fix exact per-block end lines on fresh main and produce the cut list (module contents, exports, and the five fused.js call sites plus the pass-through helpers), i.e. the cold-start file-level plan with no code written. Then hold for coord's Stage 2 GO - this bead does not implement, and no fused.js writer is authorised while it is open.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
v25a STAGE 1 FOLLOW-UP: EXACT CUT LIST. Read-only, fresh main 13b4c76, no browser rerun. Boundaries read line by line; where a proposed number was wrong I say so.

## A. MOVES to public/extensions-ui.mjs (exact, contiguous)
  1775-1786   plainCaps(declared, bounds)
  1788-1814   extRow({name, dotState, stateText, detail, disclose})
  1816-1826   extSection(listEl, rows, emptyText)
  1828-1836   the two explanatory comments + openPlanIds (1831) + planCache (1835)   <- cluster state, moves with it
  1837-1954   extensionApproval(id)                                     (118 lines)
  1956        let lastRunningExtensions = []                            <- cluster state
  1958-1994   openManageExt(ext, mode = "reconfigure")
  2066-2195   renderExtensions()                                        (130 lines)
  3902-3903   the dialog comment ("open like settings: showModal() ... focus returned to the trigger")
  3904-3915   on(els.extsOpen|extsClose) + the dialog's close handler (focus restore, aria-expanded)
  3916-3977   on(els.extCreateForm, "submit") - full create/stage-later flow
  3979-3986   extManageClose + installLightDismissFallback(els.extManageDialog) at 3980 + extManageDelete
  3988-4046   on(els.extManageForm, "submit") - reconfigure/remove, incl. the session+host token auth path
  Sum of the named function/block spans is 477 lines; with the comments and state lines above the
  contiguous cut is ~490. NOT 602, and NOT 8.7%.

## B. STAYS in fused.js - and the two places a range-based cut would damage it
  50-69       the els element refs, INCLUDING exts/extsOpen/extShelf/extManage* -- all 20 lines stay.
              Reason: fused.js:220 (the ?open=extensions router) calls els.extsOpen and 5685 reads
              els.extShelf. The map proposed deleting these; they are pass-through inputs, not dead.
  1996-2000   the comment plus `const lastToolStatus = new Map()` -- THE COUPLING. Stays.
  2002-...    sqehArtifactChip -- NOT cluster code. It sits inside the proposed 1958-2065 span, so a
              range cut there would have silently moved an unrelated function. That span is 1958-1994.
  2196+       renderEnvironments -- unrelated; renderExtensions ends exactly at 2195.
  4047-4061   the envs-help tooltip/panel block -- unrelated. The manage handler ends at 4046 (`});`);
              4047 is a COMMENT about envs-help. The proposed 4047 endpoint was one line into code that stays.
  4063+       envsOpen wiring -- unrelated.
  4255-4264   installLightDismissFallback -- the shared helper itself. Stays.
  4265-4269   the five page-level calls, including installLightDismissFallback(els.exts).
  Note the asymmetry: the shared helper is called TWICE for this cluster, once inside (3980, the manage
  dialog) and once outside (4265, the #exts dialog) in a five-call bootstrap list shared with envs/
  settings/harnesses/changelog. Simplest correct split: the list at 4265-4269 stays in fused.js
  untouched (it is a page bootstrap over els, which fused.js still owns), and the module calls it only
  for its own manage dialog. Alternative if you prefer one owner: the module exports installExtLightDismiss(els)
  and fused.js calls both. Either is one line of difference; I do not need a shared util for it.

## C. CROSS-MODULE STATE (both directions)
  READ (module needs it, stays owned by fused.js):
    lastToolStatus -- getToolStatus(name) accessor passed into the init call, or an exported
    recordToolCallStatus(name, status) that fused.js's websocket hook (5646-5647) calls. The accessor
    MUST be live: a snapshot captured at init would freeze the latency readout. See the mutant in E.
    els -- the 30+ extended element refs, passed in, never re-queried by the module.
  WRITE (module exports, fused.js calls):
    renderExtensions() at exactly three kept sites: 2386 (health poll), 3393 (propose_extension verb),
    5685 (websocket tool-call hook, guarded by lastToolStatus.size && els.extShelf?.isConnected).
    Plus the URL router at 220, which calls els.extsOpen.click() and so exercises the module's listener.
  Everything else in the cluster's 13 renderExtensions() hits (1912 comment, 2178 internal, 3908/3968/
  4015/4036 inside moved handlers) moves with the module.

## D. BOOT / IMPORT ORDERING
  index.html:32 loads fused.js as type="module"; the module graph is evaluated in order, before
  DOMContentLoaded, and fused.js already imports ./theme.mjs, ./window-manager.mjs, ./debug-transcript.js.
  So extensions-ui.mjs is imported the same way and its functions are defined before fused.js's top-level
  listener block runs. initExtensionsUI({...}) REPLACES that top-level block at 3902-4046 verbatim - the
  ordering does not change, it just moves one file to the left. The only top-level statements the module
  gains are the installLightDismissFallback call for its own manage dialog. NO pre-paint/FOUC exposure:
  the whole surface lives inside <dialog> elements, unlike theme-boot.js, so no classic boot script and no
  parity test are needed. CSP unchanged: no inline handlers, listeners stay addEventListener, forms keep
  preventDefault+fetch, and the token path reads the same meta tag.
  DOM OWNERSHIP: all ext*/exts* ids and .env-*/.ext-* classes are disjoint from every other surface
  (checked); the only external reader is the URL router noted in C.

## E. FOCUSED TESTS AND THE TWO-PART MUTANT
  test:file -- tests/extensions-ui.test.mjs (396 lines), tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs (335),
  tests/wasm-room-ui.test.mjs (65), tests/modal-panels.test.mjs (254). All four are BROWSER tier, so
  `fleet-check --fast` (unit lane) does not run them - Stage 2 must run them as a focused browser job,
  and the merger's full union gate is what covers them at landing. Expected wall time: I did NOT measure
  these four individually and will not quote a fabricated number. Basis: the whole browser tier measures
  114.5s wall at 4-way shard on this VM (from the hhkg landing). Four files, two of them small, are a
  fraction of the tier - low tens of seconds - but that is an estimate, not a measurement.
  MUTANT (fails if either wiring is wrong):
    (1) listener init omitted -- ALREADY EVIDENCED with no source edit: driving the real UI in Chromium
        at 13b4c76, clicking #exts-open opens the dialog (7 sections, 10 rows, 4 catalogue entries);
        after detaching the trigger's listeners at runtime the dialog does NOT open. So the open-path
        assertion is non-vacuous. Caveat recorded honestly: the row count stayed at 10 after the
        mutation, so row assertions alone would NOT catch a broken open path - the dialog-open
        assertion is the one that bites.
    (2) stale status accessor -- NEW, and the reason the accessor boundary matters. Mutate
        getToolStatus to return a snapshot captured at init instead of reading the live map. The
        websocket tool hook then updates lastToolStatus but the WASM-shelf latency readout does not
        move. tests/wasm-room-ui.test.mjs already asserts a latency string in #ext-shelf, so the
        required shape for Stage 2 is: drive a tool call AFTER init and assert the readout updates,
        then the snapshot mutation must turn it RED. Without that, an extraction that passes the
        accessor by value would look green while the feature is silently frozen.

## F. COHESION VERDICT (coord asked for one)
  ~490 contiguous lines move as ONE module with no shared util needed and no global moved:
  the three shared helpers (request, on, installLightDismissFallback) are PASSED IN, not extracted;
  the single cross-module datum (lastToolStatus) crosses by accessor, not by relocation; the els map is
  pass-through. The only genuine sharp edges are the ones recorded above - the two overrun boundaries
  (1958-1994 not 1958-2065; 4046 not 4047), the els refs staying put, and the live-accessor mutant -
  and each is a boundary choice, not a reason to shrink the slice.
  I am not proposing a smaller slice and I am not proposing a shared util. If you disagree on either,
  the smaller slice I would recommend instead is just the three DOM builders plus renderExtensions
  (1775-1826 + 2066-2195, ~190 lines) landing first, with the approval/manage handlers in a second
  landing - but I think that costs an extra review and an extra gate for no correctness gain.

## NEXT ACTION (one)
Approve or reject this cut list. On approval the Stage 2 branch is: create public/extensions-ui.mjs with
the exports and initExtensionsUI({els, request, on, installLightDismissFallback, getToolStatus}), move
A verbatim, add the live-accessor update path, and wire fused.js's three kept call sites - as the ONLY
fused.js writer, with ymu6 still blocked until this lands.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
EXTRACTION WRITTEN (not yet verified). public/extensions-ui.mjs created; public/fused.js 6937 -> 6462 lines.

MEASURED, and it matches the prediction: the awk reports kept 6446, skipped 491 of 6937. Cut list predicted ~490, so the cut held against the real file. Net fused.js reduction 475 lines (491 skipped minus the 3-line import and the 13-line init call).

VERIFIED AFTER THE EDIT: all six cluster functions are gone from fused.js (plainCaps, extRow, extSection, extensionApproval, openManageExt, renderExtensions); sqehArtifactChip is still there (8 refs) - it was the function the proposed 1958-2065 span would have swallowed; lastToolStatus is still defined in fused.js once; installLightDismissFallback and its five page-level calls are untouched; renderExtensions() has exactly 3 call sites in fused.js (health, the propose_extension verb, the websocket hook); the URL router at 220 still reads els.extsOpen. The tail of the file survived.

NEAR-MISS I HAVE TO REPORT, because it is exactly the class of error this bead is about. My first awk used a chain of keep-conditions joined by ||, with the last one inverted. It kept the 3902-4046 block it was supposed to delete and DELETED EVERYTHING FROM 4047 TO THE END - 2891 lines of unrelated code, gone. And node --check PASSED on the mutilated file, because a truncated file is still valid JavaScript. Syntax checking is not a completeness check. I caught it on the next grep (import of a file that had no init call, count 6937 -> 3696 instead of ~6300) and restored from a copy taken before the edit. The rewrite uses an explicit positive range list in a named skipped() function, and the awk now reports kept/skipped counts so the arithmetic is visible: 6449 kept + 491 skipped = 6937.

STATUS: IN_PROGRESS. Focused browser gate dispatched against the edited tree - the four baseline files. Docs, the two negative controls, the measured speed figure and the reviewer all still to come.

title: sv2n fixes 1 of 6 placeholders on environment.html; 5 still render UA grey at 4.34:1/3.87:1 (public/environment.css:124)
description:
Reviewed voicebox-beads-sv2n delta 83e15ff..6bc6956 (6bc6956 = 6bc6956efacc547e01b95d4945b333542877778a), branch fleet/shard-sv2n.
Repro: node /tmp/rev-sv2n-probe.mjs on 6bc6956 (startServer + launch from tests/lib; enumerates document.querySelectorAll('[placeholder]') on /environment.html, reads getComputedStyle(el,'::placeholder').color vs the input background, both prefers-color-scheme values).
Observed (light / dark): #asset-name 5.76 / 6.45 (fixed). #project-name, #machine-path, #machine-host-token, #root-path, #asset-body (textarea): all rgb(117,117,117) on --input-bg = 4.34 / 3.87. Same UA grey, same ground, same failure the bead was filed for.
Expected: the bead's title claims the PAGE's placeholder contrast is below the floor; the fix (and README/docs 07 wording 'lifts the placeholder') targets only #asset-name, so closing sv2n leaves 5 of 6 page placeholders failing the same 4.5:1 floor. The original description's 'one pair, not a palette-wide problem' measured only #asset-name.
Fix shape: the selector, not the value - e.g. '::placeholder { color: var(--muted); }' (all inputs/textarea share --input-bg via environment.css:39-40), and extend the ui-ux-accessibility assertion to every [placeholder] element in both schemes so it can see the other five. Update the xggy.3 parity baseline/README/docs wording to match.
Evidence: /tmp/rev-sv2n-probe.mjs output (table in reviewer verdict comment on voicebox-beads-sv2n).
Fix owner: voicebox-shard
close_reason: FIXED on the landed tree. LANDED as 46eb676 (merge of fleet/shard-sv2n); author tip edf1bac is an ancestor of origin/main. Verified in the landed tree, not on the branch: public/environment.css carries '::placeholder { color: var(--muted); }' and the old '#asset-name::placeholder' selector is gone (grep returns 0). All six placeholder fields on the page - project-name, machine-path, machine-host-token, root-path, asset-name, asset-body - measure rgb(89,99,109) = 5.76:1 light and rgb(154,154,171) = 6.45:1 dark, from the user agent's rgb(117,117,117) = 4.34:1 / 3.87:1. The accessibility assertion now enumerates every [placeholder] element in both schemes, with a guard that at least six were found, so it cannot pass by matching nothing. Removing the rule makes it report '6 of 6 placeholders are below 4.5:1' where the pre-fix assertion could see one element.

title: Create-project dialog loses a click made before the deferred ui.ts module loads (environment.html:260 -> browser/ui/ui.ts:729)
description:
The create-project dialog opener is wired by a **deferred module**, so a click made before that module loads is silently lost — the same class as `voicebox-beads-aenb`, but on the page's primary action, and NOT recoverable by the `aenb` init-apply trick (a click leaves no state to re-apply, unlike a search box value).

**Measured at `2e88a4c` on a real server and browser** (read-only probe, technique from `xggy.1`: `Fetch.enable` holds the request at the request stage so the document is usable without the file):

```
click while module held : {"ready":"interactive","open":false}
after module loaded     : {"open":false} -> the earlier click was LOST
a second click now      : {"open":true}  -> the module IS attached, so only the first click was missed
```

**Root cause:** `public/environment.html:260` loads `<script type="module" src="/browser/ui/ui.ts">`, and `browser/ui/ui.ts:729` is what wires `$("create-project")` to `dialog.showModal()`. A `type="module"` script is deferred by definition, so between the document becoming interactive and the module finishing there is a window in which the button is inert and gives no feedback. The second click in the probe proves the module works — only the interaction it missed is lost.

**Pre-existing, not caused by this fleet's work:** `browser/ui/ui.ts` is untouched by the `xggy.1` delta (`539c8b1..2e88a4c` touches help.html, help-search.js, server.mjs, two test files, and the docs/README), and the dialog markup carries only `aria-haspopup="dialog"` / `aria-controls`, which do not open it.

**Fix directions, for whoever takes it:**
1. Deferring is what creates the window, so either the opener runs during parsing (a classic, non-deferred script — the reasoning and the acceptance for that choice are worked out on `voicebox-beads-xggy.2`) or the platform owns the interaction.
2. The platform option is the one Modern Web Guidance recommends, guide `declarative-dialog-popover-control` (retrieved 2026-10-12): "Use the Invoker Commands API to toggle the visibility of `<dialog>` and `[popover]` elements directly from HTML buttons, eliminating the need for custom JavaScript event listeners", whose stated benefit is exactly the property this defect lacks — it "ensures interactions are functional immediately upon HTML parsing". That is `<button commandfor="create-project-dialog" command="show-modal">` plus `command="close"` on the close button. Its Baseline status is **Newly available** (2025-12-12; Chrome/Edge 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2), and the same guide's fallback section says polyfills are mandatory for older browsers, so it is a direction with a fallback obligation rather than a drop-in.
3. Not in scope anywhere yet, and deliberately not bundled into `xggy.2`, which must not touch `browser/ui/ui.ts`.

Verified against origin/main content, not the merge message: the classic opener tag is present with no defer/async/module on either loader, ui.ts no longer binds create-project, the aenb init-apply is intact in help-search.js, and the page carries 0 inline script blocks. comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
STAGE 1 READ-ONLY DESIGN — no files edited, no branch, no commit. Worktree clean; `xggy.2`'s branch stays frozen while the merger has it, and `5tv3` touches the same file (`environment.html`), so nothing here is implemented until that lands.

## What is actually broken, measured at `e5764df` on a real server and browser
Technique is deterministic rather than timing-shaped: `Fetch.enable` holds `/browser/ui/ui.ts` at the request stage, so the document is usable with none of that module's handlers attached.

| interaction (module held) | state at activation | opened then | opened after load | second activation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mouse click on "Create a project" | `interactive` | **no** | **no — lost** | **yes** |
| keyboard Enter, button focused | `interactive` | **no** | **no — lost** | **yes** |
| control, module loaded | — | — | yes | — |

So the window is not mouse-specific: **a keyboard activation is dropped too**, and neither is replayed when the module arrives. The second activation working is what proves the module is fine and only the first interaction is lost.

## Why "just add `commandfor`" is not a drop-in: the opener does three things
`browser/ui/ui.ts:729-740`: (1) resets `#dest-status` — hide it, clear the text, delete `dataset.ok` — because "a stale refusal next to a fresh dialog would describe an act nobody just made"; (2) `showDestination(chosen?.value ?? "opfs")` so the dialog and its radios cannot disagree; (3) `createDialog?.showModal()`. And the helpers are shared with the module's submit handlers (`dialogStatus` 553/659/678, `closeCreateDialog` 563/667/693/793, `showDestination` 745), so the opener cannot move without deciding who owns them.

## Where the window comes from
`environment.html:260` loads `type="module" src="/browser/ui/ui.ts"`; a module is deferred by definition, so the page is interactive before any of its handlers exist. The opener has no other owner: `#create-project` carries only `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-controls`, so the browser has nothing to do on its own.

## Options, with the costs stated rather than implied
**(A) Early classic opener — recommended.** A small same-origin classic script at the end of `<body>` owns the dialog's DOM surface: open (all three steps), close, status. `ui.ts`'s click binding is then REMOVED, so there is exactly one owner — otherwise `showModal()` runs twice on an open dialog and throws `InvalidStateError`. The module keeps its submit handlers and calls the surface it no longer owns through a documented namespaced seam, the pattern the repo already uses for `window.__voiceboxOpenAgentTracker`.
- It is the technique just landed in `xggy.2`: classic end-of-body runs while parsing, so no interaction can precede the listener. No new idea, no new dependency.
- Acceptance is the same deterministic guard: hold the file, require the document NOT to be interactive, and fail if the tag gains `defer`/`async`/`type="module"`.
- Accessibility unchanged: same `showModal()` focus trap, same `aria-haspopup`/`aria-controls` (the correct dialog-opener pattern), CSS untouched so the focus ring is untouched.

**(B) Declarative invoker commands** (`commandfor="create-project-dialog" command="show-modal"`). The browser owns the open, which the guide says makes it "functional immediately upon HTML parsing" — on supporting browsers the interaction cannot be missed at all, and focus/expanded state are managed natively.
- Honest cost, from that same guide: Baseline **Newly available** (2025-12-12), the polyfill (`invokers-polyfill`) is mandatory for older browsers, and "DO NOT unconditionally load the polyfill" — feature-detect `'commandForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype` and "Do NOT check the window or document object". The guide's CDN option is unusable here: a cross-origin import would violate the `script-src 'self'` policy this whole line of work prepares for, so the polyfill would have to be **vendored into `public/`** — a new third-party file to maintain — plus a `command` listener **on the target element** because "the native 'command' event does not bubble", plus the state-reset hook, plus a `TODO(baseline/...)` comment per the project's rules.
- It fails differently and softer: on a supporting browser with no JS yet the dialog OPENS but the status reset has not run, so a stale refusal could show briefly — degraded, not dead.
- Accessibility gain over (A) is smaller than it looks: both rely on `showModal()`'s focus trap, and `aria-expanded` is not required on a dialog opener when `aria-haspopup="dialog"` is present.

**(C) Hybrid** — (B) for the open plus (A)'s early file for the fallback and state: most machinery of the three, worth it only if the platform direction is wanted now.

**Recommendation: (A)**, with (B) written into the docs as the future platform-native direction so the eventual move is informed.

## What the fix must carry
- Deterministic readiness: hold the file, document must not be interactive; `defer`/`async`/module mutant RED.
- All three opener effects: stale status hidden, destination panels matching the checked radio, and the modal actually open.
- The keyboard path driven with real input (`Input.dispatchKeyEvent`), because that is the path lost today.
- Close paths unchanged: the close button, Esc, `closedby="any"` click-outside.
- Submit paths and the server refusal vocabulary still intact through the module.
- Accessibility station once (this is a UI change), docs and README in the same change.

## Open questions for coord
1. Approve (A), or do you want (B) with a vendored polyfill?
2. Scope: the create-project opener only. The same window also covers the module's other handlers — the drop-zone paths, the form submits, and the async gate that opens `#confirm` — but reaching those takes more preconditions than one click, so I propose noting them rather than widening this bead.
3. If (A): `public/environment-dialogs.js` as the name, and a namespaced global for the seam rather than duplicating the helpers.

## Skills, before any edit
Modern Web Guidance consulted: the `security` guide for the CSP line, and `declarative-dialog-popover-control` retrieved verbatim for (B)'s exact idiom. Craft floor read at `reference/craft-floor.md`; the skill's launcher is still absent, so per its own instruction I am stating that context loading did not run and read the reference directly. Its directly relevant line is "States: hover, disabled, loading, error, empty … plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus" — a keyboard activation that does nothing is exactly that failing. One honest note against the incumbent design rather than this bead: the floor's "A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus" refuses modals like this one; it is a three-destination chooser with a form and a protected-focus submit, and relitigating the pattern is not this bead.

## Precondition
No edits until `xggy.2` lands, so that `environment.html`'s tail is stable and there is never a simultaneous same-file edit.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
STAGE 1 ADDENDUM — the assignment comment asks for the exact plan and its **negative controls**, and my design listed the tests without naming them as controls. Here they are, each one a way the fix can be wrong rather than a way it can be right. No edits made; nothing is implemented until `xggy.2` lands.

## Negative controls (each must FAIL when the fix is absent or regressed)
1. **No early owner — blocked file.** Block the early file entirely, so it never runs: the page *is* interactive, a click and an Enter with focus do **nothing**, and the dialog stays closed. This is the control that stops the suite passing on a page whose script never ran. (Distinct from the held-file guard below, which is a different failure.)
2. **No early owner — the tag stops being able to win the race.** Hold the file at the request stage and require the document NOT to have become interactive. Adding `defer`, `async` or `type="module"` must turn this RED in the browser **and** in the unit-lane structural guard — the same pair that guards `public/environment-root.js` today, reused rather than reinvented.
3. **A second owner of project create — coord's constraint, made observable.** `showModal()` on an already-open dialog throws `InvalidStateError`, so if `ui.ts`'s click binding were left in place alongside the early one, a single click after the module loads would fire both handlers and raise. The control captures uncaught page errors from document-start and asserts the dialog is open with **no** exception — so "no second owner" is asserted, not just intended.
4. **The three opener effects.** (a) With a stale refusal visible in `#dest-status`, opening must hide it — if the reset were dropped, the stale text is still there. (b) With a non-default radio checked (the `machine` destination), opening must show the matching panel and hide the others — if the sync were dropped, the radio and the panel disagree, which is precisely what the existing comment says must not happen. (c) The dialog is actually open.
5. **The keyboard path, RED-before.** Real `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` on the focused button. Today this is measurably lost (see the design's table), so the test starts RED and the fix is what makes it green.
6. **Contract preserved through the module.** The submit paths and the server's refusal vocabulary are driven exactly as `xggy.2` does: the same request body is posted to the seam directly and the page's text must equal `refused: why` — `host-token-required` with no token, `param-missing`-class refusals with the fixture token, and a successful declaration confirmed through `GET /api/root`. If moving the opener broke a submit path, that comparison fails.

## Permissions and lifecycle, which the assignment also names
- **Lifecycle:** only the open path's load ORDER changes. `showModal()` still gives the focus trap, the inert background and Esc; `closedby="any"` still gives click-outside; the close button still closes; `dialogStatus` still writes inside the dialog (the `6uzd` fix, so a refusal stays readable where the person is standing) — all untouched.
- **Permissions:** the opener touches no authority. The three destinations keep their own requirements, the machine destination still supplies the host token, and the server still owns the refusal (`host-token-required` is measured, not assumed). "No second owner of project create" therefore means the create path's AUTHORITY stays exactly where it is — this change only decides who opens the dialog.

## Still open for you
1. Confirm (A) the early classic opener (my recommendation), or choose (B) declarative invoker with the polyfill vendored into `public/` — the guide's CDN route is unusable under `script-src 'self'`.
2. Confirm scope is the create-project opener, with the module's other handlers (drop-zone, submits, the async gate opening `#confirm`) noted rather than widened into this bead.
3. Confirm `public/environment-dialogs.js` and a namespaced seam rather than duplicated helpers.

comments.text:
`voicebox-beads-fl3g` FIXED at `59a184f` on `fleet/shard-5tv3` (new tip; the queue stays OFF and a fresh cross-family reviewer is running, because a moved tip voids the previous verdict).

## What the reviewer found, and it was right
After `Fetch.disable`, `document.readyState === "complete"` is satisfied BEFORE the resumed `ui.ts` finishes evaluating. So the single `change` event this test dispatched fired before the module had bound anything, went into the void, and the 15s wait timed out. The test was asserting a product behaviour it had never actually waited for — the worst kind of green, because it passed whenever the machine was fast.

## The fix, and I looked for the same class elsewhere
- The radio sync now DISPATCHES AND CHECKS THE EFFECT: the poll re-fires the change until the panel actually syncs, so it waits for the module's own observable work and cannot pass unless a listener is genuinely bound. No new sleep, no lifecycle heuristic.
- That wait doubles as this test's ready signal: once the panel has synced, the module has provably evaluated, so the module-owned controls asserted afterwards (the close button, the Enter dispatch control) are bound too.
- **The same latent race existed a second time**, in the one-owner test: its close click assumed the module had bound the close button. It now retries the close, bounded, and records what it observes. The reviewer found one instance; hunting the class found the other, which is why the file now tests for the effect rather than for readiness in both places.

## The control that makes the retry mean something
A retry loop is only as good as the thing it waits for, so a new test blocks `ui.ts` for good and fires **25 change events over a full second**: the panel must NEVER sync — while the classic opener must still open the dialog and still publish its seam. If anything other than a real listener could make the panel visible, that test fails.

## Evidence
- The reviewer's exact repro command now passes: `node --test --test-name-pattern="the create-project opener works while the deferred module is still in flight" tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs` → 1 pass / 0 fail.
- The opener tests were run **five times in a row**: 4 pass / 0 fail every time.
- The focused suite is re-running in the heavy-job queue, which is the concurrency this class of bug needs to be exercised under.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: The Environment page's "Create a project" button is wired by a classic parser-time same-origin script, `public/environment-dialogs.js`, instead of by the deferred `browser/ui/ui.ts` module, which deliberately no longer binds it so there is one owner. `ui.ts` is a module and therefore deferred, so the page became interactive with none of its handlers bound, and a click — or an Enter on the focused button — made in that window did nothing at all, with no state left behind to re-apply. The opener keeps its three effects in their original order (clear any stale refusal, open on the destination actually chosen, then `showModal`) and publishes the destination sync on `window.__voiceboxCreateProject`, which the module's radio handlers read instead of keeping a copy; closing, the status line inside the dialog and every submit and drop-zone path stay in the module, untouched.
WHAT: Both loader scripts on this page must stay classic and parser-blocking, and a unit-lane structural guard fails if either grows `defer`, `async` or `type="module"`. A click cannot be repaired after the fact the way the Help page's search filter re-applies a value already in its box: a click leaves no state to re-apply, so the only repair is never to miss the window.
WHAT: Ownership is proved by an **invocation count** — `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal` is wrapped before any page script runs, and exactly one call per activation is required, with a mutant inside the test that must move the count to two and a product-level check, binding the button again in `ui.ts`, that turned the clean tree's green into `Got [2,2,2]`. The count covers the `showModal` path only: a hypothetical duplicate that opened the dialog by some other route, `dialog.show()` for instance, is NOT covered and this change does not claim otherwise.
WHAT: The no-error canary is **kept, and is the weaker half**: it was the old proof, resting on my belief that a duplicate listener's second `showModal()` throws `InvalidStateError`, and that belief is measurably false — the second call is a silent no-op, so the canary stayed green with two owners restored. Separately, an earlier claim of mine that the keyboard path was lost rested on a dispatch that omitted `text`, so Chrome sent no keypress at all; it could not distinguish a lost click from an unarrived key, and was not evidence. The keyboard assertion now requires focus to actually land on the button, sends a real keypress, and carries a dispatch control — the same keystroke must close the dialog via the module's own button.
WHAT: The opener test no longer waits on `document.readyState`, which is satisfied before the resumed deferred module has finished evaluating, so its single `change` event used to fire into the void; it now re-dispatches until the panel genuinely syncs, waiting on the module's effect, and a control requires that with the module blocked for good no number of events ever syncs it.
WHY: `browser/ui/ui.ts` is a `type="module"` script, so it is deferred by definition and the page is interactive before it runs. A click made in that window was silently lost — measured by holding the module at the request stage — and a second activation worked, which is what proved only the first interaction was lost and the module itself was healthy. The button is the entry point to creating a project, so the person affected cannot tell a broken control from a slow one.
EFFECT: The Create-a-project button opens its dialog from the moment the page is interactive, by mouse and by keyboard, including with the module still in flight. Internally, the tests meant to prove that can now actually fail: one no longer depends on machine speed, the other no longer depends on a platform behaviour I had misremembered, and two claims this change was originally argued with were corrected rather than quietly kept.

title: Encoded trusted HTML alias bypasses report-only CSP scope (server.mjs:4385)
description:
Reviewed voicebox-beads-ul1m.1 delta 07121af..0b6e864 (0b6e8648c5b15d68800ec74dd3b65d3745a4a8e9).
Repro: export git archive 0b6e864 to /tmp; start tests/lib/server.mjs startServer; fetch(server.base + '/help.html', {redirect:'manual'}) and fetch(server.base + '/%68elp.html', {redirect:'manual'}); compare status, location, response body SHA-256, and content-security-policy-report-only.
Observed: both return HTTP 200 text/html, no Location, identical body SHA-256 16a24604bfc4f75f996496d82d54c48c46d1020cc9f2264209c7929e07f71f2a, containing help-search-input; canonical Help has Report-Only policy, encoded alias has no policy. resolvePublicFile decodes pathname but cspReportOnlyHeaders checks raw url.pathname. Thus actual trusted Help document is reachable without reporting and future enforcement with same route decision would be bypassable.
Expected: all GETs that serve one of the six trusted documents carry the staged policy (or aliases are refused/redirected canonically), without adding coverage for /apps/* or mini-app bridge.
Evidence: exact-tip independent isolated HTTP probe 2026-10-12; server.mjs:2243-2259,4382-4386. Fix owner: voicebox-shard

Policy selection now uses the resolved file (canonicalPublicPath over the resolver's contained realpath), so /%68elp.html, /help%2Ehtml and /help.html/ -- which served byte-identical Help with NO report-only header -- now carry it. Reviewed by rev-ul1m2 (gemini-3.8-flash) VERDICT PASS on 07121af..e9b3f71, findings none, independently reproduced via body SHA-256 comparison; full gate PASS on the merged tree e3bf4a34.

comments.text:
Readable repro (the issue description above rendered escaped newlines; no change to substance):
At commit 0b6e864, export the tree to a scratch directory; start tests/lib/server.mjs startServer; GET /help.html and /%68elp.html with redirect:manual. Both return HTTP 200 text/html, no Location, same response SHA-256 16a24604bfc4f75f996496d82d54c48c46d1020cc9f2264209c7929e07f71f2a. Canonical response has CSP-Report-Only; encoded response lacks it. See server.mjs:2243-2259 and :4385.
Expected: no alias of a trusted document silently bypasses reporting; preserve /apps and bridge exclusion.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
FIXED at a new tip — `0f30470` on `fleet/shard-ul1m1` (delta from the failing tip `0b6e864`), awaiting the cross-family review delta. Not closed: per coord this closes only once landed, and `onvu` blocks `ul1m.1`.

**The finding, reproduced widen than reported.** Keyed on the raw `url.pathname`, the selection agreed with the client's spelling instead of with the document served. `resolvePublicFile` decodes percent-escapes and `path.resolve` normalises, so three spellings reached the same Help document with no policy header:

    /help.html      200  header=YES  (canonical)
    /%68elp.html    200  header=no   identical body   <- the reported case
    /help%2Ehtml    200  header=no   identical body
    /help.html/     200  header=no   identical body   <- no encoding required to type

`/./help.html` and `/x/../help.html` already carried it (WHATWG normalises dot segments in `url.pathname` but never decodes), so the class was exactly "encodings and trailing slashes". Containment was never broken — `/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd`, `/../server.mjs` and `/HELP.HTML` all 404.

**The fix, in the file you named.** Policy selection is made on trusted resolved file identity after decode and containment: `canonicalPublicPath(file)` reduces the resolver's already-contained, already-realpath'd file to its public path, and `cspReportOnlyHeaders` tests that. This is the "resolve then decide" option rather than the "refuse or redirect aliases" alternative, chosen because every spelling collapses to one string by construction — patching the comparison with `decodeURIComponent` would have closed these three spellings and left the next alias live. No blanket MIME rule anywhere: it is a list of documents, not a content type.

**Verified after the fix** (`/tmp/ul1m1-alias.mjs`, and in the suite): six alias spellings all answer 200 **with** the header and byte-identical bodies; `/apps/*`, `mini-app-bridge.html`, assets and `/api` uncoverd; traversal still 404; a newly created probe document still uncovered, so "covered everywhere" cannot be satisfied by covering everything. Both new tests pass (2/2) with the alias matrix asserted POSITIVE and the traversal/case/probe cases asserted NEGATIVE; `docs-check: OK — 762 path claims`. The room is still covered now that `/` canonicalises to `/index.html`.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
ftqe FIXED, AND THIS BEAD'S PREMISE CORRECTED. New tip `d0de7c2` on `fleet/shard-uj16` (fast gate running).

## 1. The blocker (voicebox-beads-ftqe)
`help.html` now imports the shared owner: `public/help-theme.mjs` is one `import { initTheme } from "/theme.mjs"; initTheme();` — not a fourth copy, the same module the room uses. `theme-boot.js` resolves the system scheme once and so cannot do this; `theme.mjs`'s `initTheme()` installs the matchMedia listener.

Measured in a real browser:
- stored `system`, OS light -> light; **switch to dark -> dark**; switch back -> light  (was: stayed light)
- stored `dark` (explicit): stays dark across OS switches in both directions — an explicit choice does not move
- RED for this blocker: blocking `*help-theme.mjs*` reproduces it exactly — `system` + OS dark switch stays light

## 2. THE CORRECTION — the flash premise was wrong, and I had asserted it without measuring
I justified this bead as "help.html flashes because its copy applied the theme at the end of `<body>`, after the first paint". **That is false.** Measured on the EXACT pre-uj16 bytes (`git show 6b0bb89:public/help.html`, served on the real origin, first frame sampled inside the first rAF):

    pre-uj16 page, stored dark : first frame theme=dark, bg rgb(11,15,25), attribute set at 1ms, first frame at 13ms
    current page,  stored dark : first frame theme=dark, bg rgb(11,15,25)

The copy was an INLINE CLASSIC script, so it ran while the document was parsing — before the first paint. The xpwt flash came from a DEFERRED MODULE, which is a different timing, and I transferred that reasoning to a page it did not apply to.

So the honest justification for deleting the copy is DIVERGENCE, not timing: it ignored `system`, never set `data-theme-mode`, had no listener, and was a fourth hand-maintained copy no test related to the owner. My first version of this test asserted the flash and FAILED, which is how I found it.

Corrected where it was written: `docs/07`, both `help.html` comments, and the test's header. The test now ENFORCES the correction: section 4 rebuilds the pre-uj16 arrangement from the current file, measures ITS first frame, and asserts the stored choice WAS applied before the paint — so if anyone restores the flash premise, that assertion fails.

## 3. A control I wrote and then removed as flaky
With the guard blocked, whether the deferred module beats the first paint depends on cache and CPU — I measured it BOTH ways in this file's own runs (before the first frame when the module was cached; after it under load). A test that cannot control its timing must not assert an outcome, so that section now asserts the structural guarantee instead: the guard is classic with no `defer`/`async`, and the module carries `type="module"` and is therefore deferred by definition. I also tried per-request network throttling to engineer the delay; `Network.emulateNetworkConditionsByRule` did not take effect here in either rule ordering, so I removed it rather than leave a control that pretends to control something.

## 4. Gates so far
- `docs-check: OK — 14 generated blocks across 3 documents, 758 hand-written path claims`
- Focused: 26/26 under the eight-file concurrent run, and the help test passes alone twice (the previous tip's version was flaky; this one is not)
- fast gate for `d0de7c2` running; a fresh different-family reviewer-role verdict is still owed before this goes near the queue
No policy change anywhere in the diff.

title: stop_speaking is advertised and parsed but has NO consumer anywhere: 'stop speaking', 'quiet', 'mute', 'unmute' do nothing
description:
FOUND while fixing voicebox-beads-ucak (the switch_theme / open_panel vocabulary bug). Same defect class, different failure mode: ucak was a field-name mismatch, this one has no handler at all.

## The gap
The command exists end-to-end on the producer side and nowhere on the consumer side:
- lib/system-commands.mjs:65 declares it in SYSTEM_COMMAND_CATALOGUE (category audio_session, phrases "stop speaking", "quiet", "mute", "unmute") and :254 parses it into { verb: "system", command: "stop_speaking", mode: "interrupt" | "mute" | "unmute" }.
- tests/system-commands.test.mjs:23 and :122-132 assert that parse output, and they pass.
- docs/21-voice-system-commands.md documents it in the supported-command table.
- server.mjs's execute() forwards it like any other system command and special-cases only clear_activity (:2439).
- REGARDLESS: a repo-wide search for stop_speaking finds the catalogue, the parser, the tests and the docs — and NO consumer. public/fused.js's executeBrowserSystemCommand handles exactly copy, paste, switch_theme and open_panel (:212, :225, :250, :254). Nothing in public/audio-client.js, public/live-voice.js or lib/ reads it.
So "stop speaking", "quiet", "mute" and "unmute" parse, broadcast, get logged by the server as "Ran stop_speaking.", and change nothing in the room.

## Why this is worth its own bead rather than more of ucak
ucak's fix is a vocabulary correction: point the client at the field the producer already emits. This is a MISSING IMPLEMENTATION whose intended behaviour is three different things — interrupt playback, mute, and unmute — and there is no existing definition of what "mute" should do to a live audio session (gain? track? session state?), nor of how it surfaces in the UI. Inventing that under a vocabulary-repair bead would be the wrong change, so it is filed for its own dispatch.

## Primitives that already exist, so the fix looks small
The page has an audio client with stopPlayback() (public/audio-client.js:724, exported at :832), and public/fused.js:3767 already calls window.__voiceboxLiveClient.stopPlayback?.() for the device-change case. So the `interrupt` mode has an obvious implementation; `mute`/`unmute` need the decision above.

## Acceptance that would prove it fixed
Extend tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs (new in ucak) — it already drives the real path (type into #composer, wait for the turn to land in #session-log so the drive cannot be vacuous, then assert the observable UI). For stop_speaking, start playback in the page, type "stop speaking", and assert playback actually stopped; then the same for mute/unmute once their semantics are decided. Do NOT assert only the parser — the parser has been correct the whole time, which is exactly how this survived.

title: Voice system commands switch_theme and open_panel are dead at the client: parser emits mode/target, the client guards on theme/panel
description:
FOUND while scoping voicebox-beads-mvxl (the fused.js decomposition) — the theme extraction moves this code, so its browser acceptance has to cover it. BROWSER-VERIFIED, not a code-reading claim.

## The defect
There is no name agreement between the producer and the consumer of the system-command object.
- lib/system-commands.mjs (the catalogue owner) emits `mode` for switch_theme and `target` for open_panel. Driven in node: parseSystemCommand("dark mode") -> {verb:"system", command:"switch_theme", mode:"dark"}.
- lib/resolver.mjs returns that object VERBATIM (resolveTurn: `const sys = parseSystemCommand(transcript); if (sys) return sys;` at resolver.mjs:261 and :502).
- server.mjs:2427-2433 rebuilds the payload as {command, target, text, file, mode} — still `mode`/`target` — and broadcasts {type:"system_command", ...systemCommand} at :2435-2436, and returns the same object in the turn response at :2458.
- public/fused.js:242 guards `if (cmd.command === "switch_theme" && cmd.theme)` and fused.js:245 guards `if (cmd.command === "open_panel" && cmd.panel)`. Neither field is ever produced.
Both real client entry points carry the producer's shape, so BOTH are dead: fused.js:263 (the window "message" listener: `e.data.systemCommand ?? e.data`) and fused.js:3375-3377 (the turn response: `answer.systemCommand ?? result.systemCommand`).

## Browser evidence (headless Chromium, real page, script resolver, scratch workspace)
| driven shape | observed |
| real user path: turn whose text is "dark mode" | data-theme stays "light", localStorage["voicebox:theme"] stays null — NO EFFECT |
| {command:"switch_theme", mode:"dark"}   (the server's shape) | returns {ok:false}, data-theme stays "light" |
| {command:"switch_theme", theme:"dark"}  (the client's guard)  | returns {ok:true, theme:"dark"}, data-theme becomes "dark" |
| {command:"open_panel", target:"settings"} (the server's shape) | returns {ok:false}, #settings open=false |
| {command:"open_panel", panel:"settings"}  (the client's guard)  | returns {ok:true, panel:"settings"}, #settings open=true |
Probe: /tmp/theme-cmd-probe.mjs (read-only, no repo edits). The two shape pairs differ ONLY in the field name, so the field name is the cause; the turn drive shows it on the real user path.

## User-visible effect
Every voice/system command in the appearance and panel families silently does nothing: "dark mode", "light mode", "system theme", "switch to dark mode", "switch to light mode", and the open_panel phrases ("open files", "open history", "open settings", "open harnesses", "open activity log", "open agent tracker"). The commands parse, the server reports ok and records work activity ("Ran switch_theme."), and the browser does not change.

## Why nothing caught it
tests/ux-bubble-stage.test.mjs:784-785 is the ONLY place that drives the client boundary, and it drives copy and paste only. tests/system-commands.test.mjs:107-117 asserts the PARSER's output (mode) and never the client's expectation (theme) — so each side is tested against itself. The guard's own returns confirm the split: switch_theme yields {ok:false}, while a payload that never occurs yields {ok:true}.

## Fix direction — for the owner to decide, not prescribed here
One name must win. The catalogue in lib/system-commands.mjs is the declared owner of the command vocabulary, so aligning the CLIENT's two guards to `mode`/`target` keeps one computing site for the vocabulary and is the smaller diff. The alternative — have server.mjs:2427 emit `theme`/`panel` — puts the rename in the payload builder and leaves the client reading names the catalogue does not use. Do NOT paper over it with `cmd.mode || cmd.theme`: two names for one fact is what scripts/single-owner.mjs exists to prevent.

## Acceptance that would prove it fixed (and belongs in mvxl's browser acceptance either way)
A real-browser drive of the SYSTEM-COMMAND path, not the settings dialog: submit a turn whose text is "dark mode" through the script resolver and assert document.documentElement.dataset.theme === "dark" and localStorage["voicebox:theme"] === "dark"; and drive open_panel the same way, asserting the dialog actually opens. An assertion written against the PARSER cannot catch this class, because the parser was already correct.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
DELTA PIN for the reviewer-role lane: review c1db7ac..04b3e52 on branch fleet/shard-ucak (pushed). Bead voicebox-beads-ucak, P2.

THE DEFECT: the parser, the server broadcast and the POST /api/turn response have always carried `mode` for switch_theme and `target` for open_panel — the vocabulary lib/system-commands.mjs owns and docs/21 documents. public/fused.js guarded on `cmd.theme` and `cmd.panel`, which nothing ever produced, so neither branch could run: "dark mode", "light mode", "system theme", "open settings", "open files", "open history", "open agent tracker" and "close panel" all parsed, broadcast, were logged as "Ran <command>." and changed nothing.

THE FIX: read the producer's fields. Two `open_panel` targets had NO branch at all and are added, because a rename alone would have left them dead — `agent-tracker` mounts the built-in Agent Progress Tracker mini-app via the existing openAgentProgressTracker() (hoisted declaration at fused.js:4612), `close` returns the deck home via sqehSetState("deck") (:6262). No `cmd.mode || cmd.theme` fallback, deliberately: two names for one fact is what scripts/single-owner.mjs exists to prevent. The client keeps its extensions/environments/changelog targets although the catalogue does not emit them, because the window "message" listener accepts a system_command from outside the page.

EVIDENCE, and it is before/after rather than asserted: tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs is new (browser lane) and drives the REAL path — it types each command into the composer, waits for the turn to land in #session-log, then asserts observable UI and the persisted theme. Run against the pre-fix fused.js it FAILS with exactly "'dark mode' switches the page to dark — this is the whole point of the bead: 'light' !== 'dark'"; against the fix it passes. The #session-log wait is what makes the drive non-vacuous — without it a broken submit is indistinguishable from a dead command, which is how the first version of this investigation fooled itself.

comments.text:
CLOSURE CHECK on the one real behavioural risk in this move, verified independently of the reviewer lane that is also examining it.

THE RISK: the old applyTheme read els.themeSelect / els.themeSelectState / els.themeToggle from module scope on EVERY call, so it always saw the current values in the els cache. The new initTheme({themeSelect, ...}) captures the three element REFERENCES once at boot, and applyTheme reads the captured object. Those differ only if els.<those three> are ever re-assigned after boot.

EVIDENCE THAT THEY ARE NOT: const els = {} at public/fused.js:136 is filled by ONE loop over WANTED at :137-143 and never re-assigned — grep for assignments to els.<prop>, Object.assign(els, or els = finds none. The replaceChildren calls in the file (roomFoldersList, files, report) rebuild LISTS, not the theme controls, so the three nodes are never replaced either. Therefore the captured references and the live reads are the same three objects for the life of the page, and the change is behaviour-neutral. Had els been re-scanned, this would have been a real regression and the extraction would need to keep reading live.

THE ROOT FAMILY IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO DISPATCH STRUCTURES: `DELETE /api/root` (4042) and `GET /api/root` (4189) are entries inside the `const routes = {...}` table (3601), while `POST /api/root` is a branch of handle(). So "the root routes" cannot be extracted as one block without reconciling both structures — that is a design decision, not a mechanical move.
THERE IS NO /api/saveAs ROUTE. "saveAs" at server.mjs:3973-3978 is a FIELD of a request body inside turn/tool handling. Flagging it so nobody scopes a route that does not exist.

## 2. CAPTURED STATE (the crux — a handler cannot move while it closes over module-scope state)
Module-level mutable, read or written:
- `active` (:140) — read by GET /api/root (4189), /api/files, /api/file, /api/undo; WRITTEN by POST /api/root.
- `liveProjectContext` (:150) — cleared by POST /api/root.
- `boundPort` (:800) — read by POST /api/root (`:800`; `boundPort ?? PORT`).
- `pageSocket` (:1602) — read indirectly via pageExecutorConnected (:1609).
- `undoStackByRoot` (:2410) — read by GET /api/undo.
server.mjs helpers the routes call (definition lines): json (:1954), readJsonBody (:2088) and the handler-scoped readJson wrapper (:4287), answerOnce (:2130), rootMissing (:2043), resolveActive (:2149), askPage (:1689), pageExecutorConnected (:1609), recordWorkActivity (:873), hasExtensionAuthority (:304), execute (:2425).
Imports used by the slice: core/root.ts (ROOT_FACTS, describeRoot, reachableFromEnvironment, noRootDeclared), core/paths.ts (normaliseRelativeDir, parentDir), core/dispatch.ts (dispatchFor), lib/path-auth.mjs (authorizeMachinePath via resolveActive), lib/timing-safe.mjs (timingSafeStringEqual), lib/extensions.mjs (hostTokenOk).

## 3. THE DECIDING QUESTION — which helpers are shared with routes that stay
- `execute(action)` (:2425) — the ~1100-line executor. ALSO called by POST /api/delegate (4838), POST /api/exec (4847), POST /api/turn (5041) and the live session tool loop (5952). CANNOT move; must be injected.
- `resolveActive(name)` (:2149) — 3-line wrapper over authorizeMachinePath. ALSO used by execute's list/write/mkdir verbs (2777, 3285) and the saveAs path (3974).
- `rootMissing()` (:2043) — ALSO used by GET /api/audit (4491) and execute (2761).
- `askPage`/`pageExecutorConnected` (:1689/:1609) — ALSO used by setHostHooks (1683), executeViaPage (1724), GET /api/root (4192, 4208).
- `recordWorkActivity` (:873) — used by DELETE /api/root (4053), POST /api/exec (4850), POST /api/turn (5043), and the live session (5853+).
- `json`, `readJson`, `answerOnce` — used by nearly every route in the file.
=> The slice CANNOT be a pure move. It needs an injected context.

## 4. AUTH AND ERROR CONTRACT (must survive the move unchanged)
- Global loopback auth when VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH=1 (4303-4326): session cookie OR x-voicebox-host-token; failure 401 {ok:false, refused:"loopback-unauthenticated"}.
- POST /api/root's own authorization is at 4406-4408: 403 refused "host-token-required"; it also accepts hasExtensionAuthority for self:true and the ROOM_SESSION_TOKEN comparison via timingSafeStringEqual.
- POST /api/root refusals, by line: bad-request 400 (4373, 4385, 4419); unknown-root-kind 400 (4388); host-token-required 403 (4406-4408); path-missing 404 (4423); not-a-directory 400 (4429, 4432); success 200 (4442, 4468); a reach refusal at 200 (4475).
- GET /api/files REFUSES WITH HTTP 200 and `{ok:false, refused:<name>, why, dir, parent, files:[], entries:[]}` (4503-4512, e.g. the bad-dir branch). This contract is deliberate — the code says refusals are "named rather than quietly rewritten" — so a client reads `ok`/`refused`, NOT the status. A move that "tidies" these into 4xx changes behaviour.
- GET /api/file uses 409 for no-root-declared / root-vanished and 403/500 for unreadable, so the two read routes do NOT share one refusal status convention. Pin both.
- The five thin file verbs (DELETE/PUT/PATCH /api/file, /api/file/diff, /api/grep) delegate to execute() and pass its result through; PUT/PATCH/diff take CONTENT_JSON_BODY_MAX_BYTES (2068) as their body cap.

## 5. FOCUSED TESTS
- UNIT lane: tests/path-auth.test.mjs (owns the containment contract) and tests/root-seam-entry.test.mjs (the root seam's own entry points, driven pure — no server).
- LIVE lane: tests/file-actions.test.mjs (the main driver: /api/file GET+PUT+PATCH+DELETE, /api/file/diff, /api/grep, /api/undo), tests/path-auth-verbs.test.mjs (the live companion for authorization), plus tests/root-seam.test.mjs, tests/one-root.test.mjs, tests/activity-log.test.mjs, tests/channel-auth.test.mjs, tests/timing-safe.test.mjs, tests/sandbox-subdirectories.test.mjs.
- BROWSER lane: tests/explorer-folders.test.mjs, tests/page-writes.test.mjs, tests/opfs-scratch-room.test.mjs, tests/voicebox.test.mjs.
VERIFICATION COST, stated plainly: the route WIRING is almost entirely live-lane, so `fleet-check --fast` does NOT cover this change. Focused live runs (file-actions + path-auth-verbs) are the minimum, and the full gate runs the rest on landing. That cost is an argument for the seam shape in section 7.

## 6. AUDIO COLLISION
Zero functional overlap. 9c3r lives in public/audio-client.js and tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs; nothing in this slice touches audio, the PCM worklet, or the /live WebSocket path. The real collision is a LANE one, not a code one: this bead's assignee is voicebox-audioflake, who is also mid-investigation on 9c3r. Coord should decide whether that lane implements lrsp or finishes 9c3r first, rather than both at once.

## 7. EXTRACTABILITY VERDICT AND RECOMMENDED SHAPE
Not a pure move. Recommended: `lib/routes/workspace.mjs` exporting something like `registerWorkspaceRoutes(handle, ctx)` (or a `workspaceRoutes(ctx)` matcher), with `ctx` carrying exactly: getActive/setActive, clearLiveProjectContext, getBoundPort, pageExecutorConnected, askPage, recordWorkActivity, execute, hostTokenOk, hasExtensionAuthority, roomSessionToken, readJson, json, answerOnce, resolveActive, rootMissing, SELF_ENVIRONMENT.
WHY THIS SHAPE MATTERS MORE THAN THE LINE COUNT: the routes today close over module-scope mutable state, which is exactly why they can only be driven through a live server. An explicit ctx makes the route logic drivable from a UNIT-lane file with a fake ctx — the precedent already in this repo is tests/root-seam-entry.test.mjs (voicebox-beads-8why), which drives the root seam's entry points directly and is why root-seam-entry is the only unit-lane test in this family. That is the difference between "server.mjs got smaller" and "the seam became testable": it moves verification of the wiring out of the live lane and into the fast gate, which is the whole point of decomposing a 6314-line hotspot.

## RECOMMENDED SLICE ORDER
1. The five thin file verbs + undo + grep (4798-4834 and 4672-4689). They delegate to execute() and never touch the page channel — smallest closure set, easiest to prove.
2. GET /api/files + GET /api/file (4503-4670). They need resolveActive, rootMissing, askPage, pageExecutorConnected.
3. Root, LAST and as ONE unit — because POST /api/root (4352) must be reconciled with GET /api/root (4189) and DELETE /api/root (4042) in the routes table, or the root lifecycle stays split across two files. Moving POST alone would make that split worse.
NOT IN THIS BEAD: moving execute() itself (its own decomposition), and the mini-apps suite (4691-4796) that sits in the middle of the family.

title: A test writes git config into the REAL repo - commits were authored as a watcher FIXTURE
description:
FOUND 2026-10-11 while fixing fleet commit attribution (Paul: the fleet is not using my id).

EVIDENCE: this repo had a REPO-LOCAL git identity of user.name=watcher fixture, user.email=watcher-fixture@test.local. A repo-local identity beats the global, so every commit here was authored as that fixture. The name is a TEST FIXTURE (tests/factory-review-adapter.test.mjs builds a watcher-fixture branch), so a suite ran git config with its cwd INSIDE the production repo instead of in its own temp dir.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: those commits are attributed to nobody - GitHub shows them under an unlinked identity, and any git log audit of who changed what is wrong. Same shape as the day it was found: a check quietly mutating production.

FIX: the suite must git init in a temp dir and/or pass identity inline (git -c user.name=... -c user.email=...); never run a bare git config, and never when the cwd could fall back to the real repo. I set this repo to name="Paul Kinlan (fleet:voicebox)" so commits are correct again, but the test will clobber it on its next run.

Fleet-side counterpart, already on a branch: remote/provision.sh now ASSERTS the repo identity rather than only setting the global if unset, corrects a wrong local value, and reports what it replaced.
