title: FLAKE: ldxa-barge-in 'playback must be flushed, not left playing' fails inside the concurrent browser tier, passes in every focused control
description:
FOUND while measuring voicebox-beads-hhkg (the browser tier's shard runner). NO CLAIM that sharding caused it and NO CLAIM that it is inherited — the facts, and what would decide it, are below. Assignee is coord for ROUTING; the reporter is not claiming the fix.

## The exact failure
tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs:168
  assert.equal(interrupted.playbackActive, false, "playback must be flushed, not left playing");
Observed (verbatim from the runner's TAP capture):
  not ok 1 - barge-in in the real audio path: quiet speech does not interrupt; speech over the agent flushes playback and sends the interrupt
    error: |-
      playback must be flushed, not left playing
      true !== false
    name: 'AssertionError'  expected: false  actual: true  operator: 'strictEqual'
    at TestContext.<anonymous> (tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs:168:10)
The file test's duration_ms was 9883.7 in a 10709ms wall slot.

## Conditions
- Tier: the full 63-file browser lane through tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs, 4 workers, each file its own process/server/browser.
- Occurrence A: voicebox-beads-hhkg repeat 1 run 1, tree 527bb74. exit 1, wall 175.2s, tests 249 / pass 246 / fail 1 / skipped 2. Load average 2.06 at start, 20.35 at end. Peak tree RSS 658MB. THE ASSERTION WAS NOT CAPTURED for this occurrence (the harness kept only the test name); do not attribute A's assertion from this bead.
- Occurrence B: voicebox-beads-hhkg repeat 2 run 2, tree dbb8693. exit 1, wall 189.9s, tests 249 / pass 246 / fail 1 / skipped 2, coverage ok. Load average 7.85 at start. Peak tree RSS 731MB, peak live browser processes 7. Assertion captured, quoted above.
- Rate: 2 failures in 9 concurrent full-tier runs (pilot c=4, counted c=4, counted c=6, live-sharded, repeat1 x3, repeat2 x1 before it stopped) = ~22% point estimate, n=9, wide uncertainty. Serial full-tier runs seen: 2, both green. Do NOT read that as "serial is safe" — n=2.

## Focused controls, all green (7 runs, in /tmp/shard-ldxa-flake.log)
- target ALONE, node's own runner, ambient load ~16: 2/2 green (7.1s, 7.2s)
- target THROUGH the shard runner, alone: 2/2 green (8.3s, 8.4s)
- target + 3 other browser files at --test-concurrency=4, NO runner: 3/3 green (29 tests each)
So it did not reproduce without the runner, nor in isolation, nor under a 4-file load.

## Provenance: the same assertion is ALREADY RECORDED as environmental
voicebox-beads-y82w [gate flake] ldxa-barge-in (P2, CLOSED/merged) records, verbatim: "Additional case measured 2026-10-07 on tree 77553897: 'barge-in in the real audio path: ...' (tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs) failed inside the full gate with 'AssertionError: playback must be flushed, not left playing'. Controlled comparison, same file and same command in isolation on two trees: PASSES on the feature tree (1/1), FAILS at merge-base 56b3fde with the same assertion (0/1) - environmental like the case this bead already records, and a second distinct test in the same file failing under load."
That is the SAME assertion message with the SAME profile (inside the full gate / green in isolation). y82w's landed fix (6edfdc1/98c6d97) made the provider-interrupt assertion a delta and made the test wait for the fixture's utterance to end; it did not remove this assertion, and this bead records it firing again. WHETHER THAT IS "y82w's fix did not hold for this assertion" OR "the same environmental class has a second, unaddressed path" IS THE OPEN QUESTION — not something this bead asserts.
The mechanism the file's own comments name: "Chromium's fake-audio device lags its file under load (measured +76ms idle, +366ms at 4-core load)".

## Why it is not simply 'a loaded box'
The failure landed in the LEAST loaded of the repeats' runs in occurrence A (load average 2.06 at start) and at 7.85 in B, while occurrence B's tier ran 190-237s wall versus ~130s on a quiet box. Load is clearly involved somewhere, but a simple "load" story does not explain A.

## Next actions, in order
1. Reproduce DETERMINISTICALLY, in the style this lane has used for every prior flake (voicebox-beads-y82w built a stimulus that failed the base on demand): under the 4-worker tier, make the page slow enough that the flush and the read of playbackActive interleave — or drive playbackActive directly at the seam — and record which of the two it is.
2. Until then, the merge of hhkg ISOLATES this file (runs it after the parallel queue, alone, still exactly once). That is a SCHEDULING change with a named mechanism and evidence, not a claim the flake is fixed. Coverage is unchanged.
3. No test may be weakened to make this pass: the assertion names real behaviour and voicebox-beads-y82w already proved a mutant that puts a page frame on the wire is caught by the sibling assertion.

title: Implement 4-shard browser test runner with isolated long-lived instances
description:
Rationale
The `browser` live lane takes 396s sequentially (76% of the 522s full gate) because 43 test files each launch their own `server.mjs` and Chromium instances.

Cost
~1 lane-day. Requires creating a `tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs` to provision 4 concurrent server+browser pairs, partitioning the 43 test files across them, and refactoring tests to use injected instances (with isolated CDP contexts or cleaned states) instead of `launch()`. Moderate test churn.

Who
`implementer`

Risk if we do nothing
Gate execution remains >8 minutes, capping project velocity to ~5 landings per hour across the fleet.

Do not use flags-only concurrency or weaken tests. Start with small bounded pilot and escalate if long-lived shared server semantics conflict with fixtures.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — branch fleet/shard, tip 2049a3a (pushed).

MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER (same tree, this VM; the box's own last full-gate log ~/.fleet/checks/1cb3b418….log is the second baseline)
- browser tier, SERIAL (before): 284.3s here, 395.5s in the box's loaded log. Its log says 249 tests / 247 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped.
- browser tier, RAW --test-concurrency=4 (the ADR's "flag-only" alternative, measured): 127.8s, exit 0, counts IDENTICAL (249/247/0/2). c=6 was 144.4s — the 2-vCPU box saturates at 4.
- browser tier, SHARD RUNNER (shipped): 102.5s, 249/247/0/2, files-failed=0.
- live stage end-to-end (`npm run test:live`): server tier 35.7s (379 tests) + browser 102.5s = ~138s, was 48.3 + 395.5 = 443.8s. Against the 400s live bound that is headroom instead of a stage that could be killed for finishing.

THE ADR'S PREMISE IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, and the plan changed accordingly.
- The ADR says flag-only concurrency "failed reliably under load due to concurrent process spawn spikes". Two full counted runs say otherwise (above). Its 396s -> 115s target came from assuming per-file instance startup was the cost; it is not: cold launch() 1603ms, WARM launch() 387ms, startServer() 202-214ms, so per-file fixed overhead is ~0.6s of a ~4.5s file. Instance reuse can win ~10%; the SHARD PARALLELISM is the 2.2x.
- The long-lived shared server/browser (the ADR's literal design) is NOT available to these fixtures: 44 of 63 files pass their own VOICEBOX_INSTANCE / VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE / VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR to startServer() (process env, per file), and 10 need browser-level flags (fakeMedia, a prepared profile) that one shared browser cannot give a single tab. That is the escalation condition coord named, and it fired.
- What ships keeps per-file isolation EXACTLY as before (own process, own ephemeral-port server, own browser) and takes the parallelism. Static 4-way partitioning was rejected on measurement too: LPT over the 63 real per-file durations gives an ideal makespan of 71.4s, but the best cheap cost proxy (bytes, r=0.51 vs wall time) mispredicts the tier's longest file (pre-push, 24.3s of 284.3s) enough that a pinned 4-way split leaves one shard 63% longer — so the runner steals work and the queue is only ordered longest-first.

WHAT THE ACCEPTANCE ASKS FOR, AS EXECUTABLE ASSERTIONS (tests/test-shards.test.mjs, unit lane, 4 tests, all green)
- ALL BROWSER FILES ONCE: the runner calls assertExactCoverage BEFORE any browser opens and refuses a queue that drops, repeats or invents a file; the run ends with an explicit coverage line. The test pins the real browser lane AND all three refusals by name.
- FAST-GATE SET IS AN EXECUTABLE SUBSET OF FULL: the test reads scripts/pre-push.sh (both test stages) and package.json (test:unit / test:live wiring) and proves unit ∪ live == every tests/*.test.mjs exactly once, with every fast-gate file inside the full set. It also fails if test:live stops routing the browser tier through the runner.
- Functional coverage unchanged, not merely claimed: identical test counts on every arm.

NOT DONE, deliberately: a long-lived shared browser per shard (~15% at best, and the browser-context/OPFS isolation risk is real — tests/opfs-persistence.test.mjs documents that "a fresh profile per launch would make every assertion true for the wrong reason"). Recommend a separate bead with its own pilot if coord still wants it.

FILES: tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs (new), scripts/test-shards.mjs (new), scripts/test-lanes.mjs (its CLI now runs only under import.meta.main, so the runner can ask classify() in process), package.json (test:live), scripts/pre-push.sh + docs/12-pre-push-gate.md + AGENTS.md + docs/00-architectural-overview.md (comments/docs), tests/test-shards.test.mjs (new), tests/test-lanes.test.mjs (wiring pin updated).

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: The gate's browser test tier now runs through tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs, which takes its file list from the lane classifier, refuses it unless it covers the browser lane exactly once, and runs up to four files at a time with work-stealing. scripts/test-shards.mjs owns that queue; scripts/test-lanes.mjs only runs its CLI when it is the program. tests/test-shards.test.mjs pins both coverage claims executably.
WHY: The browser tier was the whole cost of the live stage — 284.3s serial here, 395.5s in the box's own loaded gate log, against a 400s bound — so a green branch could be refused because the stage ran out of time rather than because a test failed.
EFFECT: Landings go through the gate about 2.2x faster on the browser tier (284s -> ~103s; live stage 444s -> ~138s), with identical test coverage (249 tests / 247 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped) and unchanged per-file isolation. Operators see per-file timings and an explicit coverage line in the gate log, and a queue that dropped a file now fails loudly instead of looking faster.

The file itself records this failure mode: "Chromium's fake-audio device lags its file under load (measured +76ms idle, +366ms at 4-core load, and the flake this bead records happened at load ~8)". Its first assertions run the moment the phase is `agent-speaking`, and the fixture is a wall-clock wav (3 quiet seconds, then a voice), so a lagging fake-audio timeline can move the "quiet" passage onto the utterance.

## 3. Alone-vs-concurrent control (7 bounded runs, NO full gates)
| arm | what it isolates | result |
|---|---|---|
| A: target ALONE, node's own runner, ambient load ~16 | neither runner nor load | **2/2 green** (7.1s, 7.2s) |
| B: target through the SHARD RUNNER, alone | the runner's own code path, no load | **2/2 green** (8.3s, 8.4s) |
| C: target + 3 other browser files at `--test-concurrency=4` | LOAD, node's scheduler, NO runner | **3/3 green** (29 tests each) |

**I am not calling the failure inherited.** Coord's rule is that a serial control must reproduce it under comparable load first, and arm A did not reproduce it at an ambient load average of ~16 (the failing run's own start was load 2.06, rising to 20 as it ran). **I am also not calling it caused by sharding**: it did not reproduce through the runner alone (B), nor under four concurrent real browser files without the runner (C).

What the data supports, stated with its sample size: **1 failure in 7 concurrent full-tier runs and 0 in 2 serial full-tier runs.** A ~14% point estimate with two or three runs' worth of uncertainty — too small to conclude, too large to merge on. Note also that the failure landed in the LEAST loaded run (load 2.06 at start), which argues against "load alone causes it" as much as it argues against "sharding causes it".

## 4. Fix applied as a result (dbb8693)
On a failing run the runner exited before printing its coverage line, so run 1 read `coverage=MISSING`. That is the one reading a red run must never have. Coverage is now decided and printed BEFORE the failure exit, and it counts DISTINCT result files rather than comparing lengths, so a file that reported twice cannot stand in for one that never ran. Verified with a deliberate failure: prints `coverage ok: 1 result(s) for 1 queued file(s), 1 distinct` then `FAILED: … (exit 1)`, exit 1.

## 5. In flight
A second bounded 3-run repeat on dbb8693 with the sampler fixed (real peak browser count) and the failing file's verbatim output preserved, so a recurrence is diagnosable instead of merely counted. Then: fast gate for the frozen tip, and a reviewer-role delta verdict for dbb8693 itself (the earlier role PASS covers 8efdd37..527bb74 and does NOT cover this commit).

title: security: project node_modules/.bin is FIRST on the run_command PATH — workspace binaries shadow system tools
description:
From nightly factory delta triage (voicebox-beads-htbl), finding unclassified MEDIUM at lib/tool-index.mjs:104 (also carried as an unchanged active finding; no bead existed).

VERIFIED IN CODE on origin/main@a7c065c: buildSearchPaths (lib/tool-index.mjs:101) returns [<root>/node_modules/.bin, ~/.local/bin, mise shims, go/bin, cargo/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /bin, ...env.PATH] — the ACTIVE PROJECT's node_modules/.bin outranks /usr/bin. When the operator opens an untrusted checkout and the voice runs 'git …' or 'node …', a workspace-supplied binary at node_modules/.bin/git (dropped by a malicious postinstall, or committed) executes instead, with the host's full environment (see voicebox-beads-8b9l).

This is the supply-chain half of running shell commands inside a declared root: the root confines cwd, not the toolchain.

NEXT ACTION: decide and implement one of: (a) move project .bin AFTER the system dirs, (b) only honor it for package-script-style commands, or (c) keep first but record the decision with the threat reasoning. Add a unit test asserting a scratch root's node_modules/.bin/git does NOT shadow /usr/bin/git for run_command (whichever order is chosen, pin it).
notes: Factory 2026-10-19 audit also flags system-tools.mjs:172 (collectSearchPathDirs) placing <cwd>/bin, <cwd>/scripts, <cwd>/node_modules/.bin before /usr/bin in the system-tools runner PATH, matching tool-index.mjs:101.

title: security: extension mediated-fetch egress allowlist is hostname-string-only — no private/metadata IP block or DNS pinning
description:
From nightly factory delta triage (voicebox-beads-htbl), findings unhandled-url-construction (lib/extensions.mjs:655) and unclassified (lib/extensions.mjs:1214).

VERIFIED IN CODE on origin/main@a7c065c: lib/extensions.mjs:1214 gates a mediated extension fetch with \`(bounds.hosts ?? []).includes(url.hostname)\` — a literal hostname string compare. There is no refusal for IP-literal hosts, no private/link-local/loopback/metadata range check (127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 192.168/16, 169.254.169.254…), and no DNS pinning: a declared host's DNS can be rebound between admission review and fetch. An admitted extension declaring 'example.com' can be steered onto internal addresses; one declaring a literal private IP passes review text unchanged.

The admission plan review (host sees the declared hosts) mitigates the honest-mistake case but not DNS rebinding after admission.

NEXT ACTION: at fetch time, resolve and refuse private/link-local/loopback/metadata answers (or pin the first resolution for the call); refuse IP-literal hosts not explicitly declared as such; add a unit test driving a 169.254.169.254-bound response through the mediated fetch and asserting a named refusal. Consider reusing any existing egress vocabulary; keep the named-refusal style (host-not-allowed family).

comments.author: voicebox-miniapps
comments.text:
IN_REVIEW on fleet/miniapps @ c94a639 (3 commits, base 4c1a63c). Fast gate: npm run test:unit 604 tests / 594 pass / 0 fail; docs-check OK. Cross-family review in flight (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol); merge-queue label goes on when it reports.

WHAT I FOUND, IN ORDER, because the second finding changes the answer to the bead's question.

1. The auth failure is real and structural. The factory resolves an unset --engine to `pi`; `pi` runs inside bubblewrap with a fresh tmpfs over $HOME by design, so the operator's ~/.pi subscription logins are unreachable and it authenticates only from an allowlisted env key (lib/child_env.py). No fleet VM has one. The `claude` engine - the one adapter that reads ~/.claude subscription creds - is refused by the factory for a public target, and `antigravity` refuses every tool policy. So there is no subscription-login engine available to a public voicebox target today. Real runs reproduced it twice (accessibility 09:26, secret-scan 16:48, both rc1, "No API key found for the selected model").

2. The only reachable model is the exe.dev-provisioned deepseek integration (https://deepseek.int.exe.xyz, non-secret placeholder key, reachable from this VM), and pointing the a11y station at it produces A FALSE-CLEAN. `factory run accessibility --target <worktree> --engine deepseek` exits 0 and writes a schema-valid report whose summary says "No scanner data was supplied in the request". It was not clean: the factory's deepseek adapter reads the prompt into $PROMPT and then runs its API call from `python3 - <<EOF`, whose heredoc IS process stdin, so the adapter's own `prompt = sys.stdin.read()` returns "" and EVERY run sends an empty user message. Docs-drift in the same conditions: 492 pre-pass candidates in candidates.json, model summary claiming none were supplied, 0 findings, exit 0. comments.text:
FOUND BY: the ONE exact-tree full gate on my V4/V5 tree fdb865c, which FAILED on this and only this (244 tests, 241 pass, 1 fail, 922s, log /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/4039b98e04debefc2a59421aad1b9390348b8eb9.log). Actual: 'Reading…'; expected: /read\/write/.
ATTRIBUTION, checked rather than assumed: NOT caused by my branch. `git diff 4c8036b..HEAD -- tests/room-folders.test.mjs` is EMPTY, my branch touches no readerFacts line, and the mechanism is plainly pre-existing: public/fused.js:2654 and :2723 set els.readerFacts.textContent = reloading ? The test clicks the file and then does `await sleep(200)` before reading #file-facts, so it is a fixed-sleep race: on a loaded gate the read does not finish in 200ms and the assertion reads the placeholder. title: BUG: the environments page says a browser-stored root is read-only for turns — page-side writes landed (copy + the tests that pin it are stale)
description:
FOUND while implementing voicebox-beads-um5r (the 'explain what setup does, why, and the order' bead): the explanation cannot be true while these sentences say the opposite of what the code does.

THE FACT: a turn CAN write into a browser-stored root (OPFS) and into a picked folder. tests/page-writes.test.mjs proves it end to end — 'an OPFS project: the turn writes through the page, reads back byte-for-byte, and the page is the audit's writer': the turn returns ok: true, via: 'page', the bytes read back match, and the page is recorded as the writer. browser/acts.ts is the page-side executor ('the environment page ANSWERS routed acts'), core/dispatch.ts is the router, and the declaration answers actsVia: 'page'. Its own header quotes Paul, 2026-09-20: 'page should be able to write.'

THE STALE SENTENCES (all say turns cannot write where the code says they can):
- browser/ui/ui.ts:618 — 'the loop cannot write here yet — this project is in this browser's own storage, so only this page can act on it: the page lists and reads its files.'
- browser/ui/ui.ts:620 — '...a picked folder or this origin's storage is readable and writable only by the page until page-side writes land (voicebox-beads-2cf)' — and voicebox-beads-2cf no longer exists in the live DB, so the sentence points at a bead that is gone.
- browser/ui/ui.ts:136-137 — the header fact says the other kinds are where 'turns cannot write into this kind yet'.
- public/environment.html : 'A folder you pick in the browser stays read-only for turns for now'.
- The labels I put on the new create dialog in voicebox-beads-6uzd carry the same claims ('turns cannot write here yet', 'read-only for turns') because I preserved the page's existing sentences. They are wrong for OPFS and only half-true for a picked folder.
THE ROOM'S COPY IS THE CORRECT ONE: public/fused.js (dnwa) says for browser storage 'turns and edits save here'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (the model an explanation should state):
- This browser's own storage: the files live in this browser and TURNS' acts are routed to this page, which performs them (no path, no host token). It needs the page connected/answering: with nobody connected the server refuses the act as 'no-page' (proved in tests/page-writes.test.mjs, checks 1 and 4).
- A folder you pick: the same routing, but the browser grants write only after a click, so a turn's write is refused 'needs-gesture' with the remedy named until 'Restore write access' is used (proved in tests/one-root.test.mjs, the picked-folder test).
- A folder on this machine: the Voicebox server performs the act itself (actsVia: 'server'), so it needs the absolute path and the host token, works with no browser page connected, and the files are on disk where your own editor sees them.

BLAST RADIUS for the fix: the sentences above, plus the assertions that pin them — tests/one-root.test.mjs:304 ('the page does not say the loop cannot write there') and its header assertion for 'turns cannot write into this kind yet', and the environment page labels in my 6uzd change. The fix is a copy fix plus those assertions, no behaviour change: the routing already works.
NOT MINE TO LAND UNILATERALLY: this contradicts sentences the team wrote deliberately (they were true before page-side writes landed), so it is filed with evidence rather than fixed silently, and coord/Paul should know that two surfaces currently tell people different things about the same choice — which is plausibly part of why the page reads as 'super confusing'.

title: FLAKE: project-instruction-browser 'packages report' 8s budget expires under a loaded gate
description:
FIFTH INSTANCE of the day's gate-flake class, different test again. Seen in the MERGER's gate on tree 63a1718a8d97a332c2b728d31dff4a26d319a08c (commit a761fff), 12:16-12:51Z, log /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/63a1718a8d97a332c2b728d31dff4a26d319a08c.log:

  ✖ tests/project-instruction-browser.test.mjs:30 "the page reports the folder it is showing, and reads a room folder's AGENTS.md itself (voicebox-beads-0zi4)" (11337ms)
    AssertionError at tests/project-instruction-browser.test.mjs:27, via :123 — "No the packages report within 8000ms"

WHAT IT IS, precisely (this one is NOT a fixed-sleep bet, and should not be filed as one):
  async function until(check, label, ms = 8000) {           // :20-28
    const deadline = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < deadline) { const r = await check(); if (r) return r; await sleep(50); }
    assert.fail(`No ${label} within ${ms}ms`);
  }
  ... await until(async () => (await frames()).some((f) => f.type === "folder" && f.dir === "packages"), "the packages report");   // :123
The shape is right — it polls the CONDITION, with a deadline, and fails by name. What expired is the budget: a real app operation (clicking the `packages` row makes the page REQUEST a listing and report a `folder` frame; the test's own comment at :124-125 says the report is optimistic and the listing is a request) did not complete inside 8s on a box running a full gate. `frames()` is itself a `page.evaluate` round-trip, so the poll loop is a small load source under an already loaded box, and each round-trip is slower exactly when it matters.

NOT ATTRIBUTED, honestly: I have not measured the operation's latency in isolation or under load — the heavy slot was held (one browser job at a time) — so this bead claims only: condition + 8s deadline, expired at 11337ms total test time under gate load, on a tree whose failure has no other explanation. Two plausible causes, both needing a measurement to separate: (a) the operation is genuinely slower under load than 8s allows, or (b) the poll loop's CDP round-trips starve the thing being waited on.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP (measurement first, then a fix in one direction):
1. Instrument the wait: log the condition's latency in isolation and while a full gate runs (repeat N times), so the budget can be set as a multiple of the measured latency rather than a guess.
2. Then either raise this budget (per-call, not the default) or reduce poll cost (poll inside the page via a promise/rAF instead of a CDP round-trip every 50ms) — whichever the measurement supports.
Cosmetic while you are there: the message concatenates as "No the packages report within 8000ms".

IMPACT: like the other four, it reddens a gate on a tree whose content cannot explain it (here the merger's), and each occurrence costs a 17-26 minute gate. Filed by voicebox-roboticon from the gate-reliability work; NOT claimed by this lane, needs an owner.

title: FLAKE: mic-waveform animation asserts a requestAnimationFrame result after a fixed 60ms sleep
description:
SEEN ONCE, 2026-10-08 13:04-13:21Z, in a full gate on tree f953987211fe77c0b7124c354e91e28be19fc987 (commit 9aa3abe): browser lane 230 tests, 227 pass, 1 fail. Log /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/f953987211fe77c0b7124c354e91e28be19fc987.log.

  ✖ tests/mic-waveform-animation.test.mjs:36 "mic button waveform dynamically animates during speech output, listening, and barge-in blend (voicebox-beads-5i2i, 6vs4)"
    AssertionError at tests/mic-waveform-animation.test.mjs:227:
    "returning to listening reallocates back to 55 L segments" — 127 !== 55

NOT CAUSED BY ANYTHING UNDER TEST: that tree is origin/main 8c6c587 + two TEST-SIDE fixes only (voicebox-roboticon's cdp-process-cleanup test change and a JSONL test reader). No product, UI, waveform or animation code differs from main in it. Filed separately from voicebox-beads-5bmg because it is a different test, but it is the same class.

MECHANISM (read from the code, not inferred from the failure): the test sets `stage.dataset.voice` and swaps `window.__voiceboxLiveClient`, then does `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 60))` and reads the `d` attribute of `#input-path` (tests/mic-waveform-animation.test.mjs:203-227). The app reallocates the ring on a requestAnimationFrame tick, not on the assignment: `public/fused.js:5121` schedules `meters` via `requestAnimationFrame`, and inside it `drawInputWave(samples)` reallocates only when the sample count differs — `if (!inputInit || inputDisplay.length !== n) { inputDisplay = new Float32Array(n); ... }` (public/fused.js:5021-5024). So each of the three assertions is a bet that at least one frame runs inside 60ms. The failure is on the THIRD transition (back to listening, expected 55, still 127 from the previous speaking state) — exactly the signature of the frame not having run yet. A busy renderer defers rAF; a gate runs 4 concurrent test processes plus a per-test Chrome on 2 vCPUs.

SUGGESTED FIX (test-side, same shape as voicebox-beads-5bmg): wait for the CONDITION with a deadline instead of sleeping a fixed time — e.g. `await page.waitFor(() => (document.getElementById("input-path").getAttribute("d") || "").split("L").length - 1 === 55, { label: "the ring to reallocate to 55 L segments" })` before each read — then keep the existing exact-count assertion (which then also fails loudly if the app never reallocates). `page.waitFor` already throws by label after its timeout (tests/lib/cdp.mjs:602-612).

CONTROLLED DIAGNOSIS NOT YET DONE: the rAF-delay story is code-grounded but has not been reproduced on demand, and I have not run a load control because another lane's gate held the heavy slot and the rule is one browser job at a time. Whoever takes this: reproduce it (standalone pass, then repeated runs under a busy box, or instrument the frame timing), and record the result before claiming the mechanism.

IMPACT: this reddened a gate on a tree whose content cannot explain it, and it can redden any lane's gate; it costs a ~17-26 minute gate per occurrence.

title: BUG: JSONL pollers parse a just-created (empty) file as corrupt — gate flake in tests/lib/task-fixture.mjs
description:
DISCOVERED ON: the combined sodf/hobs tree 5eb32b81 (sha 5e9429b) while gating voicebox-beads-3lwx. Log /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/5eb32b819eae794a04de35e2fa9131abf4e8655b.log. FAIL rc1 681s: 348 pass / 1 fail / 15 skipped.

THE FAILURE:
  ✖ tests/tasks-http.test.mjs:17 "D1 real HTTP: separate authenticated connections, private/pinned record, killed environment -> interrupted, no replay"
    SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
      at Array.map (<anonymous>)
      at Object.starts (tests/lib/task-fixture.mjs:86:85)
      at tests/tasks-http.test.mjs:46:25   ← the FIRST waitFor(() => f.starts(), (e) => e.length === 1)

THE MECHANISM (proved, not assumed):
  tests/lib/task-fixture.mjs:86
    return fs.existsSync(file) ? fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8").trim().split("\n").map(JSON.parse) : [];
  The writer is one `fs.appendFileSync(starts, JSON.stringify(...) + "\n")` (tests/fixtures/task-runtime.mjs:35) — open(O_CREAT|O_APPEND) then write. Between those two steps the file EXISTS and is EMPTY. `existsSync` then answers true, `readFileSync` returns "", `"".trim().split("\n")` is `[""]`, and `JSON.parse("")` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` — the exact message in the log. Proved locally: `node -e '"" .trim().split("\n").map(JSON.parse)'` → "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input".
  The failing call is the first poll of the file, i.e. exactly when the fixture creates it. Under a full gate (two gates on 2 CPUs at the time) the create→write window is widest, which is why isolation is green and the gate is red. The same reader also cannot survive a torn tail (a read that lands mid-append leaves a partial final line).

SCOPE — the same unguarded pattern is in 10 test files (one defect, ten sites):
  tests/lib/task-fixture.mjs:86, tests/tasks.test.mjs:20, tests/task-outcome.test.mjs:32, tests/tasks-cancel.test.mjs:19, tests/pi-acp.test.mjs:74, tests/extensions-live.test.mjs:131, tests/extension-approval-ui.test.mjs:155, tests/configured-harness.test.mjs:76, tests/file-actions.test.mjs:227, tests/debug-transcript.test.mjs:31 (the last two read audit logs written by the server under the same window).

PROPOSED FIX (test-only): one shared reader that (a) treats an empty file as "no records yet" (drop blank lines before parsing), and (b) drops a final line that is not newline-terminated (a write in flight) — while still failing loudly on any COMPLETE line that is not valid JSON, so a genuinely corrupt record cannot hide. Callers keep their own existence checks.

EVIDENCE: this is the first occurrence in any VM gate log (`grep -l "task-fixture.mjs:86" /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/*.log` → only this run), so it is a latent race that load exposed, not a regression from the combined tree (the file is unchanged from origin/main in those branches).

IN_REVIEW — roboticon (branch fleet/roboticon-3lwx @ bf61af2, from origin/main d2a2db6; test-only fix in tests/cdp-process-cleanup.test.mjs + evidence).

DIAGNOSIS (proved, not assumed). The red is the LEADER-PID assertion only (:89 page.close, :200 SIGTERM); the group-empty and profile-process assertions never run because that one fails first. CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (docs/evidence/3lwx-cdp-cleanup-20261008/old-helper-repro.mjs, old helpers verbatim from d2a2db6 beside the new witness, no browser, no load):

  a process really still running                       truth: running    | old: SURVIVOR | new: SURVIVOR (leak check preserved)

Group/profile checks no longer count zombie rows (a zombie is an uncollected exit, not a running descendant). The bound is load-tolerant (100x100ms) as the SECONDARY half — the mechanism is the state/identity reading, and the experiment above is its proof. No /proc (macOS) → old semantics, stated in the code; the zombie case skips itself. PLAN (V5 half, same pass as V4): one primary "Create a project" button in the environments area that opens a real `<dialog>` (the repo's own pattern — `closedby="any"`, focus trap, inert background, Esc, as `#envs` in index.html does) containing the name field and the destination choices in the order V4 explains: browser storage (no disk, no host token) / a folder you pick (read-only for turns today) / a folder on this machine (+ host token, turns can write there). - Keep the ids (`#project-name`, `#open-form`) and the existing ui.ts handlers, so tests/dom-targets.test.mjs and the wiring stay anchored; the dialog is markup, not a second implementation.

- Do not regress miniapps' in-flight f517537 focus-visible outline on this file (it touches this file's CSS only; my changes are below it in the markup).

IMPLEMENTED (not yet reviewed or gated) on branch fleet/roboticon-v4v5, commit 06e752d, tree 6f0128536a902fefaa401bb8c161068f41d1ab4f.

The page now explains setup once, visibly, instead of stating the trade-offs three times and never stating the order:
- "What setup does": a project is a folder plus the environment that holds it, and the turns that read and save files run in the Voicebox server, so that server needs a folder it can name before it can do anything.
- "Why it is needed": with no project, reads and writes are refused — nowhere to go. This browser's own storage needs no path and no token but turns cannot write into it yet; a folder you pick is the same; a folder on this machine is the one turns can write into, and where files stay openable in your own editor.
- "The order", as a real <ol> so the numbering IS the sequence: (1) start Voicebox on the machine whose files you want to use — that server is what saves them; (2) create a project and choose where its files live; (3) if you chose a folder on this machine the loop writes there and turns save into it, while the other two are held by this page.
Every claim is one the code already makes; I did not write a sentence the app cannot back: ui.ts says a machine root is where "turns DO write" and that a picked folder or origin storage is "readable and writable only by the page until page-side writes land (voicebox-beads-2cf)". The dialog repeats the choice in the same order and keeps the per-destination sentence, so the screen and the dialog cannot contradict each other.
The new test asserts the guide is VISIBLE (not behind a toggle), that it answers what/why/order, that the order is an <ol> with three visible steps, and that the key phrases ascend in the text — presence and order, not just presence.

title: [gate infra] The live lane cannot complete within its 600s budget on a loaded VM, so gates return UNKNOWN instead of verdicts (4/4 attempts cut)
description:
FOUND BY: voicebox-roboticon, 2026-10-07, while gating voicebox-beads-h1u0.

The pre-push gate's live lane (npm run test:live) does not finish inside the budget this VM gives it, so
gates return UNKNOWN rather than a verdict, and every lane's landing depends on the merger's integrated
gate instead. This is the general case behind the individual flakes (pca1, y82w): those name the two tests
that actually failed under load, this names the lane that cannot complete at all.

MEASURED on lane roboticon, all with VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=300 VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS=600:

| tree     | commit  | result | note |
|----------|---------|--------|------|
| 46bdc2c6 | 778b8e4 | FAIL exit 1, 707s | unit lane green (624 pass / 634), live lane cut; 0 assertion failures |
| 743147f1 | d083207 | FAIL exit 1, 914s | 2 real flakes (both pass in isolation on both trees) + 11 cancelled at the bound |
| ad6bc569 | e50d393 | FAIL exit 1, 713s | unit lane green (553 pass / 0 fail), 0 assertion failures |
| 743147f1 | d083207 | live lane TIMED OUT, budget 600s, elapsed 601s (exit 124) | verdict arrived late; tail is a mass of 'Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved' for every live test file, i.e. the agent was killed mid-run |

The 600s live bound was reached four times out of four attempts on this box. Nothing here says the code

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE (recorded per coord's instruction, 2026-10-07).

The gate's live bound is a VM-wide setting, not a per-lane or per-job one: fleet-check reads its command from ~/.fleet/check.conf (CHECK_CMD/CHECK_TIMEOUT) and there is NO env-var or flag override - exporting VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS before calling fleet-check does nothing, because the conf assigns CHECK_CMD unconditionally. That file is shared by every lane on this box.

DEFAULT MEASURED BEHAVIOUR under load: with CHECK_CMD="VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=300 VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS=600 npm run gate", the live lane was cut at its 600s bound in six consecutive gates (707s, 914s, 713s, 601s, 600s, and 1101s) with the unit lane green in each. Exit 124 = completion unknown, not a verdict, and fleet-check caches nothing for a KILLED run - so a lane on a loaded VM cannot obtain a PASS, and every landing depends on the merger's integrated gate instead.

RAISED 2026-10-07 for voicebox-beads-h1u0 (coord decision (b)): CHECK_CMD now uses VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS=1200 with CHECK_TIMEOUT=3000, so unit 300s + live 1200s fits inside the bound with headroom. Backup of the previous conf: /tmp/check.conf.orig. This affects EVERY lane on the VM, not just roboticon - it buys completion at the cost of longer slot occupancy, which is the tradeoff to schedule on.

Also worth knowing, learned while refreshing that config: a FAIL record whose recorded `cmd` differs from the current CHECK_CMD does NOT short-circuit, so changing the bound makes the same tree re-runnable; and a KILLED run caches nothing and deletes its record, so the next ask runs again.

WHAT FAILED. Gate for voicebox-beads-pca1 tree cdaf7437d3a61dd8c3f227b3ea52c24425bc0db0 (sha 5ea16e3): FAIL rc 1, secs 164, live lane (npm run test:live). Log: /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/cdaf7437d3a61dd8c3f227b3ea52c24425bc0db0.log (lines 1109, 1152-1155).

A probe that times out under contention and is retried could add a second overlapping start/end pair while the first is still open, which would read as peak 5 with the pool still at 4. I have not confirmed that; it is the first thing to check, and it decides what the fix is.

comments.text:
OWNERSHIP SCOPED, with a focused reproduction. The fix surface is genuinely split, so I am proposing before editing anything - and the Voicebox-owned half is small, measured, and reproducible.

FOCUSED REPRODUCTION OF THE VOICEBOX-OWNED GAP (deterministic, ~40s):
  A harness parent started through tests/lib/server.mjs, then sent SIGTERM - which is exactly what a graceful gate timeout sends - left its detached server ALIVE and reparented to PID 1. Measured: parent 3940506, its detached child 3940516; after SIGTERM the parent is gone and the child is "YES - LEAKED". Cleaned up afterwards by exact PID (0 survivors).
  Cause: tests/lib/server.mjs:50 registers ONLY process.on("exit"), and Node does not emit "exit" for SIGTERM. tests/lib/cdp.mjs already does this correctly (:52 exit, :58-66 SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP), so the fix is to mirror the block that already exists next door into the file that is missing it.

WHAT VOICEBOX OWNS (mine, small):
  1. tests/lib/server.mjs:50 - add the SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP reapers that cdp.mjs:58-66 already has. This is the leak above.
  2. tools/page-acceptance.mjs:112 - spawns a detached Chromium with a killChromium() helper but no exit/signal registration, so it relies on its caller.
  3. tests/voicebox.test.mjs:284 - spawns a detached Chromium inside the test body with try/finally only.
  4. scripts/pre-push.sh:177 - the live lane's DEFAULT budget is 400s while this box measures the live lane at 579-766s (the VM conf currently overrides it to 1200, so the pain is mitigated but the default is stale). Options: raise the default, or split npm run test:live (package.json:13 runs a server lane then a browser lane, already serial) into bounded sub-runs so a loaded box can still produce a verdict. I would want coord's preference before changing a default that affects every lane.

WHAT VOICEBOX CANNOT FIX (foreign, ~/fleet - proposal only, no edit from me):
  1. ~/fleet/bin/fleet-check:63 - the bound is `fleet-heavy timeout -k 30 <bound> bash -c "..."`. Measured on this box (GNU timeout 9.4): timeout signals only ITS OWN process group, and every Voicebox fixture spawns servers and browsers with Node `detached: true` (tests/lib/server.mjs:141, tests/lib/cdp.mjs:102, tools/page-acceptance.mjs:112, tests/voicebox.test.mjs:284), which is setsid - so a bound can never reach them. Probe evidence: `timeout -k 2 1 bash -c 'bash -c "sleep 40" & wait'` -> no orphan; `timeout -k 2 1 bash -c 'setsid sleep 40 & sleep 40'` -> orphan survives, reparented to PID 1. Nothing in fleet-check or fleet-heavy reaps grandchildren; the only collector is the VM reaper with FLEET_REAP_MAX_MIN=120, which is precisely why the leaked server lived 122 minutes (reaper.jsonl:32, lane roboticon).
     FIX: give the job its own session and, on the bound (and after the -k 30 escalation), sweep /proc for processes whose session or process group belongs to the job - or record child pids at spawn - then SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL them. This is the durable fix for every repo on the VM, not just Voicebox.
  2. ~/fleet/bin/fleet-check:42 - `--stop` kills only the wrapper's process group, so it cannot reach a stage running inside run_stage's OWN group (scripts/pre-push.sh:121 gives every stage its own timeout, hence its own group). A stopped gate can therefore leave the stage subtree running under its own inner bound.
  3. ~/fleet/bin/fleet-check:80 - a KILLED run deletes its own record ("a kill is not a verdict: the next ask runs again"), so cut runs leave no JSON evidence. The scout confirmed no `"state":"KILLED"` record exists on disk; only .log files survive. Keeping the record with state KILLED (or moving it aside) would make cut runs auditable - this cost me real forensics time earlier today.

PID EVIDENCE ALREADY ON RECORD (found, not invented):
  - ~/.fleet/reaper.jsonl:32 - the 122-minute leak: lane roboticon, `.../node /home/exedev/worktrees/voicebox-roboticon/server.mjs`, why "running 122 min (limit 120)", dry:false.
  - The same class elsewhere: reaper.jsonl:24 (lane roboticon, /tmp/vb826z-drive/server.mjs, 121 min) and :31 (lane miniapps, 121 min); reaper.jsonl:12-29 shows orphaned 2-PID Chrome trees at 19-45 min.
  - Named pids from this bead's earlier comment: the miniapps gate's Chrome 3396187 (profile /tmp/voicebox-cdp-frFOoT, 10 children) and detached server 2977345, both reparented to PID 1 (both gone now).
  - Four 600s-budget cut logs on disk match the bead's "4/4 attempts cut": 743147f1, ad6bc569, 806b8fe3, 77553897 - all ending "[gate] pre-push REFUSED: live (npm run test:live) - TIMED OUT - budget 600s, elapsed 600/601s (exit 124)".

Revision 6edfdc1, tree a53c5b046dcf3255598b599bf90bb0aed22154bf, branch fleet/roboticon-y82w, one file (+32/-4 in tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs), no production code. Gate RUNNING; independent review f1f7dbe5 in flight.

THE DIAGNOSIS: the assertion was wrong, not the app. The page has exactly ONE interrupt sender - public/audio-client.js:800, reached only from the barge-in detector - and the client re-arms that detector on ANY incoming model frame (public/audio-client.js:468-473: playbackActive/bargeInArmed/emit("agent-speaking")). Its documented property is one interrupt PER SPEAKING PHASE, pinned deterministically in tests/client-audio.test.mjs ("one utterance sends ONE interrupt, and a new speaking phase arms the detector again": bargeIns 1 for the rest of an utterance, then 2 after a new chunk). So a late in-flight echo is enough: the fixture schedules its 20ms echo with the paused check at SCHEDULE time, so an echo already in flight still lands after the flush, and with three speech frames (about 96ms at 512 samples / 16kHz) the next qualifying frame fires a second, legitimate {type:"interrupt",source:"page"}. The old assertion counted frames across speaking phases and demanded exactly 1, so load - which widens exactly that window - turned a correct second interrupt into "2 !== 1".

REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY (this is the evidence the bead asked for, base vs fix): let the model speak again while the fixture's person is still talking - inject one sustained loud model buffer (0x8000) while the 2.5s speech passage is running. The SHIPPED assertion then fails on the base tree with exactly the recorded message and numbers: "the page must not ask a model that already stopped to stop again · 2 !== 1 (actual 2, expected 1)". The same stimulus against the fixed test PASSES 3/3 runs. So the flake is no longer a race to be waited out; it is a stimulus I can apply on demand.

THE FIX, and one correction my own driving forced. The test now waits for the fixture's own utterance to end before anything is counted (its duration is derived from the WAV spec rather than repeated as prose, so the wait cannot drift from the stimulus), and the provider-interrupt assertion became a DELTA: the model's own interrupt must not ADD a page frame. My first version took that baseline before the utterance finished - and my own repro caught it: during the remaining speech the detector legitimately fired again, the baseline went stale, and the comparison blamed the provider's interrupt for the detector's work. The baseline is now taken after the person stops talking, which is what makes the comparison deterministic; that first version would have moved the flake rather than removed it.

THE REPAIR IS NOT A WEAKENING, and that is measured too. Mutant M1 - make the provider's interrupt also put a frame on the wire (drop `source === "page" &&` from the send guard) - makes the fixed test FAIL on the new delta assertion, so the assertion still catches the regression it exists for. Mutant M2 - remove the detector's one-shot latch - stays GREEN, which matches the app's own recorded note in public/audio-client.js that the latch is a second guard no fixture can distinguish because the FLUSH ends the phase first; my test behaves like the existing suite on it rather than inventing a distinction.

VERIFIED: tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs 3/3 normal, 2/2 under synthetic load, 3/3 against the deterministic second-phase stimulus (which fails the base); tests/client-audio.test.mjs 25/25 (the app-side property pin, untouched because no production code changed); tests/ldxa-interrupt-seam.test.mjs 2/2.

FOR COORD, a separate question, not touched here and not filed as a bead without your word: the tolerated behaviour is that the page can ask a model that has already stopped to stop again, because it cannot distinguish a new turn's first audio frame from stale audio that was already flushed - there is no per-turn marker in the client today. The test repair is correct either way, but if you want the protocol to carry a turn marker, that is its own bead with this reproduction as its case.

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
REAPER KILL, MINE, AND THE CAUSE IS A PROCESS MISTAKE I MADE ON THIS BEAD. It killed a leftover `/home/exedev/worktrees/voicebox-roboticon/server.mjs` running 122 min at 0% CPU - a dev server from my own test/probe runs, not a long job I was waiting on.

CAUSE, not a guess: while cleaning up the synthetic-load burners for this bead I used `pgrep -f '[w]hile :; do :; done'`, and my OWN command line contained the literal string the pattern matched, so the kill loop SIGKILLed my own shell (exit 137, mid-command). A SIGKILLed shell never runs the test's `after()` hook or the `finally` that stops `server.mjs`, so that server survived and the reaper eventually collected it. Same class as the earlier lesson in my notes about `pgrep -f` self-matching, in a new shape: the bracket trick does not save you when the literal pattern text appears elsewhere in the same command.

WHAT I CHANGED, so it cannot recur:
1. No `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f` for process cleanup at all. I scan /proc directly in a short python script that skips my own pid and parent, and kill by EXACT pid. That is what cleaned the burners and what I used to check for leftovers here.
2. After any run that ends abnormally (kill, timeout, signal), check for orphaned children before moving on. On this check there were none of mine left: the only server.mjs processes were the hub's two fleet servers (ppid 1, 26h old, not mine to touch), the reviewer's server in its own /tmp tree, and the one my RUNNING gate is using - all correctly left alone.
3. Load generators are started with their own `timeout` so they expire even if my cleanup never runs, and they are killed by exact pid, never by pattern.

Not a correctness problem for this bead: the gate for 6edfdc1 is still RUNNING and unaffected (it starts and stops its own servers per test, and the killed process was 2 hours old). No human action needed; recorded here as the reaper asked, and it will be in the y82w handoff.

The most consistent candidate is this bead's own review process (f1f7dbe5), because checking out ee97707 is exactly what a base-vs-fix comparison needs, and my brief for it said to copy to /tmp rather than drive my worktree. I have steered it to stay in its own /tmp copy and not to run git in my worktree; if its report rests on measurements taken in my worktree while it was detached, those measurements are void and I will re-derive them myself rather than accept them.

NOTHING WAS LOST. 6edfdc1 is committed and pushed: origin/fleet/roboticon-y82w = 6edfdc1. Before restoring I verified the working tree matched the committed content exactly (`git diff 6edfdc1 -- tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs` = 0 lines), then checked the branch out again: fleet/roboticon-y82w @ 6edfdc1, tree a53c5b046dcf3255598b599bf90bb0aed22154bf, clean. The re-run measures that tree.

TWO PROCESS CORRECTIONS, both from this incident and not theory:
1. Do not `killpg` a process that was started from my own session. The gate had been launched from my tool call, so it shared MY process group; my group kill took my own shell down with it (exit 137). Earlier in this same bead the same class of mistake - a pgrep pattern matching my own command line - killed my shell and orphaned a dev server the reaper then collected. Kill EXACT pids, and build any search string at runtime from a file path so it cannot appear in the command that does the killing.

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
REVIEW f1f7dbe5 ON 6edfdc1 = APPROVE, with two P2 findings, one of which is about the robustness of this fix's own wait. It drove everything independently in its own /tmp copies and reached the same base-vs-fix result I did: base FAILS with the recorded "2 !== 1 · the page must not ask a model that already stopped to stop again", fixed PASSES 3/3 against the same injected second speaking phase.

ITS MUTANTS, which is the evidence I most wanted, since the risk in a test repair is weakening the assertion:
  (a) drop `source === "page" &&` so the provider's interrupt also sends a frame -> RED on the new delta assertion (2 !== 1). The regression this test exists to catch is still caught.
  (b) disable the page's own interrupt send -> RED twice over: "playback must be flushed, not left playing" and then "the page must ask the model to stop, saw []".
  (c) remove the new utterance wait -> GREEN on an idle box but flakes under load / with a second speaking phase, for exactly the reason I fixed: the baseline would be taken while the speech is still flowing.
  (d) send two interrupt frames per barge-in -> GREEN here but RED in three tests in tests/client-audio.test.mjs ("one interruption, one frame: 2 !== 1"), which is the right division of labour: this browser test is about the page's behaviour across an utterance, and the single-frame invariant is pinned at the client level where it is deterministic.

P2-1, ABOUT THIS FIX, and I am recording it rather than waving it through: my wait bounds the utterance by WALL CLOCK (UTTERANCE_MS + 400). The reviewer measured Chromium's fake-audio device lagging that spec: speech ended at +5576ms idle but +5866ms under 4-core load, leaving 34ms of margin against my 400ms allowance - and the original flake was recorded at load average ~8, where that lag can exceed the allowance. If the wait returns before the audio device actually finishes, the baseline can be taken while speech is still flowing, and a stale-echo second phase would fail the delta assertion: the flake could come back in a narrower form. Its suggested remedy is to wait on the app's own observed input instead of the clock (public/audio-client.js tracks `inputFloor`, which drops as soon as the input goes quiet), and I agree that is the correct shape. I am NOT folding it into this tree: the gate for a53c5b04 is running, the reviewer marked it non-blocking, and the merger has been told it can land this revision - so the honest move is a follow-up decision by coord, not a silent rework that invalidates a gate and races the merge.
  Also independently measured by it, and new to me: Chromium LOOPS `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture`, so the fixture's 3s-quiet/2.5s-speech cycle recurs; the provider-interrupt section completes well inside the following quiet passage, and the injected tail it uses is a zero-amplitude buffer, so it cannot itself trigger a barge-in.

P2-2 (protocol) agrees with what this bead already raised and coord has since captured: binary model audio frames carry no turn/epoch identity, so the client cannot tell stale in-flight audio from a cancelled turn apart from the first frame of a new one, and re-arms barge-in on it (public/audio-client.js:468-473). That is now BLOCKED P3 voicebox-beads-flxg, assigned coord, pending a Paul product decision. The reviewer reached it independently, which strengthens the case rather than adding a second bead.

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
REWORK DONE per coord's blocking ruling. Revision 514cd42, tree 1681bb448209f8be4dbe300bbb8ee86093b134f9, one file (tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs), no production code. Gate RUNNING; delta review b202b21d in flight.

WHAT CHANGED. The utterance's end is now read from the APP's own view of the input instead of the clock. The wait returns when `inputFloor` is back at room tone, but only after it has seen the floor lift: the barge-in can fire three frames (~96ms) into the utterance, when the floor is still at room tone, so "quiet now" alone can be true while the person is still talking - the same shape of blind spot as pca1's shape-only settle. Two bounds, both explicit: a 1200ms minimum rise since the barge-in was observed (a LOWER bound, so it can only lengthen the wait and cannot cause the early return the clock could), and an overall limit of the fixture's duration + 8000ms so it cannot hang.

THE THRESHOLDS COME FROM A MEASUREMENT, NOT FROM ME. The app's `inputFloor` across the fixture's utterance: room tone 0.0007-0.005 through the quiet passage, climbing to 0.124 once the 0.2-peak voice is tracked, then back to room tone. 0.02 sits between those with a wide margin.

MY FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG AND I AM CORRECTING IT. It reported a peak of 0.021 and "the voice stopped at +286ms", which would have meant the threshold was useless. Both numbers were artifacts: it sampled the fixture's SECOND quiet passage and exited early, because Chromium LOOPS --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture so the quiet/speech cycle recurs. The corrected probe requires the voice to be tracked before looking for its end. The wrong reading nearly sent me to adding a new production observable, which would have been unnecessary.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO, stated rather than glossed, because coord asked for it explicitly: reproduce the old wait's failure under synthetic load on this VM. Three attempts - 8 burners (voice observed ending +5567ms vs the 5900ms wall-clock point = 333ms margin), page-CPU throttle 3 (816ms) and 6 (782ms) - all left the clock wait with margin, so I cannot show the baseline failing here and I am not claiming I did. The case for the rework is the reviewer's measurement (+366ms lag against a 400ms allowance under 4-core load, and the flake was recorded at load ~8) plus the structural point that a wall clock is not tied to the device it bounds. The wait is now tied to the app's observation by construction, and that observation's separation is measured above.

NOT WEAKENED: with public/audio-client.js mutated so the provider's interrupt also sends a frame, the REVISED test fails on the delta assertion ("the model's own interrupt must not add a frame", 2 !== 1), so it still catches the regression it exists for.

FOCUSED: tests/ldxa-barge-in-browser.test.mjs 3/3 normal; tests/client-audio.test.mjs 25/25 (the app is untouched, so its pins must be and are); tests/ldxa-interrupt-seam.test.mjs 2/2. CLEANUP verified by exact-PID /proc scan: 0 burners, 0 orphaned servers of mine.

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
DELTA REVIEW b202b21d ON 514cd42 = APPROVE, NO FINDINGS, and it independently produced the measurement that justifies the guard I added, with its own numbers rather than mine.

THE KEY NUMBER: it sampled `inputFloor` every 50ms across the fixture. The barge-in fires at +3112ms - about 112ms after speech onset - when the floor is only 0.01523. Since 0.01523 < 0.02, a bare room-tone test would have returned IMMEDIATELY with 2.4 seconds of speech still to come, taking the baseline mid-utterance: exactly the premature-return hole the minimum-rise guard closes. The 1200ms lockout holds until +4312ms, by which point the floor has climbed past 0.12. That is the reasoning I gave for the guard, now measured by someone else.

ITS TRAJECTORY, for the record: 0.00261-0.00296 through the quiet passage; 0.00723 at +3055ms; 0.01523 at the barge-in; 0.12390-0.18723 while the voice is tracked; then a plunge on the first quiet frame at +5560ms to 0.00437 and 0.00101 by +5613ms. So the 0.02 threshold sits ~7x above room tone and ~6x below the tracked voice.

ITS DEFEAT TESTS all behaved: a missing `inputFloor` field evaluates false and fails cleanly at the 13.5s bound with the descriptive label instead of hanging; audio that never quiets also fails at the bound; and a fixture whose floor never lifts cannot fire a barge-in at all, because the detector needs >= 0.06 over three consecutive frames. Its negative mutation (provider's interrupt also sends a frame) fails the revised test on the delta assertion, so the repair still polices the regression it exists for.

ON MY REPRODUCTION GAP: it tested it rather than taking my word. With 8 worker threads plus a background gate on this 2-core VM (load 6.7 to >8) it measured ~60ms of device lag, ~340ms of margin - so it could not reproduce the old wait's failure here either, and it said so plainly instead of inferring that the failure must exist somewhere. It also agreed the fix is necessary regardless, because virtual-audio buffer lag is scheduler-dependent and the previous reviewer measured +366ms under 4-core contention.

Gate for tree 1681bb44 is RUNNING; queued only on a genuine PASS.

comments.text:
COORD'S REVIEW CHECKLIST MAPPED TO EVIDENCE ON THIS EXACT TREE (514cd42 / 1681bb448209f8be4dbe300bbb8ee86093b134f9). No duplicate review was commissioned: the delta review b202b21d already drove every item below on this tree, and I am recording the mapping rather than spending another reviewer run on it.

1. DRIVE app inputFloor quiet->lift->quiet with real fake audio: b202b21d sampled snapshot().inputFloor every 50ms across the fixture: 0.00261-0.00296 through the quiet passage; 0.00723 at +3055ms; 0.01523 at the barge-in; 0.12390-0.18723 while the voice is tracked; then 0.00437 at +5560ms and 0.00101 by +5613ms, back to 0.00071-0.00074. My own trajectory probe measured the same separation independently (room tone 0.0007-0.005, voice 0.124).
2. VERIFY an early barge-in (~96ms) does not prematurely settle: measured, not reasoned - the barge-in fires at +3112ms, about 112ms after onset, when the floor is 0.01523, which is BELOW the 0.02 room-tone threshold. A bare room-tone wait would therefore have settled immediately with ~2.4s of speech still to come. The 1200ms minimum rise holds the wait until +4312ms, by which point the floor is past 0.12. This is the item that justifies the guard.
3. VERIFY the explicit timeout stays bounded: with `inputFloor` absent from the snapshot, `undefined < 0.02` is false, so the wait runs to its bound and fails cleanly: "no the person to stop talking (the app's own input floor back to room tone) within 13500ms". Audio that never quiets behaves the same. No hang, no silent pass.
4. VERIFY the looping fixture does not fool the floor probe: Chromium loops --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture, so the quiet/speech cycle recurs - b202b21d observed the plunge at +5560ms as the file loops back to its quiet head, and my corrected margin probe reports the FIRST quiet transition after the voice is tracked (+5567ms under 8 burners, +5084/+5118ms under page-CPU throttle 3/6), which leaves the whole following quiet window for the provider-interrupt section. The earlier bogus reading (peak 0.021, "stopped at +286ms") came from a probe that sampled the SECOND quiet passage and exited early; that probe bug is fixed and recorded.

So: no baseline failure is claimed. What is carried as risk is the peer measurement of +366ms lag against a 400ms allowance under 4-core contention, at the load average the original flake was recorded at - which is thin enough that the previous revision's safety depended on the box being kind, and coord ruled it blocking on that basis.
THE ACTUAL REGRESSION TEST for this bead remains the deterministic second-speaking-phase reproduction: with the model made to speak again while the fixture's person is still talking, the shipped assertion fails on the base tree with the recorded "2 !== 1 - the page must not ask a model that already stopped to stop again", and the fixed test passes that same stimulus.

title: [gate flake] modal-panels 'timed out waiting for changelog to close' fails under load on BOTH trees (3/4 pass)
description:
MEASURED on 2026-10-07 at load average ~8 (another lane's heavy gate holding the slot).

Failing assertion (from the full gate of tree 743147f1, log ~/.fleet/checks/743147f1f9aa2e341fe745e9eaa5668fb88219e0.log):

  tests/modal-panels.test.mjs:63
  ✖ modal panels: extensions, environments, and harnesses open as native modal dialogs in the room (21116ms)
    Error: timed out waiting for changelog to close (dialog closed, aria-expanded false, focus returned); last value false
      at waitForDialogFullyClosed (tests/modal-panels.test.mjs:49 -> tests/lib/cdp.mjs:601)

REPRODUCTION IS BOTH WAYS, so this is a flake and not a regression in any one branch:

  tree                             runs   pass  fail
  e50d393 (feature branch)         4      3     1
  56b3fde (origin/main, merge-base) 4      3     1

Both trees failed once and passed three times, in isolation, back to back.

WHY IT IS LOAD-SENSITIVE: the changelog dialog's content comes from GET /api/changelog, which resolves the
commit list on the server (server.mjs:3999, cached in changelogCache at :2088) and then the test waits for
the dialog to report fully closed: dialog closed, aria-expanded false, focus returned. Under contention the
close/focus-return check misses its deadline (21-23s observed). The failing sub-check is the changelog one;
the other three panels pass in the same run.

NEXT ACTION: give the close-check a deadline that reflects the server round trip, or assert the dialog state
after the changelog response resolves instead of racing it. Do not paper over it with a longer timeout
without saying so - a flake that passes on retry is still a flake.
close_reason: Landed in 065e147; fleet-check tree cc89590e13fdc6aef80f52816ee3499c5556fe33 exit 0

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
CLAIMED AND FIXED: the mechanism is a coordinate click racing the changelog dialog's own relayout, measured, not inferred.

MECHANISM (measured in real Chromium at 1000x800). The changelog dialog is 197px tall while its fetch is in flight and 606px once 30 commit cards render: the close button moves dx=-10, dy=-205. page.click resolves the target's centre and then dispatches the events at those coordinates two round trips later, so a click resolved before the payload lands goes into the content instead of the button: the dialog never closes and the 15s close-wait reports "timed out waiting for changelog to close" with no cause in it. The gate's own stack frame named the first close after the changelog opens (tests/modal-panels.test.mjs:108), which is the only coordinate click inside a dialog whose content is still arriving. Driven and confirmed: clicking the pre-growth point does NOT close the dialog.

THE FIX, at both ends of the race. (1) tests/modal-panels.test.mjs waits for the changelog content to stop saying "Loading changes…" before driving the dialog - the race is removed by construction, not made less likely. (2) tests/lib/cdp.mjs verifies where a click would land (elementFromPoint against the target or its descendants) and re-resolves a target that is still settling, up to three attempts, then throws naming the selector and the point instead of clicking into the dark. (3) The commit carries a Docs-checked trailer: docs/12-pre-push-gate.md names tests/lib/cdp.mjs only for browser process-group cleanup, which this does not touch, and no document describes click semantics.

EVIDENCE. Deterministic A/B on the same tree with the payload delayed: the old behaviour clicks while the status is still "Loading changes…" with the button at y=277 (payload still to come, so any resolved coordinates were stale); the fixed behaviour clicks after "Showing 30 recent commits:" with the button at its final y=72, so the geometry cannot move afterwards. The guard was driven red/green with an overlay inside the dialog: the old harness reported "ok" while the click missed, the new one refuses by name. Focused: modal-panels 2/2, settings-dialog 8/8 (a heavy modal/click file, unaffected). 6/6 runs of the affected test under synthetic load.

HONEST LIMITS. The pre-fix baseline also passed its loaded runs (5/5), so the loaded runs alone do NOT discriminate - the deterministic A/B and the guard drive do. I could not make the old behaviour fail on demand: the click window is a couple of milliseconds, so randomised delays hit it rarely; that is why the evidence above is the measured mechanism plus an invariant comparison rather than a statistical reproduction.

ONE SELF-INFLICTED DETOUR, recorded because it wasted a push: my reproduction burners (4 CPU hogs on a 2-vCPU box) left load at 20, and the push that followed failed the pre-push unit lane. Re-run through the heavy queue, the unit lane is 563 tests / 553 pass / 0 fail / 10 skipped with the guard in place, so that failure was contention, not the change. Lesson: reproduce load with the smallest burner set and let the box settle before a gate-bearing push.

comments.author: voicebox-roboticon
comments.text:
REVIEW 4918973a = CHANGES REQUESTED: one P1 that is real and mine, one P2 wording. Both verified independently here, fixed in staging, and they go into a NEW tree after the running gate (no worktree edits while a gate is live).

P1 (tests/lib/cdp.mjs:505) - my guard matched an ANCESTOR of the target: `hit === node || node.contains(hit) || hit.contains(node)`. Matching an ancestor accepts a click that landed on the container instead of the target, so an element that cannot receive a click at all is reported as clicked. The reviewer is right and the `rect` helper in the same file already tests descendants only, so the extra clause was an inversion on my part, not a design choice.

VERIFIED HERE, independently of the reviewer: a button with pointer-events:none inside the page container. elementFromPoint at its centre resolves to the container (an ancestor), page.click reported "ok", and the button's own click handler fired 0 times - a silent failure of exactly the kind the guard exists to catch. That is the guard masking a miss, which is worse than the flake it was added for.

P2 (tests/lib/cdp.mjs:513) - the refusal message asserted "the element moved while its content loaded", but a target can equally be obscured (a popover, a sticky header, an in-dialog overlay). Reworded to "the element moved or is obscured".

STAGED AND PROVEN, in a /tmp worktree so the live gate is untouched: the guard's contract is now pinned by a new test (tests/cdp-click-guard.test.mjs) that drives three cases in a real browser - an ordinary target is clicked exactly once, a target whose centre resolves to its own child still counts as a hit, and an unhittable target is REFUSED with the selector named and zero handler calls. Against the current inverted guard that test FAILS (red); with the fix applied it PASSES (green).

The reviewer also drove the guard for false refusals and found none that were wrong: top-layer dialog content correctly beats a body-level overlay (a body overlay is inert under a modal), mid-animation targets get re-resolved by the retry loop, a target under a popover or a sticky header is now refused rather than silently clicked, the loop is bounded at three attempts, and it confirmed the Docs-checked trailer is true (docs/12 names cdp.mjs only for process-group cleanup, and no document describes click semantics).

comments.text:
GATE FAILED for 7d66941 (exit 1, 925s) and it was RIGHT: my fix regressed an unrelated test. Corrected revision is 5ea16e3, tree cdaf7437, one change - 32 lines in tests/modal-panels.test.mjs - with its own gate RUNNING and fresh review 380e13b1 in flight.

WHAT THE GATE CAUGHT. The live lane's only failure was tests/room-explorer-ui.test.mjs ("no element matches .file-open[data-file='from-folder.txt']"). I first reasoned it was load-related, which was WRONG, and the controlled comparison said so plainly: the same file in isolation failed 4 of 5 runs on my tree and passed 5 of 5 on the merge-base ee97707. A regression, not a flake.

THE CAUSE WAS MY CLICK GUARD, and it took two wrong hypotheses to find. Isolation proved the guard alone was responsible (3/3 fail with only it, 3/3 pass without). Instrumenting the test moved the failure from the file row to ".folder-close-btn ON RETRY", which proved the retry's second lookup was the problem; making the retry stop scrolling and tolerate a transiently absent element halved the failures but did not remove them. The real cause is line 132: `while (await page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector(".folder-close-btn") !== null)) await page.click(".folder-close-btn")` - a click-if-exists loop closing chips that the app removes asynchronously. A coordinate guard adds a round trip per click and re-resolves before dispatching, so it changes exactly the timing such a loop depends on.

SO THE GUARD IS WITHDRAWN, deliberately and in writing (it is in the commit message, not silently dropped). tests/lib/cdp.mjs is byte-identical to the merge-base. Two reasons, both measured: its blast radius is 186 click sites, and the flake's root cause is removed by the settle wait anyway. A coordinate-click guard is worth doing properly, as its own bead, with the loop pattern above as a test case - it should not ride behind a flake fix.

THE REVIEWER'S P1 IS ALSO RESOLVED BY REMOVAL. The reviewer found the guard accepted an ANCESTOR of the target (`hit.contains(node)`), so a pointer-events:none element was reported as clicked with its handler never running; I reproduced that independently (0 handler calls while page.click reported "ok"). It was an inversion on my part - the `rect` helper in the same file already tests descendants only - and it is gone with the guard. P2 (the misleading "element moved while its content loaded" message) is gone with it too.

WHAT SHIPS. One change: the settle wait. It is now generic rather than changelog-specific - it waits for the DIALOG'S SHAPE to stop changing rather than for particular text, so any terminal state counts (empty list, error) and it does not depend on what an endpoint returned on this box; bounded at 15s because the app's changelog fetch aborts at 10s. It runs after every panel open, costing about a quarter second each for panels that are already stable.

VERIFIED. tests/modal-panels.test.mjs 5/5 runs; tests/room-explorer-ui.test.mjs (the file the guard broke) 5/5 with the guard removed; tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs 8/8. The delayed-payload A/B stands: old sequence clicks while the dialog reads "Loading changes…" with the button at y=277, fixed sequence clicks after "Showing 30 recent commits:" with the button at its final y=72. STILL HONEST ABOUT THE LIMIT: I could not make the pre-fix behaviour fail on demand (the click window is a couple of milliseconds); the evidence is the measurement, the invariant comparison and the A/B, not a statistical reproduction.

comments.text:
REVISION 05f3b7a (tree cc89590e), two commits on top of ee97707, one file, +54 lines in tests/modal-panels.test.mjs. Gate RUNNING, delta review f485032a in flight.

REVIEW 380e13b1 ON 5ea16e3 = APPROVE WITH ONE P1, and the P1 was the bead's own scenario rather than a corner case, so I took it rather than deferring it. A shape-only settle cannot tell "finished" from "still fetching and nothing has changed yet": two samples a poll apart are identical while the payload is in flight, so with the response slower than one 250ms sample - which is what contention does, and contention is where this flake was reported - the wait returned with the fetch still running and the close click went back to racing the relayout it was added to avoid.

THE P1 IS FIXED AND THE FIX IS DRIVEN, not argued. Same page, same 1200ms delayed payload, both helpers measured:
  shape-only    returned at  424ms  height=197  status="Loading changes..."          (fetch still in flight)
  loading-aware returned at 1663ms  height=606  status="Showing 30 recent commits:" (content really there)
The wait now first awaits the panel's own loading statement clearing - "Loading changes..." on #changelog-status, "Checking host programs..." on #harnesses-status - and then waits for the shape to stop changing. It still accepts any terminal outcome (empty list, error); an absent or already-finished status returns immediately, so panels that are not fetching pay nothing; the whole wait stays bounded at 15s because the app's changelog fetch aborts at 10s.

The reviewer's other probes: empty changelog settles in 256ms, HTTP 500 in 260ms, and an endlessly animating dialog is NOT masked - the wait runs all 60 samples and throws "changelog content never settled: still changing shape".

THE PREVIOUS TREE'S GATE FAILED, and it was not mine. cdaf7437 FAILed rc 1 at 164s on tests/sandbox-subdirectories.test.mjs ("probe fan-out exceeded the bound: peak 5 concurrent git spawns"), a test landed earlier with bead 8d3n. Security Boundary Analysis per coordinator guidance:
1. Public Artifact Leak Risk: The upstream composite action PaulKinlan/agents/.github/actions/factory unconditionally executes actions/upload-artifact@v4 on the findings/ directory (step 4, 'if: always()'). On public repositories like Voicebox, GitHub Actions workflow artifacts are downloadable by any logged-in GitHub account.

comments.author: voicebox-miniapps
comments.text:
Root cause analysis of persistent PID 1406163:
1. /proc/1406163/status shows NSpid: 1406163 1 — it is PID 1 of Chromium's internal zygote PID namespace.
2. Because tests/lib/cdp.mjs and tools/page-acceptance.mjs do not pass --no-zygote, Chromium forks a zygote process entering a new PID namespace.
3. In Linux kernel semantics, PID 1 inside a PID namespace has all default signal handlers dropped (including SIGKILL/SIGTERM). When the browser parent aborted without closing the zygote control socket, the zygote was stranded in do_wait for zombie child 1406253 (NSpid 36 1), unkillable and consuming 0 MB RAM.
4. Remediation in uv1q: Launch Chrome with --no-zygote and --disable-crash-reporter in an isolated process group, and explicitly handle child process teardown so zygote namespaces are never created or orphaned.

comments.author: voicebox-miniapps
comments.text:
Started implementation on branch fleet/miniapps-uv1q (based on 21fa576):
1. Pass --no-zygote and --disable-crash-reporter to browser launches in tests/lib/cdp.mjs and tools/page-acceptance.mjs.
2. In tests/lib/cdp.mjs, spawn Chrome in its own process group (detached: true) and kill the entire process group (-child.pid) during teardown/abandon.
3. In tools/page-acceptance.mjs, wrap top-level spawn/teardown in try-finally and handle process group termination.
4. Add negative throw-control test verifying unhandled errors or premature teardown cleanly reaps all Chrome child/helper processes without leaking.
