title: Factory audit yield: decide the engine and agent subset that actually produces publishable findings
description:
The workflow is wired and landed (voicebox-beads-xsjw: .github/workflows/agent-factory.yml + .github/factory-agents.json, cron stripped as a cost gate). What is NOT yet demonstrated on a runner is the acceptance criterion 'files findings as beads', and the runner has now twice shown why.

MEASURED YIELD, voicebox, deepseek-chat, modern-web + docs-drift:
- modern-web: 1 finding from 151 deterministic candidates, severity HIGH. Voicebox is public, so the factory's own embargo withholds critical/high from any synced tracker — that run files ZERO beads by design (report artifact carried it; 16 lines).
- docs-drift: 0 findings from 374 candidates, with a false 'no candidates were provided' justification (filed factory-side as agents-<see agents board>). Zero beads.
So across two agents and two runs the publishable output is empty. This is a triage-quality/engine question, not a wiring defect.

THE DECISION (Paul's): what is worth paying for here.
1. Engine: deepseek-chat is the cheap proven path but has produced almost nothing usable on this repo. The action also supports pi/claude/antigravity engines; a measured comparison on the same candidate payloads is the honest way to choose, and it is also the first step of the docs-drift question above.
2. Subset: docs/21-factory-agent-proposal.md (voicebox-beads-h0nv) ranks the agents voicebox's own history justifies — qa-station (26 defect beads), test-gap (14), docs-write (pairs with docs-drift), threat-model (11 + 7), vuln-discovery/verify (11), perf-review (5). Several of those are medium-shaped, which is what the beads embargo lets through, so they are likelier than modern-web to make 'files findings as beads' observable.
3. Cadence: the nightly cron is stripped pending this. Re-arming is one commented block in the workflow.

EVIDENCE ALREADY ON FILE: bead xsjw carries the runner run IDs (36708984621 accidental full-matrix run: two model calls, two artifacts, zero beads), the three proven refusals, and the local reproductions. Nothing here needs re-deriving.
close_reason: Documented factory engine comparison and enabled medium-shaped agent quartet in docs/25-factory-agent-proposal.md and .github/factory-agents.json

comments.author: voicebox-glmflash1
comments.text:
DECISION RECOMMENDATION (voicebox-glmflash1, for Paul): the publishable output is empty because the measured engine (deepseek-chat) cannot triage this repo reliably AND the one high finding it produced is embargoed on a public repo. The decision below buys the minimum that fixes both.

═══ DECISION 1 — ENGINE: run a two-engine measured comparison before any cron re-arm; deepseek-chat becomes the cost floor, not the producer. ═══
The honest state: no cross-engine evidence exists, and deciding blind repeats the deepseek spend. The comparison is bounded and decisive because the candidate payloads are ALREADY ON FILE from the xsjw runs (modern-web's 151 + docs-drift's 374 — zero new crawling cost). Run **claude** and **antigravity** on those exact payloads (the two supported alternatives with fleet triage priors; pi already = the measured deepseek path).
**The acceptance criterion, stated before the spend:** an engine earns the production slot iff on those payloads it (a) files ≥1 finding that lands as a REAL bead — medium-shaped, embargo-passing; (b) files ZERO false justifications (deepseek's fabricated "no candidates were provided" over 374 real candidates is disqualifying on first offense — a triage layer that hallucinates its own evidence poisons every downstream decision); (c) findings survive vb-factory's fingerprint/dedup. Cost per publishable bead is the tiebreak. deepseek-chat is not discarded: it stays the free/cheap floor for the negative-path acceptance runs, and loses the production slot only until it clears (a)–(c).

═══ DECISION 2 — SUBSET: enable the medium-shaped quartet; hold the embargo-trapped and the unproven. ═══
ENABLE FIRST: **qa-station, test-gap, threat-model, perf-review** — h0nv's counts are defect-history-justified (26 / 14 / 11+7 / 5) and, decisively, their finding SHAPES are medium (flake instruments, assertion strength, containment notes, perf measurements) — exactly what the public-repo embargo publishes. These four maximize the chance the acceptance criterion is observable at all.
HOLD docs-write: it pairs with docs-drift — the agent that scored 0 findings with a false justification on this repo. Hold until the engine comparison shows the chosen engine can triage docs candidates.
HOLD vuln-discovery + vuln-verify: their findings are critical/high-shaped (XSS 1i0, SSRF bxx, traversal t80/zxb) — on a public repo the embargo withholds them by design, so they structurally cannot satisfy "files findings as beads". Keep them for an internal-run variant if Paul wants security coverage regardless of publishability.
modern-web stays enabled as the baseline agent — it demonstrated reach (the HIGH finding) but cannot publish on this repo; keep it for the artifact, not the beads.

═══ DECISION 3 — CADENCE: the cron stays stripped. ═══
Re-arm nightly ONLY after the comparison produces an engine+subset that files ≥1 publishable bead; first re-arm weekly for the winning subset; nightly only if the yield holds and Paul accepts the run cost.

═══ WHAT THIS DECISIONS ═══
Two engine runs × the two lead agents' candidate payloads, scored by the stated criterion — the minimum spend that turns "almost nothing usable" into a measured engine choice. Cron, subset expansion, and the docs/vuln agents are all gated on its outcome. The comparison reuses everything on file (payloads, runner, refusal records) — the only new cost is the model calls.

A dns timeout IS diagnostic where egress is PROVEN open by the reached literal, which is the whole point of the control; make the timeout evidence conditional on the reached arm rather than deleting it.
- shape 14 — both TCP dead + dns { error: "SERVFAIL" } → stays brokenness, dns field quoted (coded resolver failure still counts in the dead branch).

title: live lane: page-writes' model-tool assertion can flake under the serial lane, then pass alone
description:
Found reviewing voicebox-beads-5i2i (branch e055453, review worktree ~/worktrees/voicebox-5i2i-review).

Symptom: 'npm run test:live' red on tests/page-writes.test.mjs — 'the live leg: a spoken write into a page-owned root lands through the channel' failed at line 206: 'the model did not call read_file' after 2024ms (assertion timeout-normal path). Immediately re-run ALONE on the same tree: 4/4 pass, that test in 6234ms.

Why it is not the 5i2i diff: page-writes has zero references to mic/data-voice/input-wave/__voiceboxMeters (grep, empty), so the CSS+render-loop change cannot reach it; the failing assertion is about the model's tool calls (read_file), i.e. model behaviour, and it changed only in latency.

Class: the 6qu concurrency/load family, but inside the SERIAL live lane: a preceding file leaves Chromium/CPU load (or the provider is slow) and the model answers without calling the tool. File-level concurrency=1 does not bound that.

Suggested handling: treat a lone tool-call assertion failure as retryable (one bounded re-run of the file) before reporting the lane red, and record the retry in the lane output so a reviewer can tell a flake from a regression.

comments.author: voicebox-e1m0
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW VERDICT: FAIL — one required item: the live test's central assertion is model-phrasing-dependent and I measured it flaky. Reviewer voicebox-e1m0 (deepseek; author glm — different family). No merge.

MEASURED (I ran tests/live-wasm-room.test.mjs twice with GEMINI_API_KEY and the real isocan shelf present):
- Run 1: FAIL. The model DID call the hash tool by name (the deterministic first assertion passed), but the spoken text was "the hash of the text abc is ending in 0015ad." and the test demands /ba7816bf/. The tool itself returned the right bytes — I called the same executor directly: { ok: true, action: "wasm", tool: "hash", returned: 32, output: "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad", digest: "5d728a29…" (the module pin), inputBytes: 3 }. So the model paraphrased a correct result; the feature worked and the assertion failed.
- Run 2: PASS (~the author's 2.3s green). One pass, one fail across two runs of the same tree: the assertion measures the model's choice of phrasing, not the room loop.

REQUIRED FIX (small, and it makes the test stronger): assert the DETERMINISTIC evidence the live path already produces. The `{type:"tool"}` frame's `calls` entries currently carry { name, ok, action } (server.mjs pushes `seen.push({ name: call.name, ok: result.ok, action: result.action ?? result.error })`). Add the tool result's returned value (a bounded slice, e.g. `result.output` for the wasm ABI) to that entry, then assert `calls[0].ok === true && /ba7816bf/.test(calls[0].output)` — the frame is already the room-loop witness, so this proves declaration → model call → correct result with no dependence on how the model speaks. Keep the model's spoken text as a logged observation, not an assertion (or drop it). Pointing the test at the digest of the MODULE (the `digest` field) would be wrong — that is the pin (5d728a29…), not the computed hash.

VERIFIED PASS (my own runs, local suites 22/22, 0 skipped — commands + wasm-shelf + wasm-room-ui):
- Declarations: liveToolDeclarations returns admitted+driven tools only, per-ABI schemas (input; a+b for buffer-abi/diff) and the digest-pinned description; unit-pinned.
- Direct dispatch: commandToAction routes an admitted name to { verb: "extension", name, args } and still returns null without the admitted set or for an unadmitted name; the args are validated downstream by the tool's own descriptor.
- The shelf loads directly through loadRegistry with the gate fail-closed into loadFailures (gate-refused-at-load), call-time rehash unchanged, executions audited like every other tool.
- UI: the extensions view renders the "Wasm shelf — digest-pinned, callable now" section with description, digest prefix and last-run status, and the catalogue no longer double-lists `wasm-shelf-` rows — driven in Chromium by tests/wasm-room-ui.test.mjs, which passed on my run.

NON-BLOCKING NOTES: (1) tests/live-wasm-room.test.mjs defines an unused `freePort()` that calls `require` inside an ESM file — dead today, throws if ever invoked; delete it. (2) server.mjs refreshes the shelf names twice per session (an explicit call before createLiveSession plus the comma-expression inside `tools`) — harmless, but one call site would read better. (3) liveToolDeclarations does not filter names that collide with the fixed command catalogue; a shelf tool whose id equals a fixed command name would be declared but always resolve to the fixed command in commandToAction (fixed commands are matched first). No current shelf id collides; consider skipping/logging a reserved name.

comments.text:
IN_REVIEW — origin/fix/sdxn-miniapp-bridge @ 7d7e2f3 (off main 19b9d9a). Author: voicebox-dsflash1; needs an independent reviewer before the merger lands.

1. mini_app_ready DataCloneError: the bridge re-sent appChannel.port2 after transfer. It now uses the load-time channel exactly once and mints a FRESH MessageChannel per repeat handshake (appChannelTransferred guard), so the inner always gets a live port; a failed postMessage reports mini_app_bridge_error instead of throwing uncaught.

2. Sandbox localStorage SecurityError: the injected SDK installs a document-local in-memory Storage shim (feature-detected; defineProperty only when access throws) for localStorage and sessionStorage. Host storage stays unreachable; values die with the document.

3. HEAD /api/health: added to the route table (200, empty body) so the dev proxy's probe cannot fall through to 500.

4. task-card POST /api/call 403: ambient local calls still refuse task-owner-unverified (the landed test's claim), but /api/call's local branch now derives the durable local task owner — one computing site, LOCAL_TASK_OWNER, replacing two inline copies — when the request carries local authority (host token / room session / room origin), and browser/task-card.ts sends the room session token on its calls. This is the same owner the turn path and GET /api/task already used, so the card can read the task the turn created.

- mini-app-architecture: the sandboxed app stores/reads localStorage via the shim (no SecurityError) and a repeated mini_app_ready produces NO uncaught DataCloneError while a tool still answers through the fresh port.

- task-card: from the real page, the card's exact status request is authorized (the "authenticated paired caller" 403 is gone) and the card renders the named refusal.
The two tests that asserted the old buggy behavior (storageError === "SecurityError"; feedback /authenticated paired caller/) were updated to the new behavior.

comments.author: voicebox-e1m0
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW VERDICT: FAIL — one required fix: the glyph is painted BLACK, not accent, and the test cannot see it. Reviewer voicebox-e1m0 (deepseek; author glm — different family). No merge.

MEASURED ON THE REAL PAGE (my own server, 8885, scratch root with archive/projects + two files):
- The folder icon's computed fill is `rgb(0, 0, 0)` and stroke `none`; the accent (`color: var(--accent)`) is set but UNUSED, because a path is painted by fill/stroke, not by `color`. Cause: `.file-icon` (style.css:99) does not carry the presentation props that `.icon` (style.css:32) carries — `fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linecap/linejoin`.
- Dark mode is the visible failure: the card is `rgb(23,25,30)` and the folder glyph is black on near-black — effectively invisible (screenshot /tmp/35eg-review-dark-current.png; light at /tmp/35eg-review-light-current.png shows a solid black folder where the claim says accent).
- PROBE FIX (applied to my worktree, verified, then reverted): adding `fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.5;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round` to `.file-icon` gives computed `fill:none`, `stroke:rgb(152,173,255)` (the dark-theme accent), 18x18 — the intended accent OUTLINE folder, visible in both themes (/tmp/35eg-review-dark-probefix.png).
- The test passes on the broken render (my run: room-explorer-ui 2/2). Its `iconVisible` check is `getComputedStyle(icon).color !== "rgba(0,0,0,0)"` plus a non-zero box — `color` is the inherited accent and tells you nothing about what is painted, so the suite is green while the glyph is black. A check named "visible and coloured" that cannot fail for the colour it names.

REQUIRED:
1. Give the glyph the stroke presentation: either add `fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round;` to `.file-icon`, or set `class="icon file-icon"` on the SVG (`.icon` is at line 32 and `.file-icon` at 99, so the 18px logical size still wins — later declaration, equal specificity).
2. Strengthen the test to assert the PAINTED properties, not just `color`: e.g. `fill === "none"` and `stroke !== "none"` (or `stroke` equals the accent), so this defect cannot return green.

VERIFIED PASS (everything else):
- Sprite: `#i-folder` exists in the page sprite with the 24x24 stroke geometry; icon prepended to directory rows only.
- Accessibility is right: the SVG is `aria-hidden="true"` and the button's aria-label distinguishes the row — "archive, folder" vs "Read notes.md" (measured in the DOM) — so nothing is announced twice and the distinction is not icon-only.
- File rows carry no icon (contrast is real, tested); the name stays `entry.name` verbatim (`textContent` untouched).
- Docs (README bullet, docs/07, docs/08) updated in the same change; only the "accent colour" phrase is false as rendered until the fix above.
- Room-explorer suite 2/2 on my run (including the new test's structure); the new test's own screenshot is written into the scratch dir and deleted in `finally`, so it is not a retained artefact — a reviewer screenshot outside the tree would be more useful.

Re-review after the two changes is a computed-style check + the suite.

title: pi-acp: the pi adapter child inherits the host environment — scope ANTHROPIC_API_KEY like nz60, or write down why pi keeps it (with evidence)
description:
FILED FROM the nz60 landing (uiflash, 2026-09-26, coord's instruction). This is the flip side of voicebox-beads-nz60 — the same mechanism, WITHOUT the evidence of harm that nz60 had. Do not read it as a live defect.

THE FACT, source-referenced: `lib/pi-acp.mjs:288-292` builds the pi adapter child env as
    const env = { ...process.env, ...options.env, ...(piBinary && piBinary !== "pi" ? { PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND: piBinary } : {}) };
so the child inherits the whole host environment, exactly the shape `lib/claude-acp.mjs` had before
nz60 (commit 6435a46) deleted ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the claude child by default.

WHAT IS KNOWN, and it is only this:
- NOTHING in voicebox reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (grep over lib/*.mjs and server.mjs: zero hits), so the
  key's presence in the pi child is pure inheritance, never a deliberate pass-through. That is the part
  worth fixing or recording.
- A bounded search of the installed pi-acp adapter's shipped files (`~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-acp/`)
  found no reference to the key. This is WEAK evidence against the adapter consuming it — a bundled
  adapter could reference it in a form a text search misses — and it says nothing about the `pi` CLI
  binary, which is a separate program.
- The nz60 evidence was claude-specific: an inherited key overrides claude.ai login inside that adapter
  and can stall the prompt. NO equivalent measurement has been made for pi. Nobody has driven it.

THE TWO ACCEPTABLE OUTCOMES (coord's framing: "either scope it like nz60 or write the 'pi keeps it
because…' down with the evidence"):
(a) SCOPE IT: build the pi child env through one helper with the same semantics nz60 established —
    delete, never a no-value (a key present with no value is a different child env, and a spawn path
    that forwards it writes the string "undefined"); the host's own process.env never mutated; an
    explicit opt-back; tests asserting ABSENCE with `in` plus an integrated capture of the child env
    through the transportFactory ctx.env seam (my claude tests are the template).
(b) RECORD IT: name the consumer that needs the key (the pi CLI or the adapter), state the behaviour
    that needs it, and put it where the claude decision lives — docs/11's adapter child-env paragraph
    plus the generated environment table — so the default is a DECISION, not inheritance.

ACCEPTANCE for either: a diff with tests (a), or a recorded, evidence-backed note (b). In both cases the
question "why does the pi child see the host's key?" must have a written answer; a second adapter
inheriting a credential by accident is the shape this fleet keeps getting bitten by.

RELATED: voicebox-beads-nz60 (the claude fix, 6435a46, IN_REVIEW with voicebox-gemini); docs/11's
adapter child-env paragraph (added by nz60); voicebox-beads-uadl (the gate change that made this push
2 minutes instead of 15 — unrelated, noted because the nz60 diff and this filing share a day).
close_reason: Closed

title: FEATURE: execute general Unix commands and configure Git inside the sandbox environment
description:
FEATURE (Paul, 2026-09-26): execute general Unix commands and configure Git inside the sandbox environment.

INTENT: a booted L1/L1.5 fence is a PLACE (env-serve answers /health + /probe) but cannot DO general work — the model has no door to run argv inside the fence or configure git there. This bead adds that door WITHOUT weakening the fence: commands execute inside bwrap/seccomp/no-capabilities with one writable home, so the sandbox IS the boundary (docs/15: network shared and ambient reads are documented boundaries, unchanged).

DESIGN (env-serve/2):
- tools/env-serve.mjs gains POST /api/execute speaking the dialect the host's /api/call proxy already forwards ({tool, args}, Authorization: Bearer). Tools:
  * exec — args {argv: string[>=1], cwd?: string, timeoutMs?: number}. execFile (NO shell), cwd default+contained inside the fence HOME (/home/voice; outside -> exec-cwd-outside), timeout default 20s cap 120s (exec-timeout), maxBuffer 8MB (truncated flag), minimal env {PATH, HOME}. Absolute argv[0] only under HOME or /usr/bin (exec-binary-outside); bare names PATH-resolved.
  * git-config — args {action: get|set|unset|list, key?, value?}; runs git config --global inside HOME; key regex ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*$, value string <=256 chars; same bounds. Persists in the sandbox home (bound in, survives reloads).
- AUTH: the boot channel carries the pairing bearer — unit-fence-provider reads bearerFor(key) (passed from server.mjs boot route) -> VOICEBOX_BEARER rides the same property channel as VOICEBOX_BOOT_MARKER (fence-unit.sh + fence.sh --setenv). env-serve verifies Authorization timing-safe. No bearer at boot -> /api/execute refuses exec-unpaired (remedy: pair + re-boot); /health + /probe stay open (the environment's face). Wrong bearer -> unauthenticated (same family as /channel).
- HOST: zero changes — /api/call + pairing machinery already carry tool+args to environments.
- /health answers serves: env-serve/2 (+ exec availability).

ACCEPTANCE:
- tests/env-serve.test.mjs (unit lane, spawned env-serve on ephemeral port, temp HOME): health names v2; exec happy path; cwd containment refusal; timeout kill; absolute-binary-outside refusal; unpaired + wrong-bearer refusals; git-config set/get/list round-trip in temp HOME + bad-key refusal; /probe unchanged.
- Fence-level: VOICEBOX_BEARER visible inside the unit only through the boot channel (no new world-readable surface beyond systemd's own same-uid unit properties — documented boundary).
- Docs: docs/15 env-serve surface + bounds stated plainly; README env rows; npm run docs:write.
- Gates: focused then full; independent review before merge.

comments.text: INDEPENDENT REVIEW (audiofeed-ds-flash, deepseek — author gemini, cross-family OK). Reviewed feat/file-view-refresh-d4s @ d3603e5 in my own worktree; branch untouched. VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES — one demonstrated user-visible defect and one accessibility gap; the happy path, deletion error, retry, recovery and close-reset are all real. WHAT REPRODUCED: their suite independently re-run on the reviewed revision — 6/6 pass twice in 2.0s (VOICEBOX_CHROME=/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable node --test tests/file-view-refresh.test.mjs); disk-edit reload, deletion error with retry enabled, recovery, close-reset all behave as claimed; --warn is defined so the error styling is real; showFileSelection only sets aria-current, so a refresh does not steal focus. FINDINGS (evidence: ~/journal/reports/2026-09-25-voicebox-d4s-review/, probe.mjs + README, backed up to journal-data 2a165671): F1 (P2, demonstrated) CLOSE DURING LOAD RE-OPENS THE READER. Probe: click Reload, click Close, wait for the response — immediately after close reader.dataset.state='empty' and Refresh disabled (correct), but when the in-flight read lands, state flips back to 'ready' with the old file's body and the panel is visible again while Refresh stays disabled. Cause: showFile/showRoomFile set shownFile = name, await, then write data-state='ready' unconditionally (three write sites, no 'is this still the file the user wants?' check). Same shape on a fast file switch: no response sequencing, so a slower earlier response can overwrite a newer one — my uniform-delay probe could not make that happen (B won), so that half is a latent risk, not a demonstrated defect. FIX: one sequence token (const seq = ++showSeq before the await; write only if seq === showSeq and shownFile === name) bumped by the close handler — that fixes the re-open and hardens the switch. F2 (P3, demonstrated) THE BUTTON IS NOT DISABLED WHILE LOADING, despite aria-busy='true' and the implementation note. Probe in-flight: ariaBusy='true', readerLoading='true', text 'Reloading…', buttonDisabled=FALSE — refreshCurrentFile disables it and then showFile/showRoomFile immediately set disabled=false. So a second click can start a second read; and a button that is busy but enabled is an incoherent state for AT. FIX: own the disabled state in one place (do not re-enable inside the callees when a refresh is in flight), and assert it. F3 (P3, accessibility) LOADING AND ERROR ARE NOT ANNOUNCED, and this app already knows better — it uses role='status' aria-live='polite' for harness status, captions and turn reports, but the reader has no live region (probe: reader aria-live null, #file-facts null, #file-body role='region' only). Worse, the accessible name comes from aria-label='Reload file contents', so the visible 'Reloading…' text is not exposed either: a screen-reader user pressing Reload hears nothing, and a failed reload (the reason is written into #file-body/#file-facts as text) is silent. FIX: one polite live region for the reader's status line ('Reloading…', the failure reason, 'Reloaded'), matching the pattern used elsewhere. F4 (coverage) THE IN-FLIGHT LOADING STATE IS NOT PINNED by the suite: it samples aria-busy/data-loading only after the request settles, so deleting both would leave 6/6 green. Add a paused-request case (delay /api/file in the page, assert aria-busy=true + data-loading=true + the disabled claim) — probe.mjs shows how in ~15 lines. Also noted, not a defect: showRoomFile carries the same state lines but no drive covers the room-folder path; a mutation of the writer guard is what my probe exists to catch. REQUIRED FIX — tools/create-extension.mjs `--workspace` / `--extensions` are silently ignored:
The usage text advertises both flags and the body sets process.env.VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE / VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR, but lib/extensions.mjs computes PROPOSALS_DIR / EXTENSIONS_DIR as module-level consts at import time — ESM hoists the imports, so the env assignment runs too late. Fix: parse argv first, then `const { createExtension, createAndAdmitExtension } = await import("../lib/extensions.mjs")` after setting the env, or pass the paths into the library functions explicitly.

Review and approve below.", and the waiting area shows the host-review/approval-code flow. The form offers only admissible primitives, so no exec/eval shape is reachable from the page.

FINDINGS (voicebox-astra, measured against the real paths, not the docs):

THE CLAIM, rendered verbatim on the environments page for 'this machine: omarchy' (reachable): '26 tools' expanding to 'sh, bash, node, python3, pip, deno, bun, git, curl, gcc, cc, make, docker, bwrap, systemctl, ps, ls, cat, cp, mv, rm, sudo, su, mount, iptables, nft' (title: 'probed 2026-09-24T19:31:27'). Screenshot + DOM capture: ~/cap-evidence/astra/voicebox-1jk-20260925/{envs-dialog.png,envs-dialog-expanded.png,ui-claims.json}.

THE EXECUTABLE REALITY, measured three ways:
1. EXECUTOR: server.mjs's execute() verb set is list/read/write/edit/diff/grep/delete/list_agents/contact_agent/delegate_task/extensions/extension/make-tool/tool/mini_app. NO shell/exec verb exists. Zero of the 26 listed programs are invocable through the voicebox executor.
2. RESOLVER: real POST /api/turn {transcript:'run python3 --version'} → action:null, 'the script resolver only knows create/read/list/delete/edit/diff/grep/list_agents/delegate_task/contact_agent/launch_mini_app'. Same for 'run git status'. The turn path cannot even EXPRESS program execution.
3. DELEGATION: the only program-execution path is a delegated harness's OWN tools (e.g. pi's bash) under the harness's grants — not this environment's probed inventory. And on this machine right now pi delegation is REFUSED (adapter-version-unsupported), so even that path is closed here.

SEVERITY NOTE: the rendered list includes sudo, su, mount, iptables — the current framing doesn't just overpromise capability, it misstates the safety posture.

RECOMMENDATION — direction A (make the UI say only the truth), not B (add an exec verb): B is a large new security surface (arbitrary program execution as the server user), contradicts the executor's fail-closed design, and duplicates the delegation path. A is surgical: in fused.js renderEnvironments, rename the claim to what it is — e.g. summary 'N host programs present (probed <when>; not invocable by voicebox tasks)' with the expanded list headed by one line naming what the environment CAN do (read/write/list/grep/edit/diff/delete, plus delegation to a harness with its own tools). The probe itself stays — it answers 'what does this host have' for the operator; the defect is only the word 'tools' framing presence as capability. Add one driven test asserting the honest copy renders. Small diff: fused.js + one test + docs line.

Awaiting direction confirmation before implementing.

title: Investigate issues with mini-app rendering within the isolated iframe environment
description: From Paul (2026-09-25): investigate issues with mini-app rendering within the isolated iframe environment. Drive the real behaviour in a browser and report what breaks and why before fixing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION FINDINGS (voicebox-beads-wtz, P1):

Issue: Mini-app rendering completely fails inside the iframe environment; inner app never renders.

Root cause analysis driven live in headless Chromium over CDP:
1. Erroneous Outer Frame Sandboxing (public/fused.js:2799):
   outer.setAttribute('sandbox', 'allow-scripts') was mistakenly placed on the OUTER mediator iframe.
   Per docs/17-mini-apps-architecture.md and tests/mini-app-architecture.test.mjs, the outer bridge (/mini-app-bridge.html) is designed to be SAME-ORIGIN with the room to mediate communication, while the INNER frame (#inner-app in mini-app-bridge.html) possesses sandbox='allow-scripts' to isolate untrusted app markup.
2. CORS Error on Module Script:
   Because the outer frame is sandboxed without allow-same-origin, its origin is opaque ('null'). In public/mini-app-bridge.html, <script type='module' src='mini-app-bridge.js'> is fetched via CORS. Chromium blocks this with:
   'Access to script at http://127.0.0.1:.../mini-app-bridge.js from origin null has been blocked by CORS policy: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present on the requested resource (net::ERR_FAILED)'.
   mini-app-bridge.js never loads or executes.
3. Broken PostMessage Handshake:
   Because mini-app-bridge.js never runs, bridge_ready/mini_app_handshake never fire. Furthermore, postToHost calls window.parent.postMessage(msg, window.location.origin) where origin is 'null' (refused by parent window), and fused.js:2816 checks e.origin !== window.location.origin.
4. Consequence:
   inner.srcdoc remains null, inlined SDK is never injected, and the mini-app viewport remains completely blank.
5. Test Blindspot:
   tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs passed because it only asserted #mini-app-container was unhidden, outer sandbox attribute was present, and button clicks occurred — it never asserted that the inner frame populated or rendered.

Proposed fix:
- In public/fused.js, remove outer.setAttribute('sandbox', 'allow-scripts') (keeping outer bridge same-origin per doc 17; inner iframe remains strictly sandbox='allow-scripts').
- Update tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs to assert inner.srcdoc is populated and app DOM renders.

Awaiting confirmation from coord before applying fix.

title: [BUG] D1 ACP diagnostic fixture has no configured agent 'diagnostic-only' — the test can never queue its task
description:
Found by the iyq reviewer (voicebox-dsflash1) at fix/acp-pi-update-iyq @ 9a9e754, running the documented real-adapter command: VOICEBOX_ACP_ADAPTER=... VOICEBOX_ACP_PI=... node --test tests/pi-acp.test.mjs.

The 'D1 real TCP diagnostic only' test (tests/pi-acp.test.mjs) calls delegate_task for agent 'diagnostic-only' and asserts body.task.state === 'queued'. Why it hides: the test skips when VOICEBOX_ACP_ADAPTER/VOICEBOX_ACP_PI are unset, so the gate's live lane never runs it — but docs/11-acp-adapter.md documents the env command as the runnable check.

Pre-existing and unrelated to the pi-acp 0.0.34 bump. Fix options: register the fixture agent in the diagnostic runtime (or route 'diagnostic-only' through the executor's check as the runtime already intends), then drive the task lifecycle. Revert-proof: with the agent registered, the assertions that follow (queued -> running -> interrupted, no replay) become meaningful.

title: PROBE: sandbox-probe's marker can be left in the measured tree when the probe is killed inside its write window
description:
Found by bp8's new before/after delta (2026-09-25, voicebox-e1m0), in ~/worktrees/voicebox-bp8: after a live-lane run, `git status --porcelain` showed `?? .sandbox-probe-1337006-20260925174601152` — a 0-byte marker in the tree.

THE WRITER: tools/sandbox-probe.mjs writeProbe() probes a directory by creating `.sandbox-probe-<pid>-<ISO-when>` and unlinking it. Line ~155 probes `process.cwd()`, and server.mjs runs the probe for GET /api/probe with the server's cwd — which is the served/measured tree for every harness and live-test server.

WHY IT SURVIVED: the create→unlink window is two syscalls, and nothing covers a SIGKILL in between (a `finally` cannot run on SIGKILL — and the harness kills its private server at exit, live tests kill theirs). A normal foreground run cleans up (verified in /tmp/bp8-probe-repro: no leftover), so this is a kill-race, not a missing unlink. The marker's name carries the PID, which is what makes a sweep possible.

WHY IT IS bp8's CLASS: the artefact lands in the tree another process measures — the harness's delta check fails on it, and the next person reads "?? .sandbox-probe-…" as unexplained dirt (exactly the 2026-09-20 Dolt-backup symptom).

OPTIONS (pick at implementation):
1. Startup sweep: on probe start (or server start), remove `.sandbox-probe-<pid>-*` for PIDs no longer alive (kill -0). Owner-named artefacts, owner-verified cleanup.
2. Probe a path the process owns: probe cwd writability via a uniquely-named DIRECTORY under cwd, removed the same way — narrows nothing; still dirt on kill.
3. Measurement exclusion: `.sandbox-probe-*` filtered like `.beads/` in tools/tree-dirt.mjs — explicitly weakens the measurement, so only if 1 proves impossible.

NOT IN bp8's diff: bp8 is pushed and under review; this is recorded separately rather than expanding a reviewed change.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
# Modern Web Guidance Pass: Voicebox Page Architecture & Construction **Bead**: `voicebox-beads-8ht` (Task, P2) **Scope**: Read-only analysis across `public/index.html`, `public/environment.html`, `public/style.css`, `public/fused.js`, `public/live-voice.js`, `browser/ui/ui.ts`. **Grounding**: Analyzed against `modern-web-guidance` standards (Baseline status, Baseline Widely/Newly available, platform primitives) and repository-specific constraints (CSP, CDP acceptance harness, plain-language gate, served-front currency check). --- ## Executive Summary Voicebox has already adopted several modern platform primitives (`` with `::backdrop` and frosted glass, `:has()` relational selectors, dynamic viewport units `dvh`/`svh`, `text-wrap: pretty`, `color-mix()`, and `documentPictureInPicture`). However, several architectural areas either **hand-roll behaviors now provided by the platform** or **miss modern platform features**, occasionally introducing subtle bugs or fragility. Crucially, adopting platform features in Voicebox is not a free aesthetic upgrade: every feature carries specific costs and risks against Voicebox's **strict CSP**, **acceptance test timing**, **audio worklet rAF loops**, and **multi-browser support**. --- ## 1. Dialogs, Popovers & Invoker Commands ### 1.1 Declarative Invocation vs Imperative JS Listeners * **Location**: `public/index.html:43-85, 158-165`; `public/fused.js:1432-1478` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: Buttons (`#settings-open`, `#envs-open`, `#exts-open`) and close buttons (`#settings-close`, `#envs-close`, `#exts-close`) manually manage dialog lifecycle in JavaScript: - `on(els.settingsOpen, "click", () => els.settings.showModal())` - Manual `setAttribute("aria-expanded", "true"/"false")` on triggers (`fused.js:1437, 1445, 1476`) - Manual focus restoration to trigger on close (`fused.js:1446, 1477`) * **Platform equivalent**: **Invoker Commands API** (`commandfor` and `command` attributes on ` ``` The browser natively opens `` as a modal, traps focus, links accessibility states, and restores focus on dismissal without custom JS. * **What it would break / Real Costs**: 1. *Browser Support*: Invoker Commands are Baseline Newly Available (Chrome 135+, Safari 26.2, Firefox 144). Polyfilling requires an external script. 2. *CSP Violation*: Voicebox's strict CSP (`script-src 'self'`) strictly prohibits external CDNs (like `https://esm.run/invokers-polyfill`). Any polyfill would have to be vendored. 3. *Side-Effect Decoupling*: Clicking `#settings-open`, `#envs-open`, and `#exts-open` currently performs critical setup before display: `refreshDevices()`, `loadAgentSettings()`, `renderEnvironments()`, and `renderExtensions()`. Replacing `click` handlers with purely declarative commands would cause dialogs to open before data is fetched, showing empty or stale lists unless listeners are refactored to listen for `'command'` or dialog `'toggle'` events. ### 1.2 Inconsistent Light-Dismiss Fallbacks on Safari * **Location**: `public/index.html:50, 70, 158`; `public/fused.js:1449-1458, 1481-1490`; `browser/ui/ui.ts:214-225` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: The dialogs use the cutting-edge `closedby="any"` attribute for declarative light-dismiss (clicking the backdrop). Because Safari does not yet support `closedby`, `fused.js` implements a geometry-checking click fallback (`event.target === dialog && rect checking`). **The Bug/Gap**: The fallback was added for `#envs` (`fused.js:1449`) and `#settings` (`fused.js:1481`), and for `#confirm` in `browser/ui/ui.ts:214`, but **omitted for `#exts`** (`fused.js:1432`). On Safari, clicking outside the Extensions dialog fails to dismiss it. * **Platform equivalent**: A single shared light-dismiss helper or a global dialog light-dismiss event delegate. * **What it would break / Real Costs**: No breakage. This is a pure bug fix for Safari consistency that eliminates duplicate geometry-check boilerplate. ### 1.3 Top-Layer Entry/Exit Transitions * **Location**: `public/style.css:136-168, 214-239` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: `` and `` toggle abruptly between `display: none` and `display: block`. * **Platform equivalent**: Modern top-layer CSS animation using `@starting-style`, `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, and the `overlay` property: ```css dialog[open] { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); @starting-style { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.96); } } dialog { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.96); transition: opacity 0.2s ease-out, transform 0.2s ease-out, display 0.2s allow-discrete, overlay 0.2s allow-discrete; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: 1. *Harness Timing / Flake Hazard*: `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` and `tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs` use CDP to click the backdrop or Esc and immediately assert `!document.querySelector('dialog[open]')`. If an exit transition keeps the dialog in the top layer (`overlay` transition) during the exit duration, immediate assertions fail unless test scripts add explicit transition waits. 2. *Browser Support*: `overlay` transition property is currently limited (Chrome 117+, unsupported in Firefox/Safari). --- ## 2. Popovers & Anchor Positioning vs Title Tooltips ### 2.1 Inaccessible `title=""` Attributes for State Explanations * **Location**: `public/fused.js:397, 560, 571, 833, 1042`; `public/environment.html:106` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: Voicebox stores full descriptions and status details in `title` attributes (e.g. `els.rootKind.title = activeRoot.description`, `els.readerFacts.title = ...`). The author in `fused.js:555` states: *"The server's full description stays in the chip's title for anyone who asks for it, because a tooltip is not a second voice on the screen"*. * **Modern Web Guidance violation**: `modern-web-guidance: html: 5`: *"DON'T use the title attribute to create tooltip effects."* `title` attributes are completely inaccessible on touch devices/phones (no hover), unstyled, ignored by screen readers, and inaccessible to keyboard tab navigation. * **Platform equivalent**: **Popover API** (`popover="auto"` or `popover="hint"`) paired with **CSS Anchor Positioning**: ```html ...
...
``` ```css #root-kind { anchor-name: --root-chip; } #root-desc { position-anchor: --root-chip; position-area: block-end; position-try-fallbacks: flip-block; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: 1. *Browser Support*: CSS Anchor Positioning (`position-area`, `position-try-fallbacks`) is supported in Chrome (125+) and Safari (TP/27), but **unsupported in Firefox**. A fallback positioning strategy (`top`/`left` calculation or centered popover) is mandatory. 2. *Plain-Language Gate*: `tools/page-acceptance.mjs:254-300` scans all string literals and HTML elements in `public/` for internal jargon (e.g. `reachableFromThisProcess`, `executor`, ticket IDs). Expanding hidden `title` strings into rendered Popover DOM nodes increases the surface area checked by the plain-language gate. --- ## 3. Container Queries vs Viewport Media Queries ### 3.1 Media Query Inside a Fixed-Width Modal Dialog * **Location**: `public/style.css:189-201` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: Inside `dialog.envs` (which has `width: min(100% - 2rem, 460px)`), `.env-add` attempts responsive form layout using `@media (max-width: 480px) { .env-add { flex-direction: column; } }`. On a 1200px desktop screen, the dialog is only 460px wide, but the viewport query evaluates `false`. Furthermore, lines 198-201 accidentally re-declare `.env-add` with `padding: 8px 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line);` without `flex-wrap: wrap`, overriding and colliding with lines 189-195 in the cascade! * **Platform equivalent**: **CSS Container Queries** (`container-type: inline-size`): ```css dialog.envs, .envs-form { container: env-dialog / inline-size; } @container env-dialog (inline-size < 380px) { .env-add { flex-direction: column; } .env-add input, .env-add button { width: 100%; } } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: - Container queries are **Baseline Widely available** (since Feb 2023). - *Risk*: When `container-type: inline-size` is declared, the container cannot be intrinsically sized by its children. Because `dialog.envs` already has an explicit `width: min(100% - 2rem, 460px)`, layout will not collapse. - Resolves the accidental duplicated CSS rule on lines 198-201 without breaking acceptance tests. ### 3.2 Responsive Mic Stage & Reader Scaling * **Location**: `public/style.css:291-310, 318-325` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: `style.css` relies on `@media (max-width: 720px)` and `@media (max-height: 620px)` to manually shrink `.mic-stage` (268px → 228px → 180px), `.mic` (116px → 104px → 88px), and `.stage` gaps. Lines 320-323 also contain accidental duplicate overrides (`.mic` 96px then 92px in the same block). * **Platform equivalent**: Declaring `container: stage / inline-size;` on `.stage` and using fluid container query units (`cqi`) for the mic wrapper: ```css .mic-stage { width: clamp(180px, 35cqi, 268px); aspect-ratio: 1; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: - `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` lines 330-350 measure `.mic-stage` data attributes and visual activity at exact viewport widths (1200px vs 360px). Fluid scaling must maintain the minimum touch target (44px+) and preserve the exact SVG geometry for `.output-ring` (viewBox 240x240) and `.input-wave` (viewBox 100x100). --- ## 4. CSS Subgrid ### 4.1 Ragged-Edge Alignment Across Project View Cards * **Location**: `public/environment.html:81-88` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: `.views { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 12px; }` `.view { border: 1px solid #2a2a34; border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px; background: #15151b; min-height: 120px; }` Each card contains an `

`, `.authority`, and `ul.entries`. Differences in `.authority` text length cause the file lists (`ul.entries`) to start at mismatched vertical positions across sibling columns. * **Platform equivalent**: **CSS Subgrid** (`modern-web-guidance: css-layout: 3`): ```css .views { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); grid-auto-rows: auto auto 1fr; gap: 12px; } .view { grid-row: span 3; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr; grid-template-rows: subgrid; } ``` * **What it would break / Real Costs**: - Subgrid is Baseline Widely Available (Chrome 117+, Firefox 71+, Safari 16+). - *Risk*: `browser/ui/ui.ts:100` dynamically appends a `

` to `.view` when an error occurs. In a 3-row subgrid (`span 3`), an unexpected fourth child either spills into the next row or pushes adjacent cards unless track spanning accounts for error messages. --- ## 5. View Transitions (Same-Document SPA Transitions) ### 5.1 Reader Expansion and Mic Contraction * **Location**: `public/fused.js:1025-1045, 1075`; `public/style.css:268, 318-325` * **What is currently hand-rolled**: When a file is clicked, `showFile()` sets `els.reader.dataset.state = "ready"`, causing `.reader` to abruptly jump from `display: none` to `display: flex`, while `body:has(#reader[data-state="ready"])` instantly shrinks `.mic-stage`. When closed, it snaps back. * **Platform equivalent**: `document.startViewTransition(() => updateDOM())` with `view-transition-name: reader;` and `view-transition-name: mic-stage;`. * **What it would break / Real Costs (HIGH RISK)**: 1. *Freezing Live Waveform Animations*: `modern-web-guidance: same-document-transitions` warns: *"DO NOT transition elements with active animations. View transitions operate on snapshots, so any animations will appear to be paused during the view transition."* In `fused.js:1754-1770`, `meters()` continuously animates the live audio input wave and output ring via `requestAnimationFrame`. If a View Transition runs while the user is speaking or listening, the live audio waveform will visibly freeze for 250ms! 2. *Harness Assertion Races*: `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` uses CDP to click elements and immediately assert text content or element visibility. View Transitions hold the top layer in snapshot pseudo-elements during the transition, causing timing failures in test suites that do not await transition completion. 3. *Focus Abandonment*: View transitions do not manage focus. Programmatic focus routing (`els.readerTitle.focus()`) would be mandatory to avoid abandoning screen reader users. --- ## 6. Scroll-Driven Animations & Scroll Management ### 6.1 Scroll Chaining and Missing Scroll Affordance * **Location**: `public/style.css:274, 279`; `public/index.html:138` * **What is currently hand-rolled / missing**: - `#session-log` (`max-height: 132px; overflow: auto;`) and `#file-body` (`max-height: 34svh; overflow: auto;`) lack `overscroll-behavior: contain;`. Scrolling to the bottom of the log or code block chains into scrolling the main document. - `#file-body` and `#session-log` lack `scrollbar-gutter: stable;`. When content grows, the sudden injection of a scrollbar triggers horizontal layout shift (CLS). - `#file-body` (`

`) lacks `tabindex="0"`. Keyboard users cannot scroll long code snippets using arrow keys or Page Down (violates `modern-web-guidance: html: 2. Content Grouping`).
* **Platform equivalent**:
  ```css
  #session-log, #file-body {
    overscroll-behavior: contain;
    scrollbar-gutter: stable;
  }
  ```
  ```html
  

  ```
  Optional: CSS Scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: scroll()`) with gradient masks for directional scroll-shadow indicators.
* **What it would break / Real Costs**:
  - `scrollbar-gutter: stable` reserves ~15px of inline space. On a 360px mobile viewport, tests in `cap-evidence/pip-mic-drive` and `tools/page-acceptance.mjs` verify `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth`. Reserving gutter width prevents accidental horizontal overflow from sudden scrollbar appearance.
  - `tabindex="0"` on `#file-body` makes the code block focusable. Test suites checking `document.activeElement` must expect `#file-body` in the tab sequence when open.

---

## 7. Semantic HTML & Form Controls

### 7.1 Search Landmark
* **Location**: `public/index.html:112-117`
* **What is currently hand-rolled**:
  ```html
  

    
    
    
  

  ```
* **Platform equivalent**:
  `...` (`modern-web-guidance: html: 1`).
  The `` element is Baseline Widely Available (Chrome 118, Safari 17.0, Firefox 118) and provides standard landmark navigation for assistive technologies without needing `role="search"`.
* **What it would break / Real Costs**:
  Zero cost. `style.css:66` styles `.list-tools` via class selector, so changing the tag from `div` to `search` has zero visual or script regressions.

### 7.2 IME Composition Handling on Input Submission
* **Location**: `public/fused.js:1225-1233`
* **What is currently hand-rolled**:
  `fused.js` listens to `form submit` and `input` without checking `event.isComposing`.
* **Platform equivalent**:
  `modern-web-guidance: ime-safe-enter-submit`: Guarding against `event.isComposing === true` to prevent premature submission while users compose CJK or accented characters.
* **What it would break / Real Costs**:
  Zero cost; strictly enhances internationalization without changing standard English keyboard flows.

---

## 8. Summary Scorecard

| Area | Current State | Modern Platform Equivalent | Feasibility & Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dialog Invocation** | Imperative JS `click` handlers | Invoker Commands (`commandfor="settings" command="show-modal"`) | **Defer / High Cost**: Newly available; breaks CSP if polyfilled; bypasses required pre-open fetch logic. |
| **Light-Dismiss** | Hand-rolled geometry fallback for Safari (`closedby="any"`) | Native `closedby="any"` (Chrome/Edge/Firefox) | **Keep & Fix**: Native `closedby` is used; fix missing fallback on `#exts`. |
| **Dialog Entry/Exit** | Instant display snap | Top-layer animation (`@starting-style`, `allow-discrete`, `overlay`) | **Caution**: `overlay` has limited browser support; risk of CDP test assertion timing races. |
| **Tooltips / Details** | Unstyled `title=""` attributes | Popover API (`popover="hint"`) + CSS Anchor Positioning | **Defer**: Anchor positioning unsupported in Firefox; `popover="hint"` experimental. |
| **Modal Form Layout** | Viewport `@media (max-width: 480px)` inside 460px dialog | Container Queries (`@container (inline-size < 380px)`) | **High Value / Low Risk**: Baseline Widely Available; fixes duplicated/clobbered `.env-add` CSS. |
| **Project Card Grid** | Flat CSS Grid (`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`) | CSS Subgrid (`grid-template-rows: subgrid`) | **Medium Value**: Baseline Widely Available; requires handling dynamic error element spans. |
| **Reader Transitions** | Instant DOM element visibility toggle | View Transitions API (`startViewTransition`) | **High Risk**: Will freeze live audio SVG waveform animations (`rAF`); causes CDP test races. |
| **Scroll Containers** | `overflow: auto` without overscroll boundaries | `overscroll-behavior: contain; scrollbar-gutter: stable;` + `
` | **High Value / Low Risk**: Prevents scroll chaining and CLS; fixes keyboard accessibility. |
| **File Filter Landmark** | Generic `
` | Semantic `` | **High Value / Zero Risk**: Baseline Widely Available; zero style or script impact. |

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
**SCOPING (ds-flash-2, 2026-09-23) — what a harness can report, what the room shows, and the smallest piece that closes it. No code written.**

## WHAT THE HARNESS CAN REPORT — and what the protocol does not carry

`lib/acp-client.mjs:165` performs the ACP handshake (`initialize`, `protocolVersion: 1`, `clientInfo`) — and
**nothing in the client reads the response's `agentCapabilities`** (grep: no capability or tool-list read; the only
other hit is the error path for an unsupported method at line 60). So the exchange happens and its content is
discarded.

**ACP carries CAPABILITIES, not a TOOL INVENTORY.** The handshake declares what the *client* supports (fs,
terminal) and what the *agent* supports (`loadSession`, prompt capabilities, **MCP** capabilities). It has no
`tools/list` equivalent — an agent's own tools are not enumerated by the protocol. **So the honest answer to
"what does an ACP harness offer?" is: its declared capabilities, plus whatever MCP servers it has configured —
which are enumerable per server via MCP's `tools/list`, a surface CAP already has.** The tools are reachable;
they are simply not in the ACP handshake.

## WHAT THE ROOM SHOWS

**Nothing.** The only mention of a harness alongside tools in `server.mjs` is the self-probe comment (line 107);
no surface reads capabilities or lists a harness's tools. That matches Paul's report exactly: *a configured
harness lists no tools*.

## THE SMALLEST PIECE THAT CLOSES IT

**Consume the `initialize` response and surface it — the request is already being made.** Two halves, in order of
cost:

1. **read `agentCapabilities` from the handshake the client already performs** and show it in the room next to the
   harness row (this is a read of an existing response, not protocol work);
2. **list the harness's configured MCP servers and their tools via MCP `tools/list`** — the vocabulary for
   surfacing verb-like surfaces already exists (`list_extensions`/`call_extension` in `lib/commands.mjs` and
   `lib/resolver.mjs`), so this is a second caller of an existing shape rather than a new concept.

**Not the smallest piece, and worth naming so nobody reaches for it**: extending ACP to enumerate agent tools. The
protocol does not carry it, the remote side is not ours to change, and the tools are already reachable through MCP.

## LIMITS OF THIS SCOPING

Read from the code and the protocol on main `264815c`, **not from a live ACP session** — `discoverHarnesses()`
returns `adapter-not-configured` here, so *what a harness reports in practice* is unverified; what is verified is

title: The plain-language acceptance harness scans SOURCE literals — runtime-rendered vocabulary (API text) is invisible to it
description:
Found 2026-09-21 reviewing the harness-discovery surface (third instance of the same limit on three surfaces tonight). The user-facing plain-language check in tools/page-acceptance.mjs reads source files for a static word list, but the pages render text that ARRIVES AT RUNTIME from the API. Concrete case: harnesses.html rendered the internal refusal ids 'adapter-not-configured' (every non-pi CLI row) and 'absent-capability' (pi's row) raw in the page body — the static list had no entry for either, so the harness passed while the page showed internal ids to a person. They were only moved into data attributes by 8c8539b (review-driven), not by the harness.

THE LIMIT, same shape as the docs denylist (voicebox-beads-f0b): a check over source literals answers 'what did we write?' when the question is 'what is on the page?' — and those diverge exactly where data meets markup. A static list also cannot cover a vocabulary that arrives at runtime.

ACCEPTANCE SHAPE: the plain-language pass should scan RENDERED text (per-surface innerText via the existing CDP drive) against the denylist, not (only) source bytes — or maintain the denylist over the rendered-vocabulary channel. NAMED LIMIT: even a rendered-text scan is presence-of-jargon detection; it still cannot catch a sentence that is false without jargon. Progress, not coverage.

EVIDENCE: harnesses.html pre-8c8539b rendered 'Voicebox delegation: adapter-not-configured. …' on every non-pi row; review receipt in coord's hands (vb-extensions, 2026-09-21). Related: voicebox-beads-f0b (the docs-side denylist), voicebox-beads-db1 (load-flaky acceptance check).

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24) of **fix/db1-adoption-poll @ afd81fb — PASS**, with the boundary of what that means stated below. I did not write it.

THE DIFF IS EXACTLY THE TWO CLAIMS, and it is test-only (1 file, +9/−4, no product code): the one-shot 'page.evaluate(async (expected) => …, folderName)' becomes 'page.waitFor(async (expected) => …, { timeout: 15000, label: "blocked folder to be adopted into project list", args: [folderName] })'. THE PREDICATE IS ALSO CORRECTLY SHAPED, which is the part that would have failed silently otherwise: it returns FALSE while unadopted (so the wait continues) and an object once adopted (so it stops), and the assertions downstream read that object — which means the harness's waitFor must resolve with the predicate's value. BOUNDARY OF THIS PASS, so nobody over-reads it: I did NOT reproduce the original load flake, so I cannot claim the patient path ever WAITS — alone and unloaded the test passes in about a second, which is indistinguishable from adopting on the first poll. What is proven: the form is correct, the bound is finite and named, the predicate returns the right shapes, the suite passes, and the change cannot affect product behaviour because it is test-only. The 15s wait firing under load is justified by reading, not by my drive — the honest way to close that would be to slow the page's adoption deliberately (a mutation) and confirm the test still passes while the OLD one-shot form would have failed; that mutation is the one thing I did not run.

title: wasm resource bounds: run admitted modules in a worker with a time cap and a memory cap
description: From vb-resolver's review of voicebox-beads-qph (driven with digest-consistent attack modules, 2026-09-23): an admitted wasm module is currently trusted for its TIME (the export runs synchronously on the host's event loop; wasm has no fuel; an infinite loop hung the call — and with it the server) and its MEMORY (memory.grow needs no import; a grow-loop did not terminate in 30s). The digest binds bytes, never behavior. THE FIX: execute buffer-abi/1 modules in a worker (node:worker_threads) with a bounded wall-clock deadline per call and a declared memory maximum enforced at instantiation (WebAssembly.Memory maximum / a grow guard in the driver). NAMED UNTIL THEN in lib/wasm-shelf.mjs's header and the gate's admission plan: 'an admitted module is trusted for its time and memory: neither is bounded'. DONE: the loop module and the grow module are refused by name within the bound, and the KAT still passes through the seam.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW — voicebox-beads-9nk @ b745af3 (feat/9nk-wasm-shelf-hookup, author voicebox-gemini-565a). Verdict: **PASS**, with the limits of my own verification stated at the end.

REBASE AND SHAPE: clean rebase onto current main; 235 insertions across lib/extensions.mjs (62), lib/wasm-shelf.mjs (36), lib/wasm-worker.mjs (56), lib/commands.mjs (5), docs and tests. The change is focused on the three seams it claims.

THEIR SUITE: tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs passes **11/11** (76s), and the tests are about the right things:
· `through the seam: the KAT passes, and a post-admission swap is digest-mismatch at call time` — the security property is DRIVEN, not asserted: a module swapped after admission is refused at call time.
· `admission rehash: ... the digest in the manifest is the one measured` and `ADMISSION TAMPER: one flipped byte ... named with both digests` — the admission half, with both digests in the refusal.
· `diff.wasm: output format decoded and declared (Hirschberg line edit script)` — the decode claim has a test.
· `wasm shelf hookup: catalogue discovery surfaces shelf tools and callTool executes via o45 seam` — the wiring claim has a test.
· Plus named refusals rather than uncaught throws for a module whose memory does not cover the declared ABI, a loop module at the host's deadline, a grow module against the host's bounds, and a module file over the host's read bound refused BEFORE the read.

READ IN THE SOURCE, confirming the two-phase claim: lib/wasm-shelf.mjs states it ("(i) ADMISSION: readShelf rehashes each module against the manifest ... (ii) CALL TIME: callWasmTool rehashes the file before EVERY instantiation"), and the code matches — readShelf reads each module and compares digests (refusing `digest-mismatch` with both), and the call path re-reads and rehashes before the worker gets verified bytes. The parent keeps the trusted half (read, rehash, compile, imports); the worker gets only verified bytes.

A REVIEW NOTE, not a defect, and the author's own comment says it: THE SHELF ABI IS MEASURED, NOT DECLARED. The manifest declares no calling convention; the fixed addresses for hash.wasm and diff.wasm were established by driving the modules ("measured by driving (2026-09-23) ... a mechanism when the manifest learns to declare ABIs"). That is honest and correct today, and it is the thing to watch: a rebuilt shelf module with different buffer addresses would be admitted (its digest matches its own new manifest) and then read from the wrong offsets. Worth a line in the docs if it is not there, and worth a bead if the manifest is not yet able to declare an ABI.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, stated rather than implied: I ran their suite and read the source; I did NOT drive anything myself this time. I had planned an independent check of the per-call half — admit a module, call it, tamper the file BETWEEN two calls, and watch the SECOND call refuse (their test swaps before a call, which does not distinguish a per-call rehash from a cached one) — but the shelf's modules are not in this repo (they live outside it, per the manifest), so that needs an installed shelf and a writable copy, which I could not stand up in the budget I had left. So: the call-time property is verified by their seam test and my reading of the code, not by my own instrument. A reviewer with more budget should do the tamper-between-calls check; it is the one form of the claim that the existing test cannot see.

title: WASM provider: wasm asset class at the gate + admission rehash + call-time rehash (the digest half of 4vz)
description:
Implementation of voicebox-beads-4vz's decision (provider-under-gate), the half that does NOT touch o45's seam. THE THREE SENTENCES THAT ARE THE REASONING (coord, 2026-09-23): (1) 'The delegation hypothesis names an owner that has not formed' — isocan's invocation runtime is open design (isocan-ti5), there is nothing to delegate to. (2) 'An act inherits the boundary of where it executes' — hash/diff are pure functions of caller bytes, so they execute inside voicebox's own boundary. (3) 'A digest binds bytes to a manifest, not the manifest to an authority' — the trust root is the HOST'S ADMISSION (host installs the shelf; the env var is its act), and the digest checks bind bytes to what was admitted.

TWO CHECKS, TWO JOBS, SECOND NON-REDUNDANT BECAUSE ~/.isocan/modules/ IS MUTABLE AS THIS USER (the fact that justifies the second check — a second check with no stated reason gets deleted): (i) ADMISSION rehash binds the module's bytes to its catalogue entry (CAP wasm-package-authority precedent); (ii) CALL-TIME rehash binds the bytes about to execute to the admitted digest (CAP wasm-offscreen-host precedent: rehash before worker creation).

SHAPE: gate gains primitive 'wasm' with a wasm asset class (digest required 64-hex, buffer-abi declared as data); lib/extensions.mjs callTool gains the wasm branch — the ONLY way a tool runs carries the check; lib/wasm-shelf.mjs loads the isocan shelf manifest, admission-rehashes each tool, registers admitted entries.

ABI FINDING (driven, 2026-09-23): the shelf manifest does NOT declare the modules' calling convention — discovered empirically: hash.wasm input fixed at 0x400 (max 8192B), sha256(len) → 32 with the 32-byte digest at 0x2400, -1 above 8192 (KAT 'abc' → ba7816bf VERIFIED); diff.wasm buffers A 0x10000 / B 0x20000 / out 0x30000, diff(lenA,lenB) → N, output binary format undecoded. The manifest SHOULD declare the ABI; until it does, the voicebox-side ABI table carries the measured values and says they are measured. DONE: driven tests — tamper at admission refused by name; admit-then-swap refused at call by name; the real sha256 KAT passes through the seam; a wasm descriptor missing its digest is under-declared at the gate.
