title: DESIGN: under whose authority does a foreign module execute (wasm shelf ↔ voicebox delegation)
close_reason: WASM provider landed on origin/main.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Design bead splitting from idb-vector-4eh (re-homed to the isocan tracker). The wasm tool shelf (@isocan/wasm-tools, installed ~/.isocan/modules/wasm-tools/, tools hash + diff with pinned digests) is built, self-tested, installed and listed LOADED — and voicebox's only tool-execution seam (callTool → tasks.call | extensions.callTool, server.mjs:385) has no wasm branch: nothing on voicebox main can invoke a shelf tool, and functionDeclarations() (lib/commands.mjs, the ONE command list) does not name them.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD ANSWERS: under whose authority does a foreign module execute? Linked to voicebox-beads-2gq (how the host proves it is the host) — same epic, two faces: 2gq is proof of host identity; this is what host authority MEANS when the code being run came from another repo.

HYPOTHESIS TO TEST (not an instruction): if the shelf is an isocan artefact installed under ~/.isocan/, the isocan loop plausibly owns the invocation and voicebox gains a DELEGATION (voicebox asks isocan's runtime to run hash/diff and returns the result) rather than a provider (voicebox executing foreign wasm in its own process). Decide: delegation vs provider; which environment's authority bounds it (capability report? host token? a tier-table row?); how shelf tools reach functionDeclarations() without breaking the ONE-command-list rule; manifest digest verification at call time.

OUTPUT: a written design decision on this bead, then implementation beads re-homed to whichever repo owns the call.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
EXPLORATION (k3-01a0cedc, 2026-09-23 — analysis only, nothing built; surfaces cited at origin/main f852e7e).

DECISION SHAPED: PROVIDER-UNDER-GATE, not delegation. The shelf enters voicebox's OWN extension gate as a catalogue of strangers; the act executes inside the environment that runs it, under that environment's authority.

WHY NOT DELEGATION (the bead's hypothesis): it names an owner that has not formed. Isocan's own invocation model is OPEN (isocan-ti5, P1: the record, invocation, and configuration questions are all unanswered; isocan-rtt still feasibility). There is no isocan serving runtime to delegate TO — designing voicebox's call against that interface is designing against a ghost. And the authority question answers itself: an act inherits the boundary of where it EXECUTES. hash/diff are pure functions of caller-supplied bytes; they need no authority that lives in isocan, so nothing forces execution there. Re-open condition, honestly: a future shelf tool whose authority must NOT leave isocan (signing keys, isocan's own audit) forces delegation — and then it rides the environments seam (pairing + envelope + capability report, g7c landed), which is the seam 2gq sharpens. Today's shelf has no such tool.

WHY PROVIDER IS VOICEBOX'S SOLVED PROBLEM: foreign-ness is what the extension gate already is. Every tool is a stranger descriptor with declared capabilities and bounds; admission is the host's act (lib/extensions.mjs:511 — callTool the ONLY way an admitted tool runs; server.mjs:385 the one seam). A wasm module is one more stranger with a STRONGER containment story than JS: linear memory, explicit imports — the imports ARE the tier-table row, and the gate's vocabulary (under-declared, network-unbounded, absent-capability) already covers it. And placement: wasm is the one runtime that exists in EVERY placement voicebox targets, including the zero-server browser (Paul's hard requirement, 8fv.1) — a provider that executes wasm works where a delegation to a server runtime cannot.

WHICH ENVIRONMENT BOUNDS IT: the one that executes it — voicebox's own (server) or the browser environment's (E1 containment). NOT isocan's: a module admitted into voicebox's catalogue is voicebox's admission; isocan's authority ends at its own artefacts. The capability report (the S1/S2 measured report) is where 'this environment can run wasm' shows, and the tier table's absent-capability is the refusal when it cannot.

THE ONE COMMAND LIST, UNBROKEN: shelf tools do NOT enter COMMANDS (lib/commands.mjs — the one list, whose header names the failure of two lists). They ride the pattern o45 is already building (IN PROGRESS): discovery + invocation through meta-tools in the one list (list_extensions / call_extension). WARNING: a wasm-specific door would be a second list — the y5k shape. Implementation beads must hang off o45's seam, not beside it.

DIGEST VERIFICATION AT CALL TIME — two checks, two jobs, both with CAP precedent:
1. ADMISSION: stage the module, rehash, compare to the manifest digest — binds bytes to the catalogue entry (CAP wasm-package-authority.js: inventory bytes/digests/imports/memory).
2. CALL TIME: rehash before EVERY instantiation — binds the bytes about to execute to the admitted digest, because ~/.isocan/modules/ is mutable by any process running as this user (CAP wasm-offscreen-host.js: rehashes before worker creation). 1-3KB modules: the cost is noise.
And the trust-root question, answered plainly: a digest binds bytes to a MANIFEST; it does not bind the manifest to an authority. The authority is the host's admission (host token), exactly as extensions today — the manifest is data until the host says otherwise. isocan-ti5's open 'system layer + project suite' question maps onto voicebox's catalogue one-to-one.

2gq DEPENDENCE: ANSWERABLE WITHOUT 2GQ. The act never leaves voicebox's own environment in the provider shape, so 2gq's open break (WHICH machine, in the positional vocabulary) does not arise; envelope.environment (g7c, landed) already carries the stable key where it would. 2gq sharpens the seam delegation WOULD ride; it does not constrain this decision. Promotable per coord's offer.

IMPLEMENTATION HOMES (OUTPUT per the bead): the call is voicebox's → beads in the voicebox tracker, hanging under 4eh (HOOKUP, in progress): (i) descriptor gains a wasm asset class (digest, imports as declared capabilities); (ii) admission rehash at stage; (iii) call-time rehash + instantiation inside the existing callTool seam with boundsEcho; (iv) catalogue discovery riding o45's meta-tools. Nothing for the isocan tracker until a delegation case (a tool whose authority is isocan's) actually appears.

title: The currency check compares the longest line, so two different files can pass as current
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, while pushing fix/rendered-plain-language (voicebox-beads-0ye).

OBSERVED: my branch's public/fused.js differed from the served front's copy — mine carried three page fixes, the served tree at that moment carried the (then uncommitted) root-poll edit — and the pre-push gate's phase A reported 'environment is current (served modules carry current markers)' with [gate] clear anyway.

MECHANISM: tools/page-acceptance.mjs compares each served module against the pushing tree's disk by taking THE LONGEST LINE of the disk copy as a marker and asking whether the served copy contains it. When the longest line is a long shared comment (these files have many), two different revisions satisfy the check.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN EVENTUALLY: the fleet has just agreed to state a rule — 'a lane that edits the served tree must commit to its own branch immediately; no landing may ever discard uncommitted work there' — precisely because the currency check structurally rewards editing the served tree. That rule is doing work the check cannot do. A check whose name promises 'the front is serving what I am pushing' and whose mechanism accepts 'the front contains my longest line' is the same class as every other finding this week: an instrument measuring the class next to the one that matters.

THE HONEST FIX, for whoever owns the harness: compare CONTENT (hash the served bytes against the disk bytes, the way the served-vs-disk marker check already does elsewhere), or at minimum require EVERY line of the disk copy to appear rather than only the longest. The cost is a few milliseconds per module; the alternative is a green line nobody can rely on.

NOT FIXED HERE: it is the acceptance harness, not the page, and my branch was already touching that file for 0ye. Filed so the finding survives the branch.
close_reason:
LANDED on main in the 8c87e06 merge (my amended tip 1cfb5d2; the merger union-resolved keeping the amended verdict disclosure and the no-stamp NOTE path). Verified by reading main's files: tools/served-vs-disk.mjs carries the compiled branch and the string-literal comparison, tools/page-acceptance.mjs carries the identity skip, the verdict disclosure and the no-stamp note, AGENTS.md carries the sentence, and tests/served-vs-disk.test.mjs has 6 cases.

THE DEFECT, and the proof it existed: the currency check took the single longest line of the disk copy as a marker, so two different files passed as current whenever their longest line was a shared comment — observed live (a branch whose public/fused.js differed from the served copy cleared the gate with [gate] clear). FALSIFIED AGAINST THE CASE THE OLD RULE COULD NOT SEE: a scratch tree at the same sha with ONE short line changed (MAX_CARDS 60 -> 61) — the new rule failed and named the line; the old rule found its 286-char marker present and would have PASSED.

THE COMPOSED CHECK (coord's ruling: I composed, vb-resolver reviewed the seam it owns): IDENTITY decides whether the question applies (the front's published revision against the measured tree's HEAD; on a mismatch it SKIPS BY NAME, quoting both, and the verdict now discloses it — 'ALL CLEAR — but the currency check was skipped: ...'), and CONTENT answers it (every non-empty line must appear; for compiled .ts, comments and strings, measured 100/100 and 142/142; for stylesheets, declarations and design tokens, 311/311 and 9/9). Reviewed and ACCEPTED by vb-resolver, who drove all three states with its own rigs and verified both stated limits rather than trusting the description.

REMAINING GAP, filed deliberately as its own P3 bead rather than hidden: a code-only edit to a compiled .ts is invisible to the comments-and-strings comparison (vb-resolver's repro: acts.ts 2000 -> 2500 was not caught). The reason it is chosen rather than fixed: a type-stripping comparison would false-red on every run, and a gate that false-reds regularly is worse than a named-narrow one.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
FIXED in fix/currency-check @ 9e0d4b8 (stacked on the 0ye commit 988b585; not pushed yet — see WHY below, which is itself the finding).

WHAT CHANGED: the marker rule is gone. Every non-empty line of the disk copy must appear in the served copy, except the lines the dev transform rewrites by definition (module specifiers, asset URLs). Measured first, on the real front: fused.js 1734/1734 non-empty lines survive, audio-client.js 594/595 (the miss is an import specifier), live-voice.js 143/143. The served copy is legitimately a SUPERSET (Vite wraps and injects: 461 KB served against 86 KB source), so the rule asks only the question that has an answer — is this tree's content present? Stylesheets cannot be compared line by line (75 of 325 disk lines absent, minified), so their DECLARATION SET is compared with whitespace collapsed and asset URLs excluded (measured 311/311) plus design tokens verbatim (9/9). The reason names the drift, not just the module: 'fused.js: 1 line(s) ... first: "const MAX_CARDS = 61;"'.

FALSIFIED AGAINST THE CASE THE OLD RULE COULD NOT SEE: a scratch tree at main with ONE short line changed (MAX_CARDS 60 -> 61), longest line untouched, pointed at the live front. New rule: FAILS naming the line — and additionally caught a real drift nobody planted (browser/ui/ui.ts, 42 lines). Old rule on the same tree: the 286-char marker is present in the served copy, so it WOULD HAVE PASSED. That is the defect, demonstrated rather than argued.

THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which is the honest answer to 'can this check be made reliable while the served tree is a working tree?': **the premise 'the front serves the tree you are pushing' can only hold for ONE tree at a time, and the served tree is a shared, moving target.** With the strict rule, a lane whose page module differs from what the front is serving now sees the currency check red for that module — which is TRUE and is the point, but it means: (a) a page change can no longer be pushed from a side worktree while the served tree lags (it could before, because the marker could not see the drift); (b) the land-then-move-then-gate-from-the-served-tree flow is now ENFORCED rather than recommended; (c) every other lane's local npm run accept will show that one line red while somebody else holds the served tree. My own push was refused by exactly this rule, with the served tree sitting on another lane's branch (297ab6f) — the check was right and the sequence was wrong.

RECOMMENDATION: keep it strict and say (a)-(c) where lanes will read them. The alternative — keeping a rule the drift can slip through — is what this bead was filed for.

title: MILESTONE: per-process session token in served HTML to guard /channel against forged loopback Origin
description:
A same-machine non-browser process (curl, Python, local script) can connect to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/channel over raw loopback TCP and send a forged 'Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>' header. Because HTTP headers are client-controlled on raw sockets, an origin check distinguishes browser contexts (where browsers enforce immutable Origin) but cannot distinguish between the served browser tab and another local process forging the loopback origin.

Closing this requires minting an ephemeral, per-process session token into the served HTML (or via a one-time bootstrap door), which the page worker reads and presents in its hello frame. This belongs with the environment-identity and actor-provenance milestone (journal-wdq / voicebox-beads-2gq).

Part of the executor channel security roadmap following voicebox-beads-5c1.
close_reason: Fulfilled by voicebox-beads-kkc (docs/13 §4 Option A, landed on main @ 1f3a9fc): per-process session secret minted at startup, single-use bootstrap ticket redeemed into HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookie, /channel and /live local-page entitlement requires Origin AND session cookie, verified by tests/loopback-auth.test.mjs (13/13 PASS), documented in docs/18-loopback-session-auth.md.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN ANALYSIS (gemini, 2026-09-23): Why a token minted into openly-served HTML does NOT close the local process boundary, and what true local browser authentication requires.

1. WHAT AN HTML TOKEN CLOSES VS WHAT IT DOES NOT:
- What it closes: Only blind local scripts or scanners that attempt direct WebSocket upgrades to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/channel without first reading the HTTP document.
- What it does NOT close: Any local script or process that simply fetches http://127.0.0.1:<port>/environment.html first (e.g. via curl, fetch, or python-requests), parses out the token, and attaches it to the WebSocket upgrade.
- The root cause: On loopback TCP, both the HTTP server and the WebSocket server accept connections from 127.0.0.1. If the HTML page itself is served openly over unauthenticated HTTP, any secret minted into that HTML is equally readable by any local process that can reach the port. Minting a token into unauthenticated HTML creates the appearance of a credential without the substance of one.

2. WHY SINGLE-USE TOKENS INTRODUCE DOS / HIJACK RACES:
- If an HTML token is single-use, an attacker process on the same machine can query the page repeatedly, obtain tokens, race the user's browser during startup, and permanently lock out the user (or hijack the session) on reload.
- If tokens are multi-use per boot, the attacker simply fetches once and reuses the token.

3. THE TRUE ARCHITECTURAL SOLUTIONS:
To genuinely distinguish the user's browser tab from an arbitrary script on the same machine, one of two real security architectures is required:
(A) Host-Token Bootstrap (The Jupyter/code-server Pattern):
    The web server does not serve HTML openly. The launcher CLI (holding .host-token with 0600 permissions) generates a short-lived one-time ticket and opens the browser to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?bootstrap=<ticket>. The server validates the ticket, sets an HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict session cookie, and requires that session cookie for all HTML, API, and WebSocket requests. Local processes lacking access to .host-token (different UID) cannot fetch the page or the WebSocket.
(B) Browser-Generated WebCrypto Key Material & Pairing:
    The browser generates a non-extractable WebCrypto ECDSA key pair in IndexedDB. It displays a pairing code or registers with the host via a console-assisted pairing flow (mirroring /api/pair). title: The dev front answers unknown module paths with HTML, so a page module's failure is silent
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, driving the merged router on the front the owner actually uses (:5173).

THE DEFECT: the page's modules are served by the SERVER from SOURCE_DIRS = [core, browser, tools, tests, lib] (server.mjs:765) and the browser imports them as ABSOLUTE paths (/core/paths.ts, /lib/channel.mjs, /browser/worker.ts). The dev front proxied only /browser, so every other one of those requests fell through to Vite, and Vite answered with its SPA fallback: MEASURED, /core/paths.ts via :5173 -> 200 text/html, 16 KB, with /@vite/client in the body; via :8787 -> 200 text/javascript, 3.6 KB. A module worker cannot execute an HTML document, so the environment page's worker never loaded its module graph, never answered the host hello, and window.e1m0.ready stayed pending forever: THE PAGE LOOKED ALIVE AND COULD NOT ACT AT ALL.

WHY IT SURVIVED: every page test drives the page against the SERVER'S OWN PORT (startServer's base), which never touches Vite. So the suite is green and the front is broken — the instrument-measuring-the-adjacent-class shape again, same as the #send button (a text state, not a capability state) and the sparse audio feed (clearing, not stepping).

FIXED IN THIS LANE, minimising: the five SOURCE_DIRS prefixes are now proxied in vite.config.js (commit f852e7e, cherry-picked onto the landing line; content-identical to 1b1816d on feat/page-writes-room). /channel was added in the same commit — the executor channel was ALSO unproxied, which made a page-owned root report executor.connected:false and told the user 'The tab that holds this folder is not open' WHILE THE TAB WAS OPEN.

WHAT IS STILL OWED (not done, and bigger than the two-line fix): a general answer to 'the front must serve whatever the server serves for the page, or fail loudly'. A prefix list can drift again — it did once already — and the failure is silent HTML rather than an error. The options are a shared list read by both sides, or a front-side check that a module request returns JavaScript (and says so when it does not).

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THE ROUTER: no page-owned-root feature could ever have worked through :5173. The router exposed it by making the page's worker load-bearing.

LANDED: the specific breakage in f852e7e (/channel and the module prefixes proxied) and the GENERAL fix in cfe88e1 — both in main, verified by reading main's files (lib/browser-sources.mjs carries the one list; tools/page-acceptance.mjs carries the module-graph check).

THE DEFECT: the page's modules are served by the SERVER from SOURCE_DIRS = [core, browser, tools, tests, lib] and the browser imports them as absolute paths (/core/paths.ts, /lib/channel.mjs, /browser/worker.ts). The dev front proxied only /browser, so every other request fell through to Vite, which answered with its SPA fallback: MEASURED, /core/paths.ts via :5173 -> 200 text/html, 16 KB, with /@vite/client in it; via :8787 -> 200 text/javascript, 3.6 KB. A module worker cannot execute an HTML document, so it died silently — window.e1m0.ready never resolved and THE PAGE LOOKED ALIVE AND COULD NOT ACT AT ALL. Pre-existing: no page-owned-root feature could ever have worked on :5173; the router exposed it by making the page's worker load-bearing.

THE GENERAL FIX, which is what made this closable rather than patched: lib/browser-sources.mjs holds the list ONCE — server.mjs imports it (it serves those directories) and vite.config.js imports it (it must forward them), so the two cannot drift — and tools/page-acceptance.mjs fetches one real module per prefix THROUGH THE FRONT and requires JavaScript, so the next drift fails by name instead of silently.

FALSIFIED AGAINST THE REAL DEFECT rather than a synthetic mutation: a scratch front built from the pre-fix commit bc200f3 (no /core proxy), and the acceptance tool pointed at it, failed naming /core/agent-settings.ts, /tools/acp-check.mjs, /tests/acp-browser.test.mjs and /lib/acp-client.mjs each '200 text/html (the SPA fallback)' — while /browser, which WAS proxied pre-fix, passed. A blanket failure would have proved less; the partial one matching the defect exactly is what shows the check discriminates.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROTECT AGAINST, stated where the fix lives: a module the page imports from a directory the server does not serve at all. The list only covers what the server knows about — the class is now LOUD rather than silent, which is the honest claim and not 'impossible'.

THE CONSEQUENCE, stated as scope rather than as an incident: THE FRONT AND THE TESTED PORT HAVE DIVERGED ENOUGH FOR A WHOLE FEATURE TO BE UNTESTABLE WHERE THE OWNER USES IT. Every page test drives the server's own port; the owner's URL is this front. THE FAILURE MODE, in the words that make it recognisable: a 200 that means 'here is the app' answering a request for a module — and a failure with NO ERROR, because the thing that failed was the LOADING rather than the code. The page looked alive and could not act at all, which is the worst possible state for anybody debugging it, including its owner.

WHAT LANDED HERE (f852e7e, cherry-picked onto the landing line; content-identical to 1b1816d): /channel proxied (the executor channel — unproxied, a page-owned root reported executor.connected:false and the room told the user 'The tab that holds this folder is not open' WHILE THE TAB WAS OPEN), and the five SOURCE_DIRS prefixes proxied so the page's modules stop being answered with HTML.

STILL OWED, and it is the reason this bead exists rather than being closed by that commit: a prefix list can drift, and it has already drifted once. The two honest options are (a) ONE list read by both the server and the front, or (b) a front-side assertion that a module request answers with JavaScript and says so loudly when it does not. Until one of them exists, the next unproxied path fails the same silent way.

A page change cannot land while the shared front is serving something else — which is the correct property, not an obstacle. The resolution is to change the world rather than the gate: LAND THE ROUTER FIRST, MOVE THE SERVED TREE (so the front carries fused.js), and the currency check is satisfied by then. Landing order matters: landing only the wording would leave the room reading fields that do not exist yet (harmless fallback, but pointless), and landing only the router leaves the room telling people they cannot save into a folder that routes fine.

TWO INSTRUMENT ERRORS OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE THE GENERALISABLE PART:
  1. THE COMPOSER'S REFUSAL SIGNAL IS THE UTTERANCE TOOLTIP, NOT #send. #send is disabled whenever the box is EMPTY — a TEXT state, not a CAPABILITY state. A check on that button measures whether somebody typed, not whether sending is possible; it would have passed for the wrong reason one way and failed for the wrong reason the other. (Coord, 2026-09-23: worth more than the test it fixed.)
  2. The drawer's facts live in #about-facts, not #about — my first probe read null and reported an empty drawer as a page defect when the page was right.
Both times the page was right and the instrument was wrong.

title: Outer ring: the contour steps once per chunk — fixed and measured four independent ways
description:
LANDED BY voicebox-ui on coord's instruction (the ring lane had finished its branch): fix/outer-ring-janky-smoothing rebased onto main and pushed as c2d180d, gate ALL CLEAR, served tree moved to main.

THE CHANGE (one file, +7/-1): smooth(meter.output, meter.smoothOutput, 0.3) moved out of followPlayback() — which returns early unless a new chunk has started playing — into level(), which the meters() requestAnimationFrame loop calls per rendered frame. So the shift stays discrete per chunk and the contour's blend runs every frame.

CLAIM VERIFIED VS ASSUMED: the commit says 'every frame', so before landing I checked that level() is reached from a requestAnimationFrame loop (public/fused.js meters()). It is.

MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, FOUR INSTRUMENTS (old = a32ae62, new = c2d180d; identical synthetic audio driven into the page's own playback path, 100 ms chunks back to back so playback never gaps, no vendor and no provider spend):
  1. Ring geometry, rotation removed (64 on-curve points per frame, best circular alignment): old 0.078, 0.037, 0.763 / 0.091, 0.022, 0.574 — frozen then a spike, once per chunk; new 0.481, 0.371, 0.474, 0.469, 0.450 — every frame.
  2. Pixels (consecutive frames blended, mean luma of the difference): old 0.01 0.01 0.06 0.02 0.02 … repeating; new 0.06 0.06 0.07 0.07 … every frame. 6x in the still frames.
  3. cap-ds-flash, per-frame normalised RMSE (independent lane, blind A/B): old spread 5.7x with spikes ~3x typical, ~7 frames apart (≈117 ms ≈ one chunk); new spread 1.2x, no spikes, no identical pairs.
  4. cap-ds-flash, full-circumference 64-ray radius profile with rotation alignment (1024/1024 angle samples covered): old spike train 0.08-1.44 px, 18x spread, spikes 7 pairs apart ≈114 ms, and the spikes SURVIVE rotation alignment (1.44 -> 1.31) so the change is the contour, not rigid rotation; new uniform 1.10-2.08 px, spread 1.9x, no near-zero pair, and alignment removes a little of it (rotation, shared with the old build). Its caveat, kept: the circle-fit residual is ~19 px, so the values are displacement along each sampled ray, not a strict radius.

TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST, and that is part of the record: 'does the drawing move?' cannot discriminate the builds at all (98.7% vs 100% of frames move — the render phase eases per frame in both), and a sparse 4-chunks/s feed is invalid because playback GAPS at that cadence, the page returns to not-speaking, and the ring is CLEARED between chunks — so that run was measuring clearing, not stepping.

VIDEO for the owner's eye: /tmp/vb-ring-vision/handover2/ (A = old, B = new, blind labelling), each 192-193 compositor frames at 60 fps captured via Page.startScreencast, plus a 16-frame strip. The visual read is routed to a vision-capable lane; three of the four instruments above are numeric, and the numbers are the claim.
close_reason:
LANDED on main as c2d180d 'fix(live): smooth the output ring every frame rather than once per chunk' (rebased onto main, pushed as a fast-forward, gate ALL CLEAR; the served tree was moved onto it and the room's ring was verified there).

THE EVIDENCE, five instruments, and one of them a pair of eyes:
  1. ring geometry with rotation removed (mine): old 0.078, 0.037, 0.763 / 0.091, 0.022, 0.574 — frozen then a spike per chunk; new 0.481, 0.371, 0.474, 0.469, 0.450 — every frame.
  2. pixel blend, mean luma of consecutive-frame difference (mine): old 0.01 0.01 0.06 0.02 0.02 … repeating; new 0.06 0.06 0.07 0.07 … every frame — 6x in the still frames.
  3. per-frame normalised RMSE (cap-ds-flash, blind): old spread 5.7x with spikes ~3x typical, ~7 frames apart (~117 ms ~ one chunk); new spread 1.2x, no spikes, no identical pairs.
  4. full-circumference 64-ray radius profile with rotation alignment (cap-ds-flash, blind): old spike train 0.08-1.44 px, 18x spread, spikes 7 pairs apart and SURVIVING rotation alignment (so the change is the contour, not rigid rotation); new uniform 1.10-2.08 px, 1.9x spread, no near-zero pair.
  5. the visual read (gemini lane, blind): A frozen with JUMPS AT FRAMES 03 AND 10; B a travelling crest, zero stagnant frames — the same two moments as the numeric spike pairs (02->03, 09->10).
TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST and are part of the record: 'does the drawing move?' cannot discriminate the builds at all (98.7% vs 100% of frames move — the render phase eases per frame in both), and a sparse 4-chunks/s feed is invalid because playback GAPS at that cadence, the page returns to not-speaking and the ring is CLEARED between chunks — that run was measuring clearing, not stepping.

THREE NARROWINGS CAME AFTER THE AGREEMENT, all by measurement: the lane's own attribution limit (its metric supports 'the ring moves' but not independently 'the contour deforms'); my reflow hypothesis, disproved by its page-level probes; and its solved-centroid measurement, which resolved to 'the ring's centre is a constant in the code (OUTPUT_CENTRE) and the container is pixel-static, so every centre number is a summary statistic of an asymmetric travelling contour'. The discriminator was never the centre — it was the cadence.

THE OWNER-FACING ARTIFACT: /tmp/vb-ring-vision/handover2/ring-before-and-after.mp4 (3.2 s real time, 60 fps screencast frames) plus a quarter-speed cut, built with ffmpeg and no provider spend.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
TWO CORRECTIONS TO HOW THIS EVIDENCE SHOULD BE READ — from cap-ds-flash, the lane that produced instruments 3 and 4, and worth more than the agreement itself. Recorded rather than folded in because the pair of instruments is NOT two independent proofs of one claim.

1. ATTRIBUTION LIMITS OF THE RAY PROFILE. While fitting each frame's circle it also got the ring's CENTRE, and the centres are not equally stable: A's centre moves ~0.3 px in x, B's drifts ~5.7 px in x (379.8 -> 374.1) and ~2.4 px in y. Since the metric is displacement of the hairline ALONG RAYS from that fitted centre, a rigid translation of the whole ring registers exactly like a contour change. So: A's spikes CANNOT be translation (its centre is essentially fixed - that half is clean, and the spikes surviving rotation alignment corroborates it), but B's uniform 1.10-2.08 px could be partly rigid motion. 'The ring moves 1.10-2.08 px every frame' is what the ray profile supports; 'the contour deforms smoothly every frame' is what the SVG instrument supports (64 path points, rotation removed, in the path's own coordinate space). They agree; they do not independently prove the same thing; the ray profile is the weaker of the two for the attribution.

2. WHY THE RING COULD BE TRANSLATING AT ALL, which the numbers alone do not say: the ring is drawn in its own fixed viewBox, so a moving fitted centre most likely means the ring is moving IN THE PAGE (layout reflow as the state text changes width), not deforming. That cannot affect the SVG instrument - it samples the path's own geometry, not its screen position - which is why the two instruments are complementary rather than duplicative.

3. AND THE RECONCILIATION IT ASKED FOR IS ALREADY DONE, WITH FRAME INDICES RATHER THAN ADJECTIVES. It asked that the visual reader name frame pairs rather than describe. The vision-capable lane reported: A frozen frames 00-02, JUMP at frame 03, frozen 04-09, JUMP at frame 10, frozen 11-15. This lane's ray-profile spikes are at pairs 02->03 and 09->10. Same frames.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
POINT 2 CORRECTED: MY REFLOW EXPLANATION IS DISPROVED, BY MEASUREMENT, BY THE LANE THAT PRODUCED THE NUMBERS IT WAS MEANT TO EXPLAIN.

I hypothesised that the ring's fitted centre was drifting because the ring was moving IN THE PAGE (layout reflow as the state text changed width). cap-ds-flash measured it rather than accepting it: ring bbox centre per frame against two page-level structures in the same frames (the wide bottom band y470-541 and the waveform region y270-460).

  A: ring cx 372.5 -> 373.0 (spread 0.50 px)  | band cx 378.00 spread 0.00 | wave cx 378.50 spread 0.00
  B: ring cx 378.0 -> 372.5 (spread 5.50 px)  | band cx 378.00 spread 0.00 | wave cx 378.50 spread 0.00

Both page-level structures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL IN X in all 16 frames of both builds. So page-level layout did not move in this window and a general reflow is not supported. What the numbers do support: the motion is in the ring's OWN drawing. (Its honest limit, kept: two page-level probes are not proof that nothing page-level moved - a movement confined to the ring's own container would look the same.)

AND TWO DETAILS THAT SHARPEN IT, both of which make the fix's mechanism MORE visible, not less:
  - A's 0.5 px centre step lands at FRAME 10 - the same frame as its second contour spike. So A's centre summary moves on the chunk cadence too, like everything else about A.
  - B starts exactly at the page centre (378.0, the same x as the band and the waveform) and drifts to 372.5 by frame 15 - i.e. B ends where A sits. B's drift is concentrated in frames 10-15 while its contour advanced uniformly across ALL pairs, so B has two things happening at once.

MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION, offered as such and NOT as a measurement: every circular summary of this ring (bbox centre, Kasa fit centre) is biased by the contour's shape, because the contour is an asymmetric closed curve with a travelling crest - and the vision-capable lane described exactly that in B: a travelling bulge rotating smoothly round a ring whose circle stays put. If that is right, the centre drift is the crest's travel seen through a summary statistic, not the circle moving. It stays a hypothesis until somebody measures the drawn centre directly (the path is constructed as centre + r(theta)*u(theta) with known angles, so a least-squares solve for the centre per frame is available to anyone who wants it).

RECORD-KEEPING POINT, which is the actual lesson: a hypothesis offered as a hypothesis got measured and failed, and the failure is now in the same place as the evidence it explained. That is the second time today a lane narrowed its own or another's claim at the cost of some tidiness (the first being the attribution limit from the same lane), and both are worth more than the agreement.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CENTRE QUESTION CLOSED — AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THERE WAS NEVER ANY REAL CENTRE MOTION TO EXPLAIN. Do not use the bbox centre, the fitted circle, or the solved centroid on this ring again without reading this.

TWO FACTS, ONE FROM THE CODE AND ONE FROM A MEASUREMENT:

1. THE DRAWN CENTRE IS A CONSTANT. public/fused.js builds every vertex of the ring as
     points.push([OUTPUT_CENTRE + cos(angle) * radius, OUTPUT_CENTRE + sin(angle) * radius])
   at fixed evenly-spaced angles - so the circle's centre is OUTPUT_CENTRE, a constant, in BOTH builds (the fix moved a smooth() call between two functions; not one line of the drawing changed). A centre that appears to move therefore cannot be the drawn circle moving.

2. THE CONTAINER DOES NOT MOVE EITHER (measured, served page, same feed, 90 frames):
     svg.output-ring   x spread 0.00   y spread 0.00   w 268 spread 0.00   h 268 spread 0.00
     #voice-ring-wrap  x spread 0.00                     w 268 spread 0.00
   No layout change, no resize, no reflow of the ring's own box. Also re-measured here: the state text was CONSTANT ('Agent speaking - your microphone is off') for the whole window, so the reflow idea had no mechanism anyway.

SO EVERY NUMBER IN THIS THREAD ABOUT A MOVING CENTRE IS A SUMMARY STATISTIC OF AN ASYMMETRIC TRAVELLING CONTOUR, with no real component: bbox centre (0.50 px A / 5.50 px B), fitted circle (0.3 / 5.7 px), solved first-harmonic centroid (1.03 / 3.40 px). They differ between builds because the contours differ - which is the fix - and they differ between frames because the crest travels. The first-harmonic-minimised centre IS the curve's centroid, so it travels with the crest by construction; removing the crest bias from a shape summary leaves another shape summary.

MY OWN TWO WRONG INSTRUMENTS IN THIS THREAD, recorded so the next person does not repeat them: (a) I hypothesised page reflow and had it disproved; (b) I then measured path.getBoundingClientRect() thinking it was the container - it is the PATH's own bbox, i.e. another shape summary. The measurement that settles it is the <svg> ELEMENT's box, and that is the one above.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH: the fix's claim (the contour's smoothing cadence) is unaffected - it rests on the geometry profile, the pixel blend, the per-frame RMSE, the rotation-aligned ray profile and the visual read. This closes the attribution question for the centre only.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CLOSING LINE, from the source, verified independently by cap-ds-flash — plus one correction of my own:

THE DISCRIMINATOR WAS NEVER THE CENTRE — IT WAS THE CADENCE. The centre question is closed as 'no real motion component', but nothing about the fix's claim ever depended on it: the cadence is settled by five instruments that did not need the centre at all — the SVG geometry profile, the pixel blend, the per-frame RMSE, the rotation-aligned ray profile, and the visual read (jump frames 03 and 10, matching the numeric spike pairs exactly).

SOURCE CHECKS IT RAN, so the closure is not resting on my summary of my own reasoning:
  - the fix's diff is ONE file (public/audio-client.js, +7/-1) and public/fused.js is not in it — so 'not one line of the drawing changed' is literally true;
  - const OUTPUT_CENTRE = 120 is byte-identical before and after (710a0da^ vs the working tree), with the vertex construction unchanged;
  - the delta is exactly the cadence: smooth(meter.output, meter.smoothOutput, 0.3) moved out of the per-chunk path into the per-frame path.

AND MY OWN NUMBER NEEDS ITS OWN CAVEAT, in the same spirit as the ones that closed this thread. My geometry instrument sampled path points and computed their distances from (50, 50) — a reference I picked in my probe, NOT the ring's centre, which is the fixed 120. So my 'radii' were distances from an arbitrary point, and my residual was a frame-to-frame difference of that summary. That does not weaken the cadence result — frame-to-frame timing of a shape summary is exactly what the question needed, and rotation alignment was applied to the same vector — but the numbers should not be read as radii, the same limit cap-ds-flash stated for its ray profile. Third instrument in this thread with a naming/attribution limit, and the third time stating it made the result survive rather than collapse.

title: a session is running only while somebody is connected to it (runningSession never cleared)
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui 2026-09-23 while checking whether a landed fix needed a restart. Branch fix/live-session-running-flag @ 16fbe15, pushed.

THE DEFECT: server.mjs assigned `runningSession` when a live session started and NOTHING EVER NULLED IT — 'grep -n runningSession server.mjs' returns the initialiser, two readers and the assignment. The close and error handlers called only `session.close()`.

OBSERVED on the served instance: /api/health reported `live: {created:1, running:true}` on three checks over 8 seconds with nobody attached, and stayed true. POST /api/agent-settings told a person 'a session already running keeps the provider it started with' when they had no session — a change deferred to nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MESSAGE: running is the flag that distinguishes STORED from IN USE — the knob a person uses to decide whether it is safe to change the provider. A flag that stays true after the session ends means the interface can never tell them it is safe.

FIX: record which socket owns the session; clear on close/error only when THAT socket goes away. The ownership test is load-bearing: with two peers attached, clearing unconditionally reports the second peer's session as gone when the first leaves. The settings note is now conditional on the state it describes.

FALSIFIER: tests/live-session-flag.test.mjs — drives a real session through the real /live route with the vendor redirected to a local socket (tests/fixtures/live-vendor-redirect.mjs), closes the socket, requires the payload to flip back and the created count NOT to be rewritten; a second test attaches two peers, closes one, requires the other still reported as running, and asserts the note's other half.

MUTATION OUTCOMES, ALL THREE (this is the part worth keeping): guard removed -> RED, 1 fail/1 pass, clean. Clearing removed (the original defect) -> RED, 2 fail, clean. The SAME first mutation, before the teardown was fixed -> HUNG, cancelled at 240 s. A mutation has three outcomes, not two: RED (the check works), GREEN (the check is weak), HUNG (the INSTRUMENT is broken). The hung run was a failing assertion whose teardown awaited a vendor close while a socket was still attached, so a mutation that should have gone red went silent. LESSON FOR THE NEXT PERSON WRITING A MUTATION: a harness that reports only pass and fail cannot report its own failure. Close every socket your test opened; never await a peer that may not leave.

NOT CHANGED: liveSessionsCreated is still a monotonic attempt count on purpose — a refusal that still created a session is the defect that number exists to catch.
close_reason:
LANDED on main as ce78cf6 'fix(live): a session is running only while somebody is connected to it' (gate ALL CLEAR; the served tree was moved onto it and the served API verified afterwards reporting 'main @ c2d180d' with live {created:1, running:false} after a real drive — the flag flipped back on the owner's own instance, which is the fix demonstrated where it was broken).

THE THREE-OUTCOME MUTATION TABLE, as coord asked it be recorded here:
  · guard removed (clear unconditionally)            -> RED, 1 fail / 1 pass, clean, 557 ms
  · clearing removed (the original defect)           -> RED, 2 fail, clean, 8.3 s
  · the same first mutation BEFORE the teardown fix  -> HUNG, cancelled at 240 s, no verdict
The third row is a finding about the INSTRUMENT, not the fix: a failing assertion ran a teardown that awaited a vendor close while a live socket was still attached, so a mutation that should have gone red went silent — and silence is indistinguishable from 'the check is weak' unless somebody notices. A mutation has three outcomes: RED (the check works), GREEN (the check is weak), HUNG (the test is broken). A harness that reports only pass and fail cannot report its own failure. Fix: every socket the test opens is closed before the server stops; no teardown waits on a peer that may not leave.

Also recorded here earlier: this same defect had been filed twice in one session (voicebox-beads-3vp was the earlier copy, named for the symptom) — the lesson being to search the tracker for the SYMPTOM rather than the mechanism.

title: Two concepts, two names: VOICEBOX_RESOLVER and VOICEBOX_LIVE_PROVIDER (old names honoured)
description:
COORD APPROVED 2026-09-23. Branch chore/provider-env-names.

THE DEFECT (name, not behaviour): server.mjs read VOICEBOX_PROVIDER for which TURN RESOLVER answers POST /api/turn, while lib/live-session.mjs read LIVE_PROVIDER for the LIVE TRANSPORT's fallback provider. The pair read as though the second were the live-mode sibling of the first. It misled in practice: tests/lib/server.mjs records a voice-path developer exporting VOICEBOX_PROVIDER=live, which put 'live' in the RESOLVER slot and stopped turns writing.

THE JUSTIFICATION IS NOT AN OPINION: docs/07-architecture.md already described them as two different things (LIVE_PROVIDER = library fallback, VOICEBOX_PROVIDER = turn resolver). The documentation was right; the code names were what misled. The rename brings the code in line with a description that already existed.

WHAT LANDED: VOICEBOX_RESOLVER (turn resolver) and VOICEBOX_LIVE_PROVIDER (live fallback); both old names honoured for one release and NEVER silently: when VOICEBOX_PROVIDER is set the server prints either 'honouring … for this release' or 'IGNORING … because VOICEBOX_RESOLVER is set'. The generated env table in README (scanned from the source by scripts/docs-check.mjs) now lists all four names, with the two legacy rows saying they are old names.

TESTED, NOT CLAIMED: tests/env-names.test.mjs — the new name is read; the old name still works AND says so on stderr; the new name wins when both are set and the operator is told the old one was ignored; the live provider resolves old and new to the same name with an explicit provider still beating both. The both-set case failed first with the silent version, which is why the server now speaks in both directions.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: the old names are not removed in this release. Removal is a later, deliberate change (delete the fallback + the stderr lines + the two legacy tests).
close_reason: LANDED on main: chore/provider-env-names rebased onto 0635dd5 and fast-forwarded to main as 3061f00 (gate ALL CLEAR). Verified on the served tree: the page stamp reads feat/serve-help @ 0635dd5 for both halves. tests/env-names.test.mjs pins the contract (new name read; old name honoured AND loud; new name wins when both set; live fallback resolves old and new alike). The generated env table now lists all four names with the two legacy rows marked as old names. Old names honoured for one release; removal is a later deliberate change.

title: runningSession is never cleared: /api/health reports a live session forever after the first one
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, while checking whether a landed fix needed a restart.

THE DEFECT: server.mjs sets `runningSession` at line 1646 when a live session starts and NEVER CLEARS IT. The close and error handlers call only `session.close()`:
    ws.on('close', () => session.close());   // provider session closed
    ws.on('error', () => session.close());   // flag left set
`grep -n 'runningSession' server.mjs` returns exactly two lines: the initialiser (349) and the assignment (1646). Nothing nulls it.

OBSERVED, on the served instance (8787), no client attached: /api/health reported `live:{created:1,running:true}` on three checks over 8 seconds.

TWO SURFACES LIE AS A RESULT:
  1. /api/health: `running: true` for the life of the process after the first session, with nobody connected.
  2. POST /api/agent-settings: answers 'stored — a session already running keeps the provider it started with' to a person who has no session, so a settings change reads as deferred to nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MESSAGE: 'running' is the flag that distinguishes STORED from IN USE — the knob a person uses to decide whether it is safe to change the provider. A flag that stays true after the session ends means the interface cannot ever tell them it is safe.

FIX: clear it in both handlers (and anywhere a session reaches a terminal state) — one line, plus a test that starts and closes a session and reads /api/health's `running`.

NOTE ON ATTRIBUTION (kept here because it is evidence about the GATE, not about this bug): the single session counted in `created` was created by a diagnostic wire probe carrying `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8787` — entitled by construction, so a real provider session was created and paid for. That is the claim the hello gate's own comment says it cannot verify; the gate behaved as designed.

title: Plain-language gate misses dynamically rendered refusal identifiers
description: Review of feat/harness-discovery@27741b8 found adapter-not-configured rendered beside its explanation while page acceptance passed. tools/page-acceptance.mjs lines 212-264 scans source HTML/JS literals, not rendered DOM; the source contains ${row.delegation.refused}, while the actual identifier comes from API data. Widening the static word list or adding a kebab-case regex there cannot catch this case. Implement a bounded rendered-text check after exercising representative refusal states, with narrow documented treatment for legitimate command names/code examples and excluding diagnostic title/data attributes. Keep the current source check honest about its scope. Inventory now has a direct browser regression checking all seven cards preserve explanations and hide their refusal IDs; no generic gate change was made in that fix.
acceptance_criteria: Inject a previously unseen multi-hyphen refusal ID through API data and show the rendered-state gate fails; the same ID retained solely in a title/data attribute passes. Show nonzero rendered-state coverage and preserve legitimate CLI commands/code examples without blanket exemptions.
close_reason:
LANDED on main in the 8c87e06 merge (content 988b585, verified by reading the landed files rather than the report: tests/rendered-plain-language.test.mjs carries 6 cases on main).

WHAT LANDED: the plain-language gate now reads WHAT A PERSON CAN SEE, not only what we wrote. tools/rendered-plain-language.mjs holds one vocabulary used twice (source literals AND rendered text); the run's refusal vocabulary is harvested from the responses the run itself received, so an identifier that exists in no source literal is still caught; shapes cover ticket ids, an id SPELLED OUT (seven-cd) and attached ids IN CONTEXT (bead 7cd, ticket 0ye, issue #12ab) — not by shape alone, because a bare shape rule fired on 22rem and 4s; the diagnostic allowance is asserted BOTH WAYS in a real browser (visible fails, title/data-* passes, code/pre exempt by element); ZERO readable text is a FAILURE rather than a pass; and the output carries its own scope.

THREE PAGE FIXES: the listing refusal's fallback, the environment row's unreachable LABEL (it printed the refusal id), and two hard-coded ids in the settings surface (one, machine-unreachable (fix the host), was a literal no source check was looking for). All now say the thing in words with the server's term on the title. Two suites were asserting the old contract and were updated rather than deleted.

DRIVEN: green with 2758/2819 characters of visible text read; a fabricated project carrying a bead id declared THROUGH THE API -> FAIL naming seven-cd twice; undeclared -> green again (so the failure was the data, not a stale run).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: The current source check answers what did we write, while the user-facing requirement asks what is on the page; API data and markup diverge at that boundary. A rendered check must inspect visible served DOM text after data and refusal states are applied, not just initial page load, source literals or diagnostic data/title attributes. Cost is not free: it adds state setup and assertions to existing browser drives (the complete inventory drive locally is approximately 1-3 seconds, not an isolated benchmark of the proposed check). Coverage remains limited to driven pages, states and responses; it cannot prove all future provider/error text, unvisited dialogs or inaccessible shadow/frame content are plain English. Define nonzero state coverage and preserve those limitations in reporting.

title: RULE: a process that writes must write outside anything another process measures
description:
## The shape

**A process that writes must write outside anything another process measures.**
Three instances landed today, from three different authors, all the same shape: a writer leaving output where
something else reads state. In every case the symptom was MISLEADING — a dirty tree nobody dirtied by editing,
a file list that was a test's, a check that failed for a reason unrelated to the change under test.

## The three instances

1. **The one-root test suite committed its own audit logs into the repository** — which is how test-run
   artefacts reached a branch and made a change look like it carried files it never touched.
2. **The acceptance harness left its scratch root declared on the shared server**, so a person's page showed a
   test's directory as if it were theirs — the harness's own state leaking into what a human reads.
3. **A Dolt backup was written into the served tree** (`~/worktrees/voicebox-dev/backup/`, 2026-09-20T21:54:40Z)
   because the backup process's **cwd was that tree**. Dolt wrote its backup format there —
   `manifest` (`5:__DOLT__:…`), `backup_state.json` (`last_dolt_commit`, `timestamp`), a `.darc` archive,
   `LOCK`, `oldgen/` — and the acceptance harness's `git status --porcelain` check counts untracked
   directories, so **every landing attempted from that tree read as dirty for a reason no author caused.**

## The rule

- scratch dirs → temp, owned by the process that made them, removed by it;
- backups → outside every repository, and re-runnable without landing inside one;
- test output → its own tree, never the served tree and never the audited root.

## Why it matters more than a dirty directory

Each instance produced a **red check that pointed at the wrong thing**, and the cost was paid by whoever
looked next: a reviewer chasing a file they did not write, a person reading a test's directory as their own,
a lane unable to land. A check whose failure describes the tooling rather than the change is the same class as
everything else in this ledger — *the instrument has to be able to report the thing it is guarding.*

## The evidence, kept because it was diagnosable in one pass

Format named from its own files (`manifest` + `.darc` + `oldgen/`), timestamp read from
`backup_state.json`, the cwd it implies, and the owner ruled out by session cwd plus worktree list — not by
assurance. Relocated to `~/.local/share/voicebox-dolt-backup-20260920T230559` (bytes preserved, reversible,
nothing deleted) at coord's approval; the served tree's `git status --porcelain` is empty again.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
**LANDED ON A BRANCH: `fix/live-hello-auth @ bad26b7`** (0 deletions vs main; pre-push gate ALL GATES GREEN).

**THE DEFECT, DRIVEN BEFORE THE FIX** — a peer that opened /live and sent an unauthenticated frame received:
`rate` → `transport-open` → **`ready`, provider "gemini"**: a real provider session created for a connection
nothing had asked about. Refusal-then-cleanup, not a gate. That transcript is the first red this branch made.

**WHAT IT DOES NOW**: the socket does not reach the provider until the connection is entitled to it. The local
page is entitled by construction (own Origin; this host hands no credentials to a page); every other peer
presents the pairing bearer in the FIRST frame `{"type":"hello","bearer":"vbx_…"}`. Missing/malformed/wrong/
silent → a NAMED refusal (`unauthenticated-call`, `bearer-refused`) with the remedy in `why`, closed before any
session exists. A 5s bound, because silence is not a credential.

**THE SECOND HALF, WITNESSED**: `liveSessionsCreated` counts where the spend happens (before
`createLiveSession`, so a throwing create still counts) and `/api/health` reports `live: { created, running }`.
The tests assert the count, not just the refusal — *refused is satisfied by the broken version too*.

**MUTATION CHECK**: old order restored (session first, gate after) → the first test reds on *"a refused peer
must NEVER receive the rate frame"* and the paired case reds on the created count; mutant removed.

**CONSEQUENCE, DECLARED**: `tests/live-rate-frame.test.mjs` and `tests/live-voice.test.mjs` are local Node
clients of a server they spawn and now declare the local origin — the same thing a browser does for them.

**NOT CLAIMED**: "same origin" is a claim any non-browser client can make (it can set headers), so this gate
stops an unentitled peer costing a session and makes the paired path enforceable — a per-process page token
minted into the served HTML is what closes the claim itself, and belongs with the environment-identity work.
Also not driven here: audio flowing on the authenticated path (needs a real key; the session is created, the
vendor leg is not exercised).

**TWO BUGS OF MY OWN, both caught by the tests**: the project's zero-dep socket has `on` and not `once` (my
first gate threw inside the handler, so every remote peer fell through to the timeout — three identical
failures made it legible), and the local-page check compared against `PORT` (= 0 on an ephemeral bind) instead
of the BOUND port.

Gate: 204 tests, 203 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (wabt parity half, labelled).

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED & PUSHED (gemini): branch feat/pairing-revocation @ dce72e65f08f0e6055da90ab9ce2432b506546c6.

1. Design & Lifecycle Decisions:
- Revocation actively and immediately terminates authority ('this session ends now'): revoking an environment immediately closes active /channel executor sockets (1008 pairing-revoked, clearing pageSocket and abandoning waiting calls) and closes active /live voice sessions (1008 pairing-revoked).
- Revoked credentials are tracked in .pairings.json (revoked: true, revokedAt, revokedBy: 'host-token', revokedBearers: [...]), allowing the system to distinguish between a revoked credential (pairing-revoked) and an unknown token (bearer-refused).
- Host gate: DELETE /api/pair requires x-voicebox-host-token and logs to the host audit trail.

2. Driven Verification:
- Minted pairing via POST /api/pair.
- Connected active /channel executor socket and active /live voice session socket. Verified both open and operating.
- Revoked pairing via DELETE /api/pair with host token.
- Existing connections observed FIRST: /channel socket received refusal frame and closed with WS 1008 pairing-revoked; /live socket received refusal frame and closed with WS 1008 pairing-revoked.
- Fresh connections observed: /channel hello, /live hello, POST /api/execute, and POST /api/call all refuse by name with pairing-revoked (HTTP 403 / WS 1008).
- Re-pairing issues a fresh bearer that connects cleanly, while the historical revoked bearer remains refused.
- Unknown stranger bearer refuses bearer-refused, preserving distinct diagnosis.

What follows is the one thing the bead was missing: **exactly which measured report makes the refusal fire, per axis, read out of the receipts rather than the design.**

THE RECEIPT IS THE SPEC (measured, `reports/sandbox-survey-20260920/probe-bwrap.json`):
- **deny-files** reads `filesystem` — fields `home`, `pathEntries`, `dirs`, `canReadPasswd`, `mountsReadable`.
- **deny-processes** reads `tools` — one result per binary (`sh`, `bash`, `node`, `python3`, …, `bwrap`, `sudo`, `mount`), each carrying `value` when the binary RAN.
- **passthrough-network** reads `network` — `loopback`, `dns`, `outboundTcp443IpLiteral`, `outboundTcp80ByName`, `cloudMetadataService`, `interfaces`, `resolvConf`, each carrying `reachable`.

THE FIRING CONDITION, per axis — `decide(report, act)` refuses `absent-capability` when the measured outcome is the OPPOSITE of the deny the tier claims, and names the axis and the remedy:
1. `deny-processes`: a `tools.<binary>.value` present for a binary the act needs (i.e. the shell ran *inside* the fence) → refuse, axis `deny-processes`, remedy "bwrap bounds which binary, not what it can do; the fence must deny the interpreter, not the wrapper".
2. `passthrough-network`: `network.outboundTcp443IpLiteral.reachable === true` or `outboundTcp80ByName.reachable === true` — and unambiguously `cloudMetadataService.reachable === true` → refuse, axis `passthrough-network`, remedy "an egress policy, not a hint: the probe reached the metadata service".
3. `deny-files`: `filesystem.mountsReadable` (or `home`/`pathEntries`) showing a path outside the root was readable → refuse, axis `deny-files`, remedy "scope the root; a readable home is not a deny".

WHY THIS KEEPS THE PROMISE FRIABLE (the handover's key property, preserved):
`decide(report, act)` takes S1's `BoundaryReport` as data, so when the fence boots the drive is an **addition rather than a rewrite** — three fixtures, one per axis, each a *real* receipt from this file with the measured field flipped, plus the falsification that matters: **a report whose axis IS denied must produce no refusal at all** (otherwise the gate fires on everything and is decoration). I could not write those three fixtures without a fence to produce a report from, which is the reason this is a comment and not a branch.

WHAT REMAINS (a small, bounded slice for whoever picks it up):
1. `core/tier-table.ts`: `decide(report, act)` → `{ ok: false, refused: "absent-capability", axis, why, remedy }`, with `axis` a value from the receipt's own vocabulary (the three above), and the refusal quoting the measured field and its value.
2. Three fixtures built from `probe-bwrap.json` — one per axis — asserting the refusal names the axis AND the remedy.
3. The negative fixture (axis denied ⇒ no refusal), which is the one that proves it is a gate rather than a slogan.
4. Wire it into whatever reads the tier table, ONLY once S1 emits the report — the bead stays OPEN until then, which is the rule this handover came with.

description: WHAT: --unshare-net closure is driven both directions; the page cannot reach a net-fenced server. close_reason:
DECIDED & CLOSED (gemini): branch design/s3-l2-bridge @ be80a789a77b75249f3c14a27a810f3c5b8813fa.

DECISION: The inbound network bridge (socat/nsenter) is DECLARED OUT OF SCOPE for interactive server environments. S3 is closed without building a bridge. Published design document: docs/14-s3-l2-bridge-decision.md.

RATIONALE:
1. Product Contradiction: Voicebox server requires outbound WebSockets to Gemini Live / OpenAI Realtime. Under --unshare-net, outbound connections fail with ENETUNREACH. An inbound bridge allows the browser page to reach the server, but the server cannot reach any model — creating a server that serves but cannot think or speak.
2. The Proxy Trap: To restore model egress in an unshared netns, a full outbound filtering forward proxy (like Anthropic's srt proxy) would be required. As documented in journal/topics/sandbox-mechanisms.md, srt's proxy introduced loopback IPv6 bugs, NO_PROXY breakages, and path-widening CVEs.
3. Truth in Measurement: The interactive server ladder is complete at L1.5 (filesystem fenced + process fenced + systemd-run seccomp/caps lockdown). The network axis is honestly reported as 'passes' (shared with host), rather than claiming L2 via a proxy-holed network.
4. Offline Role for --unshare-net: Network namespace isolation is preserved in tools/fence.sh and reserved strictly for offline/batch execution (delegate_task under D1/D2) where no live server or model connection is required.
5. Re-open Conditions: 1) Local on-device LLM runner eliminating internet requirement; or 2) Hardened, fleet-approved outbound proxy substrate.

- Crash reconciliation: on a non-terminal record read after restart, a different boot generation does NOT by itself prove death — the host probes the recorded pid (process.kill(pid,0)); a maybe-alive prior owner refuses task-owner-unconfirmed and NOTHING is recovered or replayed; only a proven-dead owner (ESRCH) is marked interrupted with reason environment-ended-outcome-unknown (or admission-unconfirmed for a same-boot admission whose dispatch was never confirmed). Exactly the bead's 'if dispatch might have occurred, do NOT replay: inspect receipts, mark interrupted or outcome-unknown, ask'.
- The stock-server refusal (placement clarification): a stock server has no task executor — a CLI-looking name and descriptor data cannot create one (browser cannot spawn a stdio CLI; the unavailable capability refuses by name).

WHICH TEST DRIVES IT (re-run fresh, all in the default gate glob, npm test 352 total): tests/tasks.test.mjs 15/0 (record mechanics); tests/tasks-http.test.mjs + tests/tasks-browser.test.mjs 3/0 — 'D1 real HTTP: killed environment -> interrupted, no replay' and 'D1 browser: handle first, unrelated turn, independent page, reload and observed environment death' — kill mid-task, restart, state interrupted with the event log as receipts, f.starts().length === 1 (ONE dispatch, no replay), independent browser profile resolving the address, page reload doing a fresh server read. The reconnect half is served by the full pinned record (task_status by address); the reader restores event position from the record's seq-ordered events.

WHICH ORIGINAL CLAIMS WERE NEVER TRUE:
1. 'Depends on the oplog attempted-and-lost record (y69) as the receipt mechanism' — never true: y69 was a mis-filed isocan oplog issue (the 2026-09-21 clarification warned its closure was not proof of voicebox receipts); the actual mechanism is D1's own durable task record. The dependency is satisfied in name only; the content lives in 8u1.
2. 'restores last delivered event position' as a server-side cursor — never built; the full pinned record is served and position restore is reader-side over seq. The DONE (kill/restart → interrupted, no replay) never required a cursor.
3. A server-side 'summarise unfinished/newly-completed work' endpoint — never built; the record + state carries it and the reader (agent or driver) does the summarising, as the browser test's witness lines show.

DONE as written is driven and green. Closing by content.

DEPS: D1; and journal-beads-3uq (Paul's where-does-the-harness-run decision governs the transport); see also voicebox-beads-mzs (N18) if the client belongs in the library.

2026-09-21 placement clarification (supersedes universal server assumptions above):
BINDING REQUIREMENT (Paul, 2026-09-21): the harness must run anywhere, including entirely in a browser client with zero Voicebox server or local bridge. Server deployment is allowed for machine access, not required by the shared contract. Placement changes available capabilities, transport, storage and lifetime; it must not fork the coordination semantics. A browser cannot spawn a stdio CLI; refuse that unavailable capability rather than hiding a server dependency. Zero server does not mean zero remote model API.
D2 remains the ONE ACP client/real-adapter implementation; no duplicate ACP bead was created. Stdio is the first machine adapter, not the shared-library transport contract. Browser-side use must support browser-capable adapters without Node imports, process spawn or a mandatory bridge. A pi-acp subprocess itself is not browser-compatible. Separate ACP state/validation from transport/owner I/O; reuse N18 rather than importing CAP. Before a real task is admitted, prove the runtime boundary (S1 filesystem/shared-network report alone is insufficient), bounded provider access and credential isolation. Add a README/docs entry and executable one-adapter setup walkthrough naming ACP, exact verified adapter version, configuration, readiness/refusals, and browser limitations. Host-only smoke evidence must not close zero-server acceptance. Configuration follows voicebox-beads-8fv.2.
