   Reading: four workers give near-linear scaling on this workload and stay green at saturation; eight workers put loadavg at 3.5x the box and start losing runs. So the tier's width of 4 is measured-defensible on an 8-vCPU box and I recommend NO CHANGE; what is missing is not a smaller width but the ability to say afterwards what the box was doing.

3. THE FAILURE MODE AT K=8, which is the useful part: both failures are the real-mouse click losing its target, not a slow turn and not a wrong assertion (see voicebox-beads-18lh for the full capture). At loadavg 27.8 the page's hit test and the dispatch disagree, so `page.click` sends the event where the element no longer is; one run lost the click that starts the turn, the other lost the click that focuses the field for typing. Under the old arm both were indistinguishable from a hang. Consequence for this bead: load CAN break tests, but not by making a correct wait expire - so "is the tier oversubscribed?" has the answer "at 4 workers, no; past that, yes, and clicks go first".

4. PROPOSAL, for approval (no silent change):

Record host context in the gate artifact: top-level `host: { cpus, available_parallelism, loadavg: { before, max, after }, sampled_at }` in the manifest from createManifest/recordFile (a versioned change: MANIFEST_VERSION plus the validator plus its tests, because that module refuses near-right shapes), and for the browser tier the loadavg when each FILE started and finished in that file's record, since the runner already knows both moments and already records the file's `secs`.

The value is being able to say "this failed at loadavg 27" or "this failed on an idle box, so it is behaviour" without another hour of guessing, which is exactly what 18lh cost tonight.
   d. Separate, and the one I would take next if you want it: when a test's expected effect is absent after a real-mouse click, name the element that actually received it (`document.elementFromPoint` at the dispatched coordinates, recorded in the failure). That lives in tests/lib/cdp.mjs, is shared by every browser test, and is therefore a reviewed change with a blast-radius note - not something to slip in beside a P3 measurement.

THE COMBINED v3 CONTRACT for the per-suite three-condition classification (zjpm.5.2), written to be added to the shape I already pushed at 98b56bf, and to line up with 55wl's per-tier numbers rather than compete with it. You write it, I review it; this is the contract, so if you think one rule is wrong, say which and why rather than shipping a different shape.

WHAT IS ALREADY MINE AND MUST NOT BE REDEFINED: the manifest `host` block {cpus, available_parallelism, loadavg_1m {before,max,after}, sampled_at}; the per-file `loadavg_1m {start, end}`; lib/host-load.mjs as the only reader of the box (import loadavg1m/hostCores/hostSnapshot/isLoadavg, never os.loadavg directly). MANIFEST_VERSION becomes 3 with your change and that is ONE bump for zjpm.6 + zjpm.5.2 + 55wl together.

WHERE IT GOES: a `conditions` array ON THE FILE RECORD of the suite that was classified. The suite's path, its tier, its ORIGINAL verdict and its original box window are already on that record (`path`, `tier`, `status`, `secs`, `loadavg_1m`) - so do not duplicate the path or the original verdict anywhere, and do not add a second top-level keyed-by-path block. That also guarantees the property I care most about: `verdictOf` never reads `conditions`, so a classification can never soften a gate.

  {
    "path": "tests/tasks-browser.test.mjs", "tier": "browser",
    "status": "failed", "secs": 12.12, "loadavg_1m": {"start":10.04,"end":9.88},   // the ORIGINAL shard verdict and window
    "conditions": [
      {"condition":"standalone", "status":"passed", "secs":5.1,  "loadavg_1m":{"start":1.2,"end":1.4},   "worker_count":1, "command":"node --test tests/tasks-browser.test.mjs"},
      {"condition":"peer-held",  "status":"passed", "secs":18.3, "loadavg_1m":{"start":11.0,"end":11.3}, "worker_count":1, "command":"fleet-heavy timeout 300 node --test tests/tasks-browser.test.mjs"},
      {"condition":"shard",      "status":"failed", "secs":12.2, "loadavg_1m":{"start":8.6,"end":8.9},   "worker_count":4, "command":"node tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs --only tests/tasks-browser.test.mjs --workers 4"}
    ],
    "condition_verdict": {"disagreement": true, "agrees_with_shard": true}
  }

PER ENTRY, REQUIRED, and each refusal by name:
  condition     enum: standalone | peer-held | shard. Unknown refused. Duplicates refused. (A typed string is how "the three conditions" quietly become three different things.)
  status        REUSES the existing STATUS vocabulary (passed/failed/skipped/timeout/unknown) - do not invent a second status set; that is the no-parallel-schema rule applied to values.
  secs          finite number; REQUIRED unless status is "skipped", with the same rounding as the file record.
  loadavg_1m    {start,end}, REQUIRED, each a non-negative reading or null via isLoadavg. These conditions exist because of the box, so an entry with no box reading is the gap this whole bead closes.
  worker_count  positive integer, required. A duration with no worker count is not a reproduction.
  command       non-empty string, required. A condition nobody can re-run is an opinion.
  reason        REQUIRED when status is "skipped" (the same rule that makes an omitted file with no reason a refusal).
  extra keys    refused.

THE TWO DERIVED FIELDS, stamped where `summary` is stamped (the sealer) and VALIDATED if a tier record states them, so there is one computing site:
  disagreement        true when the conditions do not all share one status. This is THE signal coord wants the nightly list built from.
  agrees_with_shard   true when the `shard` condition's status equals the file record's own `status`. That is your "observed original shard verdict", and the field exists to name the comparison, not to restate the verdict.

COMPLETENESS: enforced by REFUSAL, not recorded. Fewer than three entries, or a missing one of the three, is refused (a partial classification is a claim nobody can use) - a probe that was cut short says so on the entry it affected (status timeout/unknown/skipped), because those are already in the vocabulary. I am deliberately NOT adding a `completeness` field: it could only ever say "complete" once the refusal above exists, and a field that can only say one thing is noise. If you want it for the nightly grep, argue it and it must be stamped and validated like the other two.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU, both of which I have already hit:
  1. `conditions` may only sit on a record whose `dispatch` is "ran": a probe attached to a file that never ran is not a classification of that file's shard verdict, and it is refused.
  2. If you classify a UNIT-lane suite (tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs is the obvious candidate), the file's own `loadavg_1m` is NULL - that is v2's scope, browser tier only, which coord approved. That is honest and allowed: judge the disagreement from the condition entries, which carry their own windows. Do NOT "fix" it by publishing a unit per-file window in this change; that is the scope question I already put to coord (the unit tier runs 94 files from one pool, so where those readings come from is a design choice) and it needs its own answer.

NOT YOURS TO ADD HERE: 55wl's per-tier `affected` / `affected_not_run` + `subset {files, cap_ms, wall_ms}`. That is one additive block for the whole combined change, `cap_ms` is required whenever anything was skipped for the cap, and a stated count that disagrees with the file records (selection changed|dependency and dispatch != ran) must be refused. I have given type-recover the same shape, so the two of you are writing one v3, not two.

FINALLY: coord ruled automatic three-condition classification ONLY for failing suites, targeted opt-in per named suite, and a nightly short named queue-sensitive list. So the artifact records measurements for the suites that were named and must not itself decide what "queue-sensitive" means - the list is a judgement, the numbers are the evidence, and `conditions: null` (not present) is how "this suite was not classified" is said.

CONTRACT AMENDMENT (v3, added before any edit exists - fix-85lx's design message crossed with my contract send): ONE MORE REQUIRED FIELD, `peers`, FOR THE peer-held CONDITION.

Their confirmed design is to build the peer-held condition from a peer holder plus CPU burners tuned to a target measured load, rather than by holding the fleet-heavy slot. That is a reasonable proxy and it is NOT the real gate condition: in the gate the peers are browsers and unit workers (CPU plus renderer processes, profile IO, memory), while burners are a pure CPU shape.   command remains the SUITE's command, and for peer-held it must not be the thing that describes the peers.

Also restated for their measurement, since it bites in practice: os.loadavg()[0] is the 1-MINUTE average, so "target a loadavg" only means something after the burners have run long enough for the average to move (~30s); a condition whose start reading is below the intended target records the reading and must not pretend to the intent. Both ends are already required - that is what they are for.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
**FIXED** — stacked on the uei2.9 tip as a new tip on the same branch: `fleet/type-recover-harnesses` @ **c2017a8** (was `4deca7e`; fast-forward, so both land as ONE reviewed branch). Pre-push gate: **ALL GATES GREEN (unit)**.

## Root cause
`tests/harnesses-dialog-extraction.test.mjs` clicked the check button, slept **400 ms of wall time**, then asserted the painted inventory status and rows — a bet that the `/api/harnesses` response arrives within 400 ms. Under a 1200 ms injected delay it does not, the status still reads "Checking host programs…" and the rows are empty, so the arm fails on a **correct** app. Same class as ezu7 / jeye / y1db.

## The fix (assertion semantics kept, not weakened)
Every wait is now on the observable its assertion is about:
- **the two fetch counts are taken in the SAME TICK as the click**, because the click handler issues its fetch synchronously. That deletes the clone's 300 ms sleep outright, and makes "a listener-free clone fetches nothing" evidence about listeners instead of about a window having elapsed.
- **status + rows** wait (bounded `page.waitFor`, which throws on timeout) for the delayed inventory paint.
- **the task path** waits for its changed files to be painted through the returned callback.
- **the save path** waits for the sentinel in the status line to be **replaced** — the observable that the handler got past `if (!getLastHarnessOutput()) return;`. A stale snapshot leaves the sentinel untouched and the wait FAILS, so the pair semantics are unchanged.
- **the tracker** waits for the mini-app frame to appear instead of sleeping 500 ms.

The 1200 ms delay is **kept in the arm** (injected over `/api/harnesses`), so independence from wall time is proven on every run rather than assumed.

## Acceptance
1. **Fixed test PASSES under the 1200 ms delay injection** — 4/4, the delay injected in the arm itself.
2. **A control still FAILS when the app genuinely never resolves** — new test: an `/api/harnesses` response that never settles, then the *same* wait primitive is required to reject, bounded at 2500 ms (`assert.rejects`, matched on "timed out waiting for an inventory that genuinely never resolves"). It also records what a never-resolving check honestly looks like: the check has started, the button is still disabled. It runs last because it deliberately leaves the check disabled.
3. Extra mutant for confidence: with the inventory status **never painted**, the arm goes RED with exactly `timed out waiting for the (deliberately delayed) host inventory response to be painted`. So the wait is not vacuous. Tree verified pristine after.

Cost, stated plainly: the file is still ~10 s in the **browser** lane (the host inventory probe is ~7 s, and the arm runs one check cycle). The **unit fast gate is unaffected** — this test is not part of that tier, which is why this bug reached a reviewer rather than the fast gate.

title: P3: static guard for the transient-state class (zjpm.5 follow-up) - encode the discriminator, not the grep
description:
Follow-up to the zjpm.5 audit, and the reason the audit took hand-reading rather than a grep. The mechanical
signals are all noisy in the SAME direction: the failure shape ("wait on A, assert B") is also the CORRECT shape
whenever B is written synchronously with A, and it is the accidental shape of every poll-loop helper. My three
scans over the tiers produced 100 / 36 / 50 candidates and hand-reading cleared all but one. So the guard must
encode the discriminator, not the surface form:

  a site is a candidate ONLY IF the asserted observable is written by an ASYNC path (fetch/timer/event/socket)
  AND the test's wait signal can be satisfied BEFORE that write AND the test reads once with no wait on the
  asserted observable. Separately: a wait on the FIRST writer of a SYNCHRONOUS pair is safe (the second write
  happens in the same task, measured in tests/health-auth-browser.test.mjs), which is what makes the surface
  form unusable as a detector.

Acceptance (bounded, static, no browser): a checker in the style of scripts/docs-touched.mjs that flags (1) a
fixed sleep immediately before an assertion inside a browser-lane test, unless the assertion is an ABSENCE or the
sleep is a poll interval inside a loop, and (2) an exact-string or exact-count assertion on a status observable
the test never waits for, cross-referenced against the page code that writes it. Fail-closed on candidates it
cannot classify, or print them as a review list. The value is that the next jeye/y1db is caught in review rather
than by a red gate on an unrelated union.

title: P3: live-lane readiness windows sample a cross-process state (zjpm.5 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to the zjpm.5 audit. The live lane has readiness windows that are NOT latency-only, because the
observable is written by another process (the vendor socket / the model) rather than synchronously by the test's
own click:

  tests/live-provider-seam.test.mjs:115  500ms -> session.ready === true
  tests/live-agent-settings.test.mjs:45  200ms -> states.some(ready)
  tests/page-writes.test.mjs:241         200ms -> states.some(ready)
  tests/live-project-instruction.test.mjs:373  150ms -> setups.length === 1 (an absence: legitimate)
  tests/live-session-flag.test.mjs:161   400ms -> live.running === true after a peer leaves (an absence: legitimate)

The first three sample a state that a socket event delivers, so a slow box turns them red and a slow implementation
turns them green. Acceptance: for each, wait on the observable itself (a state file, a recorded event, or the
session object the fixture owns) instead of the delay; keep the assertions unchanged; leave the two absence
windows alone and say why in a comment. Bounded to the live lane, which does not gate every landing, so this is
P3 and can ride with the next live-lane change.

comments.text:
DONE (my half - the schema). Branch fleet/v3-conditions-schema @ 71f533a, PUSHED (this is the single schema tip: it carries zjpm.6's host block, a8a2's unit-tier readings + failing-arm field, and now the v3 conditions + the refusal). WHAT IS IN THE TIP (scripts/gate-manifest.mjs):
- `MANIFEST_VERSION` 2 -> 3. The pin that said "bump this deliberately, never by accident" fired and the deliberation is the commit; v1/v2 artifacts still reconcile as the shapes they declared, so `verify` keeps reading the checks directory's history.
- `conditions` on a file record: one arm per condition from the closed set `standalone` | `heavy_slot` | `shard_concurrency`. Per arm: `condition`, `status`, `secs` (not required for `skipped`/`unknown` - neither can have a duration), `loadavg_1m {start,end}`, `worker_count` (positive int), `command` (the command that ran it), optional `counts {tests,pass,fail,skipped}`, `reason` (REQUIRED for `skipped` and `unknown`), `holder` (REQUIRED for `heavy_slot` - the burners are a proxy for the slot and a proxy is a claim). Extra keys refused. All three arms required: a two-arm check is refused by name. Arms only on a record that RAN, enforced on the write path AND in reconcile.
- `condition_verdict`, derived by the sealer from the arms and never stated: `pattern` (standalone_only_fails | concurrency_only_fails | heavy_slot_only_fails | all_agree | mixed | incomplete), `disagreement`, `agrees_with_shard`. Any arm `skipped`/`unknown` -> `incomplete` with BOTH other fields null; a stated verdict that differs from the arms is refused by name, which is where a `disagreement: false` beside an unmeasured arm stops being printable.
- The a8a2 refusal: a `failed` record whose `failure_evidence.version >= 2` names no arm is refused by name. Version-gated so pre-a8a2 evidence still audits, only for `failed`, never for `timeout`/`unknown`, and never where `counts.fail === 0`. `failure_evidence.version` is deliberately NOT bumped again - it tracks the evidence record, the conditions are a separate optional field, and they stay independent.
- `verdictOf` does not read any of it: the arms DESCRIBE, the file's own terminal status still decides.

TESTS: tests/gate-manifest.test.mjs 32/32 - the derived verdict for every pattern including `mixed` and the unmeasured `incomplete`; twelve refusals by name (unknown condition, named twice, two-arm check, missing arm, extra key, heavy_slot with no holder, skipped/unknown with no reason, string reading, worker_count 0, no command, arms on a non-ran record, stated-verdict mismatch); the a8a2 narrowings both ways (named accepted; v1 tolerated; timeout/unknown tolerated; fail:0 tolerated; a passed record not asked). tests/gate-tier.test.mjs + tests/browser-shard-runner.test.mjs green with it (52/52 together). docs/12-pre-push-gate.md carries both paragraphs and both no-waiver rules.

FOR fix-85lx'S CLI, the exact thing to emit (feed it through `recordFile(..., { conditions })` or a tier record's own `conditions`, which recordTier forwards):
  conditions: [
    { condition: "standalone",        status, secs, loadavg_1m: {start, end}, worker_count, command, counts? },
    { condition: "heavy_slot",        status, secs, loadavg_1m, worker_count, command, counts?, holder: "<who held the slot>" },
    { condition: "shard_concurrency", status, secs, loadavg_1m, worker_count, command, counts? },
  ]
Do not state `condition_verdict` (a mismatch is refused; the sealer stamps it), and do not touch either version counter.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: scripts/gate-manifest.mjs v3 adds a per-file `conditions` array with one validated arm per condition (standalone / heavy_slot / shard_concurrency) and a `condition_verdict` the sealer derives from them (pattern, disagreement, agrees_with_shard, with `incomplete` and nulls whenever an arm was not measured); a `failed` record whose v2 evidence names no arm is refused by name. docs/12-pre-push-gate.md documents both, and tests/gate-manifest.test.mjs gains the derived-verdict block, twelve refusals by name and the refusal's own narrowings.
WHY: a browser file that fails only under load left a timeout and nothing else, so "does it fail alone?" was answered by re-running it on a quiet box - and a unit-tier failure could not say which arm failed, which cost the same kind of re-run.
EFFECT: a red browser file's record now says which condition it failed under, and a failure carries the name of the arm that failed. Nothing retries, isolates, widens a bound or lowers the shard width on the strength of an arm or a reading; verdicts are unchanged and still come from the file's own status.

title: P3: sleeps that stand in for a synchronous DOM state (latency, not flakiness) - zjpm.5 follow-up
description:
Follow-up to the zjpm.5 audit (tests sample transient state). The audit's positive finding: after hand-verifying
candidates from three independent mechanical scans (wait-on-A/assert-B; bare reads with no wait; fixed sleeps
before assertions), only ONE site both sampled a transient state through a guessed delay and weakened its own
mutant: tests/changelog-dialog-extraction.test.mjs's "exactly one fetch per click" arm (fixed in the parent).

What is LEFT is a class of sleeps that are LATENCY, not flakiness: a fixed delay before an assertion whose
observable is written SYNCHRONOUSLY by the click that precedes it. They cannot flake (nothing changes after the
sleep), but each one costs its full delay in the browser tier and each one reads like a wait on an async fact.
Measured sites (all verified by reading the page's code: the handler writes the asserted state with no await):

  tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs:183  200ms -> #mini-app-container.hidden === false   (reload() -> mount() is sync, fused.js:4592/4481)

title: ARCHITECT: scope the SQEH deck shell (and the vision controls wired inside it) before any port
description:
ARCHITECT PASS (design only — **no port**) for the SQEH deck shell, recorded by the uei2.8 plan. Verified against `origin/main = 246414c`.

WHY AN ARCHITECT, NOT A SLICE: the shell is not one region but the file's cross-cutting layer —
  • `sqehWire()` — 569 lines, the single largest declaration in fused.js;
  • `sqehSetState()` (the 3-state controller), `sqehSyncMiniApps()` (104L), `sqehArtifactChip()` (63L);
  • and it PATCHES PROTOTYPES (`scrollIntoView` / `focus` / `checkVisibility`) — behaviour that is global to the page and pinned elsewhere.
Its state is read by the rest of the file, and the deck shell calls back into surfaces that are now separate modules (`miniAppController.mount`), so a straight port would move the page's wiring, not a surface.

**THE VISION-CLASS ANSWER, measured:** there is no separable vision slice today. `public/vision-grounding.mjs` already owns the overlay, `public/vision-frame-encoder.mjs` the encoding, and the vision CONTROLS are wired at what is now lines 5250-5340 — inside `function sqehWire()` (4959-5526), i.e. inside this shell. So a vision slice is blocked on this pass; that is the honest ranking rather than a port attempt.

ALSO RECORDED HERE (same class, measured): the room-folder cluster (the banner'd region around `roomFolders` / `roomFolder`, ~520 lines, 32 declarations at 246414c) is the LARGEST remaining cluster and the WORST seam: **22 of its 32 declarations are read from outside** (roomFolder, roomFolders, entries, writeRoomFile, readRoomFile, initRoomFolders, adoptRoomFolder, …) with 19 inward deps. It should not be ported as one slice; it needs either this architect treatment or a much narrower sub-slice chosen for a closed seam.

DELIVERABLE: a design that says what the shell owns, what the surfaces it wires must be handed (callbacks/accessors vs snapshots), how the prototype patching is contained, and which sub-slices (if any) fall out with a closed seam. Then file those as slices.
close_reason: Architecture decision recorded; implementation scoped in .12/.13 and routed to coord.

comments.author: voicebox-arch-sqeh
comments.text:
ADR — Do not port sqehWire wholesale; split vision controls from deck navigation, retain prototype compatibility in the host (origin/main 246414c).

Context: public/fused.js was touched by 135 first-parent landings/30d; its current changed-test closure is 159 (20 unit/63 server/76 browser, `node scripts/test-changed.mjs --dry-run --json public/fused.js`). At 246414c sqehWire spans 4959–5526 (568 lines), but its deck state, mini-app mirroring, window-manager wiring, help/settings/doctor controls, file/reader interaction, and vision/PTT controls have different owners. `sqehSetState` is also called from system commands (line 264) and mini-app/file paths; `sqehArtifactChip` has five callers earlier in the file. A monolithic lift would only rename the hotspot, and the static assertion in tests/ptt-and-thinking-settings.test.mjs currently matches fused.js by name. The parent uei2 ADR and uei2.8 already covered broad extraction; this decision answers this child only.

Decision: (1) First extract the local vision/PTT state machine into a `public/components/vision-controls.mjs` factory, leaving only one host init call in sqehWire. It owns stream/timer/encoding-in-flight/PTT/preferences and camera/screen/snapshot/stop, FPS/resolution, thinking and PTT listeners (anchor `// Core Live Vision & manual speech activity controls` through the PTT handler; debug/offline/doctor settings are NOT vision). Receive the already-owned encoder and grounding controller, `els` and the error-report callback, plus LIVE callbacks for `__voiceboxIsLiveSessionActive`, `__voiceboxSendLiveVideo`, `__voiceboxRestartLiveSession`, `__voiceboxSendActivityControl` and PiP; do not snapshot live-session state at init. Keep settings and mic click semantics, track-ended stop, metadata resize, and stop/cleanup identical. (2) Then extract deck navigation + file/mini-app tiles into `public/components/deck-controller.mjs`: it owns one state, `setState`, `openSheet`, `syncQuickFiles`, `syncMiniApps`, dock/popover/reader transitions, outside-click/Escape/window-manager coordination, and file-list observer. Its public methods are called by the host's system commands, file/mini-app mutations and the host's onToolCalls relay; take live `getCatalogMiniApps` (catalog is reassigned), live `getMiniAppController` (null until mount), live `getLaunchedMiniApps`, and callbacks for reader collapse, activity refresh/clear, file launch and `showFile`; never copy those maps/handles at boot. The host remains owner of tool-call forwarding, artifact chips/turn rendering and the settings/help/doctor block rather than dragging unrelated listeners into a 500-line module. Install window manager once at the deck init boundary; preserve initial `setState('deck')` after installation. Coordinate with pending uei2.2 (activity) and uei2.7 (mini-app host) before changing their shared callbacks.

Consequences: Keep the three prototype wrappers in fused.js as ONE guarded, documented host-only compatibility adapter for now, installed at the same boot point before consumers can invoke scroll/focus/visibility. It may route only #made-list to files state, #reader to uncollapse, and #text-form to reveal. Wrap original methods with exactly the original arg/return/this and no changes for non-target nodes; do NOT re-install per module or monkey-patch from deck-controller. Host adapter calls the new controller through a live handle (or remains entirely host-owned until the controller is initialized). Extracting it or replacing it with explicit navigation would require a separate inventory of consumers and a browser parity test, not a mechanical lift. No room-folder core state moves: 22 of 32 declarations have outward readers per uei2.8, so it is a separate design. Once fused.js stops owning these surfaces, future focused edits should select the new component's 1–3 owner tests rather than today's 159; the initial extraction still pays the full fused.js closure at merger, and actual mapping must be demonstrated by `test-changed --dry-run` with a new extraction test. No `docs/speed.md` exists on this origin/main; don't invent a numeric timing promise.

Alternatives considered: Moving all 568 sqehWire lines (retains cross-domain state and global patches); moving vision-frame-encoder or vision-grounding again (already modules with 1 mapped unit test each); porting room-folder bar with the shell (moves shared FS state and permissions). Rejected for excessive coupling or duplicate ownership.

title: Extract the environments list renderer into public/components/environment-list.mjs (uei2 slice; settings class)
description:
SLICE of uei2 (the fused.js UI decomposition), ranked **#2 for implementation** by the uei2.8 plan. Settings class. Verified against `origin/main = 246414c`.

ANCHORS (TEXT is the locator; line numbers are a hint at 246414c):
  • the code is `async function renderEnvironments()` — lines 1932-2104, **175 lines, exactly ONE declaration**, which makes this the most cohesive remaining slice.
  • START banner (for context only, do NOT trust its position): `// ── the environment list (core/environment.ts is the seam; server.mjs owns the store) ──`
  • END PROOF: the next declaration is `async function health()`.
  • TRAP FOUND WHILE PLANNING: that banner is MISPLACED — it sits ~94 lines above the function it describes, with the "THE EXTENSION SURFACE" banner wedged between them. Locating this slice by banner adjacency picks the wrong range; locate it by the function signature.

SEAM (measured): the region is CLOSED except for one name — `renderEnvironments` itself, called from four places outside (`await renderEnvironments()` in the health poll, twice more during root/room changes, and `void renderEnvironments()` twice from settings wiring). So the factory returns exactly one function and there is no mutable outward state to accessor. INWARD deps (8): els, on, request, render, plus host ROOT state it reads — `activeRoot`, `roomFolder`, `SCRATCHPAD_NAME` (and `entries`). Those three are the cross-cutting state of the room: they must arrive as LIVE accessors, because the root changes while the page lives — a snapshot would paint a stale root. `render` is the host's re-render hook.

OWNER TESTS, measured by reference to the four ids the region paints (`env-list`, `envs-count`, `env-note`, `env-active-root-val`): **`tests/environment-list-ui.test.mjs` is the primary owner**; `tests/env-create-project.test.mjs`, `tests/environment-integrated-ui.test.mjs` and `tests/environment-root-dialog-extraction.test.mjs` reference `env-active-root-val`; `tests/health-auth-browser.test.mjs` and `tests/modern-web-room.test.mjs` reference `env-note`. Six observers — a wider set than the Harnesses slice, so re-run them all. Related open work (different surface, do not fold in): `voicebox-beads-g4nq`.

COLLISION CHECK: `environment-list.mjs` appears in NO file under lib/, tools/, core/ and not in server.mjs — safe. Note `core/environment.ts` exists but that is a DIFFERENT basename and does not collide.

GATE NOTE: a new component with no mapped test is REFUSED (`unmapped-source-file`, exit 1) — ship its own extraction test (static no-leftover arm + the real page driven for one counted behaviour + mutants RED).

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
**IN_REVIEW — `fleet/type-recover-environments` @ bf678e9** (from main `7533835`, as coord directed). Pre-push gate: **ALL GATES GREEN (unit)** (94/94). `public/fused.js` **5026 → 4870** lines.

## The slice, as scoped
Region located by TEXT rather than by any line number: 174 lines from `async function renderEnvironments() {` to its brace-matched close, **end proven** by the next statement being `async function health() {`. **Exactly one declaration** inside, as the plan said. The banner describing the list sits **94 lines above** it (the extension banner is wedged between), so adjacency would have picked the wrong range — the anchor rule paid for itself again, and the numbers in the plan (1932–2104 on `246414c`) are now 1820–1993 here.

The move is **verbatim**: 174 statements → 174, and the only differing lines are the **8 lines carrying 10 rewritten occurrences** — `roomFolder` ×3 and `activeRoot` ×7, rewritten to accessor calls. Occurrence counts were measured line by line before rewriting, because my first attempt asserted *5* for `activeRoot` by counting the lines that mention it (line 1829 uses it three times).

## The seam is smaller than the plan predicted — 5 names, not 8
The renderer builds its **own rows** with `document.createElement` and attaches its **own handlers** to those created buttons (`reprobeBtn`, `removeBtn`), so no element-wiring helper is involved. My first pass reported `on` and `render` as dependencies; both were comment/string false positives ("Present on this host", "re-render once"), and `$` was once again `${…}`. The true seam:

- by value: `els`, `request`, `SCRATCHPAD_NAME`;
- **live accessors**: `getRoomFolder` / `getActiveRoot`, because the host assigns both somewhere other than their declaration. `roomFolder` is reassigned *after* the seam; `activeRoot` is assigned inside functions that run later — and its initial value is `undefined` with the host's own comment "undefined = not asked yet, null = none declared", so a snapshot taken at the seam would freeze **"not asked yet"** for the life of the page. Both are **read only** by the module (verified per line, zero writes).
- returned: `renderEnvironments`, because four host sites call it (the health poll, the "+" declare path, and the two dialog openers `#envs-open` / `#empty-link`).

## Verification
New **`tests/environment-list-extraction.test.mjs` 4/4**, with every wait on the observable its assertion is about — and a **control** that requires the same bounded wait to *fail* when the list genuinely never resolves (the a8rg lesson, applied here before it could bite).

Measured before asserting, not assumed: a click on a row's Re-probe issues its `POST /api/probe` **in the same tick** as the click, so the two counts are taken in that tick; a **listener-free clone** of that button issues **none** (0 vs 1); `#envs-open` issues exactly **one** `GET /api/environments` through the function this module returns **and still one after it settled**. The accessors are proved live by changing the host state between four renders and requiring **four different paints** — a snapshot would repeat the first answer.

Mutants RED, verified against the real files and restored: Re-probe listener unwired; root labels swapped; the readout never painted; the host's `#envs-open` handler not reaching the returned renderer. Static: leftover inline copy, dropped import, snapshot-instead-of-accessor, dropped return.

**Blind spot, documented rather than hidden**: removing the refresh that follows a successful probe **survives**, because the module's own never-probed path refreshes the list too, so "the list was re-rendered" cannot be attributed to the handler. The request count is still pinned exactly, which is the seam this file exists to guard. The test file's header says this.

My own mutant harness was wrong twice and the mutants caught *me*: one injected a marker I had already removed from the marker list, and the "snapshot instead of accessor" check initially passed because **another extracted module also takes a `getRoomFolder` accessor** — a whole-file `includes` was satisfied by it, making the check vacuous. Both the assertion and the mutants are now scoped to this seam block.

Owner suites unchanged and green (18/18): `environment-list-ui`, `environment-integrated-ui`, `env-create-project`, `environment-root-dialog-extraction`, `health-auth-browser`, `modern-web-room`.

## One finding, filed not fixed
A successful probe writes `Re-probed this machine: voicebox.` and the refresh clears it **4 ms later** (MutationObserver: paint at 1213 ms, cleared at 1217 ms), so the confirmation is invisible to users; Remove's note behaves the same. Pre-existing, not introduced here, and user-visible — so it is its own bead, **`voicebox-beads-2qxi`**, rather than a silent change inside a verbatim move.

## Cost
An edit of `public/fused.js` selects **162** test files (unit 20 / server 63 / browser 79); an edit of this module selects **2** — its extraction test plus the surface's own `environment-list-ui` owner, which the mapper brings along by name. The new test is **browser-lane**, so the unit fast gate does not execute it; its evidence is the run above.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: The environment list and the active-root readout move out of public/fused.js into public/components/environment-list.mjs, wired at one init site. It keeps its own DOM building and its own row handlers, takes els/request/SCRATCHPAD_NAME by value and roomFolder/activeRoot as live accessors (the host reassigns both), and returns renderEnvironments for the four host call sites. New tests/environment-list-extraction.test.mjs (4/4) drives the real page, proves the accessors are live across four renders, and ends with a control that must fail when the list never resolves.
WHY: public/fused.js is a 5000-line hotspot that every UI change touches, and a module no test maps to is refused by the gate. This makes the surface independently testable and moves the blast radius of future work on it from 162 test files to 2.
EFFECT: none for users: internal refactor, same behaviour and same element ids. For operators, an edit to the environments list now runs 2 test files instead of 162.

comments.text:
**IN_REVIEW** — `fleet/type-recover-harnesses` @ **4deca7e** (pushed; from main `246414c`). Pre-push gate: **ALL GATES GREEN (unit)**.

## What changed
The Harnesses modal dialog moved out of `public/fused.js` into **`public/components/harnesses-dialog.mjs`** (394 lines), wired at ONE `initHarnessesDialog({ … })` site. **fused.js 5531 → 5203 lines.** Moved region: the banner through the tracker's own `on(...)` line — 358 lines, **336 statements of which 334 moved verbatim**; the 12 differences are 10 rewritten statements plus the 2 that stay in the host. Located by ANCHOR TEXT with the next banner (`Change log modal dialog`) as the proof of the end; disjointness confirmed by anchor against uei2.2 (`Project / folder change flash`, line 323) and uei2.7 (`the interactive mini-app surface`, line 4304).

## The seam, as assigned (and what the plan's numbers turned into)
- **Accessor PAIR for the reassigned `let`**: the host keeps `let lastHarnessOutput = "";` and passes `getLastHarnessOutput`/`setLastHarnessOutput`. **The host's own call site is byte-identical** (`lastHarnessOutput = outText;` in `window.__voiceboxOnTask` needed no edit).
- **The two outward functions are returned, not injected**: `renderHarnessChangedFiles` (that same task handler) and `openAgentProgressTracker` (the system-command path, 2 sites). I read "injected as callbacks" as "handed over so the page can call them" — the only workable direction, since both are *defined inside* the moved region; a returned binding is safe because both callers run after boot. Say the word if you meant something else and I will re-shape on a child branch.
- **Three LIVE accessors**: `roomFolder`, `listingDir`, `miniAppController` — all three are `let`s the host reassigns (verified: 4, 4 and 1 reassignment sites). Eight names go in by value: `els`, `on`, `request`, `health`, `load`, `showFile`, `loadRoomFolder`, `writeRoomFile`.
- **The page global** `window.__voiceboxOpenAgentTracker` is still assigned by the host at the same boot position; nothing else in the repo reads it (checked).
- **A sharp edge the plan could not see and a mutant proved**: `miniAppController` is declared AFTER this seam, so handing over a *snapshot* is not merely stale — it is a **temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError at boot** (mutant RED). The accessor is therefore read only on demand, never during init.

## Verification
`tests/harnesses-dialog-extraction.test.mjs` **3/3**:
- static — surface gone from the host, host keeps the binding/pair/global/both outward call sites;
- **real page** — one click on the check button is exactly **ONE** `/api/harnesses` fetch while a **listener-free clone** of the same button fetches **nothing**; the host's own `__voiceboxOnTask` path renders changed files through the returned callback and then a **sentinel in the status line** proves the save handler got past its `if (!getLastHarnessOutput()) return;` (that read IS the pair); and the tracker mounts the mini-app through the **LIVE** controller;
- **standalone with spies** — the injected pair is the only path the module uses (the task path writes through the setter and reads back through the getter; the save writes `harness-analysis.md` with the value it read back).
Owner suites unchanged and green: `modal-panels` 2/2, `ux-bubble-stage` 1/1, `configured-harness` 5 (2 pass, 0 fail), `harness-inventory` 5/5.

**Five mutants, each reverted with the tree verified pristine, all RED**: snapshot for the pair; snapshot for `miniAppController` (the TDZ boot crash); the host's task handler writing elsewhere; the module never writing the pair; and a **twice-installed check listener**, which the fetch count catches as two — that count has real teeth.

Two honest notes. (1) The count arm only works *after* the check that **opening** the dialog starts has finished (~7s of host-inventory probe on this box), because the button is rightly disabled while one is in flight — my first version measured a disabled button and read 0. (2) The extraction test file therefore takes ~10s; it is a **browser-lane** test, so the **unit fast gate is unchanged** by this slice.

Gates: docs-check OK (**974** claims), single-owner OK, test-lanes ok (94 unit / 149 live), docs-touched OK. Measured closure: an edit of the new module selects **1** test file, against **160** for `public/fused.js` (unit 20 / server 59 / browser 81).

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: The Harnesses modal dialog moves out of public/fused.js into public/components/harnesses-dialog.mjs (394 lines), wired at one initHarnessesDialog({ … }) site; fused.js 5531 → 5203 lines. The host keeps the `lastHarnessOutput` binding (the page's own task handler writes it) and hands it over as a get/set accessor pair, hands `roomFolder`/`listingDir`/`miniAppController` over as live accessors because it reassigns all three, and receives back the two functions the page calls from outside. A new extraction test drives the real page and the module standalone.

PLAN DELIVERED (no source edits). Measured against **`origin/main = 246414c`** by extracting that tree to /tmp with `git archive` — my own branch was never checked out or touched. The two pending-merge regions are excluded by construction: my candidates are 1932-2104 and 3597-3955, so they cannot collide with uei2.2 (~321-458) or uei2.7 (4304-4719).

## Ranked

**#1 — uei2.9: the Harnesses modal dialog → `public/components/harnesses-dialog.mjs`** (settings class). 359 lines, 9 declarations. Seam measured by reader sweep: only **3** names are read outside — `lastHarnessOutput` is **reassigned** outside (accessor PAIR, the `catalogMiniApps` shape), and `renderHarnessChangedFiles` + `openAgentProgressTracker` are **called** outside (callbacks/returns; the tracker is also published as `window.__voiceboxOpenAgentTracker` inside the region). 16 inward deps, all plain reads. Owners: `modal-panels`, `ux-bubble-stage`, `configured-harness`.

**#2 — uei2.10: the environments list → `public/components/environment-list.mjs`** (settings class). `async function renderEnvironments()` = **175 lines and exactly ONE declaration** — the most cohesive thing left, and its region is closed except for itself (4 call sites: the health poll, two root/room changes, twice from settings wiring), so the factory returns one function and there is no outward mutable state. 8 inward deps, three of them ROOT state (`activeRoot`, `roomFolder`, `SCRATCHPAD_NAME`) → live accessors, never snapshots. Owners are WIDER than #1: `environment-list-ui` (primary) plus `env-create-project`, `environment-integrated-ui`, `environment-root-dialog-extraction`, `health-auth-browser`, `modern-web-room`.

**#3 — the vision class has NO separable slice today**, and that is a measurement, not a preference: the vision controls are wired at 5250-5340, **inside `function sqehWire()` (4959-5526)**. `vision-grounding.mjs` already owns the overlay and `vision-frame-encoder.mjs` the encoding, so what remains is inside the cross-cutting shell. Filed as **uei2.11** (architect pass, no port) with that evidence.

**Recorded, as instructed:** the SQEH deck shell is **cross-cutting** — `sqehWire` 569 lines (the largest declaration in the file), plus `sqehSetState`, `sqehSyncMiniApps` (104L), `sqehArtifactChip` (63L) and **prototype patching** (`scrollIntoView`/`focus`/`checkVisibility`) — and the shell calls back into already-extracted surfaces (`miniAppController.mount`). **No port; architect pass first** → uei2.11.
Also recorded there: the room-folder cluster (~520 lines, 32 declarations) is the LARGEST remaining cluster and the WORST seam — **22 of its 32 declarations are read from outside**, 19 inward deps. Not a candidate for a straight port.

## The five checks, and what each one caught here
1. **Anchors, not ranges.** Deliberate find: the environments banner is **misplaced ~94 lines above** the function it describes, with the extension banner wedged between them — locating that slice by banner adjacency picks the wrong range. Both beads locate by TEXT (signature/banner/proof-that-it-ends) with line numbers as a hint only.
2. **Owner tests by reference, not by name.** A: the 21 element ids the region paints lead to `modal-panels` + `ux-bubble-stage` (+ `configured-harness`). B: `environment-list-ui` is primary and FIVE more files observe `env-active-root-val`/`env-note`, so its blast radius is wider than its size suggests.
3. **Readers of extracted state.** Harnesses: the reassigned `lastHarnessOutput` and the two externally-called functions (above) — three seam decisions that would each have been a silent runtime failure if assumed to be private. Also flagged for implementation: `textNode` is declared inside that region and must be reader-swept before it moves (if any other surface uses it, it stays in the host and is injected).
4. **Live/accessor/callback, not snapshot.** Called out per name above: accessor PAIR for the reassigned `let`, callbacks for the two functions, LIVE accessors for `miniAppController` and for the three root facts.
5. **Basename collisions.** This check has a real example in this repo, not just a theory: `harness-config.mjs` — the natural name for #1 — **collides with `lib/harness-config.mjs`, which `server.mjs` references**, and would pull `server.mjs`'s whole test set into every edit of the new file (the measured 1 → 146 failure). `harnesses-dialog.mjs` and `environment-list.mjs` appear in no file under lib/, tools/, core/ and not in server.mjs.

## Gate note for both slices
A new component that no test maps to is **REFUSED** by the gate (`unmapped-source-file`, exit 1), so each slice must ship its own extraction test — static no-leftover arm, one init site handing over els + deps, live accessors, one counted behaviour driven on the real page, and negative mutants RED.

## State
Filing complete and my claim on this bead is released, per instruction. Nothing implemented, no branch, no source edit. For coord: assign **uei2.9** and **uei2.10** when you want them, and spawn an **architect** for **uei2.11** (design only — it is not an implementer bead). `gw80` remains a fold-in for the next mini-app slice, untouched here.

title: Boot audio refresh can predate the live audio client, painting system-output rows
description: Recorded by gate-recover during the jeye test-race fix and deliberately NOT fixed there: the boot refresh can run before the live audio client exists, so the boot-painted mic/output rows can carry the system-output line until something later refreshes. It is the product behaviour behind the flaky assertion (the test now waits for both observables, which is correct regardless). Fix candidate: gate the boot paint on client readiness or refresh once the client attaches; needs a focused control. No security surface.

comments.author: voicebox-gate-recover
comments.text:
AUTHOR HANDOFF — IN_REVIEW pending coord-routed cross-family reviewer. Branch origin/fleet/t1k9-boot-paint@37e4ab9 (clean, matches remote; based on origin/main a81c667). 3 files: public/components/audio-device-controller.mjs (the fix), tests/audio-device-controller-boot-paint.test.mjs (new, the control), tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs (the move's guard, extended for the cited change). No fused.js edit and no other lane's file touched.

THE DEFECT (P3, recorded on the bead from the jeye race): the output row's first branch is the live client's fact `canChooseOutput`, and that client is published by a DIFFERENT module script (`public/live-voice.js`) than the one that boots the surface (`public/fused.js`) — whose body awaits, so the two module scripts can finish in either order. Where live-voice.js lost that race, `refreshDevices()` cached the ABSENT client as `false`, and the row then claimed "This browser uses system output. Change the output in your device's sound settings." — a negative claim about the machine — over a browser that does offer output selection. The row stayed wrong until something else refreshed (a devicechange, or opening the settings dialog, which is why the user-visible path self-healed and the owner test stayed green).

THE FIX (public/components/audio-device-controller.mjs, four places, ~10 lines of code):
· `canChooseOutput` now models three states rather than two: its default is `null`, meaning NO CLIENT HAS ANSWERED. Absence is not an answer.
· `refreshDevices()` caches only a real boolean answer (`if (typeof clientCanChoose === "boolean")`).
· `renderDevices()` reads the client's answer LIVE at paint time, falling back to the last known answer — deliberately not only in refresh, so a client that attaches later is used by the NEXT REPAINT instead of needing a refresh.
· the system-output sentence is now gated on `canChooseOutput === false` and therefore spoken only for an ANSWERED false.
No routing behaviour changes: the stop-never-fall-back policy, the pickers, the preference store and the live accessor are untouched.

THE CONTROL — tests/audio-device-controller-boot-paint.test.mjs (new, live lane). The losing-race boot is FORCED, not waited for (`window.__voiceboxLiveClient = null` then a refresh IS that boot state), so it reproduces on any box, and a PRELOADED preference is used (seed + reload, because loadPrefs() reads the store once at boot). Five arms:
1. the page controller with no client: the row must NOT claim the machine cannot choose an output, and must name the saved device instead;
2. a FRESH controller that has never had a client (box-independent): same, and the picker is not offered before a capability is known;
3. the SAME page state with a client answering `false`: the system-output sentence MUST appear verbatim, and the picker stays disabled — the control that keeps arm 1 from being satisfied by deleting the branch;
4. a client answering `true`: the row names the saved device and neither fallback sentence is used;
5. a repaint with NO refresh at all after the client attaches: the new answer is used, which is what makes the fix a paint-time read rather than a warmer cache.

BEFORE/AFTER, driven on the tree rather than argued: with the module reverted to origin/main and the final test file in place, arms 1, 2 and 5 FAIL with the recorded message `before the live client answers, the row must not assert a negative about the machine: it read "This browser uses system output. Change the output in your device's sound settings."` (and arm 2's own wording, and arm 5's `the unknown state stays honest`). With the fix, all five pass. Logs: /tmp/t1k9-before-final.log and /tmp/t1k9-after2.log.

KEPT HONEST — the move's byte-identity guard: this is a cited behaviour change INSIDE the extracted region, so tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs now normalises that region's FOUR edited places as named spans, each citing voicebox-beads-t1k9, before comparing bytes; everything outside those spans must still match exactly, and the four RULES are asserted positively (`assertT1k9Rules`) with two mutants (revert the default, revert `=== false`) so a span can never become a licence to delete the behaviour. The pre-existing rewritten-statement mutant still fails the comparison outside the spans. This edits the guard in ONE place — `movedRegionFromHostAtBase()` and the constants above it — so it does not overlap cqrd's edits to the same file (cqrd normalises the refusal branch in `assertByteIdentical`, a different function).

DOCS: deliberately not edited, with the reason recorded as a `Docs-checked:` trailer. `docs/07-architecture.md` describes what this module owns — the three device facts and the stop-never-fall-back policy — and none of those statements becomes false; a third insertion into that same single-line paragraph would add a THIRD conflict there (cqrd and jeye edit it already). The sentence to add when that paragraph is next landed, so nobody has to reconstruct it:
  "The row may only claim the browser cannot choose an output once a client has actually ANSWERED that (voicebox-beads-t1k9): `canChooseOutput` defaults to null, `refreshDevices()` caches only a real answer, and `renderDevices()` reads the client live at paint time, because `public/live-voice.js` can finish loading after this surface has already booted."

FOCUSED EVIDENCE ON THIS TIP: three files together — boot-paint (new, 5 arms) + the move's guard (5) + the owner suite settings-dialog (8) = 18/18 pass, exit 0 (/tmp/t1k9-final-trio.log). `node scripts/test-lanes.mjs --check` -> 94 unit / 149 live (the new file is classified LIVE, like the sibling it sits beside: both launch a browser and a server). `test-changed --dry-run` -> 0 unmapped, and the module edit selects BOTH audio-device test files. No author full gate; the merger owns the one full union gate.

CANONICAL: `FLEET_CHECK_CONF=~/.fleet/check-voicebox.conf fleet-check --fast` PASS, rc 0, 21s, cmd `npm run test:unit`, tree 1afde6deacc9ec87a219eb7052f2fd716c8d11e0, coverage UNKNOWN — unit-only, and the unit lane does NOT contain this module's browser tests, so it is a contract check and NOT behaviour proof; the driven arms above are the behaviour evidence. Pre-push unit lane green on this tip.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: public/components/audio-device-controller.mjs no longer treats "the live client has not answered yet" as "this browser cannot choose an output": canChooseOutput defaults to null (no answer), refreshDevices() caches only a real boolean, and renderDevices() reads the client's answer live at paint time, so the system-output sentence is said only for an answered false. A new control file drives the boot race deterministically, and the move's byte-identity guard normalises the four cited places as named spans with the four rules asserted positively.
WHY: the live client is published by public/live-voice.js, a different module script from the booting public/fused.js, so on some boots the refresh ran with no client, cached that absence as false, and painted "This browser uses system output. Change the output in your device's sound settings." over a machine that does offer output selection.
EFFECT: a person opening the device settings can no longer be told their browser cannot choose an output when it can; the row names the saved device until a client actually answers, and a client that attaches later is used by the next repaint. Routing behaviour (stop rather than fall back) is unchanged.

comments.author: voicebox-gate-recover
comments.text:
INTEGRATION TIP READY (coord's priority switch; this is the branch to review, in place of fleet/t1k9-boot-paint@37e4ab9): main + t1k9 as ONE tip on origin/fleet/integration-t1k9@f4b30dc, a single commit on top of ef1d05c (cqrd is already in main as 591786e, so there is no rebase to stale its clearance).

THE CONFLICT, precisely. The module edits do NOT overlap: cqrd's refusal branch (the out-change handler) and t1k9's four sites (the prefs default, renderDevices' head, the out branch, refreshDevices) merged automatically. BOTH branches rewrote the extraction test's byte-identity arm, and that is the whole conflict (one conflicted hunk, inside assertByteIdentical; both machinery blocks - t1k9's CITED_SPANS/normaliseCitedSpans/assertT1k9Rules and cqrd's REFUSAL_BRANCH_OPENS/assertRefusalOrder - auto-merged and are both kept).

HOW CQRD'S BRANCH BECAME A CITED SPAN. cqrd normalised its refusal branch with a bespoke normaliseRefusalBranch + token; that is now the fifth entry in CITED_SPANS, and it is the one that needed a new capability from the generalisation: the span is a whole BLOCK rather than a run of lines before a marker, so it is named by its END (endThroughRe = the branch's own `return;`) and it swallows the statement's closing brace (swallowClosingBrace), so the brace does not stay behind as a stray line the two sides must agree on. The bespoke normaliser and its token are deleted; REFUSAL_BRANCH_OPENS stays, because assertRefusalOrder reads the module text from it. The comparison still normalises ONLY the cited spans: each side's count is asserted equal to CITED_SPANS.length (5), and a rewritten statement OUTSIDE them still breaks the arm.

BOTH ARMS KEPT. assertRefusalOrder (cqrd: repaint, then put the picker back, then name device and reason - asserted as ORDER, because the order is the defect) and assertT1k9Rules (t1k9: the null default, the live read, the sentence only for an answered false, the cache that takes only a real boolean) are both called from the byte-identity arm and both are driven by mutants in-run. They are separate on purpose: each names a different property, and one merged assertion would report neither failure precisely.

THE THIRD INTERACTION, which coord's brief did not name and which had to change (this is the part worth reviewing). jeye landed a control in the same test that took the client AWAY, refreshed, and REQUIRED the row to paint "This browser uses system output" - that was the pre-t1k9 behaviour, i.e. precisely the lie t1k9 removed, so on the integrated tree it fails red. The arm now drives the client's own ANSWER: answered false must paint that sentence verbatim; answered true must let the saved device be named; an ABSENT client must leave the row as the last REAL answer left it (equal to the answered-true paint, asserted as equality rather than as a literal, so it is box-independent). Nothing is weakened: the sensitivity is stronger than before (two verbatim answers plus the unanswered case).

ACCEPTANCE, driven on this tree with the module mutated and restored byte-for-byte afterwards:
- cqrd's defect reintroduced (the reason written before the repaint) -> extraction test RED with the cqrd message ("the generic repaint must happen BEFORE the refusal is written: writing it first is the clobbering this fix removes (voicebox-beads-cqrd)");
- t1k9's default reverted to true -> boot-paint RED ("and no capability is offered before one is known"), and the extraction arm also RED via assertT1k9Rules;
- t1k9's falsy rule reverted -> boot-paint RED ("a controller that has never heard from a client must not assert a negative about the machine: it read \"This browser uses system output. Change the output in your device's sound settings.\"").
Focused, integrated tree: extraction 5/5 + boot-paint 5/5 + settings-dialog 9/9 = 19/19, exit 0. Docs: the audio-device paragraph now says TWO cited changes and how each is pinned (rather than one and a bespoke normaliser), and the jeye sentence is corrected to the new sensitivity. docs-check OK (974 path claims). Unit fast gate: PASS for f4b30dc (job 42fa2fc4814e2e8bdab839806cae39b9b498356e, `npm run test:unit`, rc 0, 21s of work after 341s waiting for the heavy slot behind Gate 3; coverage UNKNOWN, since the unit lane does not contain the browser files this branch changes - the driven mutants above and the 19/19 focused run are the behaviour evidence). No author full gate: the merger runs it once on the merged union.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: one tip carrying both device-controller fixes - cqrd's refusal order and t1k9's four "an unanswered client is not a false answer" rules - with cqrd's refusal branch expressed as a fifth CITED SPAN inside t1k9's generalisation (named by its end, swallowing the closing brace), BOTH rule-assertion functions kept, and the byte-identity arm still normalising only the cited spans with their order pinned. The jeye control that required the pre-t1k9 system-output behaviour now drives the client's answer instead.
WHY: t1k9 and cqrd each rewrote the extraction test's byte-identity arm, so neither could land alone; the merger pre-check flagged the conflict and the integration had to keep both citations honest rather than dropping one.
EFFECT: none for users (both behaviours are unchanged by the integration). For the repository: the device surface can take a cited behaviour fix without the byte-identity guard being loosened, and three mutants - the cqrd order, the t1k9 default and the t1k9 falsy rule - are each still refused by their own arm on the merged tree.

title: PLAN: extract the fused.js interactive mini-app host into public/components/mini-app-host.mjs (uei2 slice plan; bridge-bearing)
description:
PLAN ONLY — no source edits made, and none until coord assigns the implementation.

VERIFIED REGION — measured on origin/main a81c667. Take the ANCHORS as the locator and the numbers as a hint: this file has already moved twice today, and every extraction shifts every later line.
  start  4304  `// ── the interactive mini-app surface (voicebox-beads-5h1, voicebox-beads-7xbe) ──`
  state  4305  `let miniAppController = null;`   ← HOST-OWNED HANDLE, see the seam contract
  state  4306  `const launchedMiniApps = new Map();`
  guard  4307  `if (els.miniAppContainer) {`   … closes at 4719
  global 4718  `window.__voiceboxMiniApp = miniAppController;`
  end    4719  the guard's closing brace. Line 4720 is `load();` and is NOT part of this surface.
  size   416 lines.

THE QUOTED RANGE IS WRONG ON CURRENT MAIN: 4663–5076 is not the mini-app host. On a81c667, 4663–4719 is only the TAIL of this surface, and 4748–5076 is the SQEH controller (`sqehSetState`, `sqehSyncMiniApps`, `sqehWire`) plus the `scrollIntoView`/`focus`/`checkVisibility` prototype patching — a different surface that the uei2 ADR ranked BORDERLINE and deliberately did not file. The ~414 LOC estimate in the instruction does match this surface's size, which is how a shifted range hides. Anchors, not ranges.

PER-MOUNT STATE (closure-private inside the guard): currentDescriptor, currentChannel (a MessageChannel), currentTools, isCollapsed, isExpanded, pendingToolCalls (a Map), nextToolCallId; plus the module-level `launchedMiniApps` Map that sits beside the handle.

HOST DEPENDENCIES THE REGION READS. Mechanical scan of the region (71 identifiers declared inside it); these nine resolve to host declarations outside it, at the lines shown on a81c667:
  els @165 (15 mini-app handles at 89–103), request @1150, load @2168, isHtmlFileName @2250, normalizeMiniAppKey @2252, catalogMiniApps @2263, syncReaderBubble @2320, renderRead @2819, sqehSyncMiniApps @4820.
  It reads no imported names, so the module needs no imports of its own.

SEAM CONTRACT (proposed; review it before the implementation is assigned):
  * One init site, inside the host's existing guard:
      if (els.miniAppContainer) {
        miniAppController = initMiniAppHost({ els, request, load, isHtmlFileName, normalizeMiniAppKey, getCatalog, setCatalog, syncReaderBubble, renderRead, sqehSyncMiniApps });
        window.__voiceboxMiniApp = miniAppController;
      }
  * It returns the SAME 11-member controller: mount, close, toggle, expandToggle, reload, editCurrentMiniApp, deleteCurrentMiniApp, callTool, getTools, getDescriptor, getContainer. The SQEH shell and four other host paths call into it.
  * `let miniAppController = null;` STAYS in the host as a live handle. Fourteen host call sites read it — 2307, 2311, 2346, 2360, 2549, 2554, 3103, 3104, 3114, 3116, 3912, 3913, 4299, 4300 — and six of them are null-guarded, so "no container ⇒ null controller and an UNDEFINED window.__voiceboxMiniApp" is part of the contract. Keeping the handle as the assignment target means none of those fourteen sites changes, exactly as destructuring the factory's returns saved the twelve call sites in uei2.2.
  * `catalogMiniApps` IS NOT READ-ONLY. The delete path reassigns it (`catalogMiniApps = catalogMiniApps.filter(...)`, line 4635). It therefore needs a live accessor PAIR (getCatalog/setCatalog, the w1f9 shape), never a snapshot — a snapshot would silently stop deletion from updating the catalog.
  * `sqehSyncMiniApps` is declared AFTER the region (4820) while the region calls it at the end of `mount`, and the shell in turn calls `miniAppController.mount(...)` (4873, 4916). It must be injected as a callback, and the module must call it at the same point in mount.
  * Keep the `if (els.miniAppContainer)` guard in the HOST: that preserves the absent-container contract without the module needing a null path.

BRIDGE RISK — this is why the ADR said the slice needs a plan, and it is what the review must look at hardest:
  * `mount` creates `<iframe id="mini-app-outer-frame" class="mini-app-frame" src="/mini-app-bridge.html?appId=…">`, appends it to `#mini-app-viewport`, and first closes any previous channel (`currentChannel.port1.close()`, 4560–4566).
  * It creates a fresh `new MessageChannel()`, sets `currentChannel.port1.onmessage = handleBridgeEvent`, and installs a WINDOW-level `message` listener `onBridgeHandshake` (4565–4586) that validates `e.origin === window.location.origin` AND `e.source === outer.contentWindow`, then removes itself, transfers `port2` with `{type:"mini_app_port"}`, and posts `{type:"load_app"}` plus `{type:"mini_app_init"}` carrying the descriptor html.
  * Tool calls are request/response over port1, correlated by `pendingToolCalls` keyed on `nextToolCallId` — so a remount while calls are outstanding is the sharp edge.
  What the extraction test must pin, because a purely source-level move could reorder these silently: the handshake listener is removed on success (no leak across remounts), the previous port is closed on remount, the origin+source validation is unchanged, `port2` is transferred exactly once per mount, and `mini_app_init` carries the descriptor html.

OWNER TESTS — measured as "references the host", not as "the mapper selects it":
  tests/mini-app-ui.test.mjs (15 host references) — PRIMARY owner
  tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs (4), tests/ux-bubble-stage.test.mjs (3), tests/agent-monitor-miniapp.test.mjs (1), tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs (1)
  tests/room-folder-ops.test.mjs and tests/multi-window-manager.test.mjs have ZERO host references. The uei2 ADR had mapped the mini-app candidate to room-folder-ops + caption-fade-and-thinking; that was the mapper's reach rather than an assertion coupling (the same correction uei2.2 produced for caption-fade-and-thinking), so listing them as owners would be wrong.

SLICE CONSTRAINTS:
  * A new `public/components/mini-app-host.mjs` that no test maps to is REFUSED by the gate (`scripts/test-changed.mjs --gate` → exit 1, `unmapped-source-file`), so the slice must ship its own extraction test importing the module — the shape used by uei2.2/.4/.5.
  * Fast gate: FLEET_CHECK_CONF=/home/exedev/.fleet/check-voicebox.conf (unit tier); the extraction test is live-lane, so run it focused.
  * Size: 416 lines is the largest fused.js slice so far (uei2.4 51, uei2.5 135, uei2.2 114). Expect a fused.js diff near -400/+30 and a real conflict surface; one lane in this region at a time.

READER-SWEEP LESSON (uei2.2, and this region has the same hazard twice): extracting STATE must sweep for every READER of that state, not just its definitions. In uei2.2 the host's clear handler still called `workActivitySeenIds.clear()` after the set had moved — a ReferenceError waiting for the first click and invisible to any load-time or verbatim check. Here `miniAppController` has fourteen external readers and `catalogMiniApps` is read AND reassigned inside the region, which is exactly why the plan keeps the handle and injects an accessor pair.

comments.text:
**IN_REVIEW** — `fleet/type-recover-miniapp` @ **a5cddfa** (pushed; from main `a81c667`).

## What changed
The interactive mini-app surface is out of `public/fused.js` and into **`public/components/mini-app-surface.mjs`** (410 lines moved, 453 with its header), wired at ONE `initMiniAppHost({ … })` site inside the host's existing `if (els.miniAppContainer)` guard. fused.js **5531 → 5138** lines. 380 moved statements, of which exactly **2** are not verbatim.

Delivered per the plan's non-negotiables:
- **Live handle, no call-site changes** — `let miniAppController = null` stays in the host; the module RETURNS the controller (the 11-member shape) and the host assigns it there. **14 external call sites verified byte-identical** (six of them null-guarded), and `window.__voiceboxMiniApp = miniAppController` is still assigned inside the host's own guard, so a page without the container still leaves the global **undefined** and the controller null.
- **Accessor PAIR for `catalogMiniApps`** — it is read AND reassigned (the delete path). `getCatalog: () => catalogMiniApps` / `setCatalog: (next) => { catalogMiniApps = next; }`; a snapshot would have silently stopped a deletion from updating the catalogue.
- **`sqehSyncMiniApps` injected as a callback** — declared after this surface, and the shell calls back into the controller; called at the same point in `mount`.
- **`launchedMiniApps` stays in the host** and the SAME Map is passed in: my reader sweep found readers *outside* this surface (`fused.js:2300`, `:4894`) that the plan's scan missed because the declaration sat inside the scanned text. It is only ever mutated in place, so passing it (not rebuilding) preserves them.

## Verification
- **`tests/mini-app-surface-extraction.test.mjs` 4/4.** Static arm (surface gone from the host, host keeps handle/Map/guard/global/accessor pair) + the real bridge: the app html **crossing into the sandboxed iframe's srcdoc** proves the handshake, the single-use `port2` transfer and `load_app`/`mini_app_init` together; the handshake listener removes itself; a remount closes the previous port and opens a fresh channel; and the installed handler is driven **directly** — a forged handshake is refused on a foreign origin **OR** a wrong source window (that arm attaches the container and neutralises the frame's `src`, because a *detached* iframe has no `contentWindow` and the handler would bail before validating anything).
- **7 mutants, each reverted with the tree verified pristine, all RED:** listener left attached; previous port not closed on remount; source check dropped; origin check dropped; descriptor html withheld; catalogue snapshotted; shared Map rebuilt. (The two validation mutants fail as `DataCloneError` — without the check the handler fires twice and re-transfers a neutered port, which is precisely what the check prevents.)
- Owner suites unchanged and green: `mini-app-ui` 3/3, `agent-monitor-miniapp` 3/3, `csp-report-only-browser` 10/10, `ui-ux-accessibility` 2/2, `ux-bubble-stage` 1/1.
- Gates: docs-check OK (**969** claims), single-owner OK, test-lanes ok (94 unit / 149 live), docs-touched OK. **Pre-push gate: ALL GATES GREEN (unit)** — the branch is pushed.

## Two findings worth your attention
1. **A basename collision cost the mapper its focus.** The module was first `mini-app-host.mjs`; `getIntermediateImporters` matches by BASENAME, so it resolved to the server-side **`lib/mini-app-host.mjs`** and dragged `server.mjs` in — an edit of that module selected **146** test files, for a change that never touches the server. Renaming to `mini-app-surface.mjs` gives **1**. Naming is a speed property, not decoration.
2. **`icon-sprite` was a real landmine and caught this slice.** The extraction took four icon literals with it, fused.js fell to 1 against a floor of 5, and **the pre-push unit tier refused the push** (the cached FAIL for `1196182` is exactly that one failure, 732/721/1/10). The floor was right; the test's hardcoded file list was incomplete — its own comment names that trap. Re-pointed (commit 2): `public/components/*.mjs` is now swept **by glob**, the fused floor becomes `fused + component >= 5` plus a floor of 4 on the component surface, and the builder sweep covers components. Mutants RED: the four literals removed (component floor); a scratch component naming an undefined icon (proves the glob covers the NEXT slice, not just today's files). While there, a probe showed the union-carry check was **blind** — it is a subset test, and `i-maximize`/`i-minimize` also appear in `index.html`, so dropping a surface from the union stayed GREEN; the union is now pinned arithmetically (dropped-or-duplicated surface fails whatever the ids are). That was pre-existing, not introduced here.

## Not done / not claimed
- **No landing:** main is RED on P1 `jeye`, and coordinator instruction is focused + unit only — no full gate run by me. The merger owns the union gate.
- I did not touch any other slice; the two parallel fused.js slices stay unstarted per your constraint.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: The interactive mini-app surface moves out of public/fused.js into public/components/mini-app-surface.mjs (410 lines), wired at one initMiniAppHost({ … }) site inside the host's existing container guard. The host keeps the live `miniAppController` handle, the `window.__voiceboxMiniApp` assignment, the shared `launchedMiniApps` Map and the container guard, so all 14 external call sites are unchanged; `catalogMiniApps` arrives as a get/set accessor pair (the delete path reassigns it) and `sqehSyncMiniApps` as a callback. fused.js 5531 → 5138 lines. A second commit sweeps the extracted component modules in tests/icon-sprite.test.mjs by glob and pins its union arithmetic.
WHY: public/fused.js is the repo's hotspot (5888 lines before this work, 190 commits in 30 days); every slice moved out of it shrinks the blast radius of unrelated edits. The icon-sprite change was required: the moved literals dropped fused.js below that guard's floor and the pre-push unit tier refused the branch, and the guard's hardcoded file list is the thing that was incomplete — it is now glob-based so the next slice cannot repeat it.
EFFECT: No user-visible change: the mini-app card, its tool catalogue and the double-iframe bridge behave identically, including the "no container ⇒ no global" case. Operators get a smaller fused.js, an extraction test that drives the real bridge (handshake self-removal, single-use port transfer on remount, origin+source validation) with 7 mutants proven RED, and an icon guard that covers future component slices; the mapper closure for the new module is 1 test file.

THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED BEFORE FIXING (main a81c667, tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs shape; probe output recorded verbatim):
on a REFUSED output switch the row read `"No reply playing"` — renderDevices() repainted from the restored preference and overwrote the `Could not use <device>. <reason>.` line, so the one thing the reader needed was the one thing they never saw. The same probe measured the second half: the stored preference had correctly reverted to `out-a` while `#out-select` still showed `out-b`, i.e. the control kept naming the device that was NOT in use.
PROBE (pre-fix, main): {"accepted":{"text":"No reply playing","stored":{"id":"out-a",...},"selectValue":"out-a"},"rejection":{"text":"No reply playing","stored":{"id":"out-a","name":"Studio monitors"},"selectValue":"out-b"}}

THE FIX (public/components/audio-device-controller.mjs, refusal branch only, 10 lines incl. comments):
`renderDevices()` now runs FIRST and the refusal is written LAST, so the generic line cannot land on top of it; and the picker is put back explicitly (`els.outSelect.value = devices.prefs.out.id ?? ""`) because fillPicker() deliberately SKIPS rebuilding an unchanged option list, so it cannot undo the value the person just picked. Everything else in the branch (restore `previous`, savePrefs, the return) is unchanged. Order matters and is why the second line is needed: repaint → restore picker → write reason.

CONTROL (the assertion the bead asked for), tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs, new arm "a refused output says WHICH device it could not use and WHY, and does not leave the row lying":
a stubbed LIVE client accepts `out-a` and refuses `out-b` with reason "the device is in use by another application"; the arm requires (1) the stored preference is the device in use (`out-a`), (2) the row reads exactly `Could not use Headset earpiece. the device is in use by another application.`, (3) `#out-select` is back on `out-a`. It drives the live client through `window.__voiceboxLiveClient` AFTER init, so it also re-proves the live-accessor seam.

· TREE MUTANT (the defect reintroduced verbatim: reason written, then renderDevices, no picker restore) -> `AssertionError: the refusal must survive the repaint and name the device and the reason: the row currently reads "No reply playing"` (exit 1). Module restored byte-identical afterwards (cmp).
· IN-FILE MUTANT in tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs: the same reordering driven into the module source must be refused by the ordered arm (`writing the refusal BEFORE the repaint must be refused by the ordered arm: that order is the defect voicebox-beads-cqrd fixed`).

KEPT HONEST RATHER THAN LOOSENED — the byte-identity arm from uei2.6: this is the extraction region's FIRST cited behaviour change, so the comparison was neither weakened nor deleted. `tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs` now normalises THAT ONE BRANCH out of the comparison (a token replaces it on both sides, so every other statement still has to be byte-identical) and pins the branch by its own ORDERED arm: `renderDevices()` before the reason, the picker restore before the reason, and the refusal still naming `choice?.name` and `applied.reason`. A rewritten statement anywhere else in the region still fails the byte arm.

FOCUSED EVIDENCE: tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs 8/8 (7 existing + the new control); tests/audio-device-controller-extraction.test.mjs 5/5; both together 14/14 in ~7s. Pre-push unit lane green. DOCS: docs/07-architecture.md's audio-device paragraph records the fix, the two measured pre-fix values, and why the byte-identity arm is normalised on this one branch rather than loosened.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: In the device controller's output-change handler, a refused switch now repaints first, puts the picker back on the device in use, and writes the refusal reason last; tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs gains the control that pins it, and the extraction test's byte-identity arm normalises only this cited branch while pinning its order.

Both re-armed the very dependency I was removing — the test would have gone red when the fleet group was really extracted.
