comments.text:
MY MISS, AND ITS ROOT CAUSE — this bead's inventory was WRONG and it cost a full gate. voicebox-beads-9r00 (filed by the merger) records the failure: tests/presence-route-seam.test.mjs:13 asserted the fleet literal beside ...agentsReadRoutes, so r9hv.3's extraction reded it on the server tier. In my report to coord I named the ARMED set as exactly {agents-read:10, changelog:17}. presence:13 was armed too and I did not name it.

THE MECHANISM, because "I missed one" is not a root cause: my sweep's criterion was an assertion pinning TWO route members, and after fixing the escaped-slash blind spot I reported that fix as if it were complete. It was not. Inside a regex literal the spreads are written `\.\.\.presenceRoutes`, so I had to normalise `\.` as well as `\/` — I did not. With `\.` unescaped, every spread inside a regex literal parsed as ZERO members, and presence:13 — which really carries two spreads and one literal — scored as a SINGLE member, below my own threshold, and was dropped from the count before I ever looked at it. The two-member threshold then hid the loss: the total still looked plausible. I reported a corrected inventory of 10 assertions across 4 files; the file set was right, the classification was not, and the one line in it that mattered was invisible to my own tooling.

CORRECTED METHOD (escape BOTH, and do not threshold on member count): normalise `\/` -> `/` AND `\.` -> `.` before tokenising; count any assertion that names at least two route members as a position guard; split them by whether they name a literal route key beside a spread. Re-run that way now, across every test that reads server.mjs, the complete inventory is FOUR hits — and after .5 and 91tp exactly ONE is live:
  * tests/agents-read-route-seam.test.mjs:15 — INERT BY DESIGN: the old adjacency guard kept as executable documentation; it is only ever driven against a synthetic mutant string, and the neighbour-extraction arm is conditional on the literal still existing. It cannot red a landing.
  * tests/changelog-route-seam.test.mjs:20 — INERT BY DESIGN, same construction.
  * tests/changelog-route-seam.test.mjs:52 — INERT: a mutant string inside assert.throws.
  * tests/presence-route-seam.test.mjs:13 — THE LIVE ONE, and the only one left. It is voicebox-beads-9r00, already claimed by voicebox-gate-recover (my claim attempt was refused by bd, correctly), so I am not touching it: two lanes fixing one test is the duplicate the rules exist to prevent.

So there is no fourth trap of this class waiting in the next full gate — that is a claim about a re-run scan, not about my earlier note. LESSON, worth keeping: a scanner that finds "the class" is only as good as its normalisation. Two escapes in the same family sat in the same expression, and I reported the first fix as if it had finished the job; the verification that mattered was re-running the corrected scan, not re-reading my own summary.

title: Selector policy: the server.mjs importer edge pins every lib/routes module's mapped closure at ~137 tests
description:
DECISION BEAD routed to coord (and the hub's selector-policy workstream), filed from the r9hv ADR's speed measurement rather than smuggled into an extraction.

MEASURED, origin/main: scripts/test-changed.mjs maps a change to server.mjs to 156 tests (24 unit / 58 server / 74 browser), and a change to ANY lib/routes/*.mjs to ~137-138 (extensions.mjs 150). The composition of lib/routes/presence.mjs's 137 is the point: 3 tests name presence.mjs, 2 name lib/room-presence.mjs, and 137 name server.mjs. The module's own closure is three tests; the other 134 are inherited purely because server.mjs IMPORTS it and the mapper treats server.mjs (and lib/, tools/, core/) as an intermediate importer whose naming tests are added to the queue.

WHY IT MATTERS: it means HTTP route extraction out of server.mjs cannot make the fast gate faster (156 -> ~137, about 12%, with a hard floor), so decomposition there must be justified by merge collisions instead — server.mjs is the repo's hottest file at 214 commits/30 days against 1-2 for each route module. It also means the two decompositions have opposite gate economics for the same reason: a public/ module is NOT scanned as an importer source, which is why the fused.js extraction (public/components/*.mjs) yields a 1-2 test closure while a lib/routes module cannot. That asymmetry is a property of the mapper's importer rule, not of either codebase.

THE DECISION ASKED FOR (this is the hub's call, already escalated; this bead is its durable record): should the intermediate-importer rule be narrowed so a module's own closure reflects its own dependencies (e.g. only count importers whose tests actually exercise the imported symbol, or scope the scan to real import statements rather than any textual mention), or should the rule stay as a deliberate wide-coverage guard and decomposition be justified by collision alone? Evidence to weigh: the current rule is what makes server.mjs edits run 137 tests, and it is ALSO what makes the fused.js extraction look like a win. Do not change it as a drive-by: any narrowing must not reduce real coverage for the routes that depend on server.mjs's helpers. NO ACTION TAKEN BY ME beyond filing this: no mapper edit, no code change, no proposal disguised as a fix.

Scope: the four contiguous entries GET /api/gemini/capabilities, POST /api/gemini/image, POST /api/gemini/video, POST /api/gemini/embed (server.mjs:3947-4036) to lib/routes/gemini-media.mjs as createGeminiMediaRoutes({...deps}), spread at the SAME table position. Named deps: json, readJsonBody, answerOnce, resolveActive. Two things make this a DELIBERATE choice rather than a safe one, both named here rather than discovered later: (1) NO existing test names /api/gemini, so this slice needs a NEW focused test written from first principles; (2) these handlers call external media APIs, so the test must not depend on a live external call — drive the seam with an injected/faked provider and assert the refusal shapes, not the model output. comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
SLICE 3 IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED — branch fleet/type-recover-gemini @ bf8a9be (full sha bf8a9be3c82fc0c1e10088b8976a6383294a76be), based on fresh main 591c471 (which already carries the landed r9hv.2 tools slice and the ezu7 fix). Ready for a cross-family reviewer; delta for the reviewer is 591c471..bf8a9be.

SCOPE, exactly as assigned: the four CONTIGUOUS entries — GET /api/gemini/capabilities, POST /api/gemini/image, POST /api/gemini/video, POST /api/gemini/embed — moved to lib/routes/gemini-media.mjs as createGeminiMediaRoutes({...}) and spread at the position they occupied (between ...activityRoutes and DELETE /api/root). 82 lines removed from server.mjs; added are one import, one factory call, one spread. Refusal shapes and their order preserved (a non-JSON body is 400 bad-request BEFORE any provider call), the image route keeps CONTENT_JSON_BODY_MAX_BYTES while video/embed keep the reader default, saveAs still writes through the host's resolveActive, answerOnce still answers once. FENCED static/CSP entries NOT touched — verified, not asserted: the diff removes nothing structural (no DELETE /api/root, no activityRoutes, no table header).

THE TWO SEAMS. (1) The active root is read LIVE: the image route honours saveAs only when the active root is a machine root, so the host passes getActiveRoot: () => active and the handler reads it per request. A snapshot would freeze the boot-time root (voicebox-beads-w1f9) and the seam test changes the accessor's answer between two calls, which is what a snapshot fails. (2) The five provider calls arrive as deps (generateGeminiImage, startGeminiVideoGeneration, pollGeminiVideoOperation, embedGeminiTexts, semanticSearchDocuments), which is what makes any test of this slice possible without a live provider.

EVIDENCE, NOT "IT SERVES". Live probe on the real server, using ONLY refusal paths so nothing external is touched: GET /api/gemini/capabilities -> 200 with the catalogue payload; POST /api/gemini/{image,video,embed} with a non-JSON body -> 400 {"ok":false,"refused":"bad-request","why":"body must be JSON"} each; GET /api/geminiX -> 404 {"error":"not found"}; POST /api/gemini/capabilities (wrong method) -> 404. New focused tests/gemini-media-route-seam.test.mjs 3/3 green, and FIVE MUTANTS DRIVEN RED each on its intended assertion: snapshotted root -> "the route must read the active root at request time — a captured snapshot keeps the boot-time root"; video refusal answering 200 -> "POST /api/gemini/video must refuse a non-object body"; a real fetch call added to the module -> "this test must not touch the network"; the spread moved out of position -> "the gemini spread must stay where the four entries were"; an inline duplicate entry -> "no inline POST /api/gemini/embed may shadow the factory". The fetch-spy mutant matters most: it proves the no-external-network requirement is a check with teeth, not a vacuous assertion. Gates: test-lanes ok (94 unit / 142 live), single-owner OK, docs:check OK (928 path claims), docs-touched OK (3 described files, 2 documents). Fast gate for bf8a9be running (unit-only, as coord instructed); NO author full gate.

NEXT ACTION: the seam test landed in the LIVE lane, not unit, so the unit fast gate does not exercise it — the reviewer's own reproduction and the merger's full gate are what cover this slice. No merge-queue label.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: Extracts the four contiguous Gemini media entries (GET /api/gemini/capabilities, POST /api/gemini/image, /video, /embed) from server.mjs into lib/routes/gemini-media.mjs, built by createGeminiMediaRoutes({json, readJsonBody, answerOnce, resolveActive, getActiveRoot, contentBodyMaxBytes, listGeminiCapabilities, liveConfigCatalogue, and the five provider functions}) and spread into the routes table at its original position. Adds tests/gemini-media-route-seam.test.mjs (source-wiring with self-proving missing-spread/shadowing/reorder/snapshot mutants; capabilities payload; all three refusal paths with no provider call; the live-root saveAs behaviour; video and embed argument shapes; a table-level negative control; and a fetch spy proving the file never touches the network). Documents the module in docs/07-architecture.md and README.md.
WHY: server.mjs is the repo's collision hotspot (214 commits in 30 days against 1-2 for each lib/routes module), and this group was the ADR's only SUBSTANTIVE slice with no module-level mutable-state writes. It also had no test coverage at all — nothing named /api/gemini — so it silently carried an untested provider boundary.
EFFECT: None for a person using the room: the four routes answer exactly as before, refusals included. In-tree, the Gemini media boundary now has a focused owner test that runs without touching an external API, and edits to it land in a file that 1-2 commits/30d touch instead of the 214-commit file. No gate time added.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
BOOT STATE: still gated on the authority ruling — the parent r9hv records r9hv.3 as "HELD by coord pending the authority decision". Nothing in the tree has changed. Everything else in this family is landed and closed on main 71de9d3 (r9hv.2 tools, r9hv.4 gemini, r9hv.5 the two armed seam guards), and .5 is precisely what makes THIS slice safe for its neighbour: the agents-read guard is now order-based over spread anchors, so extracting the fleet entries cannot red it.

I DID THE TECHNICAL HALF, and it MOVES the question rather than dodging it: the authority DECISION for contact is ALREADY in a module, not in the host.
  - lib/fleet.mjs (281 lines, createFleetManager) owns contact(): it resolves the target environment, chooses the bearer (the caller's auth.bearer or the environment's own pairing bearer), and produces the refusals — bad-request, environment-unknown, environment-not-paired ("listed but not paired — pair it before contacting agents"), environment-unreachable, session-contact-unsupported.
  - The host entry (server.mjs:3772) makes NO authority decision of its own. It reads the body (400 bad-request), MINTS an audit token — sha256("voicebox-fleet-contact\0" + SELF_ENVIRONMENT) plus a callId — forwards the CALLER's bearer, and maps a refusal reason to a status: environment-not-paired → 403, anything else → 400.
So these 28 lines are an ADAPTER that already delegates the decision to lib/fleet.mjs. Extracting them does not move who-may-contact-whom out of the host, because that rule is not in the host today.

FACTS THE RULING CAN RELY ON, each verified rather than assumed:
  1. SELF_ENVIRONMENT is a boot-time const (server.mjs:585), so passing its VALUE to the factory is behaviour-preserving — there is no live-accessor hazard of the getActiveRoot kind here.
  2. Deps are exactly the ones already named: json, readJsonBody, answerOnce, createHash (node:crypto), SELF_ENVIRONMENT, fleetManager, publicFleetProjection.
  3. The 403 list includes cross-environment-unauthorized, which contact() does NOT currently produce — the only producer is the delegate_task path (server.mjs:3301). Preservation means moving the mapping verbatim, hedge included. Recorded so nobody "tidies" it mid-port; it is not a defect and not in scope for this bead.
  4. The behaviour test owner is heavy and belongs to another lane: tests/fleet-addressability.test.mjs:308 ("fleet server: GET /api/fleet, POST /api/fleet/contact, and turn tools", 45s timeout). My seam test is the source-wiring half; that one is the behaviour half.

MY RECOMMENDATION: ALLOW both entries as ONE contiguous unit into lib/routes/fleet.mjs, spread between ...agentsReadRoutes and ...harnessRoutes (their position today, 3766-3793), because the control the ruling is protecting is already enforced in lib/fleet.mjs against pairing credentials the route itself never sees. If the ruling is instead that a bearer-forwarding adapter must stay host-owned, take ONLY GET /api/fleet and say so: the two entries would then straddle host and module, which is legitimate — my .5 guard references neither literal — but it should be a deliberate choice rather than a default.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, deliberately: no tree changes, no branch. Status set BLOCKED with the owner named and one next action, per the fleet's off-ramp rule.

description:

DEFECT (P3, test-instrument blind spot — same class as the 94of finding: the gate answers "fine" to a size it could not read). tests/type-scale-tokens.test.mjs reads declarations ONE LINE AT A TIME with a case-sensitive regex, so two valid CSS spellings produce a sub-12px size that the floor gate never sees. Both are latent today (no shipped surface uses either spelling), so nothing is live — but the gate's promise is "a reintroduced sub-12px size is refused by fleet-check --fast", and these bypass it.

    font-size:

Modern Web Guidance Teachable Moment & Compliance Record (voicebox-beads-3674):

1. Planned Approach:
Ad-hoc lifting of individual hardcoded pixel/rem sizes as single-element fixes (similar to ms0t's single badge fix).

2. Self-Derived Diagnosis (CSS Audit & CDP):
Inspection of public/style.css, secondary apps, and prototype identified 30 sub-12px literals (down to 0.5625rem / 9px) causing microcopy legibility deficits and lacking a centralized type scale on :root.

3. Guidance Citation (verbatim from `typography` and `respect-os-text-scale`):
• typography: "DON'T use px for font-size. Prefer rem to honor the user's browser font-size preferences (root font size), or em/percentages for contextual sizing."
• typography: "Use unitless numbers for line-height (e.g., 1.5) to ensure relative scaling during font-size inheritance."
• respect-os-text-scale: "Allow Text Containers to Grow: Text-containing components and containers MUST be able to grow to accommodate scaled text. Avoid fixed height or block-size values and restrictive max-height or max-block-size values that can cause clipping or overflow."

4. Adopted Approach:
Established a unified `--text-*` scale on `:root` (`--text-xs: 0.75rem` to `--text-2xl: 1.25rem`) setting an accessible 0.75rem (12px) floor across all shipped surfaces. Used unitless line-heights and avoided rigid max-height constraints to allow text elements to scale gracefully under 200% root zoom without clipping or layout shift.

title: Preserve per-file browser isolation; overlap independent server and browser tiers only behind exact coverage
description:
Context: origin/main 1f9b123 already runs four work-stealing browser file workers, each with a separate process/server/profile; 74 browser files (2 isolated) took 213.1s in the latest 331s cached full gate (tree a17ef04d, 2026-10-13). Its 62 server files took 43.46s and run BEFORE browser via `&&` in package.json. Earlier 522s/396s numbers predate landed voicebox-beads-hhkg; its long-lived shared-instance ADR g9jf was superseded after actual shard implementation. The fast cache for that tree reports coverage UNKNOWN despite state PASS; host ~/.fleet/check.conf now points to agents-factory, so a new voicebox fleet-check must not inherit that command.

Decision: Keep the existing isolated four-worker browser runner and exact-queue guard. If resource evidence supports it, run independent server and browser tiers concurrently with a bounded TOTAL worker budget, fail-closed aggregate exit and signal cleanup; hold pre-push's machine timing test and barge-in's fake-audio test isolated until deterministic under contention. Every gate must emit a machine-readable, per-test-file manifest from the same classifier that drives dispatch, with executed/passed/failed/skipped/omitted and reason; any missing, duplicated, or unrecognized test or marker is UNKNOWN/FAIL, not PASS. Full test set stays on the merger's merged union; implementer's fast tier is an explicit subset selected by changed-path mapping and has a correct project-owned command.

Consequences: Best-case overlap saves up to the measured 43s server tier (331→~288s, not yet <=240s target); contention may erase gains, so benchmark on the VM before adopting. Further ~48s must be won by fixture independence/browser-tail work rather than dropping tests. Coverage records and config enforcement cost implementation but make speed claims auditable. Alternatives considered: re-shard the already-sharded browser lane or share a long-lived browser/server (rejected: duplicated work/changes profile, env, OPFS isolation); simply run both four-worker tiers without a total budget (rejected: CPU contention flakes); accept green by ignoring missing tiers (rejected: false clearance).

title: Filter non-absolute PATH segments during local speech engine discovery
description:
Severity: LOW
Source/station evidence: lib/offline-speech.mjs:35; factory station vuln-triage (run-20261013-031933); report /home/exedev/agents/findings/voicebox-factory-delta.md.
Detail: In lib/offline-speech.mjs:35, getSearchDirectories splits PATH into directory segments without filtering path.isAbsolute(segment). If PATH contains empty or relative directory entries, resolveCandidate joins them against relative binary candidates, resolving binaries relative to process.cwd() and risking execution of untrusted local binaries in workspace directories. Contrast with lib/harness-inventory.mjs:42, which explicitly enforces searchPath.split(path.delimiter).filter(path.isAbsolute).
Next action: Add .filter((segment) => path.isAbsolute(segment)) to fromPath in getSearchDirectories() in lib/offline-speech.mjs.

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION FINDINGS (voicebox-inv-34or-stale): Root cause of first full gate STALE verdict on bb31d93.

1. Evidence from cached checks:
- ~/.fleet/checks/364c5ffb273a61908d6aeb0450c7baac857c898e.json.1: state=STALE, rc=0, secs=409, state_reason='the worktree's CONTENT changed during the run without a commit (HEAD^{tree} is still 364c5ffb273a61908d6aeb0450c7baac857c898e), so the suites read bytes that tree does not describe; re-run on a settled worktree'
- Log tail in log.1: '[gate] pre-push: ALL GATES GREEN\nfleet-heavy: warning - descendants still held slot1 after the job finished (3272458 3272459 3272460 ); killing them so the slot is released'
- ~/.fleet/checks/364c5ffb273a61908d6aeb0450c7baac857c898e.json: state=PASS, rc=0, secs=3. pre-push skipped stages via tree-receipt '.git/voicebox-gate-passed-tree'. Note: the second gate ALSO had 'fleet-heavy: warning - descendants still held slot1... (3273979 3273980 3273981 )' but recorded PASS.

2. Differentiation of causes:
- Orphan descendant / slot cleanup: NOT the cause of STALE. That warning comes from fleet-heavy cleaning up leaked slot FDs after the command process exits. fleet-heavy exits with the command rc (0).
- Dirty tree: git status remained clean (0 uncommitted files, no untracked diff).
- The actual cause: fleet-check worker computes worktree_digest at start and finish:
  git ls-files -z | xargs -0 -r stat -c '%n %s %z' | sha256sum
  where %z is inode change time (ctime).
  During live test execution (scripts/test-lanes.mjs server lane), tests/server-bind-resilience.test.mjs:204 executes:
    const watched = path.join(ROOT, 'lib', 'resolver.mjs');
    writeFileSync(watched, original);
  This writes in-place to tracked lib/resolver.mjs in the active worktree to trigger a --watch restart. Even though bytes are identical, writing advances lib/resolver.mjs ctime (%z). This causes digest_end != digest_start, tripping the STALE verdict in fleet-check:finish().

3. Why attempt 2 succeeded:
Attempt 1 ran to completion (rc 0) and minted the verified tree receipt in .git/voicebox-gate-passed-tree before finish() marked STALE. On attempt 2, pre-push.sh matched the tree receipt and skipped tests, so tests/server-bind-resilience.test.mjs did NOT run, ctime was unchanged, worktree_digest matched, and fleet-check recorded PASS.

title: Fix settings dialog opened via system command / dock: aria-expanded and refresh are skipped
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found during read-only ymu6 investigation (does not depend on ymu6; independently fixable).

EVIDENCE (origin/main cc37470, public/fused.js):
- :4386-4405 (the only open path that works) is the gear-click handler: showModal() + settingsOpen aria-expanded=true + refreshDevices() + loadAgentSettings() + loadApiKeysSettings(); :4402-4405 the close handler resets aria-expanded=false and refocuses the gear.
- :220 system command branch: 'els.settings?.showModal?.()' for open_panel=settings — no aria-expanded, no refresh.
- :6054 dock: document.getElementById('sqeh-dock-settings') click -> document.getElementById('settings')?.showModal?() — no aria-expanded, no refresh.
- :3505 is fine: it routes through els.settingsOpen?.click().
So a user who opens Settings from the system command or the SQEH dock gets stale 'Not asked yet' agent/key rows and an honest-by-luck aria-expanded=false (most recent tnxm fix was the same class of bug: aria-expanded true after close).

WHY IT MEANS WORK: opening the dialog without refreshing shows stale applied/provider state, which is the exact failure the agent-settings work exists to prevent. Suggest the fix be a single  helper both direct paths call (the ymu6 extraction will make this natural, which is why it is filed now rather than folded into ymu6's scope).

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
ADR (read-only, no source edits) — remaining cohesive UI modules in public/fused.js, and which ones are actually safe to take.

MEASURED ON: worktree @ 7271204 (= origin/main 71de9d3 + the bf8a9be/91c3e24 landings). Method: `node scripts/test-changed.mjs --dry-run --json <file>`; declarations by top-level span; purity by reading EVERY match for the 38 module-level `let`s inside each span, not by counting them (see the method caveat at the end — counting gave one false positive).

CONTEXT. public/fused.js = 5887 lines, 186 top-level declarations, 38 module-level `let`s (that is the core state: roomFolders/roomFolder/roomTruncated, entries/shownFile/listedRoot/listingDir/fileFilter/showAllFiles, timers), and a 119-entry element map (`els`/WANTED) that existing modules already receive as a pass-through. It is the hottest file in the browser tier: 190 commits in 30 days against 1 for an extracted module (server.mjs 215), and origin/fleet/gate-coverage is editing it right now — so every extraction landing rebases, and each one takes lines out of that file.

CLOSURE, measured: public/fused.js = 152 tests (unit 20 / server 59 / browser 73). An extracted UI module = 1-3 tests (components/changelog-dialog.mjs 2 browser, settings-ui.mjs 3 unit, components/environment-root-dialog.mjs 1 browser, audio-meters.mjs 1 unit). The mvxl doc recorded 148 = 19/58/71 for the same file; the drift is tests landed since, so quote the number with its sha rather than reusing 148. HONEST FRAMING, taken from the mvxl precedent because it is still true: extraction does NOT narrow the mapper and does not make the fused.js bootstrap cheap — server.mjs serves /fused.js, so a fused.js edit still selects 152. What it changes is the BLAST RADIUS of future work on that surface: 152 -> 1-3.

FILED (bounded, independent, one per candidate — all PURE-UI by the check above, each with a verified DOM owner test):
  * voicebox-beads-uei2.2 — public/components/activity-log-ui.mjs (fused.js:321-458 + the close/clear wiring at ~5354-5363, ~148 LOC). Owners: acp-console-ui, system-error-ui, ux-bubble-stage. Must RECEIVE the shared redaction, not own a second copy (mvxl: one vocabulary with the Change log dialog).
  * voicebox-beads-uei2.4 — public/components/mic-hotkey-controller.mjs (3600-3695, ~96 LOC). Owner: tests/mic-hotkey.test.mjs. Carries a window keydown listener: the double-wiring count is the point.
  * voicebox-beads-uei2.5 — public/components/sync-toast.mjs (4305-4444, ~140 LOC). Owners: health-auth-browser, ux-bubble-stage. Takes openChangelogDialog as a dep (the build stamp's link) and must keep window.__voiceboxSyncToast working.
  * voicebox-beads-uei2.6 — public/components/audio-device-controller.mjs (3423-3598, ~176 LOC). Owner: tests/settings-dialog.test.mjs. getLiveClient must be a LIVE accessor (the w1f9 shape), and the device seam stays injectable so a focused run needs no real device.

RANKED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT FILED, with the reason:
  * Mini-app host (4663-5076, ~414 LOC) — PURE, verified by reading the matches: the apparent coupling was `Map.entries()` substring hits plus a NEIGHBOURING window-globals block at 5078-5085 (`window.__voiceboxGetRoomFolders`, `__voiceboxGetActiveFolder`) that my span arithmetic absorbed. In fact this is the largest clean region, with five DOM owners (mini-app-ui, mini-app-popover, mini-app-architecture, multi-window-manager, ux-bubble-stage). Not filed only because the iframe/MessageChannel bridge deserves a slice plan of its own rather than a file-it-and-see. RECOMMENDED NEXT after the four above.
  * Harnesses / agent-delegation dialog (3822-4177, ~356 LOC) — BORDERLINE, not pure: reads listingDir (4031, 4070), reads roomFolder (4087) and calls showFile/writeRoomFile/loadRoomFolder/load. It needs live accessors plus callbacks, so it is a real seam rather than a lift. Owners: modal-panels, ux-bubble-stage.
  * SQEH deck/shell (5110-5885, ~776 LOC) — BORDERLINE and the riskiest of the large ones. It spans several declarations (sqehSetState 5116, sqehSyncMiniApps 5177, sqehArtifactChip 1865) with CALLERS inside other regions (261-263, 2269, 2312, 4946, 5009), its state lives in DOM datasets, and it MONKEY-PATCHES Element.prototype.scrollIntoView, HTMLElement.prototype.focus and Element.prototype.checkVisibility (verified, ~5413-5442). Patching globals from an extracted module is a behaviour change waiting to happen: this wants a slice plan and an oracle pass before anyone takes it. Owner: tests/ux-bubble-stage.test.mjs (1317 lines, queries #sqeh-deck).
  * Room-folders bar / grant chips (741-938, ~198 LOC) — COUPLED, and deliberately NOT now: it writes roomFolders, roomFolder, listedRoot, listingRefusal and entries, and drives File System Access permissions. This is the core state the bead title says to disentangle AFTER the cohesive UI is out, in its own ADR. Filed nothing here on purpose.

NOT CANDIDATES, said plainly: send (32 core refs), saveEditedFile, startListening, presentInspectionInReader, activeLiveTurnRole — core turn/reader/folder state. executeBrowserSystemCommand has 0 core refs but it is COMMAND EXECUTION, not UI, and it is security-relevant: out of scope for a UI decomposition and a separate decision.

WHAT EVERY CHILD MUST DO (the house shape, from docs/07-architecture.md:246-250 + README:250): verbatim move locked by the test; ONE init site handing `els` and helpers; live accessors for mutable state; an extraction test that drives the real page, counts double wiring, proves a listener-free clone does nothing, and has a STATIC arm that fused.js no longer carries the moved markers (a dead leftover copy is invisible to behaviour assertions and there is no lint gate); mutants driven RED; and docs updates (07-architecture row 11 + a per-module paragraph, README module list).

TWO HARD GATES THE CHILDREN MUST RESPECT, both measured:
  1. UNMAPPED MODULE = REFUSED: a changed source file that maps to no test makes the fast gate refuse with exit 1 (`unmapped-source-file`; `node scripts/test-changed.mjs --gate public/components/harness-dialog.mjs` -> exit 1). So each slice ships the test that maps its module.
  2. LANDMINES: ten tests assert public/fused.js SOURCE content — caption-fade-and-thinking, changelog-dialog-extraction, help-dialog-modal, icon-sprite, modern-web-room, project-switch-live-error, ptt-and-thinking-settings, room-folder-ops, settings-open-paths-seam, settings-ui-extraction. Per candidate I checked which match: activity -> caption-fade-and-thinking; mini-app -> room-folder-ops + caption-fade; sqeh -> settings-open-paths-seam; empty-state -> icon-sprite + room-folder-ops; harness/hotkey/sync-toast/devices -> none. A matching test must be RE-POINTED to the module with its assertion unchanged (the tests/ui-modern-polish.test.mjs precedent), never weakened.

METHOD CAVEAT so the next reader can reproduce rather than trust: counting substring matches for the core-state names is an UPPER BOUND — `entries` also matches `Map.entries()`, which is exactly how the mini-app region looked coupled when it is not. Every verdict above was re-read line by line. A first pass also attributed CSS to `public/main.css`, which does not exist: the deck's 95 `sqeh` rules are in public/style.css.

OPEN QUESTIONS for coord: (a) sequence — the four filed slices are independent of each other and of r9hv.3, so they can be taken in any order after the r9hv.3 ruling; (b) the mini-app host is the biggest clean win and needs a slice plan first; (c) whether the deck's prototype patching must STAY in the host even when the rest of the sqeh surface moves — that is a design question for whoever takes SQEH, not something to discover mid-port.

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: LESSON FOR REMAINING SLICES (from uei2.2, worth broadcasting): when extracting state, sweep for every READER of it, not just the definitions. uei2.2 found the host clear handler still calling workActivitySeenIds.clear() after the set had moved - a ReferenceError waiting for the first Clear, invisible to load-time and verbatim-only checks. Fix: move the operation with the state and add a re-introduction mutant. Also corrected: the ADR mapped the activity candidate to tests/caption-fade-and-thinking, but that test asserts nothing about this region and needed no re-point (mapping error, not coupling). Remaining ranked slices: mini-app host (4663-5076) is the ranked next, needing a slice plan for its iframe/MessageChannel bridge; harnesses dialog BORDERLINE; SQEH deck BORDERLINE (monkey-patches Element.prototype.scrollIntoView/HTMLElement.prototype.focus/checkVisibility - wants an oracle pass, not a port); room-folders bar COUPLED - leave to its own ADR.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
READER-SWEEP LESSON from uei2.2 (the activity-log slice), recorded here because every remaining slice can repeat it: when a slice moves STATE out of fused.js, sweeping for the moved DEFINITIONS is not enough — every READER of that state must be swept too, because a reader that survives the move is a runtime error waiting for the input that reaches it, and neither a load-time check nor a verbatim-move comparison can see it. In uei2.2 the host's clear handler still called `workActivitySeenIds.clear()` after the set had moved into the module: the page loaded fine and every test passed until the first click on Clear would have thrown. The slice fixed it by moving the clear OPERATION with the state it forgets, and tests/activity-log-extraction.test.mjs now carries a mutant that re-introduces the dangling reference so the class cannot come back silently. Relatedly: a verbatim check also cannot see a name the WRAPPER must supply — uei2.2's factory first took `createSeenSet` while the moved body called `createBoundedSeenSet`, which threw at the init site and silently skipped the rest of the boot sequence; only probing the real page caught it.
The same hazard appears TWICE in the planned mini-app host slice (voicebox-beads-uei2.7): `miniAppController` has fourteen readers across the host, six of them null-guarded, and `catalogMiniApps` is read AND reassigned inside the region. The plan therefore keeps the handle as a live host variable and injects an accessor pair instead of a snapshot. Any future slice plan should state, for each piece of moved state, its full reader list — that is now the shape of the uei2.7 plan.

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: Add to the umbrella for remaining slices: (1) MODULE NAMING IS A SPEED PROPERTY - scripts/test-changed.mjs resolves by basename, so a new component whose basename collides with a server-side module (e.g. mini-app-host.mjs vs lib/mini-app-host.mjs) inherits server.mjs and jumps the mapped closure from 1 to 146 tests. (2) tests/icon-sprite.test.mjs hardcoded its file list; it is now glob-based over public/components/*.mjs with an arithmetic union pin and mutants, so future slices are covered. (3) When extracting state, sweep its READERS (uei2.2 lesson).

CORRECTION AND WITHDRAWAL, recorded in place of my earlier claim.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I reported 'the dark arm is not driven on /, /help.html or /index.html'. That was false. Those pages do not respond to prefers-color-scheme; they carry their OWN theme mode on <html data-theme>, and the room exposes id=theme-toggle plus theme-select, Help carries data-theme directly. My emulation only drove the OS media feature, so my 'dark' pass measured the light theme twice and I read the identical numbers as 'no dark theme exists'. The evidence that it does exist was in the same run and I did not look for it: #utterance resolves to a different colour AND a different ground in dark.

WHAT IS TRUE, measured by setting data-theme on <html> and reading every [placeholder] element on each page:
  / (room)    22 placeholders, 21 below 4.5:1 in light AND 21 below in dark
  /help.html   1 placeholder,   1 below in light AND in dark
  /index.html 22 placeholders, 21 below in light AND in dark
  /environment.html 6, 0 below - the landed sv2n fix, used as the control

The COUNT is theme-independent; the RATIOS are not. Two elements show it:
  help-page-search   light rgb(117,117,117) on rgb(251,251,249) = 4.45:1   dark SAME grey on rgb(11,15,25) = 4.16:1
  file-filter        light rgb(89,99,109)  on rgb(255,255,255) = 6.12:1   dark rgb(148,163,184) on rgb(21,29,47)  = 6.56:1
So the ground moves with the theme and the user agent grey does not, which makes the failure WORSE in dark, not absent.

THE FIX PRECEDENT IS NOW IN-REPO AND EXACT: file-filter passes in BOTH themes because it uses the application's own colour rather than the user agent's. That is the same shape as sv2n - reuse the token the page already uses for secondary text. No new values.

#utterance, derived not read, composited at alpha 0.62 in both themes: light color(srgb 0.34902 0.388235 0.427451 / 0.62) over rgb(253,253,252) = 2.68:1; dark color(srgb 0.580392 0.639216 0.721569 / 0.62) over rgb(17,23,37) = 3.46:1. Both under the floor; light is the worst element on the page.

SCOPE for the fix, when approved: one scoped rule per page that owns the failing elements, reusing the page's own token, never a global ::placeholder. The composer (.composer / #utterance) and .list-tools keep their current placeholder styling deliberately - and #utterance needs its alpha preserved rather than overridden, so whatever changes there must be expressed through the same token the app uses at 0.62, not a flat colour.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
**Implemented at `2082777`** on `fleet/shard-oiod`, off fresh `origin/main 91d8347` (fetched, not cached), in its own worktree. Test-only: **no product CSS change**, the stylesheet is byte-identical (`665f589b`).

The Environment half of `tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs` asserted only `assert.notEqual(backOutlineStyle, "none")`. It now pins `style`, `width`, `offset` and `colour`. **Every value was measured on this tree rather than assumed**: with the page's rule the ring is `solid / 2px / 2px / rgb(31, 63, 208)` (= `var(--accent)` light); with the declaration removed it becomes the user agent's `auto / 1px / 1px / rgb(16, 16, 16)`. I also measured programmatic `.focus()` against a keyboard `Tab` — identical, both `:focus-visible: true` — so the existing focus technique was sound and only the assertion was weak.

**Two mutants, both restored byte-identically (`665f589b`), and the first one is the whole point:**

| mutant | old guard | now |
|---|---|---|
| REMOVE `outline: 2px solid var(--accent)` | 1 pass / 1 fail — the browser half stayed green on the UA ring | **0 pass / 2 fail**, failing on "back-nav focus ring must be the page's own, got `auto`" |
| SUPPRESS with `outline: none` | 0 pass / 2 fail | **0 pass / 2 fail** — no loss |

The `1/1 → 0/2` row is the gap this bead was filed for, now closed and demonstrated with a before *and* an after. The old result is not my memory: it is the measurement in the `xggy.3` mutant dispute, where `rev-xggy3c` was right and I was wrong.

**A trap worth recording.** My first attempt at both mutants applied **nothing** — the anchor assumed one declaration per line, but `environment.css:24` is a single-line rule (`:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }`), so the replace was a no-op and the test reported 2 pass. The script's `assert s.count(old) == 1` is what stopped me publishing a phantom RED with no mutation behind it. **A mutant that did not apply is not a mutant**, and the count check is the only thing that distinguishes them.

This file is **browser tier**, so the fast gate's coverage warning names it as unmapped — the green unit lane says nothing about this change. The evidence is the focused run (2 of 2) plus the two mutants above; the merger's union gate covers the rest of the tier.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: `tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs` pins the Environment page's back-nav focus ring to the page's own ring — `solid / 2px / 2px / rgb(31, 63, 208)`, all measured — instead of asserting only that some ring exists.
WHAT: Proven by two mutants with the stylesheet restored byte-identically: removing the author declaration now gives 0 pass / 2 fail where the old guard gave 1 pass / 1 fail on the user agent's own ring, and suppressing it with `none` still gives 0 pass / 2 fail.
WHY: `assert.notEqual(outlineStyle, "none")` could not see the page's rule at all, because the user agent supplies a focus ring of its own (`auto / 1px / 1px / rgb(16, 16, 16)`). A guard that stays green when the rule it protects is deleted is worth less than no guard, because it is believed (voicebox-beads-oiod).
EFFECT: none for users — no product file changes. A missing or muted focus ring on the Environment page now fails the accessibility test instead of passing it, and the colour assertion means a ring that silently falls back to the browser's default is caught too.

title: Zero-match test-name-pattern hangs when test.after runs before async test.before assigns server (tests/voicebox.test.mjs:42)
description:
Pre-existing test runner lifecycle race discovered while reviewing voicebox-beads-mgbv.
Repro: node --test --test-name-pattern='nonexistent' tests/voicebox.test.mjs
Observed: Test runner hangs indefinitely until killed. In Node.js node:test, when 0 tests match a pattern in a suite with an async test.before() hook, test.after() is scheduled and runs concurrently while test.before() is still awaiting startServer(). Because  is still undefined,  no-ops. When startServer() finishes, the child server runs with open stdout/stderr pipes, wedging the runner.
Expected: Clean exit 0 in <1s when no tests match.
Fix: Store the startServer promise synchronously in  during test.before and await  in test.after before calling .
Fix owner: voicebox-audioflake
close_reason: Landed origin/main 91d8347 with full merged-union gate PASS and durable independent review PASS

comments.author: voicebox-audioflake
comments.text:
READ-ONLY Stage 1 design pending mgbv landing/fresh-main implementation approval; no source edits/tests now. Root cause bounded reviewer evidence: zero-match node --test can schedule test.after() before async test.before() completes; existing tests/voicebox.test.mjs: test.before assigns server only AFTER awaiting startServer(), so after sees undefined and skips stop; startServer() later returns a live detached child with open stdio. tests/lib/server.mjs registers exact child in LIVE_CHILDREN at spawn and cleans failures itself, but a ready server returned to the caller requires stop(). Proposal for THIS test file ONLY: module-scoped let serverStart; in test.before, synchronously assign serverStart = startServer({cwd:ROOT,env:{VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE:WORKSPACE}}) as the first async operation, then await serverStart and set server/BASE; test.after obtains await serverStart before calling stop() on the fulfilled server, even when no test matched. If startServer rejects, rely on helper's own catch/stop and do not mask the original test.before failure with a second rejection; if before never ran, after no-ops. Stop only the instance returned by this fixture, no sweeping PIDs and no changes to server.mjs or shared helper. Preserve normal match behavior, scratch declared root and hook order.
RED/GREEN acceptance once approved, each with timeout -k 30 and hard N <= 20s, exact tree and no full gate: (A) disposable subprocess runs node --test --test-name-pattern="__voicebox_no_match__" tests/voicebox.test.mjs, pre-fix timeout 124 then post-fix exit 0 within bounded budget with 0 matched/fail; (B) normal matched HTTP test-name-pattern="a decoded NUL in a static path" still exits 0 and verifies 200/404. For liveness, wrapper records exact child server PID AND /proc/<pid>/stat start time from the subprocess process tree (ancestor chain under its node:test worker, command line EXACT repo server.mjs) while command runs, then asserts that same pid/start-time is gone after test exits; if PID reused, never signal it. Cleanup uses exact process-group only for a bounded timed-out RED probe; no indiscriminate pkill/port sweep. If /proc is unavailable, mark liveness unsupported rather than treating an empty scan as proof; stdout and exit alone cannot prove no orphan. Note zero-match test runner may exit nonzero on some Node versions due skipped file; assert the documented current Node behavior after measuring a clean baseline, not a guessed exit convention. No edits until coord approves after mgbv lands.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY DESIGN while `xggy.3`'s merger gate runs. No file touched, no branch cut, no browser started — the merger owns the CPU and the design does not need one.

## What the guard does today, and why `h1oo` is right
`tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs`, the token loop: `m.tokenCount === TOKENS.length`, then for each name `assert.ok(m.values[name])` and `assert.match(m.values[name], /^light-dark\(/)`. So it proves **presence, count and shape**. It cannot distinguish the real pair from any other pair, which is why the reviewer's `--bad` swap to white passes all eleven assertions.

## The replacement: pin both the declared pair and the resolved value
Two arms, because they answer different questions.

**Arm 1 — declared, exact.** A literal table of the 11 pairs as they stood before the move, asserted with `assert.equal`, so a token that is renamed, dropped, reordered into another form, or revalued fails even if nothing on screen uses it:

    --ground   light-dark(#fbfbf9, #101014)     --btn-hover light-dark(#e0e4eb, #2d2d38)     --accent light-dark(#1f3fd0, #69f)
    --card     light-dark(#ffffff, #15151b)     --line      light-dark(#d8dcdf, #33333f)     --good   light-dark(#1d6b32, #8ee39a)
    --input-bg light-dark(#f7f8fa, #17171d)     --ink       light-dark(#23262b, #e8e8ee)     --bad    light-dark(#b3261e, #f0a6a0)
    --btn-bg   light-dark(#eceef2, #23232c)     --muted     light-dark(#59636d, #9a9aab)

**Arm 2 — resolved per scheme, which is what coord asked for.** Reading a custom property with `getPropertyValue` returns its declared text, not a resolved colour — `--muted` reads back as the literal `light-dark(...)`, which is exactly how a "computed" check on this page can be vacuous without anyone noticing. So the resolved value is obtained the only way it means anything: an off-screen probe element carrying `color: var(--<name>)`, read with `getComputedStyle(probe).color`. Each of the 11 is asserted against the rgb the scheme should resolve to — light and dark separately, so a pair that is swapped arm-for-arm fails, and so does a pair where both arms were changed together.

The expected rgb values are **measured from the pinned tip at implementation time and baked in**, not typed from memory. That is the same rule I broke twice with accessibility run directories, and in a test it is worse: a remembered colour is an assertion that silently encodes whatever the author guessed.

## The mutant, per the repo's practice
Change `--bad` to `light-dark(#ffffff, #ffffff)` in `public/environment.css` and require the strengthened guard to **fail** — on arm 1 immediately, and on arm 2 in whichever scheme resolves it. Then restore the file and verify `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` is unchanged, so a mutation experiment cannot leave the gated tree describing something else. This is the reviewer's own repro, not one I invented for the test.

## Deliberate side effect, stated in the test
The table pins values as of the move, so it **constrains future palette work on purpose**: changing a token becomes an explicit, reviewed act rather than something a relocation or a tidy-up can carry in unnoticed. The comment above it will say that instead of pretending to be neutral bookkeeping.

Product CSS and the palette are untouched — no token is changed, and `sv2n`'s placeholder contrast stays exactly where it is, neither fixed nor worsened by this.

## Sequencing
Branch off the new main **after** `xggy.3` lands: this edits the file that landing changes, and cutting a branch underneath a queued change would duplicate or conflict with its delta. Then the focused CSP suites plus the mutant, an exact-tree fast gate, and a cross-family reviewer for the guard alone.

title: Environment page placeholder contrast is below the craft floor: 4.34:1 light, 3.87:1 dark
description:
Found while measuring the read-only baseline for `voicebox-beads-xggy.3` (externalising the Environment page's inline stylesheet for CSP readiness).

The page's placeholder text fails the craft floor's contrast line — *"body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1"* — in **both** schemes:

- light: `#asset-name`'s placeholder against the input background = **4.34:1**
- dark: same pair = **3.87:1**

Everything else on the page is comfortably clear: body text 14.65:1 light and 15.56:1 dark, `--muted` on the ground 5.91:1 and 6.86:1. So this is one pair, not a palette-wide problem.

Why it is filed rather than fixed inside `xggy.3`: that bead is a **relocation** whose acceptance is "preserve the computed values", and the baseline it must reproduce includes this failing ratio. Raising the placeholder's contrast means changing `--muted` or the placeholder colour, which is a visible palette change — the opposite of that bead's promise, and a decision about the page's design rather than about CSP readiness.

Not caused by the externalisation, and not made worse by it. Fixing it would be: darken `--muted`/the placeholder toward `--ink` in each scheme until both pairs clear 4.5:1, then re-run the baseline for the rest of the page to confirm nothing else moved. Whether that rides along with `xggy.3` or lands separately is coord's call — including whether it is worth doing at all given the threshold is a floor and the shortfall is small in light mode.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY DESIGN for `sv2n`, produced while `xggy.3`'s merger gate runs. No CSS edited, no browser started, no file touched.

**The measurement changes the shape of the fix.** `environment.html` loads exactly one stylesheet, `/environment.css` (line 20); it does **not** load `public/style.css`. The two `::placeholder` rules in `style.css` (`.list-tools input::placeholder` and `.composer input::placeholder`, both `color: var(--muted)`) therefore never reach this page, and `#asset-name` gets the **user agent's** placeholder colour. That is where the 4.34:1 light / 3.87:1 dark measured earlier comes from — not from a token. So this is not "a token is a shade too dark", it is a control whose placeholder was never given a colour, and the fix is to give it one.

**The bar, from the two sources that actually state one.**
- craft floor, line 9: *"**Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray."* Placeholder text is named explicitly, and "never gray" matters here: the input sits on `--input-bg`, so the colour must be tinted from the palette rather than an arbitrary grey.
- Modern Web Guidance (`color`): *"**Minimum contrast standards**: Maintain 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text or icons."* It names low-contrast "muted secondary text" as exactly the case that needs attention.

`PRODUCT.md` states **no** contrast bar. I checked before citing it rather than quoting the nearest sentence that sounded like one. What it does state is the brand commitment to isocan's voice-agent visual language, which is an argument for using a palette value here instead of an invented grey.

**The smallest token-only lift: reuse `--muted`.** One declaration, no new colour, no value changed anywhere:

    #asset-name::placeholder { color: var(--muted); }

`--muted` on `--input-bg` measures **5.76:1 light** (`#59636d` on `#f7f8fa`) and **6.45:1 dark** (`#9a9aab` on `#17171d`), computed from the token values in `environment.css` and reproducible with the same arithmetic. It clears 4.5:1 in both schemes with margin, it is already the page's secondary-text colour, and it is a blue-grey tinted from the palette — which is what "never gray" asks for. `--muted`'s own value does not change, so body and muted text keep the contrast they have today.

**The alternative, and why I am not putting a number on it.** If a smaller visual change than "the page's muted secondary colour" is wanted, the option is an exact-floor token: the smallest change that still reaches 4.5:1 against `--input-bg` in each scheme. I am deliberately **not** proposing a value, because the size of a lift cannot be minimised without first measuring what the placeholder currently resolves to, and I have not measured that yet. Misremembering a colour is the same failure I have already made twice on this branch with accessibility run directories; a designed token is a defensible choice, a guessed hex is not.

**Evidence to gather in the bead.**
- *before*: read the resolved placeholder colour in both schemes and **recompute** the ratios — do not carry 4.34/3.87 forward on trust, they come from an earlier tip — plus a close-up of the `#asset-name` input. `/tmp/xggy3-before/environment-{light,dark}.png` already show this control from the `xggy.3` recon.
- *after*: the same two shots with the declaration in place, plus the ratio read from the page in each scheme.
- *a control*: recompute with the declaration removed, so the numbers must fall back to the UA values — otherwise the screenshots show a change nobody proved came from the rule.

**Scope:** one CSS declaration, no palette change, no change to `--muted`/`--ink`/`--good`/`--bad` values, no body or muted contrast moved, and no interaction with `xggy.3`, which is frozen. `sv2n` stays assigned to coord; this is the design it asked for, not a claim on the bead.

| light | `rgb(117, 117, 117)` = `#757575`, opacity 1 | `rgb(247, 248, 250)` = `#f7f8fa` | **4.34:1** |
| dark | `rgb(117, 117, 117)` = `#757575`, opacity 1 | `rgb(23, 23, 29)` = `#17171d` | **3.87:1** |

**The premise is confirmed, mechanically rather than by argument:** the probe enumerates `document.styleSheets` and looks for any author rule whose selector contains `::placeholder`. On this page it finds **none** — the two such rules live in `public/style.css`, which `environment.html` does not load. So the placeholder colour here is entirely the user agent's.

**The detail I did not predict: the UA uses the same grey in both schemes.** `#757575` light and dark — it does not adapt to the declared `color-scheme`. The dark scheme is worse only because the input's background is much darker, not because the placeholder is. That is useful for the fix: there is one colour to reason about, and any token used here is chosen for its ground in each scheme, which `light-dark()` already expresses.

**The ratios reproduce exactly** (4.34 / 3.87 — same as measured earlier, now from a separate probe on this tip rather than carried forward on trust), and opacity is 1, so the composited value is the `color` itself. The arithmetic also cross-checks against the well-known landmark that `#767676` on white sits right at 4.54:1.

**So the fix stands as designed and stays one declaration**, with no palette value changed:

    #asset-name::placeholder { color: var(--muted); }

`--muted` resolves to `#59636d` light / `#9a9aab` dark, measuring **5.76:1** and **6.45:1** against those same two grounds — clear of the 4.5 craft floor in both, and a palette-tinted blue-grey rather than the UA's neutral grey, which is what the craft floor's "never gray" on coloured surfaces asks for.

**Still to do in the bead, in coord's order:** the browser check that the computed ratio is ≥4.5 in both schemes after the declaration, the before/after screenshots, and the CSS-removal negative. **Implementation remains deferred** until both `xggy.3` and `h1oo` land, per coord, so this does not overlap the same stylesheet and test files. No guessed hex; no PRODUCT.md contrast claim (that file states no bar — the bar quoted is the craft floor's and Modern Web Guidance's).

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
CLAIMED. READ-ONLY reconnaissance while the `5tv3` union gate runs; no edits, no test runs, nothing that touches the worktree.

## Measured, on the tree as of `8f1c2f5`
- The inline stylesheet is `<style>` at line 17 through `</style>` at line 123: **8187 bytes, 107 lines, 80 rules**. Inside it: **0 media queries**, **11 `light-dark()` pairs**, **11 custom properties**, **2 `:focus` rules**, **12 `dialog`/`::backdrop` selectors**.
- Exactly **one** inline `style=` attribute in the whole document: line 233, `<input id="asset-name" … style="min-width:16rem">`. That is the pair of reports the policy currently records for this page (`style-src-elem` for the block, `style-src-attr` for the attribute), which is what "2 → 0" has to close.
- **No `setAttribute("style", …)` anywhere** in `ui.ts` or the public scripts, which matters: CSP's `style-src-attr` blocks the style *attribute* and `setAttribute`, but not CSSOM writes (`.style.width = …`). So nothing here needs to be reworked for the externalisation — the only markup-side style is the one attribute plus the one block.

## The two things the plan has to be careful about, both cascade-order rather than typing
1. **The inline attribute is the highest-precedence way to set `min-width`.** Moving it into a stylesheet lowers its precedence, so if any existing rule targets that input's `min-width`, the computed value would change. `getComputedStyle(input).minWidth` (16rem resolves to px) is the assertion that catches it, not a diff of the CSS text.
2. **A `<link>` is render-blocking exactly as the inline `<style>` is**, so no flash should appear — but this repo has first-paint tests (`theme-first-paint`, `help-theme-first-paint`) that were written precisely because that class of assumption went wrong before. They stay in scope as the check, rather than being assumed unaffected.

## Scope limits taken from the bead
Do not touch the external root-declaration script, the create-project opener, `ui.ts` handlers, the server's CSP constants, the mini-app bridge, or policy enforcement. The deliverable is only: the stylesheet becomes same-origin CSS, the `min-width` becomes a rule, the computed values stay identical, and the page's report count goes to zero — with a control proving the new file is load-bearing rather than decorative.

Plan with the mandatory Modern Web Guidance and Impeccable read follows `5tv3` landing, for approval before any edit.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
Mandatory guidance read BEFORE any CSS edit (read-only pass; plan still waits for `5tv3` landing as coord asked).

## Modern Web Guidance
- **`security`**: *"Enumerate inline scripts and styles in server-rendered templates and static HTML — these will need nonces, hashes, or refactoring."* That sentence is the licence for this bead: refactoring is the named alternative, and it is the line already cited in `docs/07` for the two earlier extractions. The guide's own CSP example also includes `frame-ancestors`, which coord has explicitly excluded from this work and which I am not adding.
- **`dark-mode`** (similarity 0.712 on this page's exact features) carries **two MANDATORY items**:
  1. *"To help prevent a 'flash of un-themed content' (FOUC), place a `<meta>` tag in your `<head>` to ensure the browser knows which themes you support before it even starts rendering"* — `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">`.
  2. *"Apply the `color-scheme` property to the `html` element or the `:root` pseudo-class."*

## What that means for this page, measured
- The second is already satisfied: the block opens with `:root { color-scheme: light dark; … }`, and the palette is 11 `light-dark()` pairs over 11 custom properties.
- **The first is NOT satisfied**: `environment.html` has no `color-scheme` meta — only `index.html` has one. Occurrences in the file: zero.
- And this change would make that gap matter more, not less. Today the scheme is declared by an inline `<style>` parsed at line 17, inside the head, so it is in force before the body paints. Replacing it with a `<link>` makes the stylesheet a **render-blocking fetch**: the document still does not paint until it arrives, but the window in which the browser has already decided the canvas and scrollbar scheme and has not yet applied `:root` gets wider, not narrower. In dark mode that is a light flash on a page that has no theme script at all — `environment.html` loads none, its theming is entirely `color-scheme` plus `light-dark()`.
- Nothing in the repo guards it: no first-paint test mentions `environment.html`, and no test asserts a `color-scheme` meta. The existing first-paint suite covers the room and `help.html` only, and `theme-first-paint.test.mjs` already contains the comment that a guard rewriting only the meta "would leave these on the old scheme at first paint" — so the repo has met this class of problem before and solved it per page.

## So the plan will put one question to coord rather than deciding it silently
Whether the `<meta name="color-scheme">` rides with this change as a **necessary companion** to the externalisation — it is a `<head>` addition, not a server, policy or mini-app change, and it is the mitigation the guidance makes mandatory — or is filed as its own bead. Either way the evidence for it is a first-paint probe in dark mode that I will run before and after, not an argument from the guide text alone.

## What the tests must assert, taken from the craft floor
The floor's "Read the computed values" and its browser-surfaces line (*"Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset"*) are what coord's "preserving exact computed values, focus/caret/selection" is protecting, and a relocation satisfies them by preservation rather than by redesign. So the checks are: the custom-property values themselves read back from `document.documentElement`, key computed properties on real elements including the input's `minWidth`, the `:focus-visible` outline, light and dark screenshots, and a control proving the new stylesheet is load-bearing — block it and the computed values must change.

A `<link>` is render-blocking exactly as the inline block was, which is what keeps first paint honest — and the widened pre-CSS window that creates is the one thing below that needs its own decision.
2. **The inline attribute becomes a rule.** `style="min-width:16rem"` on `#asset-name` (line 233) becomes `#asset-name { min-width: 16rem; }` in the new file. This is the only change with a real precedence risk: a style attribute outranks any stylesheet rule, so if something else already targets that input's `min-width` the computed value would silently change. I will confirm nothing does, and assert `getComputedStyle(input).minWidth` rather than diffing CSS text.
3. **No other file moves.** The external root-declaration script, the create-project opener, `ui.ts`, the server's CSP constants, the mini-app bridge and policy enforcement are all out of scope, per the bead.

## The one question I am putting to coord rather than deciding
`environment.html` declares `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` but has **no `<meta name="color-scheme">`**, while the Modern Web Guidance `dark-mode` guide makes that meta MANDATORY against FOUC and `index.html` already carries one. Today the scheme is in force before the body paints because the declaration sits in an inline head stylesheet; after this change it arrives in a render-blocking fetch, so the window in which the browser has chosen a canvas and scrollbar scheme without having applied `:root` gets **wider**. On this page that has no theme script to soften it — its theming is entirely `color-scheme` plus 11 `light-dark()` pairs. So: does the meta ride along as a necessary companion, or become its own bead? Either answer is fine; what I will not do is land a stylesheet move that quietly widens a dark-mode flash with no measurement of it.

## What the tests will assert, and the control that makes it worth reading
- **CSP reporting goes 2 → 0**: the `/environment.html` row in `tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs` moves to an empty list, and the page's persistent HTTP header keeps its parity check. The existing style-missing negative control stays.
- **Computed values, not text**: the 11 custom properties read back from `document.documentElement`, `body` background/colour/font, the input's `minWidth`, and the `:focus-visible` outline — in both schemes.
- **The control**: block `/environment.css` and require the computed values to CHANGE. Without it, a test asserting the palette would pass on a page whose stylesheet never loaded, which is the mistake this branch has already made twice in other forms.
- **Screenshots**: light and dark, plus a narrow viewport for the responsive composition and the dialog open.
- **A unit-lane structural guard**: `environment.html` must carry **zero** inline `<style>` blocks and **zero** `style=` attributes, so this cannot creep back — the same treatment the classic loader scripts already got.

## Gates
Focused while iterating, exact-tree fast, accessibility station once at the final tip with `--sink file`, then a cross-family reviewer. Docs and README in the same change: the "two remaining inline style blocks" sentence becomes "none", because that is what this bead is for.

FIRST-PAINT PROBE, run read-only (repo untouched; one browser, closed in a `finally`). One result is decisive, the other is confounded — and I am reporting the confounded one as confounded rather than dressing it up.

## A. `environment.html` today, inline stylesheet — DECISIVE
With the OS preference emulated dark, the recorder's **first rAF fired at t=42ms** and read `colorScheme: "light dark"` with `body` background **`rgb(16, 16, 20)`** — the dark `--ground`. Unchanged at +150ms, and settled. So **the page is correctly themed at its first painted frame today and there is no flash to fix.** That is the baseline the change must not regress.

## B. External render-blocking stylesheet held 500ms — CONFOUNDED, prove nothing
I modelled the `<link>` by holding the room's `/style.css` for 500ms on `index.html`. The first rAF moved to **t=545ms**, so the hold did delay rendering — but both frames read `colorScheme: "light"`, and so did the settled state. The reason is fatal to the comparison: `style.css` contains `:root[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light; }`, so under the boot's `data-theme="light"` the settled value is `light` — **the same as the initial value before any CSS applies.** The run therefore cannot tell "the stylesheet had applied" from "it had not", and a test whose two states read identically is not evidence.

**I overreached in my previous message to coord.** I wrote that replacing the inline block with a `<link>` "widens the window where the browser has chosen a canvas and scrollbar scheme without having applied `:root`". The probe does not establish that. What it establishes is narrower: holding an external stylesheet delays the first frame (t=42ms → t=545ms), which is real, and the question of whether a frame gets **painted** unthemed in that window remains **unmeasured** on this page.

## So the plan's question is reframed honestly
The `<meta name="color-scheme">` case now rests on the guidance alone — the `dark-mode` guide calls it MANDATORY against FOUC and this page lacks it while `index.html` carries one — and **not** on a flash I have failed to measure. Two consequences for the work:
1. The change is built **with** the meta, since the guidance requires it and it can only help.
2. The flash question gets measured properly **as part of the change**, where the Environment page really does have an external stylesheet: the same probe, before and after, plus the variant with the meta removed so its necessity is demonstrated rather than assumed. If the numbers say the meta changes nothing, I will say so and let coord decide on the guidance alone.

The baseline in A is the regression check either way: first painted frame themed, `light dark`, dark ground.

comments.text:
**The merger's full gate failed on the union, and the failure is mine.** `tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs:24-:26` asserted the Environment page's **inline** stylesheet by reading `environment.html`. This change moves that block to `public/environment.css`, so those three assertions were looking for rules in a file that no longer holds them.

**Why my gates did not catch it, stated plainly:** `fleet-check --fast` runs the unit lane, and this file lives in the **browser tier** (confirmed by reproducing the failure through `tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs` in 5.8s). Nothing I ran could have failed. But the tier is not the whole mistake — the mistake is that I searched for tests touching the environment page only in terms of its **report count**, and never searched the test tree for assertions on the **text I was moving**. A block that moves takes every assertion about it with it, and I checked the ones I happened to think of.

**The fix, `0c16648`:** the three assertions now read `public/environment.css`, in the same idiom this file already uses for `changelog.css`. The invariants are **kept, not relaxed** — a real focus ring and the 12px tag floor are asserted exactly as before. Relaxing them is precisely what a red assertion like this invites, and that is the class of defect this branch has produced five times.

**Evidence:**
- `node --test tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs` — **2 of 2 pass**, including the browser half, so the external stylesheet genuinely still delivers the ring and the floor rather than the assertion merely being satisfied by file text.
- **Non-vacuous:** removing `outline: 2px solid` from `environment.css` fails **both** halves — 0 pass / 2 fail — and the file was restored byte-identically (blob `665f589b`), so the experiment left nothing behind.
- **Exhaustive dependent search**, because an incomplete search is the actual defect here: four files reference those selectors or tokens and I inspected each rather than assuming. `pip-window-styling` reads the pip window's own document; `theme-tokens` expects `--ground` dark `#0b0f19`, which is `style.css`, not this page's `#101014`; the other two are mine.

**The lesson, worth carrying past this bead:** when you move a block, grep the **entire** test tree for the text you moved — selectors, custom properties, and any presumption that a file contains a `<style>` — and remember that `--fast` is the unit lane, so an assertion in the browser tier cannot fail in it no matter how many times you run it.

**Sequence:** the merger removed the `merge-queue` label, so I re-add it myself once `rev-xggy3c`'s verdict is in and the fast gate for `0c16648` lands. Fresh reviewer is `zai/glm-5.3` — a third family — briefed to hunt for any *other* test that depended on the moved block, since that is the miss being reviewed.

comments.text:
`voicebox-beads-r3xp` FIXED at `8f1c2f5` on `fleet/shard-5tv3`. The finding was right, and it was right about a mechanism I had asserted rather than measured.

## Reproduced before touching anything
I ran the reviewer's mutation myself rather than accepting it: on the real tree one owner gives `{open: true, errors: []}`; with the deleted second binding restored it gives **`{open: true, errors: []}`** — identical. And asked directly, `showModal()` on an already-open dialog returns **`no-throw`** in this Chromium. So the claim was false: it is a silent no-op, not `InvalidStateError`. My one-owner test's "raises no uncaught error" assertion therefore proved nothing about ownership — it was green with two owners.

## The worse part, recorded because it is the real lesson
That platform claim was not only in the test. It was in `browser/ui/ui.ts`, in `public/environment-dialogs.js`, and in what I told coord — all written from my recollection of the spec rather than from the page in front of me, and two of those comments are exactly what a future reader consults before deciding whether one owner is still required. All three now state the measured behaviour, and the reason for one owner is stated as what it actually is: a duplicate produces a **second pass of the opener** — second status reset, second panel sync, second open — not a crash.

## The fix
`HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal` is instrumented at document-start, before any page script runs, and each activation must invoke it **exactly once**. That is the ownership property itself rather than a proxy for it.

## Two controls, because a count is worthless if it counts nothing
1. **In-test mutant**: restore the second binding in the live page and require the count to move to two — and require it to raise nothing while doing so, which is the behaviour that was previously invisible.
2. **Product mutant**, which is the one that matters: with `ui.ts` temporarily binding `#create-project` again, the test that is green on the clean tree fails with **`Got [2,2,2]`**. So the assertion detects the exact regression the finding describes.

Restores were verified by checksum, not by eye.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY DESIGN for xggy.2 — no files edited, no branch, no commit. Worktree clean at `2e88a4c`, which stays frozen for the `xggy.1` merger gate. I am reporting this for approval rather than starting, as coord required.

## Scope as I understand it
Extract ONLY the 51-line / 2304 B inline root-declaration script from `public/environment.html` to a same-origin file. The inline `<style>` (8164 B / 105 lines) and the `style="min-width:16rem"` on `#asset-name` stay, for a later CSS slice. No `server.mjs`, no CSP enforcement, no mini-app-bridge changes. The header needs no change at all: the allowlist is keyed on the RESOLVED FILE, so `environment.html` carries its Report-Only header whether its script is inline or external — the same property that made `xggy.1` need no server change.

## The load strategy is the whole design, and defer is wrong here
For the Help search filter I fixed a lost interaction by applying the value ALREADY in the box when the script attached. **That fix does not generalise.** A click leaves no state behind to re-apply, so a `click` on `#declare-root` that lands before the file attaches is **permanently lost** — and the handler here is only a click listener.

**Recommendation: a classic, non-deferred `<script src="/environment-root.js">` as the last thing in `<body>`.** It runs during parsing, when the document is not yet interactive, so **no user click can precede the listener** — behaviourally identical to the inline block it replaces, which also ran during parsing. Its cost is one small same-origin fetch that blocks the parser, and the inline original blocked that same parser for the same work, so it is cost-neutral in kind. The acceptance encodes this (below) so that anyone who later adds `defer` fails the suite rather than quietly reintroducing the window.

Consequence to preserve: the script reads four elements with `getElementById` at evaluation time, so the tag must stay at the END of the body, after them. A `<head>` or top-of-body placement would return nulls and `addEventListener` would throw.

## Report-Only expectation: 3 -> 2, and the alias signal stays non-vacuous
Removing the inline script removes the `script-src-elem` report, so `environment.html` should report exactly `["style-src-attr","style-src-elem"]` — the inline `<style>` and the `style=` attribute. Because the browser test derives the alias loop's expectation from that table rather than retyping it, the expectation follows automatically. The positive signal stays **non-vacuous** at 2 (Help, the room, changelog and harnesses all stay at 0, so Environment remains the only allowlisted page that discriminates), and the durable HTTP header assertion is unchanged — it is about the header, not the reports.

## Acceptance, built on measured vocabulary rather than invented text
I drove the real flow in a real browser (read-only) and measured all four server refusals passing through the page unchanged:

| case | result shown by the page |
|---|---|
| no token, any path | `host-token-required: declaring the project root is the host's act — it re-points every file route — and this route requires the host token (x-voicebox-host-token); the page cannot hold it, and the server cannot act on a page-owned root either way` |
| `server.hostToken`, missing path | `path-missing: '/nonexistent-xyzzy-abc' does not exist on this machine` |
| `server.hostToken`, a plain file | `not-a-directory: '<path>' is a file; a project root is a folder` |
| `server.hostToken`, a real folder | `declared: <path> — the loop writes here now.` and `GET /api/root` confirms the root actually moved |

So the acceptance asserts the SERVER's text verbatim (the vocabulary is the requirement), drives the token-authorized success path last so it is the only case that mutates the fixture, and keeps the no-token refusal as its own case — which is the honest shape, because the page legitimately cannot hold the token.

Readiness, deterministically: hold the file at the request stage and assert the document has **not** become interactive, then resume and drive the flow — the assertion that fails if anyone adds `defer`. Plus the blocked-script mutant (file blocked => clicking Declare leaves `#declare-result` hidden, so the assertions cannot pass on a page whose script never ran), and the 3 -> 2 report matrix with the header. The unit-lane structural assertion that the extracted documents carry no inline script extends to name `environment.html` as the remaining inline-STYLE document. Docs and README updated in the same change, the enforcement worklist going three -> two.

## A measured, pre-existing defect I am NOT bundling: voicebox-beads-5tv3
`public/environment.html:260` loads `type="module" src="/browser/ui/ui.ts"`, and `browser/ui/ui.ts:729` is what opens this dialog. A module is deferred by definition, so the page's PRIMARY button ("Create a project") is inert for a window with no feedback:

```
click while module held : {"ready":"interactive","open":false}
after module loaded     : {"open":false} -> the earlier click was LOST
a second click now      : {"open":true}  -> the module IS attached, so only the first click was missed
```

It is pre-existing (ui.ts last changed 2026-10-08, before any of this work) and it is the same class as `aenb` but NOT fixable the way `aenb` was. It belongs to a different seam from `xggy.2` — a classic opener script, or the declarative Invoker Commands path Modern Web Guidance recommends for exactly this property ("ensures interactions are functional immediately upon HTML parsing"), which is Baseline Newly available and so carries a polyfill obligation. Filed as its own bead with the measurement; touching ui.ts is explicitly out of scope here.

## What I need
Approval to implement, and confirmation on the one judgement call: **classic non-deferred end-of-body** rather than `defer`, on the grounds that a lost click is unrecoverable and that the classic form reproduces the inline original's timing exactly.
