APPROVED by coord, conditionally on `xggy.1` landing: classic NON-deferred end-of-body external script, the held-file CDP test asserting the document is not interactive before the listener exists (with a `defer` mutant that is RED), the server refusal vocabulary preserved exactly with a successful `GET /api/root` verified, Environment reporting 3 -> 2 style-only with the alias signal still non-vacuous and the HTTP proof unchanged. The inline style/width slice and the pre-existing P2 `5tv3` stay separate. No source edits until `xggy.1` lands.

## The design's central claim is now MEASURED, not asserted
This design rests on "a classic end-of-body script is timing-identical to the inline block it replaces". Read-only probe against the current page, clicking at the exact instant the document leaves `loading`:

```
inline baseline: {"readyStateWhenClicked":"interactive"} -> result: "host-token-required: declaring the proje"
```

So today the handler **does** exist by the time the document is interactive — the click is handled and the server's refusal comes back. That is the property the extraction must preserve, it is what the held-file assertion in the acceptance encodes (the document must not become interactive while the file is held), and it is why the `defer` mutant has to be RED: `defer` would let the document reach `interactive` with no listener, which is exactly the window `aenb` exposed on the Help page and which a click cannot recover from.

## What changed
- `public/environment-root.js` (new): the inline root-declaration script, semantically identical — I verified this by stripping comments and blank lines from both the old inline block and the new file and diffing: the ONLY remaining differences are the `<script>` tags themselves. The extra header explains why the file is not deferred.
- `public/environment.html`: the inline block is replaced by `<script src="/environment-root.js"></script>` plus a comment carrying the same reasoning, at the same end-of-body position.
- No `server.mjs` change: the allowlist keys on the RESOLVED FILE, so the document carries its Report-Only header whether its script is inline or external.
- `tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs`: the report matrix row for `environment.html` is now the two style reports, with the alias signal explicitly still non-vacuous because this is the last page that reports anything; plus the new readiness acceptance and the blocked-script mutant.

## The load strategy, which is the substance of the change
Classic parser-blocking end-of-body script, per coord's approval. A click leaves no state to re-apply, so the `aenb` fix does not generalise: `defer` would let the document reach `interactive` with no listener, and the click would be lost permanently with a button that silently does nothing.

## Evidence, all measured rather than asserted
- **Semantic identity** of the extracted script (comment/blank-stripped diff, only the tags differ).
- **Focused:** `tests/csp-report-only.test.mjs` + `tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs` — **8/8 green**, including the report matrix now reading two style-only violations.
- **The `defer` mutant is RED in BOTH guards**, deliberately applied and then reverted:
  - unit-lane structural guard: `the declaration script must stay CLASSIC and parser-blocking — defer, async or type="module" all attach the listener after the document is already interactive… Got <script src="/environment-root.js" defer>`
  - browser control: `the declaration script, held by nothing, must already have attached its listener while the deferred module is still in flight`
- **The readiness test discriminates rather than asserting what it wants:** holding `/browser/ui/ui.ts` (a `type="module"`, deferred by definition) leaves the document `interactive` and the declaration script's listener attached; holding `/environment-root.js` itself leaves the document `loading` and no listener — so a click at that moment is measurably dropped, with `#declare-result` still hidden.
- **The refusal vocabulary is compared to the SEAM, not to typed text:** for the same body, the page's text must equal `refused: why`. `host-token-required` with no token, then `path-missing` and `not-a-directory` with the fixture's own token, then a real folder declared successfully with `GET /api/root` confirming the root actually moved. My first version of this test was wrong in exactly this area — `declared()` defaulted the token to empty while `fromServer()` defaulted to the fixture's — and the fix is recorded in the file, because "one fact, one place" is the same lesson the alias expectation already carries.
- **Blocked-script mutant:** with `/environment-root.js` blocked the page renders the control and declares nothing, so the assertions above are driven by that file.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY INSPECTION + ACCEPTANCE PROPOSAL. No source file was edited for this; the worktree is untouched. Nothing below is applied yet — it is the proposal the bead asked for, plus findings from the inspection that change what the change has to include.

## 1. What the inline block actually is (measured, not assumed)

    public/help.html — exactly ONE inline script, 642 bytes, 14 lines, one IIFE at the end of <body>:
      const search = document.querySelector(".help-search-input");
      const sections = document.querySelectorAll(".help-section[data-help-section]");   // 8 sections
      search?.addEventListener("input", () => { ... sec.hidden = Boolean(q) && !text.includes(q) });
      plus a prose comment recording that the theme copy used to live here and left in voicebox-beads-uj16.

It imports nothing, holds no state, touches no theme value, and reads no storage key. That is why this is a genuinely small change: the whole filter is `query → hide the sections whose text lacks it`, and `q` empty means show everything.

**Measured consequence for the policy baseline:** this block is the ONLY report `/help.html` produces today (1 report, `script-src-elem`, inline). It has no inline `<style>` and no inline `style=` attribute, so **after extraction `/help.html` reports 0**, i.e. clean under the staged policy without any enforcement.

## 2. THE COUPLING THAT MATTERS MOST — extracting this turns a coverage test vacuous

This is the finding I would want a reviewer to check hardest, and it is not visible from the bead text:

`tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs` asserts the report set per document, and `["script-src-elem"]` for `/help.html` is asserted in TWO places — the per-document table, and the ALIAS loop added by voicebox-beads-onvu which asserts every alias spelling produces the *same* report as the canonical one. Once the inline script is gone, `/help.html` reports `[]`, and **a document that reports nothing cannot distinguish "covered and clean" from "not covered at all"** — both are the empty list, so the alias assertion would pass even if the header disappeared entirely.

Fix, in the same change:
- update the `/help.html` expectation from `["script-src-elem"]` to `[]`;
- **re-point the browser alias-coverage signal at `/environment.html`**, which still reports 3 and therefore still distinguishes covered from uncovered;
- note that the durable alias coverage is `tests/csp-report-only.test.mjs` (server lane), which asserts the header itself over HTTP on every alias spelling and is unaffected by this change. That is the test that proves coverage; the browser one should not be the only witness and must not be a vacuous one.

Also in the same change, because they name the worklist this shrinks: `docs/07` and the README say enforcement needs **four** inline blocks; after this it is **three** (the two in `environment.html`, being the root script plus its inline `<style>` and its inline `style=` attribute).

## 3. SEQUENCING — this should branch after ul1m.1 lands

1. Its policy-baseline acceptance ("`/help.html` reports 0") can only be measured once the Report-Only header is on `main`.
2. It has to edit `tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs`, which ul1m.1 introduces (currently frozen at `e9b3f71` and handed to the merger).
3. It needs **no `server.mjs` edit at all**, which is a small vindication of ul1m.1's design: the allowlist is keyed on the RESOLVED FILE, so `help.html` stays covered whether its script is inline or external.

## 4. ACCEPTANCE PROPOSAL (real browser, real server)

1. **Empty** — cleared or empty query shows ALL 8 sections.
2. **No-match** — a nonsense query hides ALL 8.
3. **Partial match** — a term present in some sections leaves at least one visible AND at least one hidden, so the filter is neither a no-op nor a hide-everything.
4. **Transitions in ONE run** — empty -> partial -> no-match -> partial -> empty, asserting the visible count at each step. This is what "transitions" has to mean: reversible and idempotent, not three independent snapshots.
5. **Non-vacuous control** — the same drive must FAIL when the external script is pointed at a missing file, proving the assertions are driven by the script rather than by the initial DOM.
6. **Policy baseline** — `/help.html` reports **0** violations (was 1), measured in the same run.
7. **Structural** — `public/help.html` contains no inline `<script>` (every script tag carries `src`); the new file is same-origin and served with a JavaScript content type; no `'unsafe-inline'` and no enforcing policy header anywhere.
8. **Theme preserved** — the guard and module tags stay byte-identical and the existing first-paint and token suites stay green.

On `defer` versus `type="module"`: both defer execution until after parsing, so no user interaction can observe a difference — a listener attached before any keystroke is the same listener. I would use a classic `defer` script for a filter with no imports, and keep the guard exactly as it is (classic, in `<head>`, not deferred). The prose comment inside the block should move to the new file's header rather than be dropped, so the uj16 history is not silently lost from the page's own commentary.

## 5. Two boundaries I am NOT crossing, and one finding to record

- **No server.mjs or bridge edit**, per the bead. Not needed anyway (§3.3).
- **The selector stays as it is.** The inline code is document-wide (`.help-search-input`), and `help.html` has exactly one such input, so tightening it is a separate question that would mix two changes.
- **Duplication, recorded rather than fixed:** `public/fused.js:6661` implements the SAME filter for the popover's help center (`#help-search-input`, 6 sections vs the page's 8, same empty/else semantics). After this extraction there will still be two copies of one behaviour. It is out of scope here (the bead says ONLY the inline script) and it would not have been caught by `scripts/single-owner.mjs`, which governs declared facts rather than duplicated logic — but it is the natural next step if a single Help-search owner is ever wanted.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
BASELINE MEASURED BEFORE WRITING ANY TEST, and it corrects a number in my own proposal above. Still read-only; no source file touched.

**Correction: the page has 7 help sections, not 8.** I said 8 in the proposal from `grep -c "data-help-section"`, which counts matching LINES, not elements. The DOM is authoritative and it says 7. Recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because a test written against "all 8" would have failed on the first run and looked like a defect in the extraction.

Measured on the CURRENT page, real browser, driving the real inline filter:

    total sections                      7
    visible before any query            7      (none hidden initially)
    query "voice"                       6      (a partial match: >=1 visible, >=1 hidden)
    query "zzz-nothing-matches-this"    0
    query cleared                       7
    "voice" again, then cleared again   6, then 7   (reversible and idempotent)

Three consequences for the acceptance, so the tests assert the right thing:

1. **"All sections visible" must be stated as "equal to the count before the query", not "equal to the total".** They happen to coincide here (7 and 7), but a page may legitimately ship an initially hidden section, and the invariant worth pinning is that CLEARING restores what was there — the same reasoning as asserting the painted ground rather than assuming it.
2. **The partial-match assertion should be `1 <= visible < 7`, not a hardcoded number.** The probe picked its term by frequency and got the MOST common word by accident, which is why "voice" hides only one of seven. A test that hardcodes 6 would be pinned to a corpus detail rather than to the filter's behaviour; choosing the term by measurement and asserting the range is the honest form.
3. **The transition sequence is already reversible and idempotent** — partial -> no-match -> partial -> clear returned 6, 0, 6, 7 — so the extraction must reproduce that exactly, and the sequence is a legitimate acceptance check rather than a new property being demanded of it.

This baseline is what the externalized version has to match. It is also the evidence that the acceptance is about behaviour, not about the DOM's initial state: the same drive must fail when the external script is missing.

IMPLEMENTED on `fleet/shard-xggy1` @ `e391a22` (cut from main `539c8b1`). IN_REVIEW; not on the merge queue until the reviewer's verdict at this tip.

## What changed
`public/help.html`'s one remaining inline script — the search filter, 642 bytes — becomes `public/help-search.js`, loaded with `<script src="/help-search.js" defer>`. The statements move verbatim and the comment explaining why there is no theme code in the filter moves with them. **No `server.mjs` change:** the Report-Only allowlist keys on the RESOLVED FILE, so `help.html` stays covered whether its script is inline or external. That is the design decision from `ul1m.1` paying off, and it is why this bead needed no server edit.

## Verification
- **Focused: 6/6** across `tests/csp-report-only.test.mjs`, `tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs`, `tests/help-theme-first-paint.test.mjs`. Exact-tree fast gate for `e391a22` in flight; `docs-check: OK — 766 path claims`.
- **Baseline measured BEFORE the move**, which is what the acceptance asserts: 7 sections, 7 visible with no query, 6 for `voice`, 0 for a query nothing matches, 7 when cleared. The test derives the baseline from the page and picks its partial-match term by measurement, so a content change cannot silently break it.
- **Mutant:** with `/help-search.js` blocked the filter must stop working and every section must stay visible. Without it, "all sections visible" would also pass on a page whose filter never ran at all — the mutant is what makes the main assertions mean something.
- **Theme preserved:** the classic in-head guard and the module are untouched and the first-paint suite is green. Accessibility station running ONCE with `--sink file` for this branch.

## Two couplings the bead did not predict, found because the suite went red
1. **The alias-coverage signal had to move.** `/help.html` reports ZERO now, and a document that reports nothing cannot distinguish "covered and clean" from "uncovered" — both are the empty list. The browser alias loop is therefore pinned to `/environment.html`, which still carries inline blocks and still discriminates; the durable spelling-coverage proof stays the HTTP header assertion in the server-lane test. The expectation is now DERIVED from that page's own entry in the table instead of retyped, which is how it first went red: I wrote `script-src-attr` where the page reports `style-src-attr`.
2. **`help-theme-first-paint`'s pre-`uj16` control had to be re-anchored.** It rebuilt the old markup by splicing the theme copy into the body-end IIFE; that block is a file now. It anchors on `</body>` and wraps the copy in its own classic `<script>` — the POSITION is what that control is about, never the script that happened to share it. Getting it wrong produced "dark at nullms": a page where the choice was never applied, asserted as though the old copy had been reinstated. Worth noting as a real risk: that failure mode would have looked like a *passing* control had the assertion been weaker.

## Skills consulted before touching client JS
`modern-web-guidance` (`security` guide) — its section 2.1 says inline scripts "will need nonces, hashes, or refactoring", so refactoring is the guide's own sanctioned path and the one taken here rather than hashing. It also surfaced two gaps that belong to enforcement, filed on the ADR `voicebox-beads-28sc` rather than acted on here: our report-only has **no** `Reporting-Endpoints`, so the guide's "run report-only over real traffic for days to weeks" phase cannot happen; and `'report-sample'` is recommended for `script-src` but would break the character-for-character parity with `index.html`'s meta that this policy is required to keep. `impeccable` — the launcher is absent on this VM, so per the skill's own rule I read `reference/craft-floor.md` directly; the change is styling-neutral, which is why "browser surfaces" (Help's focus ring, caret) means *do not regress* and the theme/style tags stay untouched.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: `public/help.html`'s search filter moves to `public/help-search.js`, loaded with `<script src="/help-search.js" defer>`. The filter logic is unchanged; the comment recording why no theme code lives in it moves with it.
WHAT: The acceptance derives its baseline from the page rather than hardcoding one (7 sections, 6 visible for `voice`, 0 for a query nothing matches, back to 7 when cleared) and covers the accepted sequence empty → partial → no-match → partial → clear, including idempotence and reversibility.
WHAT: A mutant blocks `/help-search.js` and requires the filter to STOP working, so the assertions above cannot pass on a page whose filter never ran; plus a structural assertion that the extracted documents carry no inline script and that `environment.html` is the one that still does.
WHAT: Two coupled test changes — the browser alias-coverage signal moves to `/environment.html` (with its expectation derived from the table) because a zero-report document cannot distinguish covered from uncovered, and the pre-`uj16` theme control anchors on `</body>`. Docs updated in the same change: the inline-block worklist goes from four to three.
WHY: An inline script is the one thing `script-src 'self'` would block, so Help was the last allowlisted page reporting a violation under the staged policy. This is the refactoring option rather than nonces or hashes, which is what the Modern Web Guidance security guide prescribes for inline scripts.
EFFECT: None user-visible — searching behaves exactly as before, and the page loads one same-origin file instead of an inline block. The Help page now reports no staged-policy violations, so the eventual enforcement worklist is three blocks, all in `environment.html`.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
STAGE 1 DESIGN — READ-ONLY. No code, config or repository file was edited for this. Parent `voicebox-beads-ul1m`, ADR `voicebox-beads-28sc`, related `voicebox-beads-xggy`. Cited grounding: PRODUCT.md:23 — "Browser first, with OPFS; a local safe environment and hosted environments follow. Server access and trust remain open questions." A report-only staging step is the cheap way to answer part of the trust question with measurements rather than assertion.

## 1. Route ownership — where a header can actually be attached
Two, and only two, write points serve HTML documents today:

1. **The room, by explicit route.** `"GET /"` reads `public/index.html`, injects into it, and writes it (`server.mjs:4258` onward); `"GET /index.html"` delegates to the same handler (`server.mjs:4263`). The response is built by hand, so a header here is a `res.setHeader` before the existing `writeHead`.
2. **Everything else, by ONE catch-all.** `server.mjs:4347` — `if (req.method === "GET" && !routes[key] && !url.pathname.startsWith("/api/"))` → `resolvePublicFile(url.pathname)` → served with `MIME_TYPES[path.extname(file)]` (`server.mjs:4349-4364`, MIME table at `:2156`). Every HTML document that is not the room is served here: there is no per-page route to hang a policy on, and adding one would be a routing change this bead must not make.

So the seam is **two `setHeader` calls and one shared helper**, not a middleware layer. That matters for the bounded plan in §6.

## 2. The exact allowlist
Trusted top-level documents this repository authors and serves: six paths, matched literally.

| path | why it is on the list |
|---|---|
| `/` | the room; `index.html` already enforces a meta policy, so this mirrors it rather than adding one |
| `/index.html` | same document by its other name |
| `/help.html` | ours, static, one inline script today |
| `/changelog.html` | ours, static, no inline scripts |
| `/environment.html` | ours, static, reached from the room ("Open the environment page", `public/fused.js:1456`) |
| `/harnesses.html` | ours, static, no inline scripts |

**Excluded, deliberately and with reasons rather than by omission:**
- `/apps/*.html` (`agent-monitor`, `landing-inspector`, `live-vision-studio`) — mini-app surfaces, each carrying its own inline script; they are where third-party-shaped content is rendered, and constraining them is not this change's business.
- `/mini-app-bridge.html` — the iframe host. **A policy on the bridge would reach content that is not ours:** `public/mini-app-bridge.js:1034` and `:1053` write user HTML into a `srcdoc` frame, and a `srcdoc` document INHERITS its parent's policy. That is spec behaviour, and it is a claim Stage 2 must verify with a real mini-app before any policy is put near the bridge — I am flagging it rather than asserting it as measured, because I did not drive a mini-app in Stage 1.
- Every non-HTML asset: `/fused.js`, `/style.css`, fonts, `/sw.js`. A CSP header on a script or stylesheet response is meaningless and misleading.
- Any route under `/api/`.

## 3. The proposed policy, verbatim
```
Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'
```
It is a **mirror of the meta policy `index.html` already enforces**, which is why it is safe to stage: where a meta already enforces the same thing, the report-only mirror can only report what the enforcer would have blocked. No `report-uri`, no `report-to` — there is no endpoint, by design. No `'unsafe-inline'` anywhere.

## 4. Evidence — measured, in a real browser
Prototype: a local server serving the real `public/` with the header on allowlisted paths only (`/tmp/csp-proto.mjs`), and a proxy in front of the REAL app so functionality could be driven with the header present (`/tmp/csp-func.mjs`). Violations captured with the `securitypolicyviolation` event, the only local capture available without an endpoint.

Reports per document (every one carries `disposition=report`, i.e. nothing was enforced):

    /                      header=YES  reports=0
    /help.html             header=YES  reports=1   script-src-elem   blockedURI=inline
    /changelog.html        header=YES  reports=0
    /environment.html      header=YES  reports=3   style-src-elem, style-src-attr, script-src-elem (all inline)
    /harnesses.html        header=YES  reports=0
    /apps/agent-monitor.html    header=no  reports=0
    /apps/landing-inspector.html header=no reports=0
    /mini-app-bridge.html       header=no  reports=0

Two things that table says, and I would not have believed either without measuring:
- **The room reports ZERO.** The mirror policy is exactly what the meta already permits, so staging it adds no noise on the busiest document. If that number is ever non-zero, it is a finding about the META, not about the header.
- Chromium reports the GRANULAR directive (`script-src-elem`, `style-src-elem`, `style-src-attr`), not the bare `script-src`/`style-src` the policy text names. Any test asserting this must use the granular names or it will pass vacuously.

Functional checks under the header, against the real app through the proxy:

    room /              reports=0   loads normally (title: Voicebox)
    help.html           reports=1   search filter: 7 visible -> 7/7 hidden after typing a nonsense query
    environment.html    reports=3   root control: dialog open false -> true, 3 destinations offered

`help.html` is the decisive line: the inline script is **reported and still executes**, in the same load. That is report-only demonstrated rather than asserted — and it is why `environment.html`'s root-declaration control keeps working while it reports three violations.

## 5. What the expected reports tell us (the point of Stage 1)
The four inline blocks this policy would block if it were ever enforced:
- `help.html` — the help-search script (1)
- `environment.html` — the project-root script, an inline `<style>` block, and one inline `style=` attribute (3)

So enforcement is not one change, it is those four blocks being extracted or hashed, per `voicebox-beads-xggy`. Staging report-only first is what makes that list exact instead of guessed.

## 6. The bounded plan for approval (Stage 2 — nothing done yet)
1. `server.mjs`: one helper (`isCspReportOnlyPath(pathname)`) holding the six-path allowlist verbatim, plus `res.setHeader("Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only", …)` at the two write points in §1. No new route, no middleware, no change to the meta, no policy on assets or `/api/`.
2. Tests, all new and all on the final tree:
   - header presence/absence over the exact allowlist and the exact exclusions (a new page must be added to the list on purpose, not accidentally covered);
   - violation capture asserting the exact expected set per document, using the GRANULAR directive names from §4 — so a newly added inline script fails the suite rather than quietly joining the reports;
   - the functional pair from §4 (search filter; root-declaration dialog) run with the header present, so "report-only does not block" is a regression test and not a claim.
3. Docs in the same change: `docs/07` (the trust/headers section) and the ADR `28sc` status; `docs-check`.
4. Non-goals, stated so they cannot creep in: no enforcement, no report endpoint, no `'unsafe-inline'`, no `frame-ancestors` or any other new directive, no coverage of `/apps` or the bridge, no change to `index.html`'s meta.

## 7. Open questions for coord (I have a recommendation on each)
- **Include the three pages I found** (`changelog`, `environment`, `harnesses`)? They are ours, static, and they report 0 or 3. Recommend INCLUDE: the reports are the point, and leaving them out means they are covered by nothing.
- **Add `frame-ancestors`** (absent from the meta)? That is new policy rather than a mirror. Recommend NO for Stage 1; it belongs in the ADR's own scope.
- **The bridge/srcdoc inheritance claim** in §2 is spec behaviour I did not measure. Recommend Stage 2 verify it with a real mini-app before anyone extends a policy toward `/mini-app-bridge.html`.

REVIEWER-FOUND DEFECT, FIX PREPARED AND VERIFIED — held UNCOMMITTED so the tip stays frozen at `0b6e864` until the reviewer's P2 finding lands, then committed at a new tip with a fresh fast gate and a fresh review delta.

**The defect, independently confirmed by me and wider than the reported case.** Keyed on the raw `url.pathname`, the allowlist was bypassable because `resolvePublicFile` decodes percent-escapes and `path.resolve` normalises, so several spellings reach the same document:

    /help.html      200  header=YES  (allowlisted spelling)
    /%68elp.html    200  header=no   SAME Help bytes   <-- the reviewer's case
    /help%2Ehtml    200  header=no   SAME Help bytes
    /help.html/     200  header=no   SAME Help bytes   <-- needs NO encoding to type
    /./help.html    200  header=YES  (WHATWG normalises dot segments)
    /x/../help.html 200  header=YES  (same)

So the class is exactly "encodings and trailing slashes", and containment was never broken: `/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd`, `/../server.mjs` and `/HELP.HTML` all 404.

**The fix: decide on the FILE being served, not on how the client spelled the URL.** `canonicalPublicPath(file)` reduces the resolver's already-contained, already-realpath'd file to its public path, and `cspReportOnlyHeaders(file)` tests that. Every alias collapses to one string BY CONSTRUCTION, which is stronger than patching the comparison with `decodeURIComponent` — that would have fixed these three and left the next alias live. Knock-on: `/` canonicalises to `/index.html`, so the set drops the now-unreachable `"/"` entry and the room is covered as its own file (the test still asserts the room under both spellings).

**Verified after the fix** — bypass surface none:

    /%68elp.html  /help%2Ehtml  /help.html/  /./help.html  /x/../help.html   all 200 header=YES, same bytes
    /%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd  /../server.mjs  /HELP.HTML                 404, no header
    /apps/*  /mini-app-bridge.html  assets  /api                            no header

Negative controls on both sides, per coord: the aliases are asserted POSITIVE (header present AND byte-identical to the canonical spelling, because same bytes is what makes it the same document), and traversal, case-mismatch and a newly-created probe document are asserted NEGATIVE, so "covered everywhere" cannot be satisfied by covering everything. No blanket MIME policy: still a list of documents, not a content-type rule.

Tests updated on both lanes: `tests/csp-report-only.test.mjs` (the alias matrix plus traversal/mismatch negative controls) and `tests/csp-report-only-browser.test.mjs` (each alias must produce the SAME report as the canonical spelling, the reviewer's finding as a regression test). comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
NEXT CHILD SCOPE — read-only inventory of `public/environment.html`, requested by coord. No edit, no browser gate, no source change; the worktree is untouched.

## The three inline blocks, measured

    file: 21984 bytes, 315 lines

1. **Inline `<script>` — 2304 bytes, 51 lines.** The project-root declaration form (`voicebox-beads-utj`): reads `#root-path`, `#machine-host-token`, `#declare-root`, `#declare-result`, has a local `say(text, ok)` helper, POSTs to the root seam, and deliberately passes the server's refusals through unchanged (`path-missing`, `not-a-directory`) because a second vocabulary for one fact is the thing it was written to avoid. Self-contained, imports nothing, touches no theme state, no storage key. **Extractable**, exactly as Help's was.

2. **Inline `<style>` — 8164 bytes, 105 lines.** A complete page stylesheet, and the page links no stylesheet at all, so this block IS its styling. It opens with `color-scheme: light dark` and writes its palette as `light-dark()` pairs — the same shape `public/style.css` uses. **Extractable** to a same-origin `.css`; of the three this is the one carrying real risk, because a dropped rule is a visible regression rather than a broken feature.

3. **Inline `style="min-width:16rem"`** on `<input id="asset-name">` (line 233). One property on one element. **Removable** into a rule or class; no hash needed.

**Cross-check that makes these numbers trustworthy:** static inspection finds 1 script + 1 style block + 1 style attribute = 3, and the browser measures exactly 3 report-only violations with the matching granular directives (`script-src-elem`, `style-src-elem`, `style-src-attr`). Two independent methods agreeing is the evidence; neither alone would be.

Also measured: **no inline event handlers** anywhere on the page, which is why no `script-src-attr` appears — and why nothing here would break if the policy were ever enforced.

## Acceptance shape for the child

- Reports for `/environment.html` go **3 -> 0**, and the three blocks are gone STRUCTURALLY: no inline `<script>`, no inline `<style>`, no `style=` attribute on the page.
- The root control keeps working, driven in a browser: the dialog opens, the destinations and inputs are present, and the failure path still shows the server's own refusal text rather than a re-worded one. The behaviour to preserve is `utj`'s, so the seam's vocabulary is part of the acceptance, not just the DOM.
- The theme/`light-dark` behaviour is preserved, asserted as computed values rather than as token text (the lesson from voicebox-beads-7xse: `light-dark()` accepts only a colour, and a rule can move without its meaning moving).
- No server edit needed, for the same reason xggy.1 needs none: the Report-Only allowlist keys on the RESOLVED FILE, so `environment.html` stays covered whether its blocks are inline or external.

## The end state nobody should discover late

Once Help and Environment are both clean, **no allowlisted document reports anything**. The browser "expected report set" signal is then gone entirely — an empty list cannot distinguish "covered and clean" from "not covered at all" — so:
- the durable coverage proof is the server-lane assertion that the HEADER is present on every spelling, which coord has already endorsed as the one to keep;
- the browser tests keep proving the thing that still has content: that nothing is blocked (the pages and their controls still work), not that violations were observed.
Do not build the next child's acceptance around report counts except for the one step that matters, 3 -> 0.

## Recorded, not fixed, because they are not CSP work

- The `<style>` block **duplicates the token set** in `public/style.css` (`--ground`, `--card`, `--muted`, `--accent` are defined in both). Extracting the block preserves that duplication; unifying the two is a separate change with its own visual risk.
- `public/fused.js:6661` still implements the same Help-search filter as the block xggy.1 extracts, so the duplication noted there survives this child too.

Sequencing, per coord: after xggy.1, and only once ul1m.1 has landed and its test and baseline exist on main.

Pin direct GET aliases, exact policy parity, measured browser violation set (likely inline style but do not assert without measurement), direct app behavior, and the unchanged room->bridge->opaque srcdoc WebMCP path. No remote report payloads or unsafe-inline. This is staging, not a fix for missing enforcement. (2) Separately seek explicit coord/hub security approval for an enforcing header on the FIVE trusted clean documents only, preserving index meta until identical-header compatibility proven. Acceptance: real GET parsed directives and aliases; browser Help search, Environment declaration, room UI positive controls; a deliberately inserted inline script/handler must be blocked on a trusted test document; malformed/missing header refuses; merger full union gate and independent cross-family review. Decide whether synthetic-only observation is acceptable or first add privacy-reviewed Reporting-Endpoints with bounded retention; never call synthetic tests real-traffic clearance. (3) BRIDGE/APP CAPABILITY DECISION, owner 28sc.1: choose an SDK provenance strategy and policy for arbitrary user HTML in opaque srcdoc before any enforced bridge header. Externalizing just the SDK to a same-origin JS file may be blocked by opaque-origin self rules; a hash of a stable SDK does not authorize arbitrary app scripts; either choice needs a real app-surface threat model and tool-registration/negative-mutant tests. Keep bridge excluded meanwhile; a direct /apps URL header governs navigation, NOT HTML copied into srcdoc.
BOUNDED FOLLOW-UPS (do not overlap completed xggy children): ul1m owner after approval: Stage 1 app Report-Only and focus tests; separate trusted-five enforcement bead only after security approval; 28sc.1 owner: bridge/srcdoc capability design and an approved browser candidate before any bridge policy; coord: ADR decision and reporting endpoint/privacy policy. One next action: coord/hub records explicit trusted/app staging and enforcement scope, plus 28sc.1 security direction, then dispatches one writer per seam. This parent is a proposal, NOT a reviewed/enforced CSP release.

title: ADR: Apply CSP via server HTTP headers for static HTML
close_reason: Completed: ADR adopted; Report-Only CSP header centralized in server.mjs for static HTML documents (ul1m.1 / 539c8b1)

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: COORD DESIGN ACCEPTANCE (not implementation approval): centralized CSP HTTP headers for trusted top-level static HTML, REPORT-ONLY first with bounded first-party violation evidence, then separately reviewed enforcement only after inline scripts are externalized and browser functionality remains intact. Retain index meta until compatibility proven; simultaneous header+meta intersect. Exclude opaque sandbox srcdoc/SDK and copied mini-app HTML until their own capability-boundary tests. No unsafe-inline to make tests green, no production edits from this ADR alone.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
TWO DESIGN GAPS FOUND BY CHECKING MODERN WEB GUIDANCE, recorded here because they belong to the enforcement/ADR phase rather than to the inline extraction (`voicebox-beads-xggy.1`). Source: the `security` guide (XSS/CSP/Cookies/Cross-Origin Isolation), retrieved 2026-10-12.

Its section 2.1 says inline scripts and styles "will need nonces, hashes, or refactoring" — which is exactly the enumeration ul1m.1 performed (Help 1 block, Environment 3) and the refactoring path xggy.1 takes, so the extraction is the guidance's own recommended alternative to hashes.

Its section 2.2 adds two DOs our current design does not meet, and they are deliberate on our side rather than oversights — but they are unmet, and that has a consequence:

1. **"Define a `Reporting-Endpoints` header so violations have somewhere to go, and reference its name from `report-to`."** We have no endpoint on purpose, so nothing is collected beyond a devtools console and the page's own `securitypolicyviolation` event. Fine for staging and for tests; not a substitute for collection.
2. **"Run report-only for long enough to cover real traffic patterns (typically days to weeks), not just synthetic testing."** Without an endpoint, that phase cannot happen: there is nothing accumulating over days. So the sequence "stage, observe real traffic, then enforce" is currently missing its middle step, and whoever designs enforcement should either add an endpoint first or state explicitly that this deployment accepts synthetic-only observation.

Also noted, deferred rather than adopted: the same section says to "always include `'report-sample'` in your `script-src` directives" so a violation report names the first 40 characters of the offending code. Our staged policy is a character-for-character mirror of `index.html`'s meta by coord's explicit requirement, so adding a directive now would break that parity and the test that pins it. It belongs with enforcement, where the meta and the header would be revised together.

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: COORD ROUTING 2026-10-12: assign shard bounded READ-ONLY Stage 1 on sandbox srcdoc/bridge CSP inheritance boundary after 8wm8 completion. NOT enforcement or security-policy approval. Measure in actual Chromium with current origin/main 13b4c76 (and stable served headers) how Report-Only trusted top-level header applies/does not apply to opaque sandbox srcdoc, copied mini-app HTML, and bridge; distinguish static page vs sandbox origin and inherited parent policy, violations and functional bridge behavior. No source edits, no CSP broadening/unsafe-inline, no secrets. Record bounded reproducible matrix, missing evidence and one next action on this ADR; synthetic report-only cannot prove production enforcement, reporting endpoint remains separate design gap. Coordinate browser slot and long gates; stop if it needs product/security authorization.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
28sc STAGE 1: BOUNDED READ-ONLY MATRIX, actual Chromium, origin/main 13b4c76. No source edits, no policy change, no enforcement. Claim released after this.

METHOD: the tree checked out at 13b4c76 and its own server serving its stable headers; real Chromium via the project's CDP harness; one bounded run, browser and server closed in a finally. Two things are measured separately and should not be conflated: what the SERVER sends (HTTP response headers) and what the BROWSER does with an inherited policy (securitypolicyviolation events and whether code still runs).

1. HEADER MATRIX - which documents receive Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only:
   /index.html PRESENT | /help.html PRESENT | /changelog.html PRESENT | /environment.html PRESENT | /harnesses.html PRESENT | / PRESENT (canonicalises to /index.html)
   /apps/agent-monitor.html ABSENT | /apps/landing-inspector.html ABSENT | /mini-app-bridge.html ABSENT
   Nothing here is surprising given the allowlist, but it is now measured rather than read.

2. INHERITANCE INTO AN OPAQUE SANDBOX srcdoc FRAME - the bridge's inner-frame shape (sandbox="allow-scripts", content injected via srcdoc). Measured with the parent being /help.html, which DOES carry the header:
   frame origin reports "null" (opaque); the parent CANNOT reach into it ("blocked", which is the designed property and is what makes postMessage the only channel).
   The frame posted TWO violations to its parent: script-src-elem for an inline script and script-src-elem for a cross-origin script URL.
   CONCLUSION: an srcdoc document INHERITS its parent's CSP. The opaque origin does not isolate it from the parent's policy - about:srcdoc inherits.
   Report-Only does not block: the frame's own inline script still ran (posted alive with ran:true), and the frame could reach its parent by postMessage, so the sandboxed-frame path functions end to end.

3. WHAT DOES NOT INHERIT: /apps/landing-inspector.html served as its own document is SAME-ORIGIN (the parent can read its contentDocument and sees its script tags) and carries NO policy. Sandboxing it made it opaque, but a document loaded by src is its own browsing context, not an srcdoc, so it inherits nothing either way. So the copied mini-app documents are policy-free by both routes today.

4. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR ENFORCEMENT, and it is a coupling rather than a violation count:
   public/mini-app-bridge.js:35 defines INJECTED_SDK as an INLINE <script>, and injectSdkIntoHtml() injects that payload into the mini-app HTML which is then assigned to inner.srcdoc (lines 1034 and 1053).
   Because srcdoc inherits the parent's policy, whatever is enforced on the BRIDGE'S OUTER DOCUMENT is also enforced on the opaque inner frame that runs untrusted app code.
   Today this does not bite, because /mini-app-bridge.html carries NO header, so the inner frame inherits nothing.
   It would bite the moment the bridge's outer document is added to an enforced allowlist: an enforced script-src 'self' would apply to the inner srcdoc, and INJECTED_SDK is inline, so every mini-app would break - or, in Report-Only, would be flagged on every load for something that is our own code, not the app's.

5. SECURITY DECISION REQUIRED BEFORE ENFORCEMENT (one decision, not a list): decide the provenance of the injected mini-app SDK under an enforced policy on the bridge's outer document. Either the SDK is externalised to a same-origin file and loaded by src, or the inner frame is deliberately excluded from the inherited policy by another mechanism, or the SDK carries a hash/nonce the policy names. This is not a violation to suppress - it is our own first-party code being flagged, so the choice determines whether mini-apps survive enforcement at all. It has a second-order consequence: any decision that keeps inline code inside srcdoc frames constrains what the rest of the policy can say, because srcdoc inheritance is not per-frame configurable.

UNKNOWNS AND MISSING EVIDENCE, stated rather than assumed:
  - This measures Report-Only only. Report-Only cannot demonstrate what enforcement blocks, so nothing here proves enforcement behaviour; it proves what is flagged and what still runs.
  - There is no Reporting-Endpoints and no report-to, so no violation has anywhere to go beyond the page's own securitypolicyviolation event. These are first-party, test-driven violations only: NO REAL-TRAFFIC COVERAGE IS CLAIMED, and I am not claiming the staged policy has been exercised against real user traffic.
  - I did not measure the bridge end to end with a real mini-app document from /apps, only the frame/policy shape with representative content. Whether every real mini-app is inline-script-only or some load external resources is unmeasured, and that determines how much of the app surface the injected SDK decision affects.
  - Whether /apps documents are ever framed by src rather than copied into srcdoc in the real code path is unverified by me.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN PROBE, recorded because it is the kind of error that would have made this matrix wrong: my first sandbox probe printed a caption asserting "no violation message => the parent's Report-Only policy did NOT reach the opaque frame". The data contradicted the caption - violations DID arrive. The caption was a claim I had written before measuring, and I nearly reported it as the conclusion. The matrix above states what was measured.

NEXT ACTION (bounded, one): externalise INJECTED_SDK or determine its hash, and test the mini-app path in Report-Only with the bridge's outer document carrying the header, so the inherited-policy effect is observed on the real app surface rather than on representative content. That is a measurement and a small code change, and it should be authorised separately since it edits the bridge.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
28sc STAGE 1 (SUPPLEMENT): real bridge flow, copied-mini-app-vs-bridge separated, and UNKNOWABLE vs ABSENT. Second bounded Chromium run, tree checked out at exact main SHA 13b4c76, browser+server closed in finally, no source or policy edits.

A. SERVED HEADERS, HTTP, exact SHA:
  /help.html                  report-only PRESENT, enforced absent. Directives: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'
  /mini-app-bridge.html       report-only ABSENT, enforced absent
  /apps/landing-inspector.html report-only ABSENT, enforced absent
  /apps/agent-monitor.html    report-only ABSENT, enforced absent

B. THE BRIDGE'S REAL FLOW (loaded /mini-app-bridge.html directly and observed it, rather than substituting representative content):
  On load the bridge CREATES its inner frame: id=inner-app, sandbox="allow-scripts", and the src ATTRIBUTE IS NULL - i.e. the frame is populated by srcdoc, which is the design.
  The parent CANNOT reach the inner window ("blocked") and its contentDocument reads null. So the opaque origin is real in the shipped page and the app's DOM is not reachable from the bridge.
  The bridge's outer document has NO meta CSP. Combined with A, the bridge's outer document carries NO policy at all.
  CONSEQUENCE, and this is the point of the run: because srcdoc inherits its parent's policy, and this parent has none, the inner frame inherits nothing today. That is why the inline injected SDK works. It also means the inheritance I measured in the first run used /help.html as the parent precisely because THAT parent has a policy - the mechanism is real, but the shipped bridge does not currently exercise it.

C. COPIED MINI-APP HTML - kept separate from the bridge, as asked:
  /apps/landing-inspector.html framed by src: the parent CAN read its contentDocument (same-origin), it contains 1 script tag, and it has no meta CSP of its own.
  So there are TWO distinct mini-app paths and they diverge under an enforced policy:
    - copied into srcdoc inside the bridge: inherits whatever the BRIDGE'S OUTER document enforces;
    - served as its own document (/apps/*.html): inherits nothing, own browsing context, same-origin, no policy.
  Today both are policy-free. At enforcement the first would suddenly be governed by the bridge's policy and the second would still be governed by nothing.

D. UNKNOWABLE vs ABSENT, demonstrated rather than asserted:
  Attempting to read a response from behind an opaque sandbox frame THROWS: "SecurityError: Failed to read a named property 'fetch' from 'Window'". So a sandboxed frame's own header state CANNOT be read from the parent at all.
  This matters for how the earlier matrix is read: saying "/apps/*.html and /mini-app-bridge.html receive no header" is a STATEMENT ABOUT THE SERVER's response, measured over HTTP. It is NOT a statement about what a sandboxed frame sees, which is unknowable from the parent by construction. Where I cannot observe a frame's own header state I am recording unknowns, not inferring absence.

E. THE ENFORCEMENT DECISION, restated with the bridge flow measured: public/mini-app-bridge.js:35 defines INJECTED_SDK as an INLINE <script>, and injectSdkIntoHtml() injects it into the mini-app HTML that becomes inner.srcdoc. Because srcdoc inherits, adding the bridge's outer document to an enforced allowlist would apply that policy inside the frame running untrusted app code, and our own inline SDK would be flagged under Report-Only and BLOCKED under enforcement - every mini-app would fail. The decision required is the provenance of that SDK (external file, hash, or nonce) or a deliberate exemption for the inner frame, and it must be taken BEFORE the bridge's outer document is added to any enforced allowlist.

CORRECTION, the same class of error as last time, recorded: my probe reported "messages seen by the bridge page: undefined" because I registered the listener on /help.html and then navigated away, so the array no longer existed. That value is my instrumentation bug, NOT evidence that the bridge posts no messages. I am not reporting it as a finding. (The first run had the mirror-image error, where a printed caption asserted the opposite of the data.)

STILL UNKNOWABLE, unchanged: whether some real mini-apps load external resources (which changes how much of the app surface the SDK decision touches); whether any real code path frames /apps/*.html by src rather than copying it into srcdoc; and everything about enforced behaviour, since Report-Only cannot demonstrate blocking. No Reporting-Endpoints exists, so these remain first-party test-driven violations with NO real-traffic coverage claimed.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION to my own Stage 1 write-up, accepted from coord and tightened here so the record does not overstate what was measured.

WHAT IS MEASURED:
  - The served header matrix (HTTP, exact SHA 13b4c76): allowlisted documents and / carry the Report-Only header; /apps/*.html and /mini-app-bridge.html carry none.
  - An opaque sandbox srcdoc frame INHERITS its parent's CSP. Observed directly: with /help.html as the parent, the frame posted script-src-elem violations for an inline script and for a cross-origin script URL.
  - Under Report-Only the code still RUNS: the frame's inline script executed and the frame reached its parent by postMessage. So the bridge/sandbox path functions.
  - The bridge's real flow: on load it creates inner-app with sandbox="allow-scripts" and a NULL src attribute (i.e. srcdoc); the parent cannot reach the inner window and its contentDocument reads null; the bridge's outer document carries no meta and no header at all.
  - A sandboxed frame's own header state is UNKNOWABLE from the parent - reading behind the frame throws SecurityError. The server-side absence is a statement about HTTP responses, not about what a frame sees.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, and where I over-claimed:
  - I wrote that an enforced script-src 'self' on the bridge's outer document "would be BLOCKED under enforcement - every mini-app would fail". That is a PREDICTION inferred from two measured facts (srcdoc inheritance, and INJECTED_SDK being an inline script). It is NOT an observed enforcement failure, and nothing in a Report-Only run can demonstrate what enforcement blocks. The measured part is: the inline SDK is flagged as script-src-elem under an inherited policy, and it still runs because the policy is Report-Only.
  - The actual /apps -> bridge path is unmeasured. I observed the frame shape with representative content and I observed /apps/*.html as its own document; I did not drive a real mini-app from /apps through the bridge into the srcdoc frame.

SO THE ENFORCEMENT QUESTION IS OPEN, not settled: whether the inline injected SDK survives an inherited enforced policy on the bridge's outer document, and whether the real mini-app path reaches that frame at all. That belongs to voicebox-beads-28sc.1 (P2, BLOCKED, coord) as a design/real-path decision with the externalise-or-hash choice, with no source edit or enforcement here.

Nothing in this correction changes the measured matrix. It changes the strength of one sentence in it, which is the kind of thing that should be corrected in place rather than left to read as evidence.

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: BLOCKED owner voicebox-coord after bounded read-only Stage 1: browser evidence at main 13b4c76 confirms trusted-header Report-Only inheritance into an opaque sandbox srcdoc frame with script violations and unchanged inline execution/postMessage; real bridge outer document currently receives no CSP and creates opaque srcdoc, direct /apps src-frame is separate same-origin/no policy. An enforced header on real bridge and full /apps->bridge execution have NOT been tested; do not claim blocking or all-app failure as observed. Real-traffic reporting absent. ONE next action: unblock child 28sc.1 only after architect scopes safe SDK externalization/hash plus real-path Report-Only and candidate enforce test under approved security decision; do not implement CSP enforcement from this ADR. Parent remains blocked, not DONE.

title: Help and mini-app documents are served with no Content-Security-Policy at all, while index.html carries a strict one
description: FILED OUT OF voicebox-beads-uj16 by coord's direction: the missing Help CSP is a separate finding, and uj16 must not add a policy or change one. Read-only measurement; nothing changed. ## Measured, from a running server rather than a grep Starting the real server and reading the actual response headers: /help.html status=200 header-CSP=none meta-CSP=none bytes=11176 / status=200 header-CSP=none meta-CSP=YES bytes=75345 /apps/agent-monitor.html status=200 header-CSP=none meta-CSP=none bytes=39480 So the gap is wider than one page: index.html sets `script-src 'self'` (and default-src, style-src, font-src, img-src, connect-src, object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', form-action 'none') as a meta tag, and neither the Help page nor the mini-app pages carry any policy in either form. server.mjs adds no CSP header to any of them. ## Severity, stated honestly rather than maximised This is a hardening and consistency gap, NOT a demonstrated exploit, and the difference matters for triage: - No reflection was found. Requesting /help.html with `?q=` and `?xss=` returned the page byte-for-byte without either string present, so there is no measured path from visitor input into the document. - The documents are static, and nothing in them is server-templated with user data. - What IS real: the app's own newest and most hardened page (index.html) is protected and its help and mini-app pages are not, so the policy is inconsistent across documents that share a session and an origin. Any future injection into those pages - a dependency, an extension, a mini-app's own HTML - has no second line of defence, and index.html's policy would have caught it. ## Why this is filed separately from uj16, and how the two interact The reason help.html CAN avoid a CSP today is the same reason uj16 exists: it runs an inline script (the help-search filtering, plus the theme block uj16 is removing) and an inline script needs `'unsafe-inline'` or a nonce/hash under `script-src 'self'`. So uj16's option A - load the shared /theme-boot.js and delete the body-end theme copy - removes SOME of the obstacle but NOT all of it: after uj16 the page still has exactly one inline `
notes: ARCHITECT PASS: Reviewed the CSP inconsistency. Filed ADR voicebox-beads-28sc to formalise the HTTP header approach over meta tags. Filed proposal voicebox-beads-xggy to extract inline scripts and implement the headers.
close_reason: Landed in 539c8b1 / 0f30470 / 0b6e864 (voicebox-beads-ul1m.1): staged Report-Only CSP on canonical resolved document paths in server.mjs

comments.author: voicebox-audioflake
comments.text:
READ-ONLY SECURITY DESIGN (not claimed; no source/CSP/server/browser edits while uj16 owns Help and 8tk2 merger gate). Fresh branch view at 4bf7a8a and origin/main 6b0bb89: only public/index.html:7 has CSP meta; server.mjs GET / special route :4251 and generic static fallback :4353-4358 send content-type only, no CSP response header. HTML inventory: public/help.html has inline search script :118 (uj16 theme removal leaves this), public/environment.html has inline root-declaration script :261, built-ins public/apps/agent-monitor.html :571, landing-inspector.html :477, live-vision-studio.html :456 each inline. changelog.html, harnesses.html and mini-app-bridge.html load external scripts only. /apps/agent-monitor.html may be fetched by public/fused.js:4579 and injected as HTML, not necessarily navigated directly. More importantly public/fused.js:6018+ embeds /mini-app-bridge.html, and public/mini-app-bridge.js:35 injects an INLINE SDK <script> into opaque-origin sandbox="allow-scripts" inner iframe via srcdoc at :1034/:1053. A blanket enforce script-src self on every static HTML risks breaking Help search, environment root declaration, three built-in apps AND the inner SDK/user-generated mini-app scripts (srcdoc CSP can inherit embedding document policy); a header for direct /apps/ URLs does NOT automatically cover copied HTML when embedded as srcdoc. Current documents are static, bead reports no user-input reflection or exploit; classify consistency hardening, not demonstrated XSS.
Narrow staged rollout proposal for owner/reviewer sign-off: (1) after uj16 lands, remeasure served GET /, /help.html, /environment.html, /apps/*.html, /mini-app-bridge.html headers/meta plus inline script/style/event-handler inventory; pin exact route ownership and the bridge/srcdoc inheritance decision before code. (2) Start with a document-scoped Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only response header for trusted top-level documents, equivalent to index.html meta policy where compatible; do not silently apply to mini-app bridge/srcdoc. Capture only local browser securitypolicyviolation events or bounded first-party report endpoint with no secrets/personal HTML; functional baseline before enforcing. (3) Extract Help search and environment inline code plus built-in mini-app scripts into external files, separately reviewed; or justify stable hashes for immutable built-ins, NOT global unsafe-inline. Treat opaque sandbox inner srcdoc/SDK as a separate capability boundary/policy so WebMCP handshake remains working; never weaken index policy to accommodate it. (4) After zero unexpected report-only violations, enforce on selected trusted HTML responses, maintain one policy owner in server static path and avoid contradictory header/meta (CSPs intersect). Tests must verify actual GET response headers and parsed directives, missing/malformed fail closed; drive Help search, environment root declaration, three built-ins and mini-app bridge+WebMCP registration in real browser with before/after screenshots and no unexpected CSP violations; negative inline payload in trusted docs must be blocked after enforce, and sandbox SDK/tool flow must remain functional. Stop if permissions, script timing, or srcdoc inheritance contradict expectations; full gate merger only.
Dependency/collision: uj16 still edits Help; do not mutate help.html until it lands/reviewer clears. Coord owns claim transfer and design/reviewer lane availability; no code authority from this comment.

comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: COORD DISPATCH 2026-10-14: gate-recover owns CSP gap investigation/fix. Preserve bridge functionality; explicit browser behavior and CSP verification, focused test, secret-scan if touching config, unit-only fast, independent cross-family review before landing. Avoid overlapping xggy policy design branch.

comments.author: voicebox-gate-recover
comments.text: READ-ONLY CSP/BRIDGE VERIFICATION on origin/main@91bd969; no repository edits, no production headers changed, no author full gate. Real-server GET matrix (200 each): /, /help.html, /environment.html, /changelog.html, /harnesses.html => Report-Only YES, enforcing header NO; /apps/{agent-monitor,landing-inspector,live-vision-studio}.html + /mini-app-bridge.html => both NO. Room / alone retains enforcing meta. Browser production path: host window.__voiceboxMiniApp.mount -> /mini-app-bridge.html?appId=... -> sandbox=allow-scripts opaque inner srcdoc with injected webMcp SDK -> registerTool -> callTool => ok true. Existing focused test browser: continuous host -> page -> bridge -> inner DOM PASS 1/1, visual screenshot pixel delta. Test-only localhost reverse proxy (unchanged app bytes, header appended only to actual bridge response, no repo/server modification) proves policy risk: Report-Only mirrored strict policy => bridge inline style reports style-src-elem disposition=report; SDK registration + callTool still succeed. SAME exact probe with enforcing bridge header => inline style disposition=enforce and SDK tool registration absent after 1.5s, while srcdoc and bridge frame exist. This paired contrast supports a functional break under the candidate policy; it does NOT isolate SDK blocking as the only cause, since inner-frame CSP events were not observed. Artifacts: /tmp/voicebox-csp-bridge-probe.mjs; /tmp/voicebox-csp-bridge-{probe,enforce-probe}.log; screenshots /tmp/voicebox-csp-bridge-{report,enforce}.png. Candidate policy: staged Report-Only only for direct /apps/*.html resolved files (three built-ins), explicitly exclude bridge/srcdoc; separately request security authorization for enforcing trusted 5 clean documents; keep bridge outside enforcing allowlist until design proves real SDK + arbitrary app JS under inherited CSP. Acceptance after approval: GET exact directives/aliases and excluded bridge; browser Help search, Environment root, direct apps, room mini-app WebMCP positive; inline negative mutant blocked on trusted docs; bridge SDK remains functional; no real-traffic claim without Reporting-Endpoints. BLOCKED owner voicebox-coord: ADR 28sc/28sc.1 explicitly withhold enforcement approval and coord forbids production CSP header edits; one next action: coord/hub approve exact trusted-doc and app Report-Only scope plus bridge capability design, then reassign a scoped implementer.

title: system-command-browser read an asynchronously-set title as if it were synchronous: the tracker-mount assertion raced its own fetch (test landed with ucak, inherited on main)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF voicebox-beads-xpwt BY COORD, because this is a test-readiness defect in an assertion that landed with ucak, distinct from the theme/FOUC work on that bead. The fix IS in the xpwt branch (4330bcf) and lands with it; this bead exists so the defect has its own record and its own provenance.

## The defect
tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs asserted the agent-tracker mini-app had mounted by READING `#mini-app-outer-frame`'s title immediately after the turn landed:
  await say("open agent tracker"); const tracker = await read();
`say()` returns when the TURN lands, which is the correct signal for every other command in that file because they apply synchronously. This one does not: openAgentProgressTracker() (public/fused.js:4576) awaits `fetch("/apps/agent-monitor.html")` and `res.text()`, and only then calls `miniAppController.mount(...)`, which creates the outer frame and sets its title at :6024. So the read raced the fetch, and when the mount landed after the read the title was null.

## Provenance: inherited, not caused by xpwt
`git diff --stat origin/main 6e9fd29 -- tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs` is EMPTY - xpwt never touched the file, so the racy form that failed is main's own text, landed with ucak. What xpwt changed was the PROBABILITY: it adds tests/theme-first-paint.test.mjs, so the browser lane carries one more file at the same four-worker width.

## The failure, from the merger's cached gate record (not reconstructed)
Tree aed3ff34e5fb464610a7f963ed91a5a7b498e1b6, commit 2ec47da, /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/aed3ff34e5fb464610a7f963ed91a5a7b498e1b6.{json,log}: state FAIL, kind full, rc 1, secs 147. Failure at tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs:127:10, ERR_ASSERTION strictEqual, actual null, expected 'Agent Progress Tracker', test duration 2421ms, file 2548ms, bracketed by `[shards] ---- end ... ----` so it ran as a shard worker. 2.4s is not a timeout: the read happened and found nothing.

## The fix, and its limit
4330bcf waits for the effect with a bound (page.waitFor, 15s default) and then asserts. Non-vacuity is PROVED, not argued: with `miniAppController.mount(` disabled by mutant the test fails with "timed out waiting for the Agent Progress Tracker mini-app mounted", so a dead branch still fails exactly as the ucak bug did. After the fix: 2/2 alone and 5/5 twice at --test-concurrency=4.
HONEST LIMIT, per coord: the fetch-before-mount code path plus the mutant make this a hypothesis-backed INVARIANT fix; it is NOT a reproduction of the original gate race. No reproduction was obtained - 6 idle instrumented runs had the title present before the read, 3-way and 4-way concurrency passed repeatedly, and network throttling did not widen the race because it slows the turn POST equally. A faithful repro would need to slow only that one fetch, which needs CDP Fetch interception, and tests/lib/cdp.mjs exposes no event API to continue paused requests.

title: help.html is a third, divergent implementation of the theme decision: inline, weaker whitelist, not pre-paint
description:
FOUND while correcting my own mis-reading of help.html for voicebox-beads-7xse. Not bundled there.

## What is wrong
public/help.html:118 carries an inline theme boot, at the end of <body>:
    const savedTheme = localStorage.getItem("voicebox:theme");
    if (savedTheme === "dark" || savedTheme === "light") { document.documentElement.dataset.theme = savedTheme; }
Three problems, in order of severity:
1. DIVERGENT WHITELIST. It accepts only "dark" and "light". theme.mjs and theme-boot.js both accept "light" | "dark" | "system" and fall back to light for anything else. So a person whose preference is "system" gets a different outcome on help.html than on the room: help.html leaves the attribute alone and falls through to whatever the CSS default is. (After 7xse removes the hardcoded attribute that fallthrough becomes the OS scheme, which happens to be right, but the divergence remains: the two implementations no longer agree on what a stored value MEANS.)
2. THIRD COMPUTING SITE. This decision now lives in three places: public/theme.mjs (owner), public/theme-boot.js (pre-paint restatement, held equal by tests/theme-boot-parity.test.mjs), and this inline copy, which NOTHING holds equal to the other two. It is the same class of problem the parity test was written to prevent, one site further out.
3. WEAKER PRE-PAINT GUARANTEE. theme-boot.js is a classic non-deferred script in <head> precisely so it applies before the first paint; this one runs at the END of <body>, after the whole document is parsed. It is not covered by tests/theme-first-paint.test.mjs, which only drives index.html. Whether it flashes in practice was not measured; that is a reason to measure rather than to assume.

## Suggested fix, for whoever picks it up
Have help.html load public/theme-boot.js (same-origin external, and help.html has no Content-Security-Policy at all — no meta, no header from server.mjs — so nothing blocks it) and delete its inline copy, leaving the help-search code where it is. That removes the third site and the divergent whitelist in one change. If that is judged too broad, the smaller step is a test asserting help.html's whitelist matches theme.mjs's, so the divergence cannot grow silently.

## Why it is not in 7xse
7xse is the no-JS/OS fallback and its help.html change is the one-line attribute removal, which already fixes "system" there as a side effect. This is a duplication/divergence problem with its own fix and its own risk, so it gets its own bead rather than widening that diff.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY PLAN — no edits made. Per coord: `public/help.html` stays untouched until `voicebox-beads-7xse` lands. Everything below is read from the tree; line numbers are quoted, not recalled.

## What is actually on current main (`046e6f2`)
- `public/help.html:2` — `<html lang="en" data-theme="light">`
- `public/help.html:7` — `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css">`
- **There is no Content-Security-Policy on this document** — no meta (`grep -c Content-Security-Policy` = 0) and none added by `server.mjs`. So unlike `index.html`, an inline script here is legal, and nothing forces the external-file form.
- The third implementation sits at the END of `<body>`, in the same IIFE as the help-search filtering — two unrelated concerns in one block. Its theme half is `:121`–`:125`:
```js
      try {
        const savedTheme = localStorage.getItem("voicebox:theme");
        if (savedTheme === "dark" || savedTheme === "light") {
          document.documentElement.dataset.theme = savedTheme;
        }
      } catch {}
```

## What 7xse changes here, and what it does not
7xse removes ONLY the attribute on `:2` — the line becomes `<html lang="en">` — and moves nothing else. It deliberately leaves this block alone, because `uj16` owns it; `git diff origin/main -- public/help.html` on that branch is exactly one line. So the moment this bead unblocks, the page is "no forced attribute + a body-end script that applies the stored choice after the paint".

## The substantive defect is not the duplication — it is the timing
1. **It runs after the first paint.** The script is the last thing in `<body>`, so a person who chose light or dark paints the other scheme first and then flips. That is exactly the bug `xpwt` fixed on `index.html` (measured there: FCP 76ms, theme applied 78ms), and it is still live on this page.
2. It accepts `dark|light` only — `system` is missing from the whitelist that `theme.mjs` and `theme-boot.js` both implement.
3. It never sets `data-theme-mode`; both shared implementations set that attribute too.
4. It has no `prefers-color-scheme` listener, so a device change while the page is open is not followed.
5. It is a third hand-maintained copy of the key and the whitelist, with no test relating the copies — which is why 1–4 could drift without anyone noticing.

One accident worth recording rather than "fixing" blind: because it ignores `system`, a stored `system` leaves the attribute unset, and after 7xse an unset attribute follows the OS. So the `system` case is CORRECT by accident post-7xse; the stored light/dark case is the one that flashes.

## Options
- **A — recommended: load the shared guard.** `<script src="/theme-boot.js"></script>` in `<head>`, mirroring `index.html`'s order (guard at `:21`, stylesheet at `:31`), and delete `:121`–`:125`. The file is standalone — no imports, no dependency on `fused.js` — and already handles the tri-state, both attribute names, the throw case and the OS resolution. Three implementations become one and the page stops flashing. Cost: the page gains a dependency on a `public/` file it does not currently load (it already depends on `/style.css`), and the no-script case is unchanged because 7xse's CSS already carries it.
- **B — keep it inline, move it into `<head>`, align the whitelist.** A smaller diff, and legal here since there is no CSP — but it creates a FOURTH copy of the decision with no test tying it to the others, which is the pattern that produced 2–5. It fixes the flash while preserving the bug class.
- **C — leave it.** Accepts a flash on every help.html load for anyone who chose light or dark.

## Expected resulting markup (option A), starting from current main
Before (current main `046e6f2`):
```
2  <html lang="en" data-theme="light">
...
7    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css">
8  </head>
```
After 7xse lands, before this bead:
```
2  <html lang="en">
...
7    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css">
8  </head>
```
Expected final state:
```
2  <html lang="en">
3  <head>
4    <meta charset="utf-8">
5    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
6    <title>Voicebox — Comprehensive Help & User Guide</title>
7    <script src="/theme-boot.js"></script>
8    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/style.css">
9  </head>
```
with the body-end script reduced to its search half:
```
  <script>
    (() => {
      const search = document.querySelector(".help-search-input");
      const sections = document.querySelectorAll(".help-section[data-help-section]");
      search?.addEventListener("input", () => { /* unchanged */ });
    })();
  </script>
```
The absolute `/theme-boot.js` is deliberate: `index.html` loads it as a relative `theme-boot.js` because it is served at the root, and help.html is too — but the absolute form cannot break if either page ever moves. If option A is chosen and that divergence is unwanted, the fix is to make `index.html` match, not to make both relative.

## Acceptance (proposed)
- A browser test that seeds `voicebox:theme=dark`, loads `/help.html` and asserts the theme AND the computed `color-scheme` inside the first `requestAnimationFrame` — the shape already proven by `tests/theme-first-paint.test.mjs` — plus stored `light`, stored `system` against both OS schemes, and the no-JS case read through the CDP CSS domain (with scripting disabled `page.evaluate` throws, measured on 7xse).
- Negative control: with the guard removed from `<head>`, the stored-dark case must go RED.
- If the guard is shared, extend the existing parity coverage to this page rather than writing a fourth set of expectations.

## Boundaries
`public/help.html` only. It must not re-open 7xse's CSS, and it must not bundle the mini-app pages under `public/apps/` (they already carry `<html lang="en">` and their own `prefers-color-scheme` handling). No edits until 7xse has landed and coord says go — and if that landing shifts the line numbers above, re-read the file rather than trusting them.

ftqe FIXED, AND THIS BEAD'S PREMISE CORRECTED. New tip `d0de7c2` on `fleet/shard-uj16` (fast gate running).

## 1. The blocker (voicebox-beads-ftqe)
`help.html` now imports the shared owner: `public/help-theme.mjs` is one `import { initTheme } from "/theme.mjs"; initTheme();` — not a fourth copy, the same module the room uses. `theme-boot.js` resolves the system scheme once and so cannot do this; `theme.mjs`'s `initTheme()` installs the matchMedia listener.

Measured in a real browser:
- stored `system`, OS light -> light; **switch to dark -> dark**; switch back -> light  (was: stayed light)
- stored `dark` (explicit): stays dark across OS switches in both directions — an explicit choice does not move
- RED for this blocker: blocking `*help-theme.mjs*` reproduces it exactly — `system` + OS dark switch stays light

## 2. THE CORRECTION — the flash premise was wrong, and I had asserted it without measuring
I justified this bead as "help.html flashes because its copy applied the theme at the end of `<body>`, after the first paint". **That is false.** Measured on the EXACT pre-uj16 bytes (`git show 6b0bb89:public/help.html`, served on the real origin, first frame sampled inside the first rAF):

    pre-uj16 page, stored dark : first frame theme=dark, bg rgb(11,15,25), attribute set at 1ms, first frame at 13ms
    current page,  stored dark : first frame theme=dark, bg rgb(11,15,25)

The copy was an INLINE CLASSIC script, so it ran while the document was parsing — before the first paint. The xpwt flash came from a DEFERRED MODULE, which is a different timing, and I transferred that reasoning to a page it did not apply to.

So the honest justification for deleting the copy is DIVERGENCE, not timing: it ignored `system`, never set `data-theme-mode`, had no listener, and was a fourth hand-maintained copy no test related to the owner. My first version of this test asserted the flash and FAILED, which is how I found it.

Corrected where it was written: `docs/07`, both `help.html` comments, and the test's header. The test now ENFORCES the correction: section 4 rebuilds the pre-uj16 arrangement from the current file, measures ITS first frame, and asserts the stored choice WAS applied before the paint — so if anyone restores the flash premise, that assertion fails.

## 3. A control I wrote and then removed as flaky
With the guard blocked, whether the deferred module beats the first paint depends on cache and CPU — I measured it BOTH ways in this file's own runs (before the first frame when the module was cached; after it under load). A test that cannot control its timing must not assert an outcome, so that section now asserts the structural guarantee instead: the guard is classic with no `defer`/`async`, and the module carries `type="module"` and is therefore deferred by definition. I also tried per-request network throttling to engineer the delay; `Network.emulateNetworkConditionsByRule` did not take effect here in either rule ordering, so I removed it rather than leave a control that pretends to control something.

- `docs-check: OK — 14 generated blocks across 3 documents, 758 hand-written path claims`

No policy change anywhere in the diff.
