title: The served-page CSP assertion greps raw text including comments, so a correct comment about the policy fails it (hit for real, blocked a merge)
description:
FOUND BY ACCIDENT, WHILE BLOCKING A MERGE. tests/voicebox.test.mjs:113 asserts:
  assert.doesNotMatch(page, /script-src[^;]*'unsafe-inline'/);
where `page` is the raw text of public/index.html. Because it is a text grep rather than a read of the parsed policy, an HTML COMMENT that mentions the keyword satisfies the pattern - the regex matched starting at the `script-src 'self'` inside a comment and ran (no semicolons) to the quoted keyword further down the same comment.

WHAT HAPPENED: I added a comment explaining that the theme guard is an external file rather than an inline script BECAUSE the policy refuses inline and making it work would mean adding that escape. The comment therefore contained the escape written out, and the assertion that exists to prevent the escape failed on a comment that REFUSES it. It cost a full union gate run and a merge attempt (merger, xpwt, 2026-10-11). Fixed in 6e9fd29 by writing the keyword unquoted.

WHY IT IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT JUST MY CLUMSINESS: the test cannot distinguish "the policy allows inline" from "the text discusses inline", so it fails closed on prose. Two consequences:
1. Anyone who writes a correct comment near the CSP meta breaks a security test, with a failure message that points at the page rather than at their comment.
2. More importantly it does NOT test what it claims. Grepping for a substring cannot tell whether the CSP actually forbids inline scripts - a policy written `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` in a different order, or split across a header instead of the meta, or with a nonce, would all pass this grep while allowing exactly what it means to forbid. So it is simultaneously over-sensitive (comments) and under-sensitive (real policy shapes).

SUGGESTED FIX: parse rather than grep. Read the CSP from the meta tag (or, better, assert against the response header the server sends), split on `;`, find the script-src directive, and assert the token list does not contain the escape - comments and ordering then cannot matter. A cheap intermediate step is to strip HTML comments before grepping, which fixes the false positive but leaves the under-sensitivity.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM MY CHANGE OR BY DESIGN: the assertion predates xpwt, and nothing in xpwt weakened it. This is a latent hazard that my change happened to trip. Verified: with the comment rewording reverted, the assertion fails; with it in place, tests/voicebox.test.mjs is 13/13.

title: Theme changes do not follow another tab: no storage listener anywhere, though PRODUCT.md commits to several live instances
description:
SPLIT OUT of voicebox-beads-xpwt by coord, deliberately NOT bundled with the pre-paint guard.

## The gap
Modern Web Guidance's dark-mode guidance asks for the override to stay in sync across tabs: "The override can change from another tab: handle `window`'s `storage` event to stay in sync." There is no `storage` listener anywhere in public/ - verified by searching for "storage" across public/*.js and public/*.mjs, which finds only reads/writes of localStorage, never a listener. So changing the theme in one tab leaves another open tab on the old scheme until it is reloaded.

## PRODUCT.md citation (this is not a theoretical nicety here)
- Capabilities and Constraints: "Several live instances may work on the same machine-backed project in separate execution roots."
- Capabilities and Constraints: "A confirmation can be answered from another live instance of the same project."
Both make multiple live tabs an intended usage, not an edge case. This is a different behaviour from the first-paint flash (xpwt): xpwt is about the scheme at load, this is about a scheme change after load, in a different tab, and it is fixed in theme.mjs rather than in the guard.

## Shape of a fix
`window.addEventListener("storage", ...)` in public/theme.mjs, re-applying only when the changed key is THEME_KEY (the module already exports it, and the parity test keeps the guard's copy in agreement), and NOT persisting in response (a storage-sync must not echo back and must not overwrite the other tab's choice). Note the guidance's explicit anti-pattern nearby: do not delete the stored value when the system preference merely coincides with it (theme.mjs already complies - there is no removeItem in it).

## Acceptance
Two real pages in one browser profile (or two CDP targets): change the theme in one, assert the other's data-theme and data-theme-mode follow without a reload, and assert the first tab is not re-persisted into a loop. Existing precedent for driving a real browser is tests/theme-browser.test.mjs.

title: No-JS and guard-failure fallback: without JS the page cannot follow the OS scheme at all (no prefers-color-scheme default in style.css)
description:
SPLIT OUT of voicebox-beads-xpwt by coord, deliberately NOT bundled with the pre-paint guard.

## The gap, stated truthfully
The guard (public/theme-boot.js) requires JavaScript. Two cases where it cannot help:
1. JS disabled or failed to load entirely: public/index.html's hardcoded data-theme="light" stands, and style.css:5 puts the whole light token set on an un-attributed :root with NO `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block anywhere. So the page is light, permanently, for a user whose OS is dark - it cannot follow the OS at all.
2. The guard throws (e.g. an unexpected error, or the script fails to load): the same result, because there is no CSS default to fall back to.
The guard itself is careful - its storage read is inside try/catch and a blocked read falls back to "light", mirroring theme.mjs's initTheme - but "it does not throw" is not the same as "there is a fallback when it is absent".

## Why it is separate from xpwt
xpwt is about the wrong scheme for a fraction of a second; this is about the wrong scheme permanently, under a different failure mode, and it is fixed in a different file (style.css, not the guard). Bundling them would have made the xpwt diff argue about CSS tokens, which xpwt deliberately does not touch.

## PRODUCT.md citation (the product already commits to this)
- Product principle: "Let the user leave and return without losing the objects, the active work or the unanswered decisions." A browser with JS disabled or a sandboxed embed is a return path; the preference is not honoured on it.
- Brand Commitments: Paul wants the visual language of isocan's voice agent. A page that always renders Warm Paper regardless of the person's environment is not that language under a dark OS.
- Impeccable's craft floor, "Browser surfaces": the parts nobody drew (scrollbars, caret, text selection, form controls) ship with browser defaults that must be themed. Those follow `color-scheme`, which today is set only from the JS-applied attribute.

## Shape of a fix, for whoever picks it up
A `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block in public/style.css carrying the dark token values as the default when no explicit attribute is present, so: no JS at all -> the OS scheme; JS present -> the guard's explicit choice still wins (attribute selectors outrank a media query at the same specificity only if ordered/specified correctly, so this needs care and a test for each of the four combinations: JS x OS scheme). Acceptance should assert the painted background and color-scheme in a real browser with JS disabled, not just read the CSS.

## Verified while scoping xpwt, so it need not be re-derived
- style.css:5-6 is `:root, :root[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light; ... }`; :root with no attribute is already the full light set.
- There is no `prefers-color-scheme` media query anywhere in public/style.css.
- tests/theme-first-paint.test.mjs and tests/theme-boot-parity.test.mjs cover the JS path; neither covers no-JS.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
STAGE 1 SCOPE — READ-ONLY, for coord's approval. No files edited. Working unclaimed because coord's claim/transfer hit the embedded-Dolt lock; claim me when it is visible.

## The defect, measured in a real browser rather than read off the CSS
With JavaScript disabled and the OS set to dark, the page is LIGHT: computed `color-scheme` is `light` and the painted background is `rgb(251, 251, 249)`. So a person whose OS is dark gets a permanently light Voicebox with no way to change it. Three causes, all needed:
1. `public/index.html:2` hardcodes `<html ... data-theme="light">`.
2. `public/style.css:6-7` puts the entire light token set on `:root, :root[data-theme="light"]` and pins `color-scheme: light`.
3. There is no `prefers-color-scheme` rule anywhere in style.css — `grep` finds it only in `public/theme.mjs:37` (the JS path) and in three self-contained mini-app pages under `public/apps/`.

## Why the obvious fix does not work, and the specificity evidence
Adding `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { ...dark tokens... } }` is what I expected to propose, and it FAILS: the media block's selector is `:root` (0,1,0) while the hardcoded `:root[data-theme="light"]` is (0,2,0), so the attribute wins and the media block never applies. Measured, not reasoned: with the attribute present and the OS dark the resolved scheme stays `light`.
And the tempting variant — putting `:root[data-theme="light"]` INSIDE the dark media query so it outranks — is worse: it would also override a user's EXPLICIT light choice, which must win. Measured the other direction too: `data-theme="dark"` with the OS light stays dark, so explicit choice beating the OS is behaviour we must preserve.
CONSEQUENCE, and it is the load-bearing part of this bead: the hardcoded `data-theme="light"` in index.html has to go whichever design we pick. That is also why this cannot be edited while xpwt is with the merger — xpwt touches index.html.

## Recommended design (Option 1): let `color-scheme` drive `light-dark()` tokens
Deliberately NOT a duplicated dark block in a media query. Style the tokens once:
  :root { color-scheme: light dark; --ground: light-dark(#fbfbf9, #0b0f19); ...all 11 tokens... }
  :root[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light; }
  :root[data-theme="dark"]  { color-scheme: dark; }
and remove the hardcoded attribute from `<html>`.
The explicit choice is then expressed ONLY through `color-scheme`, and the tokens resolve themselves. Measured against a prototype of exactly this (no repo files touched, /tmp/ld-test/): no JS + OS dark -> dark `rgb(11,15,25)`; no JS + OS light -> light; explicit dark + OS light -> dark. So the OS becomes the default and an explicit choice still wins.
Guidance basis, both retrieved: the `dark-mode` guide says "MANDATORY: Apply the color-scheme property to the :root or html element... Browsers specifically look to the root element to determine the theme for the entire viewport", and recommends `light-dark()` because it "eliminates the need for redundant media queries". The `selector-atrule-combinations` guide exists precisely because combining a media query with a selector duplicates code — which is the trap Option 1 avoids.

## The honest trade-off, for coord to weigh (Option 2)
Option 1 promotes `light-dark()` from "used in 2 rules" (style.css:650, :1115) to "the entire palette". It is Baseline Newly available and this repo has no stated legacy matrix, but if that is judged too much, Option 2 is a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block carrying the dark tokens — no new dependency, but a SECOND computing site for 11 values, so it would need a parity test holding it equal to the attribute block, the same pattern xpwt uses for the theme guard. My recommendation is Option 1: fewer moving parts, no duplication, and it is what the guidance prescribes.

## Acceptance: browser, negative AND positive, with one measured constraint
Constraint found during scoping that would otherwise waste an implementation cycle: with JavaScript disabled, `page.evaluate` THROWS ("2 is not a function"), so a no-JS test cannot read the DOM the usual way. It must read computed styles through the CDP CSS domain instead — enable `DOM` and `CSS`, `DOM.getDocument` + `DOM.querySelector`, then `CSS.getComputedStyleForNode`. Verified working with `Emulation.setScriptExecutionDisabled` + `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia` (case E read the correct dark background with JS off).
Cases: (1) JS disabled, OS dark -> dark; (2) JS disabled, OS light -> light; (3) JS ON, stored dark, OS light -> dark; (4) JS ON, stored light, OS dark -> light; (5) JS ON, stored system, OS dark -> dark; (6) guard absent but theme.mjs present -> the stored choice is still honoured. NEGATIVE CONTROL, mandatory: case 1 must FAIL against today's tree — measured, it currently resolves to light, so the test is non-vacuous only for the right reason. Screenshots for the no-JS dark and light cases.
PLUS a value-preservation test in the unit lane: parse style.css and assert every `light-dark(light, dark)` pair equals today's `:root` and `:root[data-theme="dark"]` values exactly, for all 11 tokens. The two blocks are already perfectly parallel (identical key sets, verified), so this makes the refactor provably colour-preserving and stops a mis-paired argument from silently breaking contrast in one scheme.

## One semantics question I need a decision on
With JS working but storage BLOCKED, `theme.mjs`'s `initTheme` currently defaults to `light` (deliberately mirrors what the guard does now). Under Option 1 the natural meaning of "no stored choice" is "follow the OS", but initTheme sets an explicit attribute that would override it. So: should a blocked-storage user on a dark OS follow the OS, or stay light? My recommendation is to leave the JS path exactly as it is in this bead (out of scope, no behaviour change for anyone with working storage) and document the result, but the opposite is defensible and it is a one-line change if you want it.

## Scope boundaries
No palette, typography, spacing or shape change — the values must be provably identical. Not bundling vtf3 (cross-tab). Touch set: `public/style.css`, `public/index.html`, a new browser test, the value-preservation unit test, plus docs/00, docs/07, docs/08 and README (Paul's rule: docs and README in the same change). Skills: modern-web-guidance `dark-mode` and `selector-atrule-combinations` retrieved and applied; Impeccable's craft floor read earlier this session and will be re-read immediately before the edits, per the skill's own rule — its relevant checks here are contrast holding in BOTH schemes and the browser-surface point, which is what this change is about.

comments.text:
STAGE 1 FINDING THAT CHANGES THE APPROVED DESIGN, measured in a real browser before any edit. Option 1 as accepted says "each of the 11 tokens written as a light-dark(light, dark) pair". That is WRONG for one of them, and it fails SILENTLY.

`light-dark()` resolves to a `<color>`. `--shadow` is a box-shadow, not a colour, so wrapping it in light-dark() makes the declaration invalid and the property falls back to nothing at all. Measured both ways in Chromium with the real palette values:
- `--shadow: light-dark(0 18px 40px -20px rgba(38,48,60,.2), 0 18px 40px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.7))` -> computed `box-shadow` is `none` in BOTH schemes. Not a wrong colour: NO shadow.
- `--shadow-ink: light-dark(rgba(38,48,60,.2), rgba(0,0,0,.7)); --shadow: 0 18px 40px -20px var(--shadow-ink)` -> correct in both: light `rgba(38, 48, 60, 0.2) 0px 18px 40px -20px`, dark `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7) 0px 18px 40px -20px`.
So the fix is to split the shadow's COLOUR out as its own light-dark() token and keep the geometry in place. The other 10 tokens are genuine colours and work as accepted — verified the alpha case too: `--line: light-dark(#d8dcdf, rgba(255,255,255,.12))` resolves to `rgb(216, 220, 223)` light and `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12)` dark.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ACCEPTANCE, and this is the part worth remembering: a value-preservation test that compares TOKEN TEXT would PASS while the page had no shadows, because the custom property would still contain the light-dark() text. The test must therefore assert the COMPUTED value of the consumers - `box-shadow` not `none`, in both schemes - not only that the tokens pair up. Without that, the test would certify exactly the regression it was written to prevent.

Count unchanged: 11 tokens in, 10 become light-dark() colours and 1 becomes a light-dark() colour plus an unchanged geometry wrapper. Palette values stay exact.

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED on `fleet/shard-7xse` @ `0c0932b` (fresh main `046e6f2`). Fast gate running.

## The mechanism, and why a media query was not an option
Removed the forced attribute from `public/index.html` and `public/help.html`, and made `public/style.css` carry the decision: `:root { color-scheme: light dark; }` with all ten colour tokens as single `light-dark(light, dark)` pairs. The two attribute rules now set ONLY `color-scheme`. A `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block would have been silently defeated — `:root[data-theme="light"]` is (0,2,0) and `:root` inside the media query is (0,1,0) — which is exactly why the attribute had to go rather than be worked around.

## The shadow trap, measured
`--shadow-ink: light-dark(rgba(38,48,60,.2), rgba(0,0,0,.7))` and `--shadow: 0 18px 40px -20px var(--shadow-ink)`. Wrapping the shadow ITSELF in `light-dark()` makes the declaration invalid because `light-dark()` resolves to a `<color>` — the computed value becomes `none`, in both schemes, with no error. Confirmed in Chromium. So the acceptance asserts the COMPUTED shadow, not just the token text: a text-only comparison passes on the broken version.

## The matrix, measured in a real browser on this exact tree
Read via `page.evaluate` where scripting is on, and via the CDP CSS domain where it is off (with scripting disabled `page.evaluate` throws — `2 is not a function` — so the no-JS cases cannot use it).

- NO JS, OS dark   -> ground rgb(11, 15, 25)  WARM DARK, shadow rgba(0,0,0,.7) 0 18px 40px -20px  <- the bug, fixed
- NO JS, OS light  -> ground rgb(251, 251, 249), shadow rgba(38,48,60,.2) ...
- nothing stored, OS dark (JS) -> LIGHT  <- coord's decision preserved, `System` is the opt-in
- stored dark,  OS light -> dark   (explicit beats OS)
- stored light, OS dark  -> light  (explicit beats OS)
- stored system, OS dark -> dark   (`data-theme-mode="system"`)
- stored system, OS light -> light
- guard BLOCKED (theme-boot.js), JS on, stored dark, OS light -> dark  (theme.mjs still honours storage)

## Non-vacuity: the negative control
Restored `data-theme="light"` to `index.html` and re-ran the new browser test: **fails**, `AssertionError: with JavaScript disabled on a dark OS the page must PAINT dark — this is the whole point of the bead. Without the fix it is always rgb(251, 251, 249)`. Restored immediately; `git diff --stat public/index.html` shows only the intended one-line removal. The test is not vacuous.

## Tests
- `tests/theme-os-fallback.test.mjs` (new, browser): the matrix above, incl. computed `box-shadow != none` in both schemes.
- `tests/theme-tokens.test.mjs` (new, unit): every token pinned to its pre-refactor value, the shadow's shape, `color-scheme: light dark`, and that the overrides set ONLY `color-scheme`. Also asserts neither page forces a scheme. (Its own first run caught a parser bug in itself: a comment between `{` and the first declaration has no `;` in front of it, so the split took the comment's prose as the declaration name.)
- Focused: 22/22 (theme + voicebox), 36/36 on the `help.html` tests.
- `docs-check: OK — 14 generated blocks across 3 documents, 754 hand-written path claims`.

## Docs updated in the same change
`designs/README.md` (the rationale PRESCRIBED the attribute this change removes — rewritten, not deleted: following the OS is not the complaint recorded there, which was a theme applied REGARDLESS of preference), `docs/07` (the no-JS sentence that said the fallback "is not implemented and is tracked separately" is now false and replaced; new `public/style.css` bullet), `README.md` (theme toggle), and `public/theme-boot.js`'s header (it described the hardcoded attribute as the reason it exists — its remaining job is the stored choice, and its absence now costs a flash, not a wrong scheme).

## Asymmetry, stated rather than implied (coord)
With scripting, nothing stored still means LIGHT; without scripting the page follows the OS. The two paths differ on purpose, and the docs now say so in those words instead of implying one behaviour.

description:
FOUND while implementing voicebox-beads-ri9x (the theme extraction) after the fleet's mandated Modern Web Guidance read. MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, not inferred from reading code.

## The measurement
Headless Chromium, the app's own server, nothing stored vs dark stored. A script registered with Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument samples document.documentElement.dataset.theme every 1ms from document-start and records the first time it equals "dark"; the comparison baseline is the browser's own paint timing entries.
  nothing stored:   theme light throughout; first-paint = FCP = 152ms.
  dark stored:      data-theme is "light" from t=11ms (the value the HTML shipped);
                    first animation frame t=29ms -> theme "light", computed body background rgb(251, 251, 249) (the LIGHT background);
                    first-paint = first-contentful-paint = 76ms;
                    the theme becomes "dark" at 78ms.
So the first frame and the first paint both happened in LIGHT while the person's stored preference is dark, and the flip landed 2ms after first contentful paint. The control run is clean, which rules out the sampler itself inventing a value: with nothing stored the scheme is light the whole way through, because light IS the correct answer there.

## Why it happens
public/index.html:2 ships `<html lang="en" data-theme="light">` — the attribute is HARDCODED light in the markup. The real preference is applied by public/theme.mjs (before voicebox-beads-ri9x: inline in public/fused.js) which is loaded as `<script type="module" src="fused.js">` (index.html:18). Module scripts are DEFERRED, so the attribute cannot be corrected until fused.js has been fetched, parsed and executed. Nothing in the document applies the stored value earlier: there is no inline script in <head>.

## What the guidance says (the reason this is a finding and not an opinion)
Modern Web Guidance, guide `dark-mode-toggle`, section "Persistence and FOUC prevention":
  "To avoid a flash of the wrong scheme, apply the stored value in an inline script (NOT `type=module`, NOT `defer`) placed immediately after the `<meta>` element"
  "This inline script exists **only** for FOUC prevention. Keep it as small as possible; additional JS for handling color scheme toggling can load later."
  "In rare cases `localStorage` access can throw ... Wrap in `try .. catch` if this matters. Ensure the theme is still applied to the page, even if it cannot be persisted."
The same guide's `dark-mode` page also calls the `<meta name="color-scheme">` tag MANDATORY for FOUC; that part the repo already does (public/index.html:6). So the repo does half of what the guidance requires.

## Impact, stated honestly
On a warm local load the flash is 2ms of light before dark — real, measured, and not visible to a person at that size. The reason it is worth fixing anyway is that the window is not bounded by anything: it is however long a 311KB deferred module takes to fetch and execute. On a cold cache, a slow disk, a slower device or a throttled connection the same code path yields a much longer flash of the wrong scheme, and the mechanism is identical. This is a latent defect, not an observed-in-production one.

## Not caused by voicebox-beads-ri9x, and not made worse in any way that matters
The condition is pre-existing: fused.js has always been a deferred module and the HTML has always hardcoded data-theme="light". ri9x moved the theme code out of fused.js into public/theme.mjs and PRESERVED this behaviour exactly, deliberately, because that bead is an extraction and not a behaviour change. The extraction adds one same-origin module fetch to the chain (theme.mjs is imported by fused.js, so it resolves before fused.js executes). One extra round trip on localhost is sub-millisecond, and it is dwarfed by fused.js's own size, so ri9x neither causes nor materially worsens this; it just makes the owner of the theme easy to find, which is how it was measured.

## Suggested fix, and the acceptance that would prove it
An inline, render-blocking snippet in <head> immediately after the color-scheme meta (index.html:6), roughly: read localStorage["voicebox:theme"], resolve "system" through matchMedia, and set documentElement.dataset.theme before any stylesheet-dependent paint. theme.mjs's initTheme() stays as it is and remains the owner of the tri-state, the controls and the persistence — the inline snippet only removes the dependency of FIRST PAINT on the module, and it must be deliberately minimal (the guide says so) and wrapped in try/catch so a blocked localStorage still applies a usable theme.
ACCEPTANCE (the shape this bead should be closed with): a browser test that stores "dark", reloads, and asserts the theme was already dark NO LATER THAN first contentful paint — i.e. darkAt <= first-contentful-paint from performance.getEntriesByType("paint"), or equivalently that the first animation frame's computed body background is the dark one. That fails today (78 > 76) and is exactly the assertion this measurement is built from; /tmp/fouc-probe.mjs is the reusable driver.

## One more deviation, recorded but NOT proposed as a change
The same guide says "Persist the override in `localStorage`; remove the entry when returning to the system default." This repo instead stores "system" as an explicit third value (public/theme.mjs THEME_KEY). That is a defensible tri-state design choice — data-theme-mode keeps the preference distinct from the effective scheme — and it is NOT a defect. Noting it only so the next reader does not file it as one.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY SCOPE (no code changed). voicebox-beads-xpwt, P3, FOUC: a stored theme is applied after first paint.

## The defect, as measured (not read)
With `voicebox:theme = "dark"` stored, the page paints LIGHT and only turns dark after the module runs:
first-rAF t=29ms theme=light/bg rgb(251,251,249); FCP 76ms; darkAt 78ms -> "dark applied AFTER first contentful paint (delta 2ms)".
Control, nothing stored: light throughout, FCP 152ms, no flash - so the control does NOT reproduce and that is expected, since light is what the hardcoded default already says. Probe: /tmp/fouc-probe.mjs, prints a VERDICT line. Re-probed on the current tree and unchanged by ri9x.

## WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL - two facts that remove the easy fixes
1. `public/style.css:5-6` is `:root, :root[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light; ... }`. The `:root` rule with NO attribute is already the full light set, and there is no `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block anywhere in style.css. So removing the hardcoded `data-theme="light"` from index.html:2 - the obvious first idea - changes NOTHING: an un-themed document still paints light. There is no CSS-only fix, and this also means the pre-existing system-mode-dark case flashes too, not just an explicit stored dark.
2. `public/index.html:7` is a STRICT policy: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; ...` - no `'unsafe-inline'`, no nonce, no hash. The Modern Web Guidance fix for exactly this ("Persistence and FOUC prevention") is an INLINE script immediately after the `<meta>`: "apply the stored value in an inline script (NOT type=module, NOT defer)". On this page that script is BLOCKED BY THE PAGE'S OWN CSP. The guidance is not wrong, it is incomplete for CSP-strict pages: it gives no CSP-compatible alternative. (Reported to the operator separately, with a prefilled upstream issue link; not opening it myself.)

## What the guard must do (and the duplication trap)
The pre-paint guard cannot import public/theme.mjs: modules are always deferred, which is the very thing being fixed. So any guard REPLICATES the theme rule - `THEME_KEY = "voicebox:theme"`, the `light|dark|system` whitelist with unknown->light, the matchMedia resolution, and the two attribute names (`data-theme` = effective, `data-theme-mode` = preference). That is a second computing site for the same facts, which is exactly what `scripts/single-owner.mjs` exists to refuse (its own header: "TWO PLACES COMPUTING THE SAME ANSWER").

Three routes, in order of increasing machinery:
- A. STATIC guard + agreement test (recommended, least machinery): a tiny `public/theme-boot.js` as a classic script in head, plus a unit test that asserts its copy of the key, the whitelist and the attribute names equal theme.mjs's exports. No generation, no CSP change, and the duplication is test-enforced rather than hoped for.
- B. GENERATED guard (strictest single-owner): index.html is ALREADY templated at serve time (server.mjs:4259 replaces `__VOICEBOX_BUILD_STAMP__` and `__VOICEBOX_SESSION_TOKEN__`) and at build time (vite.config.js:209). A `__VOICEBOX_THEME_BOOT__` placeholder could be substituted with source derived from theme.mjs, so nothing is duplicated at all. Costs a placeholder in two pipelines plus a route (or an inline+hash, below).
- C. INLINE guard + CSP hash: keeps the guidance's literal shape with zero extra requests, but requires adding `'sha256-...'` to the meta policy AND a test that recomputes the hash from the script bytes, because a hash that silently stops matching is a fix that silently stops working. Do NOT add `'unsafe-inline'` under any route - that weakens the policy for the whole page to fix one 6-line script.

## First-paint acceptance, designed (this is the part that must not be hand-waved)
Deterministic design, prototyped already:
- Inject at DOCUMENT-START via CDP, before any page script runs, a recorder that captures `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` inside the FIRST `requestAnimationFrame` callback (rAF callbacks run before the first paint) and the FCP from `PerformanceObserver('paint')`.
- Cases: (1) `voicebox:theme="dark"` -> themeAtFirstRaf MUST be "dark"; (2) "light" -> "light"; (3) "system" with emulated `prefers-color-scheme: dark` -> "dark"; (4) nothing stored -> "light" at FCP with no regression (the control that must stay green).
- NEGATIVE CONTROL, mandatory: the same test run against the CURRENT tree must FAIL case (1) with themeAtFirstRaf === "light". Without that, the test could pass on a broken implementation - the same mutant discipline used for ri9x.
- The assertion is on the value at the first rAF, not on "dark eventually": every bug in this class still ends up dark, just too late, so an "eventually dark" assertion is vacuous.
- Lane: this needs the quoted `"cdp.mjs"` signal to be classified BROWSER (scripts/test-lanes.mjs:61-65); the default is LIVE, so a guard test that lands in the wrong lane silently never runs. One browser at a time, closed in a finally.

## Security checklist for whichever route
- No `'unsafe-inline'`; if inline, the hash is added to script-src and test-enforced.
- The guard reads ONE localStorage key, whitelists to light|dark|system, and NEVER interpolates a read value into an attribute without that whitelist - so a poisoned localStorage value cannot reach the DOM.
- Wrap the storage read in try/catch: blocked site data must not throw before paint (theme.mjs already try/catches on write).
- Keep it to the theme and nothing else: it runs on every page load before anything has been parsed.
- Degradation, worth designing in: add `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` to style.css so that if the guard throws or fails to load, the page degrades to the OS scheme rather than to a scheme the person explicitly rejected. This is defence in depth, not a substitute for the guard.

## Verified while scoping, so the implementer does not have to re-derive it
- theme.mjs does NOT commit the guidance's named anti-pattern: there is no `removeItem` anywhere, so the stored value is never deleted when the system preference happens to coincide.
- theme.mjs:37 resolves system via matchMedia and :84 re-applies on change; ri9x's browser test covers that.
- SEPARATE GAP, not xpwt, do not bundle: the guidance also asks the override to follow another tab via a `storage` listener, and there is none anywhere in public/. That is cross-tab sync, a different behaviour from FOUC; it should be its own bead.

## Cost and gates for the eventual change
Touches public/index.html, a new tiny guard (+ its test, browser lane), possibly public/style.css and, only for route B, server.mjs + vite.config.js. docs-touched will fire: docs/00, docs/07 and docs/08 all describe index.html, so the change updates them in the same commit (Paul's rule, voicebox-beads-ths).

This is a REFINEMENT, not a redesign: per the skill, "Refinement preserves; redesign replaces... keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope". So the fix changes only WHEN the theme is applied, never what it looks like: no palette, spacing, typography, icon or copy change. (Note: craft-floor.md is explicitly for "immediately before any UI edit" and says "do not load it for planning-only work" - correctly not loaded here; the implementer must load it before touching index.html.)

THE BAR, from the skill's own theming rubric (reference/audit.md): the top score is "4=Excellent (full token system, dark mode works perfectly)", and the rubric names two relevant defects - "Broken dark mode" and "Theme switching issues: Values that don't update on theme change". A first-paint flash is exactly a case of dark mode not working perfectly: the values are correct eventually, so any check that samples after settle scores it 4 and misses it. This is why the acceptance must sample at the FIRST rAF (previous comment), not after the theme settles - the Impeccable lens and the acceptance design agree on that point.

THE CORRECTION IMPECCABLE FORCES ON THE GUIDANCE'S MECHANISM, and it is not cosmetic: Modern Web Guidance's FOUC example sets the CONTENT OF THE `color-scheme` META and relies on `light-dark()` to follow. This repo drives its whole token set from `:root[data-theme="light"]` / `:root[data-theme="dark"]` custom properties (style.css:5-31), and only two rules in style.css use light-dark(). A guard that only set the meta's content would therefore fix UA-painted surfaces (scrollbars, form controls) while leaving the page's OWN tokens light - the page would still flash, and the flash would be mixed. The guard must set the attribute the tokens actually read: `data-theme` (effective scheme) AND `data-theme-mode` (the stored preference), which is precisely what theme.mjs's applyTheme does. Getting this wrong is a plausible outcome of following the guidance literally here, and it is the reason the guard needs an agreement test with theme.mjs rather than a copied one-liner.

PRODUCT GROUNDING, from PRODUCT.md rather than generic UX language - the product already commits to this behaviour, so the flash is a product regression, not a nicety: "Let the user leave and return without losing the objects, the active work or the unanswered decisions." A stored theme is exactly such retained state; painting light to a person who chose dark is the interface briefly presenting a state that is not theirs, on every return.

EDGE CASES the harden lens adds to the security checklist (reference/harden.md):
- Storage unavailable or throwing (site data blocked, private modes): the guard must still paint a defensible theme and must not break the page. Fall back to the OS scheme, which is what the CSS media-query degradation buys.
- No-JS at all: the page stays usable and should follow the OS where possible - another argument for the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback rather than relying on the guard alone.
- A guard that throws must degrade to the OS scheme, never to a scheme the person explicitly rejected.
- Do not let the guard become a second place that owns the theme: agreement test with theme.mjs (see the single-owner point in my previous comment).

PRODUCT-RELEVANT SIDE FINDING, now worth more than a footnote: PRODUCT.md says "Several live instances may work on the same machine-backed project" and "A confirmation can be answered from another live instance of the same project" - so multiple live tabs are an intended usage, not an edge case. The missing cross-tab `storage` listener (guidance asks for it; there is none in public/) therefore has product weight. Still a SEPARATE behaviour from FOUC and still not bundled here - it wants its own bead, now with this product citation.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN CSP CLAIM, caught by voicebox-rev-xpwt's note and now fixed. Recording it because the bead's earlier comments contain the imprecise version and I do not want the record to keep a claim I know is wrong.

WHAT WAS WRONG: I had placed theme-boot.js ABOVE the Content-Security-Policy meta in index.html, and a `<meta>` CSP governs only resources fetched AFTER it is parsed. Two consequences, both mine:
1. The guard sat OUTSIDE the page's policy, which is the opposite of what my own comment asserted ("it keeps the policy strict rather than weakening the whole page"). A script above the meta is not governed by it at all.
2. My headline claim — "the page's own CSP blocks the guidance's inline script" — was imprecise. An inline guard placed where the Modern Web Guidance recipe says (immediately after the color-scheme meta) would ALSO have been above the policy, and so would NOT have been blocked either. The CSP argument only holds for a guard placed BELOW the meta, which is what I have now done.

THE FIX, at f33a154: the tag now sits below the CSP meta. This is both correct and, unlike before, PROVABLE. Driven in a real browser (not read off the code): an inline script added after the meta does NOT run — CSP genuinely enforced — while this same-origin file loads with status 200 and the theme is applied before the first frame. So the guard is demonstrably INSIDE script-src 'self' rather than escaping it, and the external-file form is required for the precise reason I originally gave, only now it is measured.

RE-VERIFIED AFTER THE MOVE: the four first-paint cases still pass, the parity test still agrees with theme.mjs, docs-check OK, and the browser-driven CSP check above. No other behaviour changed; the pre-paint guarantee is unaffected (still a classic, non-deferred script in <head>).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: had I left it, the bead would have shipped a guard that escaped the page's own security policy while claiming to be protected by it, and a future reader changing the CSP would have had no idea this file was outside it. The reviewer's note was worth more than the rest of the review.

NOTE ON THE UPSTREAM GUIDANCE ISSUE: the placement subtlety also sharpens the report I drafted for Modern Web Guidance. The guide's inline recipe is blocked when the CSP meta precedes the script, and escapes the policy when it does not — either way the guide does not mention CSP, and it should say which side of the policy the guard belongs on.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
CLOSING THE ONE PLAUSIBLE HOLE IN THE PRE-PAINT CLAIM before the reviewer does: could public/sw.js delay theme-boot.js past the first paint? Checked against the code, not assumed.

1. ON THE FIRST LOAD THERE IS NO SERVICE WORKER AT ALL. The worker is registered from public/fused.js:161, i.e. after the page's module scripts run, so the very load this guard exists to fix is not controlled by a SW. The first-time-visitor case — the one where a flash is most noticeable — cannot be affected.

2. ON LATER LOADS IT IS CONTROLLED AND STILL ORDERED CORRECTLY. sw.js calls skipWaiting() (:23) and clients.claim() (:38), and its fetch handler is network-first (event.respondWith(fetch(event.request), :42/:63) with a cache fallback (:75). So a controlled reload fetches this asset through the SW. That can make the guard arrive LATER, but it cannot make it run AFTER paint: theme-boot.js is a classic, non-deferred script in <head>, so the parser blocks on it and nothing is rendered until it has executed. The guarantee this bead rests on is an ORDERING guarantee, not a speed one — the SW can move the clock, not the sequence.

3. THE BOUNDED CAVEAT, stated honestly rather than buried: sw.js falls back to caches.match("./index.html") (:78) when the network fails, so an offline or lie-fi load can be served a CACHED index.html. If that cached document predates this change, its markup has no guard tag and it will flash — because that document's markup is what runs. That is a cache-freshness property of serving any cached document, not something this change introduces, and it is not fixable from the guard. Worth knowing before anyone reads 'offline still flashes' as a failure of this fix.

No action taken on sw.js: it does not need to change, and I did not touch it.

LANDING LESSON (my own error, worth one line of record): the landing message's RELEASE-NOTE section shows two `none:` lines and OMITS the real user-facing note, and the cause is a bug in how I wrote the trailers rather than in the tooling.

WHAT HAPPENED: `fleet-land-message` reads Release-note trailers with `git interpret-trailers --parse` per commit. That parser only accepts a trailer block in which EVERY line is a trailer line, and I let two of my values wrap:

  Release-note: Reloading no longer flashes the wrong theme. The theme you chose is applied before the page
  is first painted, instead of a moment after.

The second line has no `token:` prefix, so git rejected the WHOLE block — silently. Verified per commit: 5b30296 -> [] (the real note, dropped), 7d5df06 -> [] (dropped), f33a154 -> parsed, edf315f -> parsed. So the branch's most important note is the one that vanished, and the only two that survived say `none:`.

FIX FOR NEXT TIME, cheap and checkable before pushing: make every Release-note trailer a SINGLE line (no wrapping), and confirm with `git log -1 --format=%B <sha> | git interpret-trailers --parse`. It is silent when wrong, which is exactly why it needs checking rather than remembering.

WHY I DID NOT REWRITE IT: fixing it needs the tip commit's message changed, and the review verdict keys on the commit SHA — `fleet-land-message` reports reviewed_sha vs tip_sha and unreviewed_commits, so a tree-identical amend still reads as an unreviewed commit (measured: I amended to 3fd545f with an identical tree aa5bf81e, and the tool would have called it stale). That would cost a fifth reviewer lane to re-assert a commit-message line, while the user-facing note is already delivered to Paul in the USER-VISIBLE EFFECT section of the same landing message. I reverted to the reviewed tip edf315f instead. If the merger would rather have a clean RELEASE-NOTE block than a clean verdict chain, say so and I will re-tip and re-review it properly.

comments.text:
EVIDENCE FOR THE SECOND UNION FAILURE, as coord asked: cached gate trace, regression-vs-inherited, hypothesis, and what I could not reproduce. Fix is 4330bcf (pushed); rev-xpwt5 is reviewing it.

## 1. The cached gate trace, read rather than assumed
From the merger's own gate record for the union, tree aed3ff34e5fb464610a7f963ed91a5a7b498e1b6 (commit 2ec47da), at /home/exedev/.fleet/checks/aed3ff34e5fb464610a7f963ed91a5a7b498e1b6.{json,log}:
- state FAIL, kind full, lane merger, rc 1, secs 147, cmd `VOICEBOX_GATE_UNIT_SECS=300 VOICEBOX_GATE_LIVE_SECS=1200 npm run gate`.
- The failure is `tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs:127:10`, failureType testCodeFailure, ERR_ASSERTION, strictEqual, actual `null`, expected `'Agent Progress Tracker'`, message "'open agent tracker' mounts the Agent Progress Tracker mini-app — it had no handler before ucak".
- The file's own duration was 2548ms and that test 2421ms, and the log brackets it with `[shards] ---- end tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs ----`, so it ran as a shard worker. A 2.4s run is NOT a timeout: the read happened and found nothing.

## 2. REGRESSION OR INHERITED: inherited, and this is deterministic rather than statistical
`git diff --stat origin/main 6e9fd29 -- tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs` is EMPTY. xpwt never touched that file before 4330bcf, so the exact racy form that failed in the union gate is main's own code, landed with ucak. A clean-main control cannot differ from the failing artefact because the artefact IS clean main's text.
What xpwt plausibly did was change the PROBABILITY, not the defect: this branch adds tests/theme-first-paint.test.mjs, so the browser lane has one more file and every worker carries more load under the same four-way width. That is the honest account of why it surfaced on this union and not on the last one.

## 3. The hypothesis, stated so it can be falsified
H1: the read races an ASYNCHRONOUS effect. `openAgentProgressTracker()` (public/fused.js:4576) awaits `fetch("/apps/agent-monitor.html")` and `res.text()`, and only then calls `miniAppController.mount(...)`, which creates `#mini-app-outer-frame` and sets its title at :6024. The test's `say()` returns when the TURN lands, which is the right signal for every other command in that file because they apply synchronously - it is the wrong signal for this one.
H1 predicts: on an idle machine the title is present before the read (so serial runs pass), and under CPU starvation the mount's continuation lands after the read (so the gate fails). Both predictions match what was observed.

## 4. What I tried to reproduce, and the honest result
- Serial, current and old form: passes. 6 instrumented idle runs: the title was already present the instant the turn landed, every time.
- Three-way and four-way browser concurrency: passes, repeatedly.
- Network throttling (latency 600ms) to widen the race: DID NOT widen it, because it slows the turn POST by the same amount, so the ordering is preserved. This is why I am not claiming a reproduction.
- A faithful repro would need to slow only the mount's fetch - which needs CDP Fetch interception, and tests/lib/cdp.mjs exposes no event API to continue paused requests. I stopped there rather than build a second CDP client for it.
So: no reproduction. The case rests on section 3 (the code path) and section 2 (the file is main's), not on a failing run I produced.

## 5. The fix, and why it is not vacuous
4330bcf waits for the effect with a bound (`page.waitFor`, 15s default) and then asserts. It does not weaken the assertion, and that is PROVED rather than argued: with `miniAppController.mount(` disabled by mutant, the test fails with "timed out waiting for the Agent Progress Tracker mini-app mounted", i.e. a dead branch still fails exactly as the ucak bug did. fused.js was restored, diff clean. After the fix: 2/2 alone, 5/5 twice at --test-concurrency=4.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text: LAND-SUMMARY WHAT: public/theme-boot.js is a new, tiny CLASSIC script (no type=module, no defer, no async) loaded from AFTER the Content-Security-Policy meta, so the stored light/dark/system choice reaches data-theme and data-theme-mode before the first paint. public/index.html gains that one tag; tests/theme-boot-parity.test.mjs drives the guard and public/theme.mjs through the same fake DOM over one matrix and fails on any disagreement, so the guard's deliberate restatement of the storage key, the whitelist, the matchMedia resolution and the two attribute names cannot drift; tests/theme-first-paint.test.mjs asserts the theme AND the computed color-scheme inside the first requestAnimationFrame. docs/07, docs/00 and README.md describe the guard, why its placement below the CSP meta is load-bearing, and the degradation cases it does not cover. WHAT: SECURITY, and the reason the file form is required rather than merely preferred: the guard is a same-origin EXTERNAL classic script, so it OBEYS the page's own Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self'), and no 'unsafe-inline', nonce or hash was added to make it work — the policy is unchanged. Measured in a real browser rather than argued: an inline script added after the meta does NOT run, while this same-origin file loads 200 and applies the theme before the first frame, so the guard is demonstrably INSIDE the policy rather than escaping it. This SUPERSEDES this branch's earlier commits, which had the tag ABOVE the CSP meta — a position that left the guard OUTSIDE the policy entirely, because a CSP governs only what is fetched after it is parsed. Moving the tag below the meta is what makes the claim provable instead of asserted; the pre-CSP placement in commits 5b30296 and 7d5df06 is superseded and must not be restored. WHAT: ALSO IN THIS BRANCH, and distinct from the theme work: a test-readiness fix in tests/system-command-browser.test.mjs (voicebox-beads-fxl7). Its agent-tracker assertion read a title that an async mount sets only after openAgentProgressTracker() awaits a fetch of /apps/agent-monitor.html (public/fused.js:4576), so the read raced the fetch, and the merger's four-worker union gate caught it once as "expected 'Agent Progress Tracker', got null". That file was untouched by this branch before the fix - the racy form is main's own, landed with ucak - so this removes a pre-existing flake for everyone. The fix waits for the effect with a bound; non-vacuity is proved by disabling the mount and watching the test fail with "timed out waiting for the Agent Progress Tracker mini-app mounted". Test-only, no product file changed. HONEST LIMIT: this is a hypothesis-backed invariant fix, not a reproduction of the original race - no reproduction was obtained, by the author or by two reviewers. WHAT: Verified rather than asserted. The negative control is mandatory and was run: with the guard absent the dark case fails at the first frame ("First frame was light at 43ms (bg rgb(251, 251, 249))"). Eight hostile stored values (attribute-quote splitting, , __proto__, 5000 chars, newline) all resolved to light with no attribute injected, and an independent reviewer killed four non-equivalent parity mutants (wrong key, fallback-to-dark, whitelist accepting auto, missing themeMode). WHY: The theme was applied by public/theme.mjs, which fused.js imports — and module scripts are always deferred, so the apply ran after the first paint. A person who chose dark was painted light first, on every single load. There was no CSS-only fix: index.html hardcoded data-theme="light", and style.css puts the entire light token set on an un-attributed :root with no prefers-color-scheme query, so the document is light until JavaScript runs. EFFECT: Reloading no longer flashes the wrong scheme — the chosen theme, including the browser-drawn surfaces (scrollbars, caret, text selection, form controls), is correct from the first frame instead of a moment after it. Nothing else changes visually; no palette, spacing or typography is touched, and the Content-Security-Policy is unchanged with no 'unsafe-inline'. Three gaps are deliberately EXCLUDED and filed separately rather than silently bundled: the no-JS and guard-throws OS-scheme fallback (voicebox-beads-7xse), cross-tab theme sync (voicebox-beads-vtf3), and the offline case where public/sw.js serves a cached index.html whose markup predates this guard (that document's markup is what runs, so it still flashes — a cache-freshness property, not something the guard can reach).

title: ADR: Decompose server.mjs HTTP routing into lib/routes/ domain modules
close_reason: Completed: ADR adopted, domain routes decomposed into lib/routes/ and route harness/change-detection finalized in ybwq

comments.author: voicebox-audioflake
comments.text:
READ-ONLY ADR DISPOSITION / proposed ONE next child slice (no claim or source/test edit, no suite). r9hv description is empty: do NOT treat the title as blanket authorization to decompose all of server.mjs. Accept only INCREMENTAL domain seams on gdq2 after owner approval. Main 372aed3 family map: routes table server.mjs:3603-4282 still owns presence (GET/POST), agents/fleet/harnesses/tasks/tools, key/settings/activity, Gemini endpoints, root/health/changelog and fixed pages/static; handle() :4376-5180 owns root declaration, audit/undo, mini-app CRUD/tool, delegation/exec/transport/task, environments/probe/turn/agent updates, permissions/pair/bootstrap/call/execute. lib/routes/workspace.mjs and extensions.mjs are separate exact dispatch owners. Credential/mutation/image/exec and static/CSP modules are poor first slices.
SMALLEST USEFUL NEXT SLICE proposal for NEW CHILD bead only AFTER shard security branch lands and coord approves: extract exactly the contiguous GET /api/presence + POST /api/presence table entries (~60 lines :3604-3661) into lib/routes/presence.mjs via createPresenceRoutes({roomPresence,json,readJsonBody,answerOnce,broadcastChannel}), spread into routes at the same table position; keep createRoomPresenceCoordinator() and WebSocket broadcast owner in server.mjs. Do not catch BodyRefusal or duplicate parser/auth. Negative HTTP controls in focused new test + existing tests/room-presence.test.mjs: GET empty snapshot 200, POST requestFloor without participantId ->409 invalid-participant plus unchanged snapshot; malformed/non-object JSON ->400 bad-request, wrong content type ->415, >default 1MiB ->413, all no state/broadcast; valid join + heartbeat + caption + leave and GET snapshots with exact status/payload, unknown /api/presenceX route not swallowed. comments.author: voicebox-coord
comments.text: COORD DISPATCH: type-recover read-only ADR on server.mjs HTTP routing decomposition, bounded plan/test seams and collision/speed impact; no overlapping edits with CSP implementation. Record decision and follow-up implementation beads, then release claim.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
READ-ONLY ADR (type-recover, 2026-10-14). No source, test or doc edits; measured on fresh origin/main (5859 lines, routes table 3749-4185, handle() 4209-5081). Nine route modules already exist (activity, agents-read, branches, changelog, doctor, extensions, harnesses, presence, workspace) — so the previous lane's proposed presence slice has LANDED and is not re-proposed here.

1. THE SPEED FINDING, MEASURED, AND IT IS NEGATIVE — READ THIS FIRST.
Mapped test closure per changed file (scripts/test-changed.mjs --dry-run, origin/main tree):
  server.mjs                156 tests (unit 24 / server 58 / browser 74)
  lib/routes/extensions.mjs 150
  lib/routes/workspace.mjs  138      lib/routes/harnesses.mjs 138      lib/routes/branches.mjs 138      lib/routes/doctor.mjs 138
  lib/routes/presence.mjs   137      lib/routes/changelog.mjs 137      lib/routes/activity.mjs 137      lib/routes/agents-read.mjs 137
Composition of lib/routes/presence.mjs's 137: 3 tests name presence.mjs, 2 name lib/room-presence.mjs, and **137 name server.mjs**. That last edge is the whole closure, and it is structural, not accidental: the mapper treats lib/, tools/, core/ and server.mjs as intermediate importers, so the moment server.mjs imports a route module, server.mjs becomes an importer of it and drags in every test that names server.mjs. Extracting a route therefore buys 156 -> ~137, about 12%, and cannot go lower. (Contrast public/components/*: the mapper does NOT scan public/, so a public/ module has no importer edge — which is why the mvxl extraction got a 1-2 test closure while a lib/routes module cannot.)
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ADR: decomposing server.mjs's HTTP routing does NOT make the fast gate faster. Do not justify these slices by gate time, and do not promise it. If the hub wants fused.js-style speed wins for server.mjs, the lever is the selector policy (137 test files name server.mjs), which is a separate decision already escalated — I have filed it as its own bead rather than smuggling it into an extraction.

2. THE COLLISION FINDING, MEASURED, AND IT IS THE REAL JUSTIFICATION.
Commits touching each file in the last 30 days (origin/main): server.mjs **214**, public/fused.js 190, lib/routes/presence.mjs 1, lib/routes/workspace.mjs 1, lib/routes/extensions.mjs 2. So server.mjs is the repo's single hottest file and every route module is cold. That, plus ownership clarity, is why these slices are worth doing — merge-collision reduction, not gate time.

3. WHAT IS LEFT AND ITS COUPLING (measured per group: module-level deps called, and whether it writes module-level mutable state).
  · tools  3864-3881 (18 lines): deps json, listTools/searchTools, reads `active` root. NO mutable writes. Test owner: tests/tool-index.test.mjs (1 file names /api/tools).
  · fleet  3752-3779 (28 lines): GET /api/fleet + POST /api/fleet/contact. deps json, readJsonBody, fleetManager, publicFleetProjection. NO mutable writes. 2 test owners.
  · gemini 3947-4036 (90 lines): capabilities/image/video/embed. deps json, readJsonBody, answerOnce, resolveActive. NO mutable writes. **0 existing test owners** (no test names /api/gemini) and it calls external media APIs (cost/credentials).
  · keys 3882-3920 (39 lines): credential READ and WRITE (apiKeysStatusPayload / writePersistedApiKeys). NOT a first slice.
  · agent-settings 3921-3946 (26 lines): deps as keys PLUS it WRITES the module-level `agentSettings` binding — moving it means moving state. NOT a first slice.
  · tasks 3780-3863 (84 lines): 9 module-level deps including activateHarnessInProcess + broadcastChannel; delegation authority. NOT a first slice.
  · root+health 4037-4114 (78 lines): WRITES module-level `active` and `liveProjectContext`; /api/root is host-owned authority (36 test files name /api/root). NOT a first slice.
  · static/pages 4115-4185 (71 lines): **FENCED.** Touches cspReportOnlyHeaders and resolvePublicFile; overlaps gate-recover/CSP work in flight. No extraction here, per coord's constraint and the previous lane's note.
handle() (4209-5081) is much worse: bootstrap, audit/undo, mini-apps CRUD/tools, delegate, exec, transport import/export, turn, agents PATCH, permissions pending/resolve, pair/complete, git surfaces, call, execute — authority-bearing throughout (exec/pair/call/bootstrap/permissions/delegate). Nothing in it is a good first slice.

4. RECOMMENDED SLICE ORDER (implementation beads filed separately, unassigned so coord can sequence):
  #1 **GET /api/tools -> lib/routes/tool-catalog.mjs** (18 lines, 2 deps + a live root read, no state writes, existing test owner). A PILOT, not a size win: take it because it proves the seam shape on a read-only route at near-zero risk.
  #2 **fleet routes -> lib/routes/fleet.mjs** (28 lines, no state writes). Requires an explicit decision on /api/fleet/contact's cross-environment authority — named, not hidden.
  #3 **gemini media -> lib/routes/gemini-media.mjs** (90 lines, the only substantive group with no state writes), but only with a NEW focused test (there is no existing owner) and with the external-API cost named in its bead.
Seam shape for all three, from the established modules: a factory createXxxRoutes({...deps}) exported from the module and spread into the routes table at the SAME table position, so dispatch order and the global auth wall are untouched.
Test seam per slice: the focused test must assert (a) the exact status/payload for the route's success shape, (b) that the route still reads the dynamic active root at request time where applicable (not a snapshot), and (c) one NEGATIVE control — an unknown sibling spelling (e.g. /api/toolsX) must NOT be swallowed by the new module, i.e. must still fall through to the existing 404/no-such-route behaviour. Existing owners (tool-index.test.mjs, the 2 fleet-naming files) keep driving behaviour unchanged.

5. WHAT THIS ADR DOES NOT CLAIM: no source edits were made; no suite was run (read-only task); the coupling counts come from reading each group's lines and are stated as counts of named deps, not guesses; and the speed finding is a measurement of the CURRENT mapper, not a proposal to change it. If a future selector fix removes the server.mjs importer edge, revisit section 1 — the ranking in section 4 survives either way because it is a risk ordering, not a speed one.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text: IMPLEMENTATION FOLLOW-UPS FILED (unassigned deliberately, so coord sequences them; I yielded rather than claiming any):  GET /api/tools pilot,  fleet routes,  Gemini media, and a separate decision bead voicebox-beads-njeb for the selector/importer-edge finding that is the ADR's speed section. The pilot is the one to take first: it is read-only, has 2 deps and an existing test owner, and proves the seam shape. None of the three promises a fast-gate speed win — see section 1 of this ADR.

comments.author: voicebox-type-recover
comments.text:
CORRECTION + UPGRADE TO THE SECTION-3/4 RECOMMENDATION (same read-only session, after a structural scout's report which I then verified line by line). Two things in my first record were wrong or weaker than the house standard, and section 3's numbers for one group were wrong.

(a) MY DEP COUNT FOR /api/tools WAS WRONG. Section 3 said "2 deps + a live root read". Reading the 18 lines in full, the GET /api/tools handler needs: activeMiniAppRegistry.getAllTools(), harnessInventory(), listHarnessesWithConfiguredAgents(inv, agentRegistry), the LIVE `active` root read, the ROOT constant, and searchTools/listTools, plus json — about nine deps, including TWO registries. My counting script had missed imported functions and singletons because it only matched identifiers declared at column 0 in server.mjs. The deps are all READS (no mutable writes), so the group still passes the hard filter, but it is not the low-dependency slice I described.

(b) FLEET, read in full (3752-3778), is genuinely the lower-coupling group: seven named deps (fleetManager, publicFleetProjection, json, readJsonBody, answerOnce, createHash from node:crypto, SELF_ENVIRONMENT), zero module-level mutable writes, contiguous, and it has a direct test owner (tests/fleet-addressability.test.mjs). REVISED ORDERING with a decision rule rather than a preference: **fleet first, tools second — UNLESS the owner rules that POST /api/fleet/contact's cross-environment authority must stay host-owned.** That handler forwards `req.headers.authorization` as a bearer and computes a sha256 authority hash before calling fleetManager.contact, and the refusal mapping (403 for cross-environment-unauthorized/environment-not-paired, else 400) is authority semantics. If that ruling is "stays in server.mjs", take tools first (read-only, GET only) and drop the contact entry from any fleet slice; if the ruling is "may move behind an injected fleetManager", fleet is the better pilot because it exercises the factory seam with FEWER things handed over. I have written this same condition onto both child beads rather than leaving the ordering implicit.

(c) MY TEST-SEAM REQUIREMENT WAS WEAKER THAN THIS REPO'S ESTABLISHED PATTERN. tests/agents-read-route-seam.test.mjs is the house standard and it is stronger than the "success + negative control" list in section 4:
  1. a source-wiring assertion on server.mjs that pins the EXACT factory call with its dep names, the EXACT spread order (`...presenceRoutes, ...agentsReadRoutes, "GET /api/fleet":` is the position a fleet extraction must preserve), that NO inline key may shadow the factory, and that the host's separate privileged POST for the same path is still present;
  2. SELF-PROVING MUTANTS inside that assertion's own test — it builds a missing-spread mutant and a duplicate-inline mutant and asserts the wiring check throws for each, so the guard cannot silently stop working;
  3. behavioural assertions against the factory directly with injected fakes (fresh host read per request, filtering, and no secret ever leaving the projection).
Section 4's list stands as a minimum; this is what "verifiable on its own without narrowing coverage" actually looks like here, and the child beads now carry it.

(d) FENCE CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY (section 3's FENCED entry): cspReportOnlyHeaders at 2251, canonicalPublicPath 2235, CSP policy/paths 2224-2232, resolvePublicFile 2318, CSP call sites 4152 (GET /) and 4261 (static fallthrough), and there is NO /api/csp-report endpoint. The global loopback auth wall is 4224-4252 and runs BEFORE any dispatch, so no slice may move, duplicate or re-implement it. The static/pages entries 4115-4185 stay untouched, as coord required.

No source, test or doc edits were made; this is a record correction. Nothing else in the ADR changes: the headline speed finding (156 -> ~137 floor, because server.mjs stays an importer of every lib/routes module) and the collision case (214 commits/30d vs 1-2) stand, and the section-4 ranking is a risk ordering, not a speed one.

comments.text: COORD ADR ACCEPTED: route extraction is collision reduction, NOT fast-gate speed; measured importer edge ~137 tests per lib/routes module. Pilot read-only GET /api/tools first, fenced CSP/static untouched; fleet contact authority requires separate ruling. Parent tracks child slices and stays open until pilot evidence.

title: A startServer() child can outlive a fully green browser-tier run (found while measuring voicebox-beads-hhkg)
description:
FOUND WHILE MEASURING voicebox-beads-hhkg (not caused by it, and not specific to the shard runner — the same file leaks under the serial lane).

A voicebox server from tests/lib/server.mjs survived a FULLY GREEN browser-tier run:
  PID 1242652  started 21:24:55  ppid 1  cwd /home/exedev/worktrees/voicebox-shard
  cmd  /usr/bin/node /home/exedev/worktrees/voicebox-shard/server.mjs
  env  PORT=0  VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/tmp/voicebox-ext-wSjitt
The plain `voicebox-ext-` prefix with no suffix is unique to tests/lib/server.mjs:131 (every other mkdtemp site uses a suffixed prefix), so this was a bare startServer() call. At 21:24:55 the only thing running was the counted browser-lane arm (63 files, `node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-concurrency=4`), which exited 0 with 249 tests / 247 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped. So the server outlived a run in which no file failed and nothing was killed.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT: tests/lib/server.mjs reaps its children on `exit` and on SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, and a test's own after/finally/t.after calls stop() — every browser-lane file that starts a server also names stop() somewhere, so the gap is conditional (a hook that did not run, or a stop() that returned past STOP_BOUND_MS at 2000ms without waiting the child out), not a missing call anyone can grep for.

IMPACT: an orphan holds its ephemeral port, its scratch extensions directory and a copy of the host token file, and `ppid 1` means the VM reaper is the only thing that will ever collect it.

NEXT ACTION: reproduce by running `npm run test:live` (or just the browser tier) repeatedly while watching `pgrep -f '<worktree>/server.mjs'`, then find the fixture whose cleanup misses and make the reason explicit at that site. Do NOT "fix" it by adding a global sweep — tests/lib/server.mjs is deliberately the one owner of child reaping and the note at tests/lib/server.mjs:100 says why a leaked directory is preferred to a delete that races a live writer.
close_reason: Landed origin/main 70c1e0b, reviewer PASS and full union gate PASS; original orphan cause unknown

comments.author: voicebox-audioflake
comments.text:
READ-ONLY ownership/cleanup map (unclaimed; no browser while merger gate runs): tests/lib/server.mjs:124-221 is sole startServer owner. It spawns detached process group with private scratch extensions dir and registers child in LIVE_CHILDREN at :163; stop() at :173 calls reap(child), waits exitOf up to 2000ms and retries kill, but reap() at :36-48 removes child from LIVE_CHILDREN immediately after sending SIGKILL, before observing child exit. process exit/signal fallback walks only LIVE_CHILDREN, so if neither kill attempt yields exit (e.g. process-group kill/fallback fail, uninterruptible state), stop() returns with live child and no tracked last-chance cleanup; it deliberately leaves scratch directory on timeout. This is a deterministic STATE-MACHINE leak precondition, not proven as cause of the shard PID 1242652 incident (kill normally works and test.after calls stop in browser fixtures). All 9 obvious optional-stop files inspected use test.after or finally; no missing site established. Do NOT claim kill failure occurred from the existing PID evidence.

title: Decompose public/fused.js UI monolith
description:
Rationale
`public/fused.js` is 311KB and was modified 123 times in the last 30 days. It is the second largest collision hotspot and centralizes frontend logic.

Cost
~1.5 lane-days. Extract logical UI components into separate modules under `public/components/` or similar, reducing the single-file blast radius.

Who
`implementer`

Risk if we do nothing
UI feature agents will block each other on git conflicts in `fused.js`.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
READ-ONLY SCOPE (coord request). No edits, no branch, NOT claimed. Every claim below was checked in this tree and is cited; the structural sweep was a scout subagent (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash), and I re-verified its load-bearing claims myself rather than passing them on.

## Shape
public/fused.js is 6957 lines / 311238 bytes, an ES module whose only top-level imports are ./debug-transcript.js, ./room-folder-ops.js and ./window-manager.mjs (fused.js:8-10). Entry is public/index.html:18 (`<script type="module" src="fused.js">`).
SERVING NEEDS NO REGISTRATION: any regular file under public/ is served by resolvePublicFile (server.mjs:2216, called at 4273 and 4329) and `.mjs` is already text/javascript (server.mjs:2157, next to `.js` at 2156). So a new public/theme.mjs is fetched by native ES module resolution with no server or manifest change.

## Smallest independent extraction: the theme preference block, fused.js:152-200 (~49 lines)
Contains THEME_KEY (:153), applyTheme() (:154), and the boot wiring block (:181-200). Inbound references from OUTSIDE the block: exactly one, applyTheme at :243 inside the system-command dispatcher. Everything else is internal (:188, :191, :195, :198).
Shared mutable state: none — no `els`-cache object, no timer, no cache. Browser globals: localStorage, document.documentElement.dataset, matchMedia.
THE ONE REAL SEAM DECISION: applyTheme writes the cached elements (`els.themeSelect` :164-165, `els.themeSelectState` :167-168, `els.themeToggle` :171-178 including `querySelector("use")`), and the wiring block attaches handlers with the file's own `on()` helper (:186-:197). So the module must be HANDED those three elements (and an `on`/or its own listener calls), or look them up itself. Passing them in keeps the module ignorant of the WANTED dictionary and is the smaller contract; it also keeps the `WANTED`/`els` pins in help-dialog-modal and ptt-and-thinking-settings untouched, since those still describe fused.js.

## Affected tests — the binding constraint
THE BINDING ONE: tests/icon-sprite.test.mjs:68 asserts `fusedRefs.length >= 7 && pipRefs.length >= 2`. public/fused.js contains EXACTLY 7 icon literals — `#i-folder` x1, `#i-maximize` x2, `#i-minimize` x2, `#i-moon` x1, `#i-sun` x1 — so the floor has ZERO headroom. Two of them (`#i-sun`, `#i-moon`) sit at fused.js:179 INSIDE the theme block, so extracting it drops fused.js to 5 and FAILS :68.
THE FIX IS SANCTIONED, NOT A WEAKENING: the same file's header states the invariant — "the surface list below is hardcoded and complete TODAY (repo-wide grep). The invariant: if you add a file that names an icon, add it to the file list in the test below." So: read public/theme.mjs, add its refs to the `references` union (:76-80), lower the fused.js floor to >=5 and add a theme.mjs floor of >=2. The union check (:83-86) still demands every reference resolve to a defined sprite symbol, so coverage of the two moved literals is preserved rather than dropped.
Eight test files read public/fused.js as raw text: caption-fade-and-thinking, help-dialog-modal, icon-sprite, modern-web-room, project-switch-live-error, ptt-and-thinking-settings, room-folder-ops, ui-modern-polish. The scout counted 23 assertions pinned to fused.js CONTENT across them (these files hold many more asserts about other things; the count is its measurement, the icon-sprite floor is the one I verified). For the theme slice, icon-sprite is the only one that breaks.

## Does it need a browser gate?
Wiring is unit-verifiable (icon-sprite and the text pins are all unit-lane), but theme PERSISTENCE is only exercised in a real browser, through localStorage["voicebox:theme"]. The fast gate alone is therefore not sufficient evidence for this slice — one browser test must drive theme persistence, and the repo's own Functional Verification Mandate says a green unit gate is not "it works".

## Overlap with voicebox-audioflake (9c3r)
NONE for this slice. The theme block is ~3400 lines from the audio device code (fused.js:3627-3802) and shares nothing with public/audio-client.js. The single audio-adjacent line in the file is fused.js:3766 reading `window.__voiceboxLiveClient?.state?.playbackActive` — a different region, untouched.
WORTH KNOWING: the scout's second-best candidate by text-pin risk was the audio meters / waveform cluster (fused.js:5127-5430), which breaks ZERO of the text pins. It is also the one cluster that reads `window.__voiceboxLiveClient` (:5378) and drives requestAnimationFrame rendering, i.e. the cluster to DEFER until 9c3r closes, because it would add ambient audio-rendering load to an in-flight audio-timing investigation. Third candidate was reasonFrom/size/bytes (:1018-1030, 12 lines) with 23 call sites — no text-pin risk but negligible blast-radius gain.

## Constraints
scripts/single-owner.mjs declares two kinds of fact: ENV FACTS (owner lib/state-dirs.mjs) and CODE-SHAPE SITES (owner lib/path-auth.mjs). Frontend moves touch neither, so it stays green — but its header records that "the page cannot import lib/", so extracted frontend modules must live under public/ (public/components/ or public/*.mjs).
Precedent voicebox-beads-q0a3 (lib/path-auth.mjs out of server.mjs) is the shape to copy: one concern, an owner module, its own test file, and a declaration in the enforcement script so the fact cannot be re-implemented elsewhere.

## Recommendation
First slice: public/theme.mjs (fused.js:152-200), elements passed in as an argument, plus the icon-sprite repoint above. It proves the public/ ESM extraction path end to end at near-zero collision risk, ~1 file of production change. Larger slices (extensions/reader 1782-3110, room explorer 1133-1644) share the `els` cache and multiple mutable globals and are not independently extractable without a seam that passes state.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
BROWSER ACCEPTANCE DESIGN for the theme slice (coord request). Read-only design; nothing implemented, mvxl still unclaimed.

## What already exists, and it is a real baseline
tests/ux-bubble-stage.test.mjs is browser-lane and already drives the SELECT path properly: it reads #theme-select initial state (options system/light/dark, #theme-toggle present-and-hidden, light body bg), then dispatches a real `change` event with value "dark" and asserts data-theme="dark", data-theme-mode="dark", localStorage["voicebox:theme"]="dark", #theme-select-state text "Dark mode", and a changed computed body background; then "system" and back to "light" with the same assertions.
That covers applyTheme() and the select handler and the persist write — i.e. much of what moves.

## The gaps — each is code the extraction moves, and nothing covers it
1. BOOT RE-HYDRATION (fused.js:185-188: read localStorage, applyTheme(initialTheme)). NOTHING reloads with a stored theme. This is the highest-risk moved path because it runs on every page load, and it is exactly the "did the extraction keep the boot side working" question.
2. #theme-toggle CLICK (fused.js:186-190). ZERO coverage anywhere: ux-bubble only asserts the button is present and hidden; no test clicks it. Verified by grepping tests/ for theme-toggle.
3. matchMedia PREFERS-COLOR-SCHEME LISTENER (fused.js:198, system mode follows the OS). NOTHING drives it. It is drivable in the browser: CDP Emulation.setEmulatedMedia with prefers-color-scheme, then assert data-theme flips while data-theme-mode stays "system".
4. THE SYSTEM-COMMAND PATH (fused.js:242-243, applyTheme(cmd.theme, {persist:true})). Nothing drives the client with the real payload shape — and it is BROKEN today, filed as voicebox-beads-ucak with browser evidence.

## Proposed acceptance: tests/theme-browser.test.mjs, a browser-lane file owned by this slice
Shape it like the q0a3 precedent (lib/path-auth.mjs got its own tests/path-auth.test.mjs as the owner's surface), dedicated to the theme module rather than growing ux-bubble-stage's widget survey. Assertions:
1. first load with empty localStorage -> data-theme "light";
2. select -> dark, then system, then light: data-theme, data-theme-mode, localStorage["voicebox:theme"], and the state text (keep these — they are the moved behaviour and they must not regress);
3. RELOAD after storing "dark" -> data-theme is still "dark" and data-theme-mode "dark" (gap 1);
4. CLICK #theme-toggle from light -> flips to dark, persists to localStorage (gap 2);
5. system mode + emulated prefers-color-scheme:dark -> data-theme "dark", data-theme-mode stays "system"; then emulate light -> back (gap 3);
6. the SYSTEM-COMMAND path with the resolver's REAL shape — a turn whose text is "dark mode" -> data-theme "dark" and localStorage "dark" (gap 4, and it is the user-visible path that is broken today).

## LANE CONSTRAINT — verified in this tree, and it is easy to get wrong
A new test file only enters the browser lane if it carries a browser signal. scripts/test-lanes.mjs:61-65 defines BROWSER_SIGNALS as: a QUOTED value naming cdp.mjs (import, spawn argument, path.join segment), page-acceptance.mjs, or --remote-debugging-port/DevToolsActivePort. Classify every doubt as LIVE (the header says why). So the new file must reference the harness by a quoted "cdp.mjs" path or it lands in the UNIT lane, where a browser drive never runs and the acceptance is silently absent — the exact failure mode this design exists to avoid.
Cost: one more file in the browser tier (the tier is 114.5s wall on the merged tree; expect roughly +10-20s). It must NOT go on the ISOLATED list — that list is for CPU-contention casualties, not for lanes.

## Sequencing, and this matters
Land voicebox-beads-ucak's fix FIRST (or in the same landing): assertion 6 encodes the CORRECT behaviour, so a test written before the fix is red, and one written after the fix but without it is impossible. Accepting theme persistence while the theme VOICE command is dead would enshrine the wrong behaviour in the very test that is supposed to guard the module.

## Reminder for the icon-sprite repoint (already in the scope comment)
tests/icon-sprite.test.mjs:68 floors fused.js at >=7 refs while fused.js has EXACTLY 7, two of them (#i-sun, #i-moon) inside the theme block. Add public/theme.mjs to that file's scanned list and the references union, floor fused.js >=5 and theme.mjs >=2; the union check still requires every reference to resolve, so the moved literals stay covered. Its own header sanctions exactly this.
