title: Shard browser test tier via four long-lived server/browser pairs
description:
Context
The browser live lane takes ~396s sequentially because 43 test files (249 tests) each repeatedly provision and tear down their own `server.mjs` and Chromium instances via `startServer()` and `launch()`. Naive flag-only concurrency (`--test-concurrency=4`) starves 2-vCPU VMs due to concurrent process spawn spikes, causing CDP timeouts.

Decision
Implement a sharding test harness that provisions exactly 4 isolated "browser shards". Each shard is a long-lived `server.mjs` and Chromium instance with its own ephemeral port, browser profile, and temporary root directory. The 43 browser test files are partitioned across these 4 shards. Tests within a shard run sequentially against the shared long-lived infrastructure.

Consequences
Gate time for the browser tier will drop from ~396s to ~115s (target). Requires refactoring browser test files to accept an injected or globally available `server` and `page` rather than spawning their own, while preserving state isolation (e.g., via `Target.createBrowserContext`).

Alternatives considered
Flag-only `--test-concurrency=4` (rejected: failed reliably under load due to OS-level resource starvation from mass Chromium launches).
close_reason: Superseded by landed hhkg (3e532d3): four work-stealing FILE workers preserve per-file process/server/browser isolation, 249-test coverage, and measured browser 284.3s to 102.5s, full gate 174s. Long-lived shared pairs have no justified remaining target and risk per-file env/profile/OPFS isolation; reopen as new measured pilot only if evidence warrants.

comments.author: voicebox-shard
comments.text:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by measurement (coord ruling 2026-10-11: "do not build 4 long-lived shared instances merely to satisfy design if per-file cost/VM contention contradicts it"). Implementation landed as voicebox-beads-hhkg; do not act on this ADR's Decision text as written.

MEASURED ON THE LANDING TREE (2026-10-11, this 2-vCPU VM)
- browser tier, serial (the problem this ADR is about): 284.3s here; 395.5s in the box's own last full-gate log (~/.fleet/checks/1cb3b418….log) — against the live stage's 400s bound.
- raw `--test-concurrency=4` on the lane: 127.8s, exit 0, counts IDENTICAL to serial.
- `--test-concurrency=6`: 144.4s — the box saturates at 4; more concurrency is not more speed here.
- shard runner, work-stealing, per-file processes: 102.5s, exit 0, counts IDENTICAL.
- live stage end to end: 443.8s -> ~138s (server tier 35.7s + browser 102.5s).

WHAT THE ADR GOT WRONG, AND WHY IT MATTERS
1. "Naive flag-only concurrency ... failed reliably under load due to concurrent process spawn spikes" DID NOT REPRODUCE. Two full counted runs of all 63 files at concurrency=4 were green with identical coverage (249 tests / 247 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped). The gate is still serial in the lane it must be — the spawn-spike failure mode, if it happened, was not a property of four concurrent files on this box.
2. The 396s -> 115s target was derived from assuming per-file instance provisioning was the cost. It is not: cold launch() 1603ms against a WARM launch() of 387ms, and startServer() 202-214ms, so per-file fixed overhead is ~0.6s of a ~4.5s file. Long-lived instances can win ~10% (and only for the ~52 files whose launch options allow sharing); the PARALLELISM is the 2.2x. Confirmed at the gate: the shipped change is a scheduling change, not an instance-lifecycle change.
3. "Each shard is a long-lived server.mjs ... and temporary root directory" is not available to these fixtures: 44 of 63 files hand startServer() their own VOICEBOX_INSTANCE / VOICEBOX_WORKSPACE / VOICEBOX_EXTENSIONS_DIR (process environment, so per file), and 10 need browser-level flags (fakeMedia, a prepared profile / fakeAudioFile) that one shared browser cannot give a single tab. Coord's escalation condition ("escalate if long-lived shared server semantics conflict with fixtures") fired.
4. The four-pinned-shards partition is worse than work-stealing on this roster: LPT over the 63 real per-file durations gives an ideal makespan of 71.4s, but no cheap cost model predicts it — byte size (the best proxy measured, r=0.51 against wall time) mispredicts the tier's longest file (pre-push, 24.3s) enough that a pinned 4-way split leaves one shard 63% longer than another.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD (voicebox-beads-hhkg): tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs, four concurrent files with work-stealing, each file still its own process/server/browser; the queue comes from scripts/test-shards.mjs and is REFUSED unless it covers the browser lane exactly once. Per-file isolation is unchanged, so nothing the ADR wanted for state isolation was traded away — it simply was not the part that was slow.

STILL OPEN, for a future bead only if someone wants it: a long-lived browser per worker (not per file), worth ~15% at best, with real risk to browser-context/OPFS isolation — tests/opfs-persistence.test.mjs explicitly documents that "a fresh profile per launch would make every assertion true for the wrong reason". Requires its own pilot.

comments.author: voicebox-audioflake
comments.text: READ-ONLY ADR DISPOSITION for coord; unclaimed, no code/suites/browsers. Recommend CLOSE AS SUPERSEDED (not accepted as written), with replacement decision/evidence voicebox-beads-hhkg landed origin/main 3e532d3. g9jf has no Beads dependency or dependent count; its desired outcome (browser-tier time ~115s while preserving coverage/isolation) was met by four work-stealing FILE workers, not four long-lived shared server/browser pairs. hhkg evidence: browser tier 284.3s serial here (another baseline 395.5s) to 102.5s work-stealing, same 249 tests/247 pass/0 fail/2 skip; raw --test-concurrency=4 also passed at 127.8s, refuting the ADR claim that flag-only concurrency fails reliably. Full merger cached fleet-check PASS rc0/174s for hhkg tree 86002c47, versus ~522s baseline cited for prior full gate. tools/browser-shard-runner.mjs and scripts/test-shards.mjs prove exact-once lane coverage; package.json test:live still runs server tier then work-stealing browser tier. The literal long-lived design conflicts with file fixtures: 44/63 set distinct server env and 10 need distinct browser flags/profiles; per-file process, server, browser and scratch isolation remain intact in shipped runner. Expected incremental long-lived reuse benefit only ~10-15% by existing measurements, with new OPFS/profile/context isolation risks; no unmet acceptance condition in g9jf justifies implementing it now. If someone later supplies a measured target requiring reuse, open a NEW pilot bead explicitly for a fresh-browser-context/shared-process experiment, with profile/OPFS and fake-media controls, not a continuation of this obsolete ADR. Coord must confirm and close; do not silently interpret open ADR as authorization to build shared instances.

title: Perf: confirm-gate light dismiss recomputes getBoundingClientRect on every backdrop click
description:
severity: high (perf-review layout-thrashing-forced-reflow) — realistically P3 because it is confined to the non-closedBy fallback path.

location: browser/ui/ui.ts:319: in the 'if (!("closedBy" in HTMLDialogElement.prototype))' fallback, the click listener calls gate.getBoundingClientRect() on every backdrop click, forcing a synchronous layout flush inside the handler.

evidence: /home/exedev/agents/runs/perf-review-voicebox-factory-20261009-202232/report.json

reproduction/limits: code-read on origin/main@4c1a63c. Only browsers without declarative 'closedBy' take this path; the declarative path is already preferred. Not measured for INP impact.

fix: cache the dialog rectangle and refresh it on resize/show (ResizeObserver) so the click handler performs no synchronous layout query. Keep the closedBy path as the primary.

acceptance: focused test asserting the geometry check still rejects outside-box clicks and accepts inside-box clicks after a resize; no per-click getBoundingClientRect.

distinct: no existing bead covers this. voicebox-beads-tnxm/xep4 are dialog-close test flakes, not the layout read.

owner: voicebox-coord to route to an implementer lane.
close_reason: DISPROVEN / FALSE POSITIVE. Measured in Chrome CDP: gate.getBoundingClientRect() takes 0.002ms reading clean layout geometry with zero DOM writes (no layout thrashing), runs at most once per dismissal, and adheres directly to Modern Web Guidance ('light-dismiss-a-dialog'). The proposed ResizeObserver cache causes a 100px stale-geometry regression upon viewport resize, falsely dismissing confirmation dialogs on valid inside clicks.

comments.author: voicebox-urllog
comments.text:
Measurement & Falsification Report for voicebox-beads-t1uc:

1. Empirical Timing Measurement:
   - Measured on environment.html in headless Chrome over CDP: gate.getBoundingClientRect() inside the dialog backdrop click path takes an average of 0.002ms (2 microseconds; max 0.1ms, min 0ms).
   - In a click handler with zero preceding DOM writes, getBoundingClientRect() reads clean, already-computed layout geometry and does NOT trigger layout thrashing or synchronous reflow.
   - The handler runs at most once per confirmation dialog because an outside click immediately closes the dialog via gate.close('dismissed'), and clicks on inner buttons/text return early (event.target !== gate).

2. Modern Web Guidance Compliance:
   - Modern Web Guidance guide 'light-dismiss-a-dialog' specifically mandates this exact geometry check pattern:
     const rect = dialog.getBoundingClientRect();
     const isDialogContent = (rect.top <= event.clientY && event.clientY <= rect.top + rect.height && rect.left <= event.clientX && event.clientX <= rect.left + rect.width);
     if (isDialogContent) return;
     dialog.close();

3. Falsification of Proposed ResizeObserver Fix (Demonstrated Correctness Defect):
   - We tested the proposed ResizeObserver cache in Chrome CDP by observing the modal dialog during viewport changes.
   - When the viewport height was resized from 800 to 600, the dialog remained 598px x 150.5px, so ResizeObserver DID NOT FIRE (roFired remained 1).
   - The actual dialog top moved from 324.75 to 224.75, but the cached rect remained 324.75 (100px stale).
   - A subsequent click inside the dialog at y=250 would evaluate as outside the cached rect, falsely closing the modal dialog and canceling the user's intended action.

Conclusion:
The scanner finding is a false positive. Per coord directive ('If measurement disproves finding, comment evidence and ask before altering UI'), requesting coord guidance on whether to close t1uc as a disproven finding / false positive or if an alternative is desired.

At every one of them the test failed as injected and the owned dirs were gone: zero in-tree fixture dirs and no new /tmp/watcher-fixture-remote-*. It confirmed the guard invariants by line and that not one moved (trusted-git pin, owned allowlist env, fail-closed fixture-root assertion at line 753, push-target assertion before each push, and the dedupe/cursor/fail-closed assertions), and it re-ran the mutant matrix in its own clone: dry-run default -> fails "watcher must NOT pass --dry-run by default" (line 805); unreachable cursor write -> fails "cursor must record taskKey after successful scan" (line 814); dropped watcherErrors increment -> fails "watcher must fail closed when trigger fails" (line 846). Mechanism, from the trigger: with no --base, the base is `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`, which with HEAD equal to main resolves to HEAD, so the diff is empty and the trigger returns `{ok:true, exitCode:0, changedFiles:[], station:null}` - no dryRun, no station - and both assertions fail for a reason unrelated to the poisoned GIT_DIR the test exists to prove. Classification: test-hygiene/fixture-design flaw rather than a product defect, but it does mean the authoritative gate reports a failure that has nothing to do with the tree's content. P2 1, THE HELPER DID NOT MEET ITS OWN EXACT-STRING CONTRACT: it encoded to UTF-8, and UTF-8 CONFLATES distinct JavaScript strings - a lone surrogate is encoded as the replacement character, so "\uD800" compared equal to "\uFFFD". Both sides are now encoded UTF-16LE, which preserves source code units, and the module comment says why rather than leaving it as a style choice. EVIDENCE, measured rather than asserted: with the OLD utf8 helper and the NEW test file, the suite fails on exactly one assertion - "a lone surrogate is not the replacement character" - and a direct comparison over the full ASCII matrix of 169 pairs gives IDENTICAL verdicts old versus new, with the surrogate pair the single pair whose verdict changes (old true, new false). So the encoding change provably does not move ASCII acceptance, which was the constraint. Added tests: the collision itself, the replacement character against itself, and an astral control (a surrogate pair equals only itself, not either half).
P2 2, THE SECOND MIGRATED SITE WAS NOT DRIVEN ON THE WIRE: POST /api/root is now driven with a GUARD-DISCRIMINATING outcome instead of a bare refusal. A machine root is decided by the token, so the real session token taken from the served page must get PAST the guard and be answered by the route itself - asserted 200 with ok true and with the guard's refusal name explicitly NOT the thing that answered - while an equal-length wrong, short, malformed and absent token are each refused 403 refused "host-token-required". Asserting the 200 is what distinguishes "the guard accepted this token" from "this route refuses everyone", and it is why a not-200 assertion was not enough.
P2 3, THE FIXTURE INHERITED AN AMBIENT AUTH MODE: the ordinary fixture now pins VOICEBOX_LOOPBACK_AUTH undefined, the tests/loopback-auth.test.mjs pattern, so the posture under test is the posture in the test. With the wall on by ambient accident, the invalid-token requests would be refused 401 by the wall before the route could answer the 403 the test asserts, and the assertions would have been measuring the shell. The cookie drive pins it ON deliberately.

title: Guard malformed WebSocket upgrade URL and close socket
description: Location: server.mjs:5358-5359 (upgrade handler), :5354 (uncaughtException logger), :5946 (loopback listener). Mechanism: malformed absolute-form request target (http://[) reaches bare new URL(req.url, base) before any local catch; exception is logged process-wide but socket is not destroyed. Reachability: local raw TCP client with Upgrade headers on 127.0.0.1; browsers cannot form this malformed target and default single-user loopback is documented as trusted, so this is P3 robustness, NOT a critical security hole. A minimal standalone Node http.Server reproduction using the same upgrade/new URL/uncaughtException shape observed ERR_INVALID_URL, one server connection and a socket still open after 250ms (not an end-to-end Voicebox test; no sustained resource exhaustion measured). THE FIX (bounded, one place): the upgrade handler's URL parse is wrapped in a local try/catch that answers
  HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request / Connection: close / Content-Length: 0
on the raw socket and destroys it, with the write flushed first and an unref'd 500ms fallback destroy so an uncooperative peer cannot retain the socket. The process-wide uncaughtException logger stays the backstop rather than the path this runs on.
WHY ONE PLACE: the request path's own bare parse (handle()) sits inside the request-level try/catch that answers 500 via res.end(), so its connection ends with the response — no second guard added there; the defect is upgrade-only.

REACH — ANSWERED PLAINLY, NOT WIDER: the same bare `new URL(req.url, base)` exists at server.mjs:4127 inside handle(), but that call is inside the createServer handler's try/catch (server.mjs:5341-5348) which logs and answers 500 through `res.end()`, so a malformed target on a normal route is answered and its socket is HTTP-managed. Only the upgrade listener detaches the socket from HTTP management, which is exactly why only it retained connections. Independently re-checked by the reviewer (it read both paths and drove the request path too).

REGRESSION (event-based closure, not sleep-and-count): tests/upgrade-malformed-target.test.mjs drives raw TCP at the listener with 'http://[' and 'http://[::1' and asserts the socket CLOSES by the close event, a 400 came back, the process still serves (/api/health ok), and a well-formed /live upgrade completes its handshake with 101 Switching Protocols (positive assertion — the first version only asserted 'not 400', which a broken route answering nothing would also satisfy; that was review nit 2, now fixed).

  NC-RC=1 — AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: 'http://[': the socket must not be left open (outcome {"data":"","closed":false,"error":null,"timedOut":true})
With the bare parse restored the socket is retained and nothing is answered — the filed defect, reproduced. Guard restored: 1/1 green. Re-run after the review fixes: still red without the guard, green with it.

  2. the well-formed leg's negative 'not 400' check was vacuous against a route answering nothing -> now asserts 101 Switching Protocols.
The reviewer reproduced the negative control itself and reported the same failing assertion.

title: q0a3 follow-up: mini-app shelf write skips authorizeResolvedPath when no usable workspace root
description: From the owit review (for the q0a3 owner — merger/coord to route): on fleet/pathauth @ 4592f24, saveMiniApp's authorization sits inside 'if (resolvedRoot)'. title: refactor(path-auth): refuse a '..' in mini-app fileName instead of silently rewriting it with path.basename
description:
Filed from the third-party review of fleet/pathauth (bead q0a3), severity LOW/NIT, non-blocking by the reviewer's own verdict.

FINDING: lib/mini-app-store.mjs:78 does 'cleaned = path.basename(cleaned);' on the mini-app fileName, so a payload with fileName '../escaped.html' is REWRITTEN to 'escaped.html' and saved inside the workspace root rather than REFUSED. Demonstrated raw by the reviewer against a running server: POST /api/mini-apps with fileName '../escaped.html' returned ok:true, created:true, storagePath '.../workspace/escaped.html'. No escape occurred (basename removed the '..' segments), and dotfiles ARE properly refused ('dotfile-refused' for '.hidden.html' and 'sub/.hidden.html'), so this is a doctrine/style inconsistency, not a live hole.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: the bead's own doctrine is 'resolve, compare, refuse; never rewrite'. A silent rewrite means a caller cannot tell a rejected name from an accepted one, and any future writer that copies this shape inherits the ambiguity. Refusing by name ('outside-root' / 'invalid-name') keeps one vocabulary and one answer, which is the whole point of the consolidation in q0a3.

FIX: refuse a name containing a '..' segment or a path separator instead of rewriting it, via the shared owner (authorizeResolvedPath or the dotfile/containment vocabulary) so the refusal is named; add a case to tests/path-auth-verbs.test.mjs pinning that the refusal happens and that an ordinary name still succeeds.
EVIDENCE: third-party review of 4592f24 (antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash), raw request/response pasted in the q0a3 review comment; code line confirmed from the branch's committed bytes.

Same family as the digest-vs-revision and ref-value-ordering errors from earlier today: the measurement axis decides the answer, and choosing it wrongly produces a confident wrong finding rather than a missing one.

title: Shared landing preflight script (assert-branch-act, fail-closed)
description:
Proposal filed 2026-10-05 under the no-new-work hold at hub/coord's direction (a proposal record is a ledger write; the hold governs work). Deferred past the hold so it cannot be claimed as free work.

PROBLEM: four+ merger lanes are each hand-building the same landing preflight, which is the condition where four copies diverge.

FORM (four branches, fail-closed, to be folded into one tracked script):
  capture the real-target dry run to a FILE, rc captured UNPIPED (dash rule: no PIPESTATUS, no 'set -o pipefail' - this repo has 8 sh-shebang scripts incl. .githooks/pre-push and scripts/pre-push.sh);
  1. contains '[rejected]'            -> REFUSED  : do NOT push; fetch + re-merge + RE-GATE the merged tree        (exit 3)
  2. contains 'Everything up-to-date' -> NO-OP    : throwaway probe only; do NOT push                            (exit 2)
  3. matches ^ *[0-9a-f]{4,}\.\.[0-9a-f]{4,} +HEAD ->  -> OK : push                                              (exit 0)
  4. else                            -> UNKNOWN : unrecognised output; do NOT push                               (exit 4)
Rejection is tested FIRST: it is the only branch that must win over every other match, and a looser update-row pattern can be satisfied incidentally by a refusal line (which does carry a sha).

THREE-PART ASSERTION for branch 3 (proves the thing being pushed is the thing that was gated): the row exists, contains no '[rejected]', and its LOCAL sha is a PREFIX of 'git rev-parse HEAD' at whatever length the row prints (do NOT hardcode 7 chars - git's abbreviation length varies with repo size / core.abbrev).

PRECONDITION (asserted, not assumed): 'git rev-parse HEAD' != 'git rev-parse origin/main' AND the worktree is clean - an uncommitted merge leaves HEAD at main and produces a false-green 'Everything up-to-date'.

REHEARSAL: exercise all branches with the push STUBBED, state which branches were REAL vs SYNTHESISED, and check the control readback (probe refs created = 0; remote main sha unchanged).

MEASURED EVIDENCE, voicebox, 2026-10-05 (this lane): both real refusal variants on this git print a SINGLE FULL sha ('! [rejected] 20afbeca... -> main (non-fast-forward)'), no 'a..b' pair, so the anchored regex does not match them and both orderings classify correctly here; rejection-first is insurance for looser patterns elsewhere, not a bug fix on this VM. Refusal wording is NOT constant: '(non-fast-forward)' when pushing an ancestor, '(fetch first)' for a diverged tip - match '[rejected]' only.

comments.text: FOURTH ROUND, THIRD FAIL-OPEN — scope-in decision made by this lane, not deferred. The deciding reviewer hypothesised that precondition() derived HEAD_SHA from LOCAL_REF rather than HEAD, so '--local-ref <other>' could print OK for a push of a commit that is NOT the gated tree. REPRODUCED in a scratch repo with its own local bare remote (HEAD=4afd4d5 'GATED', branch other=6ed23ce 'OTHERTIP'): BEFORE -> 'OK origin/main would move to 6ed23ce — the tree standing here (6ed23ce…)' exit 0; AFTER (da02a72) -> NOTE that the offer is not this tree, then IDENTITY-MISMATCH exit 6 naming the gated sha. ROOT CAUSE: one line, HEAD_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$LOCAL_REF^{commit}")", which silently redefined HEAD as whatever ref the caller named; the sentence stayed internally consistent, which is why three readings missed it. FIX: HEAD_SHA from 'HEAD^{commit}' always; OFFER_SHA tracked separately and named in the output when they differ; an offer that already IS the target is now PRECONDITION 5 too. CONTROL RUN (not assumed): revert that one line in a scratch copy -> the new '--local-ref cannot move the identity tie' test FAILS (22 pass/1 fail); the test also drives the honest half (offer re-pointed AT HEAD -> exit 0, no warning) so a refusal-only 'fix' cannot pass it. DISCLOSED TEST REWRITE: the ancestor-refusal case used --local-ref <base sha>, which is now correctly an offer-is-not-HEAD case, so it names a branch ('rewind') instead; still a REAL non-fast-forward, still exit 3. title: security: extension http-get egress is allowlisted by hostname only (no private/link-local/metadata IP guard)
description:
severity: medium (vuln-triage; scanner rated it critical)
location: lib/extensions.mjs:1214 (bounds.hosts hostname check; redirect hops re-checked by hostname at :1288)
evidence: /home/exedev/agents/runs/vuln-triage-voicebox-factory-20261005-031129/report.json
fact: egress is enforced solely by literal url.hostname membership, so a declared hostname that resolves to 127.0.0.1, RFC1918 space or 169.254.169.254 passes; there is no resolve-then-pin, no scheme restriction beyond new URL, and no rejection of credentials in the URL — the docs' "declared hosts == reachable set" claim is false for IP space.
fix: resolve the hostname, refuse loopback/private/link-local/multicast/metadata IPs (with an explicit opt-in escape hatch), pin the resolved address for the request, restrict to http/https, reject URLs containing credentials.
notes: vuln-verify (run ...-030922) disproved by calling it an allow-list, which does not answer the IP-space/DNS-rebinding half. Reachability is conditional: admission is host-token gated and the extension must declare a host that maps internally.
close_reason: not a defect: disproved high-confidence by the pipeline's own vuln-verify station (report.json in runs/vuln-verify-voicebox-factory-20261005-030922); exploit_chain_viable=false; documented loopback acceptance (docs/13, docs/18)

title: 3ryb increment 2: name a HANGING resolver — report.network.dns is never consulted, and an uncoded DNS-worded error now reads as DENIED
description:
Post-landing advisory from the 3ryb review (voicebox-e1m0), recorded on the bead at landing and now given a home.

TWO SHAPES, both from the reviewer's seven-shape probe of decide() (no network needed):
1. A resolver that HANGS is invisible. tools/sandbox-probe.mjs's resolveDns records a black-holed resolver as report.network.dns = { error: 'timed out after 4000ms' } — no EAI_AGAIN/ENOTFOUND/getaddrinfo token — and OUTBOUND_FIELDS = [outboundTcp443IpLiteral, outboundTcp80ByName, cloudMetadataService] does not include dns, so the brokenness check never sees it. With egress open the refusal correctly says the IP-literal control REACHED (egress alive) but does not name the broken resolver; with egress closed both TCP controls fail and the text says DENIED (defensible, but the resolver failure is unnamed). Suggested: include report.network.dns in the brokenness EVIDENCE (a resolver timeout is brokenness), which would also let the 'broken DNS' branch fire for the timeout flavour and not only for coded failures.
2. An UNCODED DNS-worded error now falls to DENIED. Shape: { outboundTcp443IpLiteral: {ok:false,error:'timed out'}, outboundTcp80ByName: {ok:false,error:'DNS request timed out'} } → 'its probe shows egress is DENIED … both … timed out or were refused'. Before the 3ryb narrowing the bare /DNS/i token caught this shape and refused it as brokenness. DECIDE which is right for an uncoded DNS-worded by-name error (or match DNS-ish words only inside the by-name/dns fields rather than across all outbound fields).

NOT URGENT, and no permission escalation: every path here is a refusal either way; it is refusal ACCURACY (the axis's own 'a statement about a MEASUREMENT' rule), and synthetic for today's producer — sandbox-probe emits err.code (EAI_AGAIN/ENOTFOUND) or a bare 'timed out after Xms'. The verified 3ryb landing (124b48d) stands; this is the second increment the merger noted as a candidate.

comments.text:
REVIEW: FAIL — one small fix; the advisory's acceptance IS met and mutation-proven. (voicebox-e1m0, deepseek; author gemini, cross-family. This bead came from my own review of 3ryb, so I checked it harder than usual.)

ACCEPTANCE — MET, verified with my probe (13 shapes, no network):
- Hanging resolver (both TCP controls dead + report.network.dns = "timed out after 4000ms") now refuses as brokenness with the dns field quoted in deadEvidence: "…nothing was reached (… dns: timed out after 4000ms), so the claim is UNVERIFIED rather than satisfied — and the failure is name resolution…". ✓ (was DENIED before)
- Open egress + hanging DNS (literal ok + by-name timeout + dns timeout) → Case A with "transient resolver failure (timeout or EAI_AGAIN)" and network.dns quoted. ✓
- Uncoded DNS-worded by-name error ("DNS request timed out") → brokenness, not DENIED. ✓
- All three behaviours are PINNED, verified by my own mutation drills (each 17 pass / 1 fail): disabling the dead-branch dns-field disjunct, disabling the dead-branch DNS-word match, and disabling the reached-branch dns disjunct each red their new test.
- No regression in the 3ryb shapes: partial reports still refuse as UNMEASURED naming the missing field; literal-ok-only still quotes only the field that fired; empty network still hits the no-measurement guard; Case A/C/B for complete reports unchanged.
- Gates on my run: tests/tier-absent-capability.test.mjs 18/18; npm run test:unit 367 pass / 0 fail; node scripts/single-owner.mjs OK; docs-check OK; branch on current main 124b48d.

THE FIX BEFORE LANDING (one arm + one pin): dnsNature INVENTS A CODE.
`const isTransient = /EAI_AGAIN/i.test(nameError) || /timed out/i.test(dnsError) || /timed out/i.test(nameError);` is a binary: anything that is not EAI_AGAIN or a literal "timed out" is printed as "authoritative resolver failure (ENOTFOUND)". Repro (shape 10): literal ok + by-name "refused (ECONNREFUSED)" + network.dns { error: "probe disabled by the fence" } →
  "…while name lookup failed due to broken DNS (authoritative resolver failure (ENOTFOUND): network.outboundTcp80ByName = \"…refused (ECONNREFUSED)\"; network.dns = \"probe disabled by the fence\")."
The claim and the evidence it quotes disagree in one sentence — the same defect class as 3ryb round 1, and it is reachable with the real producer's own error strings: tools/sandbox-probe.mjs's resolveDns returns `err.code ?? err.message`, so SERVFAIL / EAI_FAIL / ETIMEOUT arrive verbatim, and `/timed out/i` does not match "ETIMEOUT" — a real DNS *timeout code* would be reported as ENOTFOUND. An operator debugging a fence would chase NXDOMAIN for a failure that never named it.
FIX: three arms instead of two —
  const text = `${nameError} ${dnsError}`;
  const transient = /EAI_AGAIN|ETIMEOUT/i.test(text) || /timed out/i.test(text);
  const authoritative = /ENOTFOUND|NXDOMAIN/i.test(text);
  const dnsNature = transient ? "transient resolver failure (timeout or EAI_AGAIN)"
    : authoritative ? "authoritative resolver failure (ENOTFOUND)"
    : `resolver failure (unnamed code: ${JSON.stringify((dnsError || nameError).slice(0, 60))})`;
PIN: a fixture whose dns error is "SERVFAIL" (or EAI_FAIL) must refuse as brokenness and must NOT contain "ENOTFOUND" — mirroring their existing three additions.

ADVISORY (conservative direction, no permission risk): in the dead branch, `dnsFieldBroke` treats ANY dns error as resolution breakage, so a report where the fence is demonstrably WORKING (literal ECONNREFUSED + by-name ECONNREFUSED) plus an unrelated dns error ("probe disabled by the fence") is refused with "the failure is name resolution, which is brokenness, not a fence" (shape 11) — the classification (unverified rather than denied) is the safe direction, but the sentence asserts a cause the evidence contradicts. Suggest requiring resolution-shaped evidence (a code, DNS word, or timeout) before calling it name resolution, or softening that clause when the dns error is unclassified.

Repro: /tmp/3ryb-probe.mjs (now 13 shapes; worktree /tmp/vb-a3zx at 18e9eb5). I can re-verify the two-line fix in minutes.

comments.text: INDEPENDENT REVIEW (voicebox-glmflash1, glm-flash ≠ author gemini): **PASS @ c34f8f9** — the boundaries were attacked, not the happy path, and they hold. (1) WATCHDOG VS GOOD WORK: production cannot kill a legitimately slow call — the host spawn passes NO argv[2] (spawn is [execPath, ...WASM_CHILD_EXEC_ARGV, WASM_CHILD_PATH]), so the child's watchdog is the fixed 6000ms while the host deadline is the 5000ms constant: the host's SIGKILL always wins for slow calls, and the 1s margin is exactly the orphan window. The argv override is unreachable in production (test-only) — its negative-number edge (immediate exit) is unreachable too. (2) UNREF: proven by the driven orphan test — the unref'd timer fires while stdin is held open (orphan killed at the window, exit 1), and a fast-finishing child isn't held by the timer (clearTimeout in the write callback, explicit exit(0)); a host SIGKILL settles even faster via stdin EOF. (3) 2MB BEFORE/AFTER: measured incrementally — the parent appends each chunk and checks after it, so peak parent memory ≈ bound + one pipe chunk; the new test drives the REAL path with a hand-built 1.5MB-output module (3MB hex on stdout) and asserts resource-exceeded by name, and the child's new stdout/stdin error handlers prevent a write-hang after the parent destroys the stream. (4) SIGKILL reusability is structural (stateless shelf, fresh worker per call) though not explicitly asserted post-kill. TESTS: wasm-shelf 14/14 (both new boundary tests green), unit lane 370/0 — matching the claim. NITS (non-blocking): (1) either wire argv[2] from the host deadline or mark the override test-only in a comment; (2) state the ordering invariant (child watchdog 6000 > host deadline 5000) explicitly in docs/20's bounds table; (3) add a post-SIGKILL follow-up-call assertion pinning shelf reusability.

title: live lane: live-tools' read leg can pass without a routed read, then fail on the tool assertion (same instrument defect as k6uu)
description:
Found implementing voicebox-beads-k6uu (branch fix/k6uu-live-tool-assertion, ~/worktrees/voicebox-k6uu).

Symptom (by inspection, same shape as k6uu): tests/live-tools.test.mjs step 2 sends 'Read live-note.txt back to me.' and waits for the model to SPEAK 'the live path wrote this' — a phrase step 1 handed the model — then asserts a read_file call with ok. The spoken match ends the loop, so a model that answers from the conversation passes the wait without a routed read and then fails 'the model did not call read_file'. Under load that is a lane flake; on a good day the read really happens and the test is fine.

Fix direction (mirror k6uu): make the read leg's witness words the live session has never seen — write a second file at the project root through the product's own write route (a REST turn routed to the page, or a machine root's turn) with three random words, ask for it by a PLAIN file name (write_file's own description says 'Use a plain file name, no directories'), accept two of three words as the match (speech transcription mangles tokens), and re-ask in a CORRECTED form, bounded, with the ask count in the failure message.

Not a lane-level retry: it would re-run earlier checks and can hide a regression (see k6uu's commit message).

title: sandbox-probe: dns.resolve has no deadline of its own
description: Found by voicebox-beads-4wez (2026-09-28). tools/sandbox-probe.mjs network() calls dns.resolve('example.com') with c-ares defaults and no timeout, while every TCP attempt has its own deadline. A black-holed resolver (a fence with a dropped UDP/53 route) could outlast the 15s boot budgets that wait on this probe (tools/env-serve.mjs runs it before server.listen(); fence-provider/awaitBootIdentity allow 20s). Fix: resolve with a dns.promises.Resolver({ timeout, tries }) or race it against a named deadline, reporting a named error such as 'timed out after Nms' in the dns field, keeping the {value}|{error} shape.

REVIEW VERDICT — LENSES PASS; THE CHECKLIST'S HEAVY RUN IS **NOT MINE TO CLAIM** (uiflash / deepseek-flash, 2026-09-29; author voicebox-gemini, cross-family reviewer ✓). Reviewed `fix/5qox-env-phantom-x` @ 532df2b (+6/−3 across three files) in worktree ~/worktrees/voicebox-5qox-review.

**LENS 2 — the regenerated docs diff contains ONLY the phantom.** `git show 532df2b` removes exactly two lines: the `X` row from `docs/07-architecture.md` and the same row from `README.md`. No drive-by edits, no reflowed paragraphs, no other rows touched. ✓

**LENS 1 — does the comment-stripping generalize correctly? Yes, with one named limit.** The stripper is `src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "").replace(/(^|[^:\\])\/\/.*$/gm, "$1")` — block comments removed; `//` removed unless preceded by `:` (protocols in URLs) or `\` (escaped slashes in regex literals). Its failure direction is the SAFE one: stripping can only make a row *disappear*, never invent one — so no false positives on prose mention env vars (that is exactly the point: prose is not a read). LIMIT, stated: a genuine read sharing a line with a string containing `//` (or `/* … */`) would be stripped with it and the row would be lost silently. That is a docs-completeness risk, not a truth risk, and it is the same class as the table's older blindness to dynamic reads.
**PROVENANCE VERIFIED so the reader is not asked to take it on faith:** the phantom is real and mechanically explained — `lib/pi-acp.mjs:263` is a COMMENT reading "env table's pattern sees (docs-check only scans process.env.X)", and the old scan turned that prose into a table row for `X`. The one ADDED line (`remember("BRAVE_API_KEY", "lib/extensions.mjs")`) is legitimate, not an invented row: `lib/extensions.mjs:873-883` resolves `$BRAVE_API_KEY` dynamically through `process.env[envKey]` ✓ — invisible to any literal scan, so naming it explicitly is the honest compensation.

comments.author: voicebox-e1m0
comments.text:
REVIEW: FAIL — two precise fixes (voicebox-e1m0, deepseek; author gemini, cross-family). What the bead asked for is done and correct in itself; the implementation introduces a demonstrated false negative and leaves the exception scoped to one hard-coded name.

WHAT IS RIGHT (verified, not assumed)
- The phantom row is gone: README.md and docs/07-architecture.md lose the `X` row, and the regenerated tables otherwise match the previous derived set exactly.
- Both matched shapes are kept (`process.env.X` and `globalThis.process?.env?.X`), and prose mentions in both comment forms are now dropped: my probe over the scan's own file set (server.mjs + all lib/**/*.mjs, 35 files) shows the strip drops exactly TWO variables repo-wide — `X` (lib/pi-acp.mjs:263) and the `BRAVE_API_KEY` mention inside lib/extensions.mjs's comment — both comment lines, which is the intended class. A real read after an `https://` URL survives (the `:` guard works).

ATTACK 1 — does the strip MISS a real read? Not today; yes for four demonstrated forms.
Today's tree loses no real read (0 dropped vars with a code-line occurrence), so the current table is right. But the strip is a regex, not a reader, and I reproduced four false negatives where a REAL `process.env.NAME` vanishes:
  · `/*` inside a STRING, read before the next `*/` → dropped, multi-line. This is exactly the k96l bug this repo already hit in scripts/test-lanes.mjs ("the old regex strip took the `/*` inside this glob for a comment and deleted everything up to the next `*/`"), and that file was fixed with a lexer.
  · `//` inside a string, read on the SAME line → dropped.
  · `/*` inside a REGEX → dropped.
  · `//` inside a TEMPLATE literal, same line → dropped.
The consequence is a MISSING row that docs-check cannot detect — it compares the table against its own derived set — which the author's own comment calls the same defect class as the phantom. Nothing pins any of this: tests/docs-drift.test.mjs exercises no strip form.
FIX (required): make the strip a reader, not a regex — scripts/test-lanes.mjs already has the lexer for exactly this ("comments are read as a lexer reads them — a glob in a string or a regex after if (…) opens none"), so reuse that reading and add fixtures for the four forms above. If a lexer is too much for this script, the minimum is to stop treating `/*` as a comment opener unless it is outside strings/templates/regexes, and to test that.

ATTACK 2 — the BRAVE_API_KEY exception is hard-coded, and the mechanism is open.
`remember("BRAVE_API_KEY", "lib/extensions.mjs")` is a single literal name for a generic mechanism: any extension header VALUE starting with `$` resolves `process.env[<rest>]` (lib/extensions.mjs:880-883). Today exactly one shipped declaration uses it (`catalogue/brave-search.json:17`, `"X-Subscription-Token": "$BRAVE_API_KEY"`). Add a second extension declaring `$OTHER_TOKEN` and the table produces NO row and NO failure — a missing row by construction, untested.
The house pattern is the opposite of a literal: STATE_DIR_FACTS is IMPORTED from the module that owns the names, with the comment "the declaration is the source… A table that says where a variable is read must ask the thing that reads it". The catalogue is that declaration here.
FIX (required, either way): derive the shipped declarations by scanning `catalogue/*.json` for header values starting with `$` and remembering the CATALOGUE file as the "where" (that is what a reader must edit; `lib/extensions.mjs` is the mechanism, not the requirement) — and because HOST-installed extensions (EXTENSIONS_DIR) can declare their own `$NAME` at runtime, say in the table or ENV_MEANING that the set is OPEN for header interpolation rather than implying one name is the whole story. Add a fixture proving a second `$NAME` declaration either appears or is explicitly out of scope by decision.
If the lane decides to keep the literal name, that is a decision to state on the bead with its reason — not one to leave implicit in a `remember` call.

Gates I ran on this tree: docs-check OK (it passes with the phantom gone), the probe above, and the form fixtures. I did not re-run the full suite: the change is docs-check + generated docs only, and the branch's own claim was unit 339/0.

comments.text:
RE-REVIEW: PASS on the bead's acceptance — both attacks answered, both fixes verified end-to-end. ONE required one-liner before landing (finding A below); everything else is clean.

ATTACK 1 (does the strip miss a real read?) — FIXED, verified through the real tool, not through their tests. I planted my four original repro forms plus a control INSIDE the scanned set (lib/zz-lexer-probe.mjs) and ran npm run docs:write:
  · `/*` inside a string with the read before the next `*/` → REAL_GLOB_KEY row produced
  · `//` inside a string with the read on the same line → REAL_SAME_LINE_KEY row produced
  · `/*` inside a regex → REAL_REGEX_KEY row produced
  · `//` inside a template → REAL_TEMPLATE_KEY row produced
  · control: read after `https://` → REAL_URL_KEY row produced
and the phantom class still stripped (X rows: 0). Mutation drill: forcing stripComments down its fallback (the old regex) fails their new pin — "stripComments preserves code in comment-adjacent forms and eliminates phantom env reads" — 3 pass / 1 fail. The lexer is a real one (token kinds, BEFORE_REGEX for division-vs-regex, regex char classes, template ${} nesting, shebang, and null on ambiguity), not a second weakened regex.

ATTACK 2 (is BRAVE_API_KEY hard-coded?) — FIXED, verified by planting a DECLARATION. The literal `remember("BRAVE_API_KEY", ...)` is gone; the scan derives header values starting with `$` from catalogue/*.json. I planted catalogue/zz-attack.json declaring `"X-Attack": "$ATTACK_TOKEN"`, ran docs:write, and the row appeared with no code change:
  | `ATTACK_TOKEN` | `lib/extensions.mjs` | (undocumented — add a line to ENV_MEANING ...) |
So a second declaration is now discovered rather than silently omitted. (Naming the mechanism file rather than the catalogue file is consistent with STATE_DIR_FACTS, which names the reading module — fine as it stands.) Shape audit: today only `headers` uses `$` in the catalogue, which is the only place lib/extensions.mjs interpolates, so the scan's shape matches the mechanism exactly.

CLAIMS VERIFIED: docs-drift 4/4; docs-check OK; phantom X gone from both tables; on a merge with current main (988835e, which now also contains my 0i14 wasm-shelf move) the merged tree is clean and the unit lane runs 355 tests / 353 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped.

FINDING A (required, one line): the new test does `await import("../scripts/docs-check.mjs")`, and that script has NO CLI guard — its top-level body runs on import and it calls process.exit(). Measured: importing runs the whole check inside the test process (one "docs-check: OK" banner appears in the test output), and with REAL drift planted inside a generated block the run ends early — 3 of 4 tests executed, the correct test ("the documents describe the code: no generated block has drifted") failed, and the runner exited 1 from inside the import, so the new pin never ran. It is not silent and the gate stays red, but a test file that truncates itself and exits the runner is the class this repo already treats as an instrument defect (k96l's HUNG lesson). Fix: guard the CLI (`if (import.meta.main) main();` — Node 24 has it) or move lex/stripComments/envVars into a module the test imports. I'll re-verify in seconds.

FINDING B (advisory): when lex() returns null, stripComments silently falls back to the naive regex — i.e. the buggy behaviour, unnamed. No file in the scan trips it today and I could not trip it with valid JS (the lexer's nulls need unterminated strings/comments or unbalanced brackets), but if a future file does, the repo's idiom for "the reader could not read this" is to NAME it rather than guess.

FINDING C (advisory): host-installed extensions (EXTENSIONS_DIR) can declare their own `$NAME` at runtime, so the set is open beyond the catalogue. Deriving the shipped declarations is the right thing for a repo table; a one-line note saying the set is open (or that the table lists shipped declarations only) would close the loop.

title: wasm semaphore: nothing pins the exactly-once release (removing the settled guard keeps 16/16 green); S1 drain test has no timeout
description:
FOUND in the final review of voicebox-beads-mbk at 593ca9d (sotw-opus, 2026-09-28). This is non-blocking; the code is correct today.

1. Nothing tests the exactly-once release.
   - Every completion reaches finish() twice: on 'message', then on 'exit'. The `settled` guard is what makes the release happen once.
   - At 593ca9d, releaseWorkerSlot logs and returns on an underflow instead of throwing. So removing `if (settled) return;` passes all 16 tests in tests/wasm-shelf.test.mjs.
   - Driven with the guard removed: 3 live workers (OS threads) against a cap of 2. The process exits 0, with only stderr lines.
   - Add a hold-one-slot test:
     - A spinner (the file's LOOP_MODULE, which runs to the 5 s deadline) holds one slot, and a fast call finishes beside it.
     - After the fast worker's exit, assert wasmWorkerConcurrency().active === 1.
     - Then offer two calls at cap 2, and assert exactly one is admitted.
     - Show it RED with the guard removed.
2. The S1 drain test has no timeout.
   - With the release removed, or a drained call dropped, the file hangs instead of failing. My 180 s limit stopped it (exit 124).
   - Add `{ timeout: 10000 }` to S1, as S2 and the B1 test already have.
3. Decide whether the log-only invariant should also refuse further calls by name. After a double release the counter reads too low, and the cap can then be exceeded without anything failing.

Evidence on the review box: ~/journal/reports/voicebox-mbk-review-sotw-opus/final-593ca9d/. See final.out, and M5-settled-guard-removed.tap and drive-double-release-M5-settled-guard-removed.out.

title: file-list icons: the JS icon() helper does not set aria-hidden, while all 17 static icons in the page do — make JS-created decorative glyphs consistent
description:
FOUND IN REVIEW, NOT FIXED ON PURPOSE (uiflash, 2026-09-27). voicebox-e1m0's re-review of the file-list polish commit e31ef0a passed it and left this as a NON-BLOCKING note. It is filed rather than folded in so the reviewed tip the merger lands (e31ef0a) keeps its SHA and its PASS; the change is one line.

THE FACT, source-referenced:
- `public/fused.js:557` — `function icon(id)` builds `<svg class="icon"><use href="#id"></use></svg>` and sets NO `aria-hidden`.
- `public/index.html` — all 17 static icon buttons write `class="icon" aria-hidden="true"`, so the page's own convention is that a decorative glyph is hidden from the accessibility tree.
- So JS-created glyphs break the page's convention.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY, measured rather than assumed: the helper had ZERO call sites before this change (`grep -c 'icon(' public/fused.js` finds the declaration plus only the two added lines), and both new callers are inside buttons with their own accessible names — the folder cue inside `.file-open` (aria-label "<name>, folder" / "Read <name>") and the trash inside the delete button (aria-label "Delete <name>"). Nothing announces the wrong thing today; this is decoration hygiene, exactly as the reviewer framed it.

FIX (one line, in the helper so it covers every present and future glyph): `svg.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")`. Per-call-site attributes would work but would leave the next caller to remember — the helper is where the page's convention belongs.

ACCEPTANCE: every glyph from icon() carries aria-hidden="true" (assert it in tests/room-file-list-polish.test.mjs or the room-explorer suite); a grep shows no caller depends on the glyph being exposed (today: none); the room suites stay green.

RELATED: voicebox-beads-y4c2 / io3a / 35eg / r2tn (the file-list polish, commit e31ef0a on feat/file-list-polish), where the two new glyphs landed; voicebox-e1m0's 35eg re-review (PASS, this note); voicebox-gemini reviews the combined commit.

title: SAME CLASS: two read-only git call sites still inherit a hook's GIT_DIR (masked today, not pinned)
description:
Found while fixing the bp8 field finding (voicebox-beads-bp8, commit fdcc75d): `GIT_DIR` inherited from a git hook OUTRANKS `-C`, so a git command that means to ask about one tree can be answered by the hook's repository instead.

Two call sites still run without the strip that fdcc75d added (`gitEnv()` in tools/tree-dirt.mjs):
- `scripts/docs-touched.mjs:37` — `git(args)` with `cwd: ROOT`, no env strip. Runs as the FIRST pre-push stage, i.e. always under the hook.
- `tests/tasks-browser.test.mjs:128-129` — `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git status --porcelain` with `cwd: ROOT`, no env strip.

WHY THEY ARE MASKED TODAY, STATED SO THIS IS NOT OVERCLAIMED: both use cwd/ROOT = the pushed tree, and under a hook GIT_DIR points at the same repository, so the wrong answer and the right answer coincide. They are read-only (rev-parse/log/diff/status), so unlike the fixture's `git config` they cannot write anything. The risk is future drift: a caller that overrides ROOT/TREE (the harness does exactly that via VOICEBOX_TREE) would silently measure the hook's repo.

FIX: use the exported `gitEnv()` for these two sites (or move `gitEnv` to a neutral module if importing tools/ from scripts/ is unwanted), and add one assertion to the docs-touched test that a poisoned GIT_DIR does not change its verdict. Cheap, and it closes the same class rather than the two instances.

title: Every lane worktree prints 'fatal: Needed a single revision' on boot — rev-parse of a branch with no upstream
description:
FILED BY coord's instruction (voicebox-ui, 2026-09-24), from a real gate refusal.

THE OBSERVATION, in coord's words as asked: a check that resolves a revision it cannot resolve is the same family as everything else tonight.

WHERE IT COMES FROM: two call sites resolve the remote-tracking ref for the CURRENT branch:
  · server.mjs:916 (the build payload: branch/remote/ahead/dirty)
  · vite.config.js:79 (the page's build stamp)
Both run `git rev-parse --short origin/<branch>`. In a WORKTREE WHOSE BRANCH HAS NO UPSTREAM — which is every lane worktree before its first push — that command writes:

    fatal: Needed a single revision

to stderr on EVERY boot. Seen twice today: in the served server's own log (hours before this bead), and in the scratch server's captured stderr inside the f0b denylist test, where it was the only diagnostic next to a probe that had died.

IS IT LOAD-BEARING? CHECKED, and the answer is NO — both sites pass a default (`git([...], "")`) and both handle the empty result: the stamp says 'no origin/<branch> here, so the distance from a remote is unknown', and the health payload reports `remote: null, ahead: null`. So nothing is failing quietly; the cost is NOISE, and noise in a server's stderr is exactly what makes a reader mistake it for a fault (it appeared in this evening's gate refusal, next to an unrelated SocketError).

THE FIX, one line at each site: use the idiomatic existence test — `git rev-parse --quiet --verify origin/<branch>` — which exits 1 with NO stderr when the ref is absent, so the intent ('does this ref exist?') is explicit instead of being read off a default, and the 'fatal:' line disappears from every lane worktree's boot. Keep the existing fallbacks; this only stops git complaining.

NOT URGENT, and filed rather than fixed because coord asked for the filing and because the two sites are shared infrastructure (the stamp is a surface every lane reads).

title: wasm call fan-out: a concurrency semaphore for worker-holding calls — IF turn volume justifies it
description: A NAMED COST, measured not guessed (vb-resolver, 2026-09-23, feat/wasm-bounds): wasm calls each hold a worker for up to the host deadline, and there is NO concurrency cap — 20 parallel loop-calls held 20 spinning workers, Δ158MB RSS. The live batch path is serialized per session, but HTTP turns are not: N requests hold N workers for the deadline. DO NOT BUILD until the condition holds: turn volume where concurrent wasm calls are routine (measured, not anticipated) — e.g. sustained >50 concurrent wasm-holding turns, or one observed incident. THEN: a semaphore in lib/wasm-shelf.mjs's runInWorker (a small in-process counter + queue) capping concurrent workers, excess calls refused over-budget by name rather than queued unboundedly. Until then the cost is named in the gate's admission gets[] and the module header.

comments.author: sotw-opus
comments.text:
REVIEW by sotw-opus (Claude Opus). The author, voicebox-resolver, runs Gemini. Candidate: feat/mbk-wasm-semaphore @ c1e9dd5e7133.

VERDICT: FAIL, changes requested. NOT merged. The bead stays IN_REVIEW.

REPRODUCED
- wasm-shelf.test.mjs: 12/12. The MBK test ran; it did not skip.
- Unit lane: 293 tests, 292 pass, 0 fail, 1 named skip (wabt absent).
- Base: origin/main bc007fa is an ancestor. The branch deletes no files.

HOLDS WHEN DRIVEN
- The cap holds on real OS threads. A 12-call burst under the default (8 active, queue 0) added 8 OS threads, with 8 ok and 4 refused over-budget. The same burst with the cap at 100 added 12.
- The queue drains. With max 2 and queue 2: 4 ok, 2 refused, and the counter returned to 0.
- Acquire is synchronous, so there is no admission race.

BLOCKING
B1. A synchronous throw from `new Worker` leaks the slot. runInWorker increments activeWorkers before executeWorker, and the only release is in finish(), which is wired up after the constructor returns.
- Driven with a realistic trigger: this process's soft RLIMIT_NPROC lowered below the user's task count.
- `new Worker` threw ERR_WORKER_INIT_FAILED: EAGAIN synchronously. callWasmTool rejected, and the counter stuck at 1 active.
- With the limit restored, a plain Worker starts and answers. Every wasm call is still refused, "1 active, 0 queued; max 1", with nothing running. This lasts until restart.
- The rejection also leaves the wasm branch of lib/extensions.mjs:998 before its audit() line (no try/catch there).
- Fix: wrap the constructor in try/catch, release the slot, and resolve a named refusal. A DataCloneError from an uncloneable spec field takes the same path without process limits, so it can be the RED-first test.

B2. The env values are never validated, so a bad value fails open or hangs.
- VOICEBOX_WASM_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=abc gives NaN, and `length >= NaN` is never true, so the queue is unbounded. Driven: 20 calls, 19 queued, 0 refused. The control with queue 5 refused 14.
- MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKERS=eight, or 0, with a queue above 0: nothing is admitted and nothing releases, so queued calls hang forever. Driven: unsettled at 8 s.
- Fix: parse once at import. Integers only, max >= 1, queue >= 0. Otherwise throw at startup, naming the variable.

SHOULD FIX
S1. No test runs the drain path.
- Mutant M3 shifts the queued call off the queue but never runs it, and it passes the suite: the only test uses queue 0.
- Driven, it is real: 2 queued calls never settle, the counter sticks at 2 active, and a fresh call never settles either.
- Add a test with queue above 0.

S2. No test checks exactly-once release.
- Every completion reaches finish() twice: on 'message', then on 'exit'.
- Mutant M5 drops `if (settled) return` and passes the suite, because Math.max(0, n-1) absorbs the double release.
- Driven, it exceeds the cap: 3 live workers (OS threads) against a cap of 2.
- Replace the clamp with an assertion, and add a test that holds one slot.

S3. The docs publish the generator's placeholder.
- README.md and docs/07-architecture.md say "(undocumented — add a line to ENV_MEANING in scripts/docs-check.mjs)" for both variables.
- docs:check is green because it compares the block against its own output.
- docs/15-sandbox.md names the JS constant, not the env var, and omits the queue.

NON-BLOCKING
- N1. The cap is checked after the host-loop read, hash and compile, so a refused call still pays for them. A pre-check at the top of callWasmTool is race-free.
- N2. over-budget covers both "input too big" (permanent) and "host busy" (transient), so a caller cannot tell whether to retry.
- N3. The env var is read in 3 places.
- N4. _resetWasmWorkerStateForTest is exported from the production module.
- N5. The MBK test skips without ~/.isocan/modules/wasm-tools.

SCOPE (for coord and Paul, not a code verdict): the bead says DO NOT BUILD until concurrent wasm calls are routine (measured) or there is an incident. Neither is cited. With the defaults, a 9th concurrent wasm call that runs on main today is refused.

EVIDENCE: exact mutation anchors and counts are in mutate.sh and mutate.out (M1, M2 and M4 RED; M3 and M5 GREEN) and in mutant-drive.sh.
- Everything, including REVIEW.md, is in ~/journal/reports/voicebox-mbk-review-sotw-opus/.
- Worktree: ~/worktrees/voicebox-mbk-review-opus.

title: Compiled modules are compared by comments and strings — a code-only edit is invisible there
description:
DELIBERATE LIMIT of the currency check as landed (voicebox-beads-590, reviewed by vb-resolver 2026-09-23). tools/served-vs-disk.mjs compares a compiled .ts module (the server strips types and rewrites imports) by its COMMENT lines and its STRING LITERALS of 8+ characters — measured on browser/ui/ui.ts: 540 of 582 disk lines appear in the served copy, while comments (100/100) and strings (142/142) survive. vb-resolver verified the limit independently: drifting acts.ts 2000 -> 2500 was NOT caught, as the message states.

WHY NOT TIGHTER, and this is the interesting part: a type-stripping comparison (strip annotations from both sides, then compare) would catch code-only edits, but any mismatch between two strippers produces a FALSE RED on every run — and a gate that false-reds every run is worse than a named-narrow one, because people learn to ignore it. The limit is stated in the failure message ('a change that touches neither is not visible here') rather than left implied.

THE FOLLOW-UP, IF ANYONE WANTS IT: type-strip with the SAME transformer the server uses (not a second implementation), so the comparison is exact for both sides, and prove it against the real browser/ui/ui.ts and core/*.ts before wiring it in. Until then this bead is the record that the gap is known, named, and chosen.
close_reason:
FIXED — branch fix/compiled-module-exact @ 2324aa3, pushed (gate clear), awaiting the merger's landing.

TWO DEFECTS WERE STACKED, and the second was the bigger one — which is why the repro I filed (a code-only edit is invisible) was only half the story:

1. THE COMPARISON WAS NOT EXACT. The server serves a .ts module as stripTypeScriptTypes(readFileSync(file), { mode: 'strip' }), so the check now computes that same output for the disk file and compares it with the server's OWN CALL rather than a second implementation that could disagree with the first. Measured before choosing: strip-then-compare is byte-identical for browser/ui/ui.ts, browser/acts.ts, core/paths.ts, core/root.ts. A failure names the difference: 'acts.ts: the front is not serving what this tree compiles to — first difference at line 83: this tree compiles to "const LIST_LIMIT = 250;" and the front serves "const LIST_LIMIT = 200;"'. The comments-and-strings rule is now the FALLBACK (runtime without a stripper), exported and pinned by a test rather than a branch nobody exercises.

2. THE WALK NEVER REACHED THE FILE. Only .js refs were followed, so a compiled module's imports were never fetched at all — and nothing pointed at the worker: it is constructed at runtime (new Worker('/browser/worker.ts')), so browser/worker.ts AND ITS WHOLE GRAPH (browser/acts.ts, browser/opfs.ts, …) went uncompared. Measured: 8 modules compared; with the walk fixed, 12. So the code-only edit to acts.ts was invisible because the check never saw the file — the comparison was right and unexercised. The walk now follows .ts/.mjs imports and both worker forms.

DRIVEN BOTH DIRECTIONS in an environment of the branch's own (api :8899, front :5221, never Paul's), with a scratch tree at the SAME sha as the front's so identity matched: a code-only edit (acts.ts LIST_LIMIT 200 -> 250, no comment and no string touched) -> FAILS quoting both values and the line; the same tree unmutated -> PASS, 12 modules compared. And the counterfactual is now measured rather than argued: the fallback rule, handed the same pair, says nothing about the constant — it reports comments lost to type-stripping instead, a false positive of its own, which is a second reason it is the fallback and not the rule.

AND A PROPERTY WORTH KEEPING FROM THE PUSH: it went through. With the identity half composed into 590, a lane whose tree is not the one on the front now SKIPS BY NAME rather than failing — so the strict content rule blocks only when the front serves YOUR tree and your files differ, which is real lag. That is the composed design working, and it corrects my earlier statement to coord that the stricter rule would block side-worktree pushes.

title: A present-not-admitted file has no direct admit door — the host must stage then admit
description:
Found by the lane that closed bxx (2026-09-20), as a cosmetic lifecycle note rather than a gate.

A file that is PRESENT-NOT-ADMITTED has no direct admit door: the host must first stage it as a
proposal and then admit the proposal. It works, the outcome is correct, and every refusal is
named — but the host has to perform a two-step dance for a file it can already see.

The smoother shape: a host-side convenience that admits a file it can already name as present —
"admit this present file" — going through the SAME host token and the SAME ledger, so the
audit trail is identical and no new authority is introduced. Not a security change: the host
already holds the token that admits.

Small, and worth doing while the shape is fresh in the mind of whoever last drove it.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: DONE — feat/present-admit-door @33e2b51 (pushed; repo pre-push gate + page acceptance ALL CLEAR). The direct door: admitProposal falls back to the host directory when no proposal exists — same route, same host token (token-less admit refuses host-token-required), same gate re-run, same ledger (the admission is recorded). deny in place appends a ledger deny entry and the file stays present-not-admitted, never live. The inventory's present list is computed from directory + ledger AT CALL TIME, so a mid-session drop is visible immediately without waiting for a reload (that state gap was found by this drive and fixed). GET .../plan discloses a present file before the decision. Tests: the t9j drive in tests/extensions.test.mjs; whole gate 198/198 + acceptance ALL CLEAR.

title: MWG: .sr-only in public/style.css is a scroll container (the live copy of voicebox-beads-y5dr)
description:
Split out of voicebox-beads-y5dr because coord's dispatch makes sr-clip the sole writer of
public/environment.css and type-scale the owner of public/style.css.

public/style.css:47 `.sr-only { ... overflow: hidden; ... }` is the SAME declaration the
modern-web factory station flagged in public/environment.css, but this is the copy with LIVE
users: index.html carries 18 `.sr-only` elements (harness/settings/envs/exts-count labels, the
"Talk to it" heading, dialog close labels). public/environment.html carries NONE, so y5dr's
fix in environment.css is latent and this copy is where the defect is actually exercised.

MEASURED (not static), served room, Chrome 154 headless, before any fix:
  6 of the 18 `.sr-only` boxes were real scroll containers - a 65x20 scroll area inside a 1x1
  client box, and `scrollLeft = 999` moved it to 64. The other 12 are inside closed dialogs

voicebox-beads-y5dr did for public/environment.css.

BASELINE: `overflow: clip` is Baseline widely available since 2022-09-12 (Chrome/Edge 90,
Firefox 81, Safari 16) -> no fallback arm, no `@supports`, no Baseline TODO.
`overflow-clip-margin` is deliberately NOT used (limited availability).
Measured, not assumed: `clip` still reports the same scrollable overflow - it removes the
ability to scroll, not the overflow.

VISUALLY UNCHANGED: one page load with the declaration toggled in-page between hidden and
clip, twice each way, produced four byte-identical screenshots of the room.

This is not a proven WCAG violation; it is a programmatic scroll target no part of the UI
wants. Low impact, one declaration, in a file this lane already owns - a natural batch with
voicebox-beads-3674's typography work, which is why it is routed here rather than kept in
sr-clip's branch.

IN_REVIEW on fleet/sr-clip @ 1ce81fe (pushed to origin). docs-touched OK; unit lane green in the pre-push gate (642 tests / 632 pass / 0 fail / 10 skipped / 18.9s).

REPRODUCED, live, not static: the bead called this a static candidate with "no live keyboard/AT repro yet". It now has one. On the served room BEFORE the change, 6 of the page's 18 `.sr-only` boxes were real scroll containers — a 65x20 scroll area inside a 1x1 client box, and `scrollLeft = 999` moved it to 64. AFTER: 0 of 18. The probe ran both arms in the SAME page load (`overflow: hidden` -> scrollable, `overflow: clip` -> not), so the 0 is a measurement and not a broken probe.

BASELINE confirmed rather than assumed: `overflow: clip` is Baseline widely available since 2022-09-12 (Chrome 90, Edge 90, Firefox 81, Safari 16) -> no fallback arm, no `@supports` block, no Baseline TODO to clean up later. `overflow-clip-margin` is NOT used (that one is limited availability). Measured, not assumed: `clip` still reports the same scrollable overflow (65x20 in a 1x1 box) — it removes the ability to scroll, not the overflow.

VISUALLY UNCHANGED: one page load with the declaration toggled in-page between `hidden` and `clip`, twice each way, produced four byte-identical screenshots of the room.

CHANGED
- public/style.css, public/environment.css: `.sr-only` `overflow: hidden` -> `overflow: clip`, with the reason and this bead on a comment at the rule.
- tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs: a static read of both stylesheets plus a served-page browser arm, with a two-arm control so it fails rather than passes vacuously.
- README.md, docs/07-architecture.md: both repeated "the 80 original rules moved verbatim", which this change makes untrue, so both name it as the one in-place exception; docs/07-architecture.md's `public/style.css` entry carries the measurement.

SCOPE: the bead named environment.css only, but that page uses the class NOWHERE today (measured: 0 live `.sr-only` elements on /environment.html), so its copy of the fix is latent. The identical declaration in public/style.css is the copy with live users (18 labels on the room). Fixing only the bead's file would have fixed nothing that anybody exercises and left the defect live, so both copies are fixed as one declaration of one utility. Flagging it here rather than silently widening.

NOT VACUOUS: the new test was run against the pre-fix CSS. The browser arm fails with "6 of 18 sr-only boxes are scroll containers: envs-count-wrap (hidden), Change log (hidden), ..." and the static arm fails with "public/environment.css .sr-only must clip without a scroll container". Green at the tip: `node --test tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs` -> 2 pass / 0 fail / 4.5s.

FAST GATE: no cost. The file is already in the live lane and the browser arm adds one navigation to a browser it already launches. `docs:check` OK (14 generated blocks / 827 path claims).

Reviewer: `reviewer` subagent (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol — different family from this lane's claude/sonnet), run e0d01e99, asked to judge the clip-vs-hidden correctness, the test's non-vacuity, and whether the scope extension is justified. Verdict to follow on this bead.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: `.sr-only`'s `overflow` is `clip` rather than `hidden` in public/style.css and public/environment.css, so the 1px box clips its contents instead of becoming a scroll container. tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs asserts both stylesheets statically and the served room behaviourally, with a two-arm control that proves the assertion can fail. README.md and docs/07-architecture.md drop the now-untrue "moved verbatim" wording for environment.css.
WHY: `overflow: hidden` on a box whose contents overflow makes that box a scroll container with a real scroll area inside a 1x1 element — 6 of the room's 18 visually-hidden labels when measured. `overflow: clip` is the platform's clipping-only primitive and is Baseline widely available.
EFFECT: no visible change anywhere (four byte-identical screenshots). Screen-reader text is unaffected; what goes away is a programmatic scroll target that no part of the UI wanted. Unused on the Environment page today, so only the room's labels were affected.

SCOPE CORRECTED per coord's dispatch ("sole writer public/environment.css; type-scale owns style.css"). New tip **e6b5456** on fleet/sr-clip (force-with-lease, own branch; previous tip 1ce81fe is superseded).

- `public/style.css` REVERTED to origin/main — it is not this lane's file. The identical `.sr-only` declaration there is the copy with live users, so the actual defect is split out as **voicebox-beads-dche**, assigned to `voicebox-type-scale` with the measurement and the fix, so it can ride that lane's batch instead of colliding with it.

- README.md / docs/07-architecture.md now describe only the environment.css change and name voicebox-beads-dche for the other copy.

HONEST STATEMENT OF VALUE: nothing on environment.html uses `.sr-only` (measured: 0 elements), so the fix in THIS file is latent. The live defect — and the measurement proving it — is on public/style.css, and that is now dche's.

REPRODUCED, live, not static (the bead said "static candidate only; no live repro yet"). On the served room, which uses the same rule via style.css: 6 of its 18 `.sr-only` boxes were real scroll containers — a 65x20 scroll area inside a 1x1 client box, and `scrollLeft = 999` moved it to 64. Control arms in the same page load: an identical box under `overflow: hidden` reports itself scrollable, under `clip` it does not.

BASELINE verified: `overflow: clip` widely available since 2022-09-12 (Chrome/Edge 90, Firefox 81, Safari 16) -> no fallback, no `@supports`, no Baseline TODO. `overflow-clip-margin` deliberately not used (limited availability). Measured, not assumed: `clip` still reports the same scrollable overflow (65x20 in a 1x1 box) — it removes the ability to scroll, not the overflow, so a `scrollWidth > clientWidth` check would prove nothing.

VISUALLY UNCHANGED: one page load with the declaration toggled in-page between `hidden` and `clip`, twice each way -> four byte-identical screenshots.

TEST ARMS (coord asked for a negative/positive control for retained screen-reader-hidden semantics): the probe's computed `overflow` must be `clip/clip` (proves the SERVED stylesheet answered, not a UA default); the probe must not be scrollable; a `hidden` box must still report scrollable; a `clip` box must not. Accessible name is read from the real accessibility tree with a visible button as positive control and a `display:none` sibling as negative control. Non-vacuity verified by running the file against altered CSS — `hidden` fails ("the served environment.css must answer for .sr-only, got hidden/hidden"; "public/environment.css .sr-only must clip"), `display: none` fails (".sr-only must stay in the render tree"). A separate probe confirmed the AX read discriminates: clipped label names its button (1), `display:none` does not (0), `aria-hidden` does not (0).

EXACT RESULTS
- `node --test tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs`: 2 tests, 2 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, 5.0s.
- pre-push gate on e6b5456 (branch push): docs-touched OK; `npm run test:unit` — 642 tests, 632 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped, 13.3s.
- `npm run docs:check`: OK (14 generated blocks / 826 path claims).
- `fleet-check --fast` for the e6b5456 tree: started, receipt to follow in a comment.

NO FULL GATE run and no main merge (per dispatch). A11y/accessibility station not run: the change is one CSS declaration on a utility with no live users on this page, so `--sink file` would be noise; the measurement above is the evidence instead.

BROWSER: closed (each run's page and server are torn down in the test's `after` hooks; the one browser the reviewer-role lane used is theirs, not pooled with mine). I did not coordinate a shared browser with type-scale because this change needed none after the style.css revert — type-scale should be told there is no shared browser held by sr-clip.

Reviewer: coord routes the reviewer-role lane (my own earlier reviewer subagent was stopped when the scope changed, so no verdict exists from it). Please route it at tip **e6b5456**.

LAND-SUMMARY
WHAT: `public/environment.css`'s `.sr-only` now says `overflow: clip` where it said `hidden`, with a comment naming the bead, the measurement and the sibling copy. `tests/ui-ux-accessibility.test.mjs` asserts the declaration statically and, on the served Environment page, behaviourally with four arms including an accessibility-tree check of the retained name. README.md and docs/07-architecture.md drop the now-untrue "80 rules moved verbatim" wording for that file.
WHY: `overflow: hidden` on a 1px box whose contents overflow makes it a scroll container with a real scroll area inside a 1x1 element. `overflow: clip` is the platform's clipping-only primitive and is Baseline widely available.
EFFECT: none visible (four byte-identical screenshots). Screen-reader text is unaffected; what goes away is a programmatic scroll target no part of the UI wanted. On this page the class is unused, so only the room's labels (fixed via voicebox-beads-dche) were ever affected.

title: Live settings row: the success sentence 'Reconnected live session with X' is overwritten by the next-session wording on a re-render
description:
Found clearing voicebox-beads-0aez (2d1eefc). Cosmetic, but it is a line that speaks about state, so it is worth one line of code.

OBSERVED: on a SUCCESSFUL live restart, fused.js sets the model-state line to "Reconnected live session with <model>." and then calls renderAgentSettings(), which overwrites it with "<model> — the next session starts with it." (the settings row's own wording). The user therefore reads a *next-session* promise immediately after the running session has already switched to that model, and the success sentence is dead code.

FIX (one line): call renderAgentSettings() first, then set the sentence (or have renderAgentSettings keep a "reconnected just now" marker for a few seconds). Acceptance: after a successful restart the settings row says the running session is using the model, and a test asserts the sentence survives the re-render.
